Vitals were unremarkable and her oxygen saturation was >95% on her home oxygen requirement of 4 L by nasal cannula. Her pulmonary status and oxygen requirement were at her base-line. Her abdomen was soft， non-tender， and non-distend-ed， with normoactive bowel sounds and no rebound tender-ness or guarding. Laboratory values demonstrated a baseline， stable leukocytosis of 14 K/mm’ and serum potassium level of 2.8 mmol/L. Liver-associated enzymes were normal (AST21 U/L， ALT 34 U/L， alkaline phosphatase 115 U/L， total biliru-bin 0.3 mg/dL)， and stool H. pylori was negative.

【10】With her symptoms of epigastric pain and vomiting， similar to her symptoms when gastric sarcoidosis was initially diag-nosed， recurrence of gastric sarcoidosis was diagnosed with-out performing a repeat upper endoscopy. She was started on corticosteroid therapy with prednisone 30 mg daily with a planned 6-month slow taper. She was also placed on a PPl and H2 blocker and given a bowel regimen. Her symptoms persist-ed without significant change， so Speech Therapy was consult-ed on hospital day 4. A modified barium swallow (MBS) during this presentation showed esophageal dysmotility with stasis of contrast in the upper esophagus and tertiary contractions in the mid-esophagus. Speech Therapy recommended a liquid wash during solid meals to aid in bolus transit. This Speech Therapy strategy instructs patients to have alternating liquids and solids to aid in esophageal clearance of the food bolus. The Gastroenterology consultation service was following her case and determined on hospital day 7 (after 2 days of multi-disciplinary intervention) that she had objective improvements in her ability to advance her diet， more meals being tolerated， decreased use of antiemetics， and decreased quantitative re-ports of number of abdominal pain episodes. An inpatient re-peat endoscopy was not done because her symptoms improved with our multidisciplinary approach. Post-hospitalization fol-low-up 5 months later found she had intermittent right-sided pain and mild bloating without dysphagia， epigastric pain， or emesis described during her hospitalization. No repeat endo-scopic procedure was planned. Her clinical symptoms， prior in-terventions， current interventions described in this case， and outcomes are summarized in Table 1.

【11】Discussion

【12】The disease course and clinical manifestations of sarcoidosis are highly variable and dependent on the organ systems in-volved and the severity of the disease. Sarcoidosis has predom-inant pulmonary involvement in more than 90% of patients. Roughly 7% of patients have extrapulmonary involvement at onset， which increases as the disease course progresses . Among patients with Gl tract involvement， the stomach is the most frequent site compared to esophagus， intestines， gallbladder， liver， and pancreas . Notably， Gl sarcoidosis in the literature is described mainly in white patients， while our case highlights this entity in an African American patient. Granulomatous inflammation and fibrosis of the gastric wall can cause peptic ulcerations， narrowing of the gastric lumen， pyloric obstruction， and diminished peristalsis. Sarcoidosis can be concurrently active in one organ system and latent in another， making diagnosis and treatment difficult . In fact， there are no published reports examining changes in lung le-sions when gastric lesions recur； there does not appear to be a correlation in disease severity in one organ system (lung) based on expression of disease in another organ system (GI tract). Despite this patient’s multiple pulmonary sarcoid flares， the only confirmed gastric sarcoidosis flare was on diagnosis and was managed with weekly methotrexate and PPI. At that time， symptoms of emesis and heart burn improved on fol-low-up， without complete resolution. Only after this admission with quiescent pulmonary symptoms and active Gl complaints were her physicians able to recognize this as Gl sarcoidosis and employ multimodal therapy including steroids.

【13】The diagnosis of Gl sarcoidosis is particularly difficult because its symptoms can mimic many other Gl diseases such as irri-table bowel syndrome (IBS)， gastroesophageal reflux disease(GERD)， gastroparesis， and even gastric cancer. In the stomach， sarcoidosis is often clinically silent but can present with epigas-tric pain， reflux， nausea， vomiting， and weight loss.Epigastric pain and emesis are the 2 most common symptoms， at 70%and 33% of cases， respectively . Given the non-specific na-ture of symptoms， it is important to obtain histological evi-dence to make the diagnosis and guide treatment.

【14】The optimal treatment approach to Gl sarcoidosis is not de-finitively known. Most case reports demonstrate benefit with corticosteroids， typically starting at prednisone 20-40 mg/day and then tapered over time， although the timeline of the ta-per is varied . Disease-modifying immunosuppressive drugs such as methotrexate may play a role in steroid-refrac-tory cases. For severe gastric sarcoidosis， gastric resection may be needed to control life-threatening bleeding or bow-el stricture causing obstruction . For most patients， includ-ing ours， clinical symptoms are followed to determine the impact of treatment. To be as objective as possible， one can follow time to tolerating diet， percentage of meal tolerated， use of antiemetic therapy， pain scale for abdominal pain， and frequency of abdominal pain episodes. The patient discussed in this case had improvement following initiation of Speech Therapy's recommendations， suggesting this had a large im-pact in her improvement. At present， there are no standard-ized criteria to monitor Gl sarcoidosis symptoms and response to therapy. At follow-up， our patient’s symptoms and their im-pact on quality of life were assessed to determine the next steps for management.

【15】Our patient's symptoms of abdominal pain and vomiting were non-specific and could reflect (in addition to gastric sarcoid-osis) GERD， IBS， and esophageal dysmotility. Thus， we opted to pursue a broader treatment approach. We initiated prednisone30 mg daily dose with a slow taper over a period of weeks. We also treated her with a PPI， H2 blocker， and a bowel regi-men. MBS showed esophageal dysmotility with stasis of con-trast in the upper esophagus and tertiary contractions in the mid-esophagus.Speech Therapy initiated liquid washes with meals to aid in bolus transit， which aided in symptomatic relief.

【16】Conclusions

【17】Our case report highlights the importance of using prior histo-logical evidence of gastric sarcoidosis to help guide manage-ment of Gl symptom flare. Gastric symptoms such as epigas-tric pain， nausea， vomiting， and early satiety can be presenting signs for a sarcoidosis flare in a patient with pulmonary sar-coidosis， which is important for both pulmonologists and gas-troenterologists to be cognizant of. Gl sarcoidosis can mim-ic other diseases such as achalasia， GERD，IBS， or malignancy， so biopsy evidence of non-caseating granulomas on histolo-gy is needed for diagnosis. In addition to steroids for gastric sarcoid， a PPI， bowel regimen， and speech therapy techniques are important components of treatment. Our broader， multi-disciplinary approach has not been demonstrated in previous reports of Gl sarcoidosis flares and provided the patient with significant relief of symptoms.

【0】Background：

【1】Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (NBCCS)， also known as Gorlin-Goltz syndrome (GGS)， is an inherit-ed autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in the patched (PTCH) tumor-suppressor gene， which has high penetrance and variable phenotypic expressivity In 1960， Gorlin and Goltz defined the condition by3 main characteristics： multiple basal cell carcinomas， odontogenic keratocyst (OKC)， and skeletal anomalies. Nowadays， many neurologic， ophthalmic， endocrine， and genital manifestations are known to be associated with this syndrome. Considering the complexity of the clinical manifestations， a multidisciplinary approach is necessary for the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with NBCCS.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We report the case of a 27-year-old woman who presented with multiple maxillary and mandibular OKCs， as well as mandibular dentigerous cysts， all detected by X-ray. The medical records of the patient reported other findings such as falx cerebri calcification， osteolysis in femoral bones， and focal bone alteration suggestive of simple bone cysts. Based on the presented manifestations， it was concluded that the patient had characteris-tics of NBCCS. A multidisciplinary approach was necessary， and odontological intervention was used in man-aging treatment of the jaw cysts.

【4】Conclusions： In view of this combination of findings， it is of primary importance for dental surgeons and physicians to be able to recognize the signs and symptoms of NBCCS in order to achieve an early diagnosis and avoid the pro-gression of oral cysts， the metastasis of skin lesions， and progression of other less frequent manifestations.

【5】Keywords： Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome · Bone Cysts·Odontogenic Cysts

【6】Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (NBCCS)， also known as Gorlin-Goltz syndrome (GGS)， is a rare autosomal domi-nant disorder. It has a prevalence of 1 case in every 56 000to 256 000 individuals， and it is predominantly (in 70-80% of cases) caused by hereditary mutations . In 1960， Robert James Gorlin and Robert William Goltz established a classic triad which characterizes NBCCS： the presence of multiple ne-void basal cell carcinomas，jaw cysts， and congenital skeletal abnormalities. This classification was subsequently modified by Rayner et al， who added ectopic calcifications and plantar or palmar pits .

【7】Numerous other manifestations are known to be present in NBCCS， such as labial or palatine cleft， frontal humps， hyper-telorism， Sprengel deformity， thoracic deformity， vertebral al-terations， syndactyly， bone cysts in the hands， macrocephaly， pontification of sella turcica， ovarian fibroma， and medullo-blastoma . Due to the huge variability in mutation sites and presentations of the syndrome， there is no clear mani-festation in every patient . Thus， the current criteria for di-agnosis， established by Kimonis， consider some major and minor criteria， making it possible to establish an NBCCS di-agnosis based on the number and type of manifestations . More prevalent lesions， such as multiple basal cell carcinomas， OKCs， and skeletal anomalies at the ribs， are considered ma-jor criteria， while other less frequent manifestations (eg，ver-tebral alterations， syndactyly， bone cysts in the hands， macro-cephaly， pontification of sella turcica， and ovarian fibroma) are classified as minor criteria. When there are 2 major criteria or1 major and 2 minor criteria， the clinical diagnosis of NBCCS can be made . Aside from these described manifes-tations， the existence of a first-degree relative with GGS is an additional major criterion .

【8】Therefore， it is also very important to be able to recognize the variety of NBCCS manifestations and their long-term be-havior to ensure safe treatment. Thus， we report the case of a woman presenting with NBCCS who was followed up over a period of 17 years.

【9】Case Report

【10】A female patient， now 27 years of age， attended the ambula-tory clinic of the Dental School at the Universidade Federal do Para (UFPA)， Belem-PA Brazil， for the first time in 1999 when she was 10 years old， for a general dental appointment. Routine ra-diographic examination revealed the presence of a radiolucent， well-circumscribed area associated with tooth 43 ； thus， the diagnostic hypothesis were dentigerous cyst and odontogenic keratocyst. The lesion was assessed， and as the treatment of choice， enucleation of the cyst was performed and tooth 43 was maintained. The histopathological examination revealed a lesion compatible with a dentigerous cyst (the his-topathological report is provided in supplementary material 1).

【11】Three years after the first appointment ， a panoram-ic radiograph was taken to monitor the eruption process of tooth 43， which in addition revealed a radiolucent area distal of tooth 37 . The patient did not keep the annual follow-up appointment as recommended，and returned after3years . At that point， she presented a lesion (the sec-ond lesion) compromising the entire left ascending ramus of the mandible， and another less extensive lesion in the maxilla between the roots of teeth 14 and 15， without any clinical al-teration or expansion of the mandible cortex bone . The clinical and radiographic aspects of those findings suggest-ed the hypothesis of OKC， central giant cell lesion， and ame-loblastoma， which were then submitted to histopathological examination and confirmed the diagnosis of OKC (the histo-pathological report is provided in supplementary material 2).

【12】A computed tomography (CT) examination was performed (in2005)， in which the extension of the left mandibular lesion was delimited in 16.3x36.6 mm， and the maxillary lesion was locat-ed between the roots of teeth 14 and 15 measured 11.5 mm. With the aid of CT， it was also possible to observe the presence of 2 other areas of uniform bone rarefaction， which were well-circumscribed and located in the maxillary posterior region， in both sides of the maxilla . These maxillary find-ings were not clearly evident on panoramic radiography due to the overlapping of the maxillary sinus images. The diagnos-tic hypothesis was also OKC and the histopathological exam-ination confirmed the diagnosis of OKC  (the histo-pathological report is provided in supplementary material 2).

【13】In a medical appointment in May 2010， computed tomogra-phy of the femoral bone was performed， which showed the presence of well-defined lyticimages. Moreover， magnetic reso-nance imaging of the brain was also performed， in which could be seen a lamellar calcification of the falx cerebri in the inter-hemisphere region and the tentorial  (the medical report is provided in supplementary material 3).

【14】One year later ， another magnetic resonance imag-ing of the left leg showed osteolytic areas measuring approxi-mately 11.5 cm， suggestive of a simple bone cyst. In that same year， completing a total of 12 years of disease evolution， de-compression of the maxillary left side cyst was performed. In June 2015， 16 years since the first diagnosis， a new magnetic resonance imaging of the legs showed osteolytic areas in the left and right legs  (the medical report is provided in supplementary material 4).

【15】The combination of the first finding of a dentigerous cyst， mul-tiple and periodic incidence of OKC， medical reports of bone alterations suggestive of simple bone cyst lesions， and lamel-lar calcification of the falx cerebri suggested the possibility of the patient being affected by NBCCS， even though she had not yet presented basocellular nevus carcinoma of the skin.

【16】Routine laboratory tests were requested， which presented normal results， except for an alteration in alkaline phospha-tase (118 u/L). Periodic maxillofacial radiographic monitoring was suspended because the patient became pregnant soon after starting the treatment. In January 2017， a new panoram-ic radiograph showed normal radiographic appearance of the mandible and reduction of the right posterior maxillary lesion.

【17】Based on the presenting manifestations， it was concluded that the patient had characteristics of NBCCS， including multiple maxillary and mandibular OKCs (major criteria)， dentigerous cyst (minor criteria) falx cerebri calcification (minor criteria)， os-teolysis in femoral bones (minor criteria)， bone alteration sug-gestive simple bone cyst， and presence of head and neck skin maculae. Based on the dental history of the patient， the der-matologist then performed  remov-al of the skin lesions  as a preventive intervention， avoiding further manifestation of basocellular nevus carcinoma.

【18】Areas of osteolysis were also observed on the left leg and right shoulder， without a conclusive diagnosis； however， these were suggestive of simple bone cysts， which can also be associated with NBCCS. Thus， chest， skeleton， skull， and abdomen radio-graphs are useful for detecting other manifestations of NBCCS. The patient in the present study signed a consent form. The full chronology of orofacial findings and interventions in the present case is displayed in Table 1.

【19】Discussion

【20】Although the clinical symptoms are well known， the current case presents a combination of manifestations that are less frequently reported in the literature， thus contributing to a better understanding of the phenotypical variability of NBCCS， and also reinforces the need for a multidisciplinary approach in the diagnosis and follow-up of NBCCS patients.

【21】The NBCCS diagnosis is quite challenging because of the vari-ety of manifestations， which requires the attention of a multi-disciplinary team. These manifestations are frequently treated separately by different professionals according to the area af-fected， and diagnosis of the syndrome usually takes too long to be performed. Among the various findings， basal cell carci-nomas are very common and generally appear during puber-ty or from the second to third decade of life； however， they can also be seen in infants. The number oftumors varies con-siderably among affected individuals， and are more common in White than in Black people . They frequently appear in areas of skin that are not exposed to sunlight， although they commonly arise in the middle region of the face .

【22】The presence of OKC is also common， appearing in at least 75% of cases. OKC generally occurs in the mandibular ascending branch and it is commonly associated with unerupted teeth； thus， it can mimic dentigerous cysts on radiographs. Accordingly， it is possi-ble that the first lesion， initially diagnosed as a dentigerous cyst， could be the first OKC， since the presence of inflammatory infil-trate is able to modify the pattern of the cyst epithelium，mak-ing precise diagnosis at histopathological examination harder.

【23】There are rare reports in the literature of OKCs in NBCCS pa-tients that are not associated with dental elements . In our case report， OKCs were seen in the mandible and maxillary posterior region， with the maxilla being the most common l0-cation for cysts in syndromic patients according to Kumar .

【24】Skeletal anomalies are present in 60% to 75% of patients with this syndrome . A characteristic lamellar calcification of the falx cerebri， evidenced in skull radiographs or in CT images with anteroposterior incidence， is a common finding seen in the majority of affected patients .

【26】OKC-odontogenic keratocyst.

【27】The simple bone cyst is an intraosseous non-epithelium-lined cyst formation that can be empty or filled with serous or bloody fluid. In the present case， magnetic resonance imaging of the left leg suggested the presence of cystic lesions on the ex-tremities， which are not commonly reported in the literature in association with NBCCS.

【28】Tarnoki et al  reported the case of a patient diagnosed with NBCCS who presented cystic lesions in cortical and subcor-tical bone of the tibia and fibula on radiographs and CT scans， without a well-defined cyst aspect， being described by the au-thors as looking"mouse-eaten"， and they attributed these in-juries to the long-term use of isotretinoin (a retinoid derived from vitamin A) by the patient . However， McMullen et al reported that the long-term use of acitretin (as the dose administered daily， the total dose， or the dose administered throughout the duration of treatment)， which is composed of vitamin A， was not associated with osteopenia or osteoporosis compared to the control group . In addition， Vestergaard et al  concluded that the risk of bone fractures was not associated with treatment with increasing doses or durations of vitamin A analogs， isotretinoin and acitretin， when compar-ing to the control group .

【29】In our particular case， the patient only used Aderogil D3 (which is a vitamin D compound associated with vitamin A) for 1 year during childhood. However， the intake of vitamin A does not appear to be associated with the outcomes reported in the present case in the long bones， since they differ from the case reported by Tarnoki et al  due the well-defined and cir-cumscribed appearance in our patient.

【30】Over 100 minor criteria for diagnosing NBCCS have been re-ported in the literature . If the main criteria， such as basal cell carcinomas， mandibular cysts， or calcification of the ce-rebral sickle， are absent until adolescence， other radiologic manifestations of the disease may allow early diagnosis in childhood . It is recommended that patients be followed clinically and radiographically for a long period for early di-agnosis of the manifestations and to allow use of less inva-sive interventions.

【31】Long-term follow-up is very challenging and it depends in part on patient collaboration. The complexity of the case and the various professionals involved in the management of the pa-tient may have limited the compilation and acquisition of the complete medical history of all outcomes presented by the pa-tient， which might be a limitation of this study.

【32】Considering the complexity and recurrence of the clinical man-ifestations， a multidisciplinary approach is necessary for the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with NBCCS. Therefore， it is of primary importance for dental surgeons and physicians to be able to recognize the signs and symptoms of NBCSS in order to achieve an early diagnosis and avoid the progression of oral cysts and the metastasis of skin tumors and other less frequent manifestations， thereby improving the quality of life of NBCCS patients.

【0】ABSTRACT Spondylodiscitis is a diagnostic and therapeutic emergency. The association of spondylodiscitis with infective endocarditis has been reported previously， but at a rarer frequency compared to other complications of infective endocarditis. On admission， the patient was stable with sign of sepsis， with abnormalities of the neurological and cardiovascular examination. The lumbar MRI showed a signal remodeling of the D10 and D11 vertebrae， evoking an early infectious focus， without paravertebral collection or epidural signal abnormality. On the biological assessment， the infectious markers were disturbed. In view of the sponylodiscitis and the infectious biological signs， a transthoracic echocardium was performed， visualizing two large mobile vegetations at the level of the atrial side of the mitral valve， one of 18x12 mm at the level of A2  and one of 14x12 mm at the level of P2 ， causing a medium mitral insufficiency， without other detectable vegetation images. The blood cultures came back positive to a multisensitive aerococcus viridans， notably to amoxicilin clavulanic acid， ceftriaxone， gentamycin， imipenem and vancomycin. The incrimination of aerococcus viridans in infective endocarditis has been very rarely reported in the literature， especially in those associated with spondylodiscitis and in immunocompetent patients. Given the aggressive nature of A. viridans endocarditis and the often long delay in diagnosis， early recognition of symptoms， blood cultures， and echocardiography， including transesophageal echocardiography， are required to initiate appropriate treatment.

【1】KEYWORDS spondylodiscitis，aerococcus viridans， infective endocarditis， case report

【2】Introduction

【3】Spondylodiscitis is a diagnostic and therapeutic emergency. Two routes of inoculation are possible： hematogenous route， which is more frequent， or direct inoculation following surgery or disc puncture. The association of spondylodiscitis with infective en-docarditis has been reported previously， but at a rarer frequency compared to other complications of infective endocarditis. Al- though aerococci have been reported to be of low virulence， they can still cause severe disease， even in immunocompetent hosts. The incrimination of aerococcus viridans in infective endocardi-tis has been very rarely reported in the literature， especially in those associated with spondylodiscitis and in immunocompe-tent patients. We report the case of a patient， visibly without immunodepressing factor， admitted with spondylodiscitis in whom explorations revealed the presence of aerococcus viridans infective endocarditis.

【4】Case report

【5】An 81-year-old man， operated for a prostate adenoma 10 years ago， presented to the emergency room with back pain that had been evolving for 4 months， associated with headaches， fever， asthenia and altered general condition. A probabilistic antibi-otic therapy was prescribed without clinical improvement. On admission， the patient was pale， generally altered， conscious， hemodynamically and respiratorily stable， with a fever of 37.9°. The neurological examination revealed a positive bell sign， with-out motor or sensory deficits. The cardiovascular examination revealed a systolic murmur at the mitral focus. The rest of the examination was unremarkable. The lumbar MRI showed a signal remodeling of the D10 and D11 vertebrae ， with a moderate hypersignal of the intervertebral disc at this level evoking an early infectious focus， without paravertebral col-lection or epidural signal abnormality. The biological workup showed a microcytic hypochromic anemia at 9.7 g/dL with a ferritinemia level of 750 ng/ml， an elevated neutrophil count of 9680/uL， an elevated CRP level of 163 mg/dL， an elevated fibrinogen level of 6.8 g/l and an elevated procalcitonin level of 1.7 mg/1. In view of the sponylodiscitis and the infectious biological signs， a transthoracic echocardium was performed， visualizing two large mobile vegetations at the level of the atrial side of the mitral valve， one of 18x12 mm at the level of A2  and one of 14x12 mm at the level of P2 ， causing a medium mitral insufficiency， without other detectable vegeta-tion images. The cerebro thoracic abdominal pelvic CT scan showed a right frontal brain abscess and a splenic infarct. The blood cultures came back positive to a multisensitive aerocoCCus viridans， notably to amoxicilin clavulanic acid， ceftriaxone， gen-tamycin， imipenem and vancomycin. The surgical indication of endocarditis was given in front of a size of mobile vegetations exceeding 15 mm with multiple symptomatic emboli. Surgery was refused by the patient. He was put under intravenous an-tibiotic therapy with ceftriaxone at a meningeal dose of 4g/day and gentamycin 160 mg.

【6】Discussion

【7】The coexistence of spondylodiscitis， more frequently lumbar，in patients with IE has already been reported . The frequency of this coexistence varies according to the studies， ranging from 1 to 10%. However， this rarity contrasts with the high reported frequency of back pain in patients with IE . These spinal pains are due to microemboli of immune complexes with or without bacteria . The intensity of spinal pain is highly variable， sometimes very moderate， and may even be absent， in about 6% to 8% of spondylodiscitis associated with infective endocarditis， which is a particularity to be known. The coexis-tence of these two infections is more frequent in men after the fifth decade. Favouring factors are found， leading to immunode-pression： such as alcoholism， diabetes and renal insufficiency.

【8】MRI is the most relevant examination for the diagnosis of spondylodiscitis. Identification of the germ is essential， and is based on blood cultures， sampling of a potential entry point， and discovertebral puncture-biopsy， which allows the germ to be isolated in 70 to 80% of cases. From a microbiological point of view， a distinguishing feature between spondylodiscitis asso-ciated with IE and spondylodiscitis alone may be the infectious agent involved： a large predominance of streptococci is found in patients with spondylodiscitis associated with IE， versus a predominance of staphylococci in patients with spondylodiscitis alone.

【9】A parenteral， probabilistic bi-antibiotic therapy should be started rapidly， and then adapted to the isolated germ， with an oral relay if decided. It must be prolonged， for a period of 6 to12 weeks. Neurosurgery is not necessary， except in the case of rare complications such as severe neurological compression.

【10】Therefore， the search for IE is essential， and this is done by systematically performing a transthoracic echocardiography， or even systematically performing a transesophageal echocardiog-raphy， or at least in predisposed patients with heart failure， a sep-tic state on admission， valvulopathy， chronic renal insufficiency and end-stage renal disease . And conversely， any spinal pain， regardless of severity， during IE should prompt spinal MRI to look for infectious spondylodiscitis. Spondylodiscitis does not appear to worsen the prognosis of IE， although the need for heart valve replacement appears to be more common in IE patients with spondylodiscitis.

【11】The genus Aerococcus has been known since 1953. There are 7 species described to date， including Aerococcus viridans which is an aerophilic Gram-positive cocci found in indoor air(hospitals， classrooms， factories， offices)， dust， raw vegetables， animals ， animal products， and human skin. It causes urinary tract infections， endocarditis， meningitis， spondylitis and sep-ticemia ， mainly in immunocompromised people. The risk factors for systemic A viridans infections have not yet been fully elucidated；however， leukopenia， previous antibiotic ther-apy prolonged hospitalization， invasive procedures and foreign body implantation have been associated with severe A viridans infections . Very rarely， no obvious immunosuppressive fac-tors are found as in the case of our patient. Studies have shown that they are generally susceptible to B-lactams including peni-cillin and vancomycin . On the other hand， resistance to quinolones， tetracycline， clindamycin and streptomycin has been noted . Gentamicin resistance has also been reported occasionally .

【12】Cases of A viridans endocarditis are rare. The rare isolation of this germ may be due to the fact that it grows poorly on media other than blood agar， and that in case of polymorphic flora it is largely masked by faster growing germs. On the other hand， the appearance of the colonies may cause confusion with streptococci and staphylococci.

【13】In all reported cases， the endocarditis involved the mitral or aortic valves， resulting in congestive heart failure and death in one patient . In three cases， the isolated strain of A viridans was resistant to penicillin or quinolones . Biologically， there was a non-specific elevation of inflammatory markers. A viridans endocarditis follows a chronic course， with symptoms lasting 12 weeks to 7 months， retains a comparatively lower mortality rate (9%) compared to Staphylococcus aureus infective endocarditis of the left native valve. It nevertheless requires a surgical approach in 45% of reported cases .

【14】Conclusion

【15】An IE must be evoked in front of any febrile infectious spondy-lodiscitis or evolving in a context of altered general state im-posing the systematic realization of a TTE or even a TEE if predisposing ground. Any spinal pain during an IE should be investigated for infectious spondylodiscitis by MRI. Appro-priate antibiotic therapy should be continued for at least 6 weeks in case of osteoarticular complications. The incrimination of A. viridans in IE， especially associated with spondylodiscitis， has been rarely reported. Given the aggressive nature of A. viri-dans endocarditis and the often long delay in diagnosis， early recognition of symptoms， blood cultures， and echocardiography， including transesophageal echocardiography， are required to initiate appropriate treatment.

【0】ABSTRACT Spondylodiscitis is a diagnostic and therapeutic emergency. The association of spondylodiscitis with infective endocarditis has been reported previously， but at a rarer frequency compared to other complications of infective endocarditis. On admission， the patient was stable with sign of sepsis， with abnormalities of the neurological and cardiovascular examination. The lumbar MRI showed a signal remodeling of the D10 and D11 vertebrae， evoking an early infectious focus， without paravertebral collection or epidural signal abnormality. On the biological assessment， the infectious markers were disturbed. In view of the sponylodiscitis and the infectious biological signs， a transthoracic echocardium was performed， visualizing two large mobile vegetations at the level of the atrial side of the mitral valve， one of 18x12 mm at the level of A2  and one of 14x12 mm at the level of P2 ， causing a medium mitral insufficiency， without other detectable vegetation images. The blood cultures came back positive to a multisensitive aerococcus viridans， notably to amoxicilin clavulanic acid， ceftriaxone， gentamycin， imipenem and vancomycin. The incrimination of aerococcus viridans in infective endocarditis has been very rarely reported in the literature， especially in those associated with spondylodiscitis and in immunocompetent patients. Given the aggressive nature of A. viridans endocarditis and the often long delay in diagnosis， early recognition of symptoms， blood cultures， and echocardiography， including transesophageal echocardiography， are required to initiate appropriate treatment.

【1】KEYWORDS spondylodiscitis，aerococcus viridans， infective endocarditis， case report

【2】Introduction

【3】Spondylodiscitis is a diagnostic and therapeutic emergency. Two routes of inoculation are possible： hematogenous route， which is more frequent， or direct inoculation following surgery or disc puncture. The association of spondylodiscitis with infective en-docarditis has been reported previously， but at a rarer frequency compared to other complications of infective endocarditis. Al- though aerococci have been reported to be of low virulence， they can still cause severe disease， even in immunocompetent hosts. The incrimination of aerococcus viridans in infective endocardi-tis has been very rarely reported in the literature， especially in those associated with spondylodiscitis and in immunocompe-tent patients. We report the case of a patient， visibly without immunodepressing factor， admitted with spondylodiscitis in whom explorations revealed the presence of aerococcus viridans infective endocarditis.

【4】Case report

【5】An 81-year-old man， operated for a prostate adenoma 10 years ago， presented to the emergency room with back pain that had been evolving for 4 months， associated with headaches， fever， asthenia and altered general condition. A probabilistic antibi-otic therapy was prescribed without clinical improvement. On admission， the patient was pale， generally altered， conscious， hemodynamically and respiratorily stable， with a fever of 37.9°. The neurological examination revealed a positive bell sign， with-out motor or sensory deficits. The cardiovascular examination revealed a systolic murmur at the mitral focus. The rest of the examination was unremarkable. The lumbar MRI showed a signal remodeling of the D10 and D11 vertebrae ， with a moderate hypersignal of the intervertebral disc at this level evoking an early infectious focus， without paravertebral col-lection or epidural signal abnormality. The biological workup showed a microcytic hypochromic anemia at 9.7 g/dL with a ferritinemia level of 750 ng/ml， an elevated neutrophil count of 9680/uL， an elevated CRP level of 163 mg/dL， an elevated fibrinogen level of 6.8 g/l and an elevated procalcitonin level of 1.7 mg/1. In view of the sponylodiscitis and the infectious biological signs， a transthoracic echocardium was performed， visualizing two large mobile vegetations at the level of the atrial side of the mitral valve， one of 18x12 mm at the level of A2  and one of 14x12 mm at the level of P2 ， causing a medium mitral insufficiency， without other detectable vegeta-tion images. The cerebro thoracic abdominal pelvic CT scan showed a right frontal brain abscess and a splenic infarct. The blood cultures came back positive to a multisensitive aerocoCCus viridans， notably to amoxicilin clavulanic acid， ceftriaxone， gen-tamycin， imipenem and vancomycin. The surgical indication of endocarditis was given in front of a size of mobile vegetations exceeding 15 mm with multiple symptomatic emboli. Surgery was refused by the patient. He was put under intravenous an-tibiotic therapy with ceftriaxone at a meningeal dose of 4g/day and gentamycin 160 mg.

【6】Discussion

【7】The coexistence of spondylodiscitis， more frequently lumbar，in patients with IE has already been reported . The frequency of this coexistence varies according to the studies， ranging from 1 to 10%. However， this rarity contrasts with the high reported frequency of back pain in patients with IE . These spinal pains are due to microemboli of immune complexes with or without bacteria . The intensity of spinal pain is highly variable， sometimes very moderate， and may even be absent， in about 6% to 8% of spondylodiscitis associated with infective endocarditis， which is a particularity to be known. The coexis-tence of these two infections is more frequent in men after the fifth decade. Favouring factors are found， leading to immunode-pression： such as alcoholism， diabetes and renal insufficiency.

【8】MRI is the most relevant examination for the diagnosis of spondylodiscitis. Identification of the germ is essential， and is based on blood cultures， sampling of a potential entry point， and discovertebral puncture-biopsy， which allows the germ to be isolated in 70 to 80% of cases. From a microbiological point of view， a distinguishing feature between spondylodiscitis asso-ciated with IE and spondylodiscitis alone may be the infectious agent involved： a large predominance of streptococci is found in patients with spondylodiscitis associated with IE， versus a predominance of staphylococci in patients with spondylodiscitis alone.

【9】A parenteral， probabilistic bi-antibiotic therapy should be started rapidly， and then adapted to the isolated germ， with an oral relay if decided. It must be prolonged， for a period of 6 to12 weeks. Neurosurgery is not necessary， except in the case of rare complications such as severe neurological compression.

【10】Therefore， the search for IE is essential， and this is done by systematically performing a transthoracic echocardiography， or even systematically performing a transesophageal echocardiog-raphy， or at least in predisposed patients with heart failure， a sep-tic state on admission， valvulopathy， chronic renal insufficiency and end-stage renal disease . And conversely， any spinal pain， regardless of severity， during IE should prompt spinal MRI to look for infectious spondylodiscitis. Spondylodiscitis does not appear to worsen the prognosis of IE， although the need for heart valve replacement appears to be more common in IE patients with spondylodiscitis.

【11】The genus Aerococcus has been known since 1953. There are 7 species described to date， including Aerococcus viridans which is an aerophilic Gram-positive cocci found in indoor air(hospitals， classrooms， factories， offices)， dust， raw vegetables， animals ， animal products， and human skin. It causes urinary tract infections， endocarditis， meningitis， spondylitis and sep-ticemia ， mainly in immunocompromised people. The risk factors for systemic A viridans infections have not yet been fully elucidated；however， leukopenia， previous antibiotic ther-apy prolonged hospitalization， invasive procedures and foreign body implantation have been associated with severe A viridans infections . Very rarely， no obvious immunosuppressive fac-tors are found as in the case of our patient. Studies have shown that they are generally susceptible to B-lactams including peni-cillin and vancomycin . On the other hand， resistance to quinolones， tetracycline， clindamycin and streptomycin has been noted . Gentamicin resistance has also been reported occasionally .

【12】Cases of A viridans endocarditis are rare. The rare isolation of this germ may be due to the fact that it grows poorly on media other than blood agar， and that in case of polymorphic flora it is largely masked by faster growing germs. On the other hand， the appearance of the colonies may cause confusion with streptococci and staphylococci.

【13】In all reported cases， the endocarditis involved the mitral or aortic valves， resulting in congestive heart failure and death in one patient . In three cases， the isolated strain of A viridans was resistant to penicillin or quinolones . Biologically， there was a non-specific elevation of inflammatory markers. A viridans endocarditis follows a chronic course， with symptoms lasting 12 weeks to 7 months， retains a comparatively lower mortality rate (9%) compared to Staphylococcus aureus infective endocarditis of the left native valve. It nevertheless requires a surgical approach in 45% of reported cases .

【14】Conclusion

【15】An IE must be evoked in front of any febrile infectious spondy-lodiscitis or evolving in a context of altered general state im-posing the systematic realization of a TTE or even a TEE if predisposing ground. Any spinal pain during an IE should be investigated for infectious spondylodiscitis by MRI. Appro-priate antibiotic therapy should be continued for at least 6 weeks in case of osteoarticular complications. The incrimination of A. viridans in IE， especially associated with spondylodiscitis， has been rarely reported. Given the aggressive nature of A. viri-dans endocarditis and the often long delay in diagnosis， early recognition of symptoms， blood cultures， and echocardiography， including transesophageal echocardiography， are required to initiate appropriate treatment.

【0】ABSTRACT Objective： Avascular Necrosis happens to be one of the most common diseases in patients presenting with a chronic painful hip. We have evaluated these patients in the background of demographic details. Material and Method：Prospective study evaluating 319 patients using conventional X-ray and MRI. Imaging findings were evaluated， and staging of AVN was done on both modalities. Demographic details were documented in the background of clinical settings. Results： 10.6% of the cases were diagnosed on X-Ray (34 patients). Sequential MRI examination picked up 21%MRI (68 patients). X-ray was missing the diagnosis of AVN in nearly 50% of the cases. 46% of the cases (147 patients) were from age groups ranging from 20-40 years， followed by older patients. It is comparatively rare in young and， if present， is associated with other systemic diseases. 60% of the patients were male， and 40% were females. Bilateral hip pain was present in 31% of the cases (100 patients). Right side involvement (37%) was slightly more common than left (32%) in cases with unilateral hip pain. Commonly encountered imaging findings associated were femoralhead marrow ooedema in 59 patients (87%)， double-line sign in 54 patients (79%)， subchondral cysts in 42 patients (62%)， followed by joint effusion， joint space reduction， femoral head altered contour， femoral head fragmentation with collapse. Conclusion： X-ray alone can miss up to 50% of the cases of Avascular Necrosis of the femoral head， especially in milder and potentially salvageable cases. Correct imaging interpretation and grading make the role of MRI pivotal.

【1】KEYWORDS Chronic non-traumatic hip pain， AVN， X-ray， MRI， Bone Marrow Oedema.

【2】Introduction

【3】Avascular necrosis of the femoral head or Osteonecrosis of the femoral head is the cellular death of the bone cells due to compro-mised blood supply. High-risk asymptomatic patients should be screened to detect earlier stages of AVN to facilitate early treat-ment and prevention of subsequent bone destruction. Apart from establishing the presence of AVN， MRI also determines the percentage of involvement of the femoral head weight-bearing surface . MRI uniquely shows bone marrow signal alterations in patients with a wide variety of musculoskeletal complaints . MRI is essential for the overall evaluation of hip pain，cover-ing both bony and soft tissue causes， and it can more precisely pick up articular cartilage pathology . The ever-evolving diag-nostic role of MRI in hip osteonecrosis is widely accepted. AVN is successfully managed by early treatment prior to sub-chondral fracture and cartilage damage . Unluckily， radiography of-ten fails to demonstrate the disease until a substantial portion of the weight-bearing surface of the femoral head is involved. By that time， pathophysiological ischemia of bone marrow and eventual death of trabecular bone becomes inevitable. Screen-ing of asymptomatic， high-risk patients may enable early inter-vention . In 5% to 25% of cases， a history of corticosteroid use was present. The classic presentation was Deep， throbbing Groin pain which was worse with activity. Range of motion was decreased， predominantly in cases of effusion. C sign-pain is described by a cupped hand placed above the greater trochanter. MRI has a Specificity of 98% and sensitivity of 97% in differenti-ating AVN from a non-AVN disease of the femoral head.

【4】This study attempts to estimate the proportion of Avascular Necrosis patients with painful hip， study the spectrum of find-ings， and detect AVN at an earlier stage. We included patients presenting with non-traumatic hip pain (acute or chronic) and all age groups of both sexes. Patients with trauma， frank contraindi-cation to MRI (MRI incompatible implants， Metallic foreign body in situ)， or a history of claustrophobia were excluded.

【5】Pathophysiology of Avascular necrosis of the proximal fe-mur is a disease process which is complicated and initiated by an interruption of blood supply to the femoral head， causing bone tissue death. AVN varies in presentations depending upon the stage. Osteochondritis dissecans is said when an infarction affects the local segment of bone. This is most often seen in weight-bearing bones. When infarction affects an entire epiph-ysis in a growing child， it is called epiphyseal ischemic necrosis. The proximal femur is the most common location for this occur-rence . The aetiology of femoral head avascular necrosis is diverse. Though avascular necrosis can develop idiopathically， most conditions that disrupt the blood supply to a segment of bone can be divided into three categories： Conditions that re-sult in external blood vessel compression or disruption near or within the bone， such as infection or steroid administration. Conditions that result in blood vessel occlusion because of thick-ening of the vessel wall， such as radiation therapy， systemic lupus erythematosus， or giant cell arteritis. Conditions resulting in blood vessel blockage from thromboembolic processes， su chas alcoholism， diabetes， or sickle cell disease .

【6】Radiographic Findings in evaluation in the initial stages of AVN may appear normal for several weeks. One of the first radiographic signs， seen as early as 4 weeks post-injury is a radi-olucent crescent image， representing the collapse of the necrotic subchondral bone of the femoral head. This crescent sign is seen parallel to the superior rim of the femoral head， subjacent to the articular surface. Sclerosis and cyst formation at the femoral head are other characteristic signs of the initial necrotic processes and healing attempts. These radiographic signs can be differen-tiated from the similar characteristic signs of osteoarthritis by the normal preservation of the radiographic joint space， which is not involved in the necrotic process. In advanced stages of AVN， the femoral head will collapse or be flattened because of structural weakness and impaired ability to withstand weight-bearing forces .

【7】The entire femoral head and neck will become more radio-dense because new bone attempts to heal the trabeculae micro fractures and calcification of necrotic marrow. Eventually， the progressive collapse of the femoral head will change joint sur-face congruity and involve the acetabulum. At this advanced stage， joint space will be markedly compromised. Radiologists identify the stages of disease progression by the presence of the foregoing signs. The plain film does not detect stage0 and 1AVN. Between the onset of symptoms and the appearance of radiographic abnormalities delay of 1-5 years may occur. There-fore， normal radiographic findings do not necessarily mean that the disease is not present. A staging system using radiographic findings has been developed by Ficat and Arlet and has been used widely for treating avascular necrosis. This has been sup-planted by the classification system of Steinberg et al.， which incorporates MRI and scintigraphic findings .

【8】Magnetic resonance imaging has recently emerged as the most sensitive， specific， and widely used diagnostic tool for avascular necrosis of the femoral head. In most reports， MRI can diagnose very early lesions with a greater than 90 percent specificity and sensitivity . Asymptomatic， high-risk patient screening may enable early intervention. Imaging findings have been that signal intensity bands or lines within the femoral head are seen surrounding the area corresponding to ischemic bone onT1-andT2-weighted images. The band is thick onT1-weighted images and is thinner and with a second inner band of high signal intensity on T2-weighted images. The appearance on T2-weighted images is known as the “double-line sign"and is considered highly specific for AVN. This band is supposed to represent the reactive interface that separates normal marrow from infarcted marrow .

【9】The signal intensity of central infarcted bone corresponds to areas of bone necrosis seen at histologic examination. High signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images are seen within areas of necrosis when viable， and fatty marrow is still present with prolonged ischemia and necrosis， the necrotic bone has a signal intensity pattern re-sembling that of fluid， with low signal intensity on T1-weighted images and high signal intensity on T2-weighted images. When fibrosis and sclerosis of the involved bone occurs， it is reflected by low signal intensity on bothT1-and T2- and weighted images. Secondary signs and sequelae of AVN can also be seen at MR imaging. The joint effusion or cartilaginous thinning may be present. AVN progresses to the instability of the femoral head with fragmentation and eventual collapse . In the early stages of the disease， there may not be any alteration of the nor-mal signal intensity of the femoral head. The first sign of AVN is nonspecific： diffuse areas of decreased signal intensity are noted in the normally high-signal-intensity fatty marrow on T1-weighted images. This is supposed to be due to ooedema within the marrow. Focal findings along the anterosuperior aspect of the femoral head are more specific： a low-necrotic segment of bone.

【10】Materials and methods

【11】It is a Cross-sectional observational and descriptive study con-ducted in a tertiary care center. Data is analyzed using propor-tions.

【12】All patients underwent MRI with anterior surface coil imag-ing. Oblique imaging planes were used for optimizing the demonstration of normal and abnormal hip anatomy . Long T2 of free water makes detection of body fluids easy T2- in which the fluids have an intense signal relative to solid tissues . True coronal and axial planes give symmetric， bilateral images， which are important in diagnosis and time factors， especially for the femoral head， neck， and intertrochanteric region. Supporting lig-aments， musculature and articular space are better appreciated on axial MR images .

【13】All the MRI examinations， including the image mentioned above， were carried out either on a 3Tesla MRI machine or a1.5Tesla machine. In addition， x rays were carried out on CR/DR system of 1000mA. The presence or absence of joint fluid was analyzed qualitatively， which had an intense high signal cor-responding with that of fluid. Before starting radiographic ab-normalities， mostly increased joint fluid presents， and signal intensity becomes highest after loss of femoral head contour， revealing MRI helps in detecting fluid in the hip joint highly sensitive .

【14】Radiographs were taken with 1000mA X-ray machine of MED-ITRONICS in the department. MR imaging was done with a3Tesla MRI machine or 1.5Tesla machine using abdominal sur-face coils as they allow increased signal-to-noise ratio and im-proved spatial resolution. Radiograph views are taken： Pelvis with both Hips-AP. The patient was given a supine position， and both feet were internally rotated at an angle of 15°. The posi-tion helps in reducing the normal 25 to 30° femoral anteversion， making the femoral neck more clearly visible .

【15】Special views depending on aetiology

【16】MRI was done with the same patient positioning， and the fol-lowing sequences were taken：

【17】a) T1W， T2W (Axial， Coronal)

【18】b) STIR(Axial， Coronal)

【19】c) PD-(Coronal)

【20】d) Fast spin-echo & Gradient echo were used in indicated cases.

【21】Patients were positioned by palpating the greater trochanter and centring the images at that level. A set of coronal T1-weighted scout images was then obtained. Coronal images were planned to depict the posterior-to-anterior portion of the femoral head.

【22】Results

【23】Pathology most frequently identified in our study is AVN of the femoral head as the cause of painful hip joint. In 68(21%， n=319) cases of AVN diagnosed on MRI， nearly half cases were identified on plain radiography.

【24】34 cases diagnosed on plain X-Ray 1(2.9%，n=34) case showed minor osteopenia suggestive of stage I AVN (FICATS staging). 5(14.7%，n=34) cases showed mixed osteopenia or sclerosis with subchondral cysts suggestive of stage II AVN (FICATS staging). 15 cases (44%， n=34) show stage Ⅲ disease with a crescent sign and cortical collapse (FICATS staging). 13 cases with stage Ⅳ(38%， n=34) of disease present as end-stage with evidence of secondary degenerative change (FICATS staging).

【25】55(80%， n=68) cases had double line sign on MRI， seen on T2W sequences of medullary bone as high signal intensity line， within a parallel rim of decreased signal intensity， often with serpentine borders. Corresponding T1 demonstrate both high and low intensity together. This finding corresponds with Zurlo et al. ， who also found double line signs in 80% of cases. Figure 5 shows complications as a sequela to AVN. Different grades of AVN were also noted in a few cases， for example， in Figure 6.

【26】Out of 68 cases diagnosed on MRI， 3(4.4%，n=68) cases were stage I AVN of disease.22(32%，n=68) cases were stage II， and29(42%， n=68) cases were stage Ⅲ AVN. In 14(20%， n=68) cases， femoral head contour abnormality with degenerative changes suggested stage IV AVN.

【27】Zoia and Colab et al.  studied AVN by various modali-ties. Our study matched this in various spectrums of findings in different stages of AVN. Manaster et al.  suggested scle-rosis as early changes of AVN on the radiograph. Huang et al. suggested MR signal alteration in-band or ring-like patterns as a common finding. Our study had comparable findings. In a similar study， HayamAbdElmonsifAbdElatifDrar et al.  assessed painful hip with MRI and found AVN in 25% of cases. Our study is comparable to it， as we found 21% cases of AVN.
