【0】Background：

【1】Omental masses can histologicaly correspond to several entities， for instance， epiploic tumors， omental infarction， acute diverticulitis， acute appendicitis， traumatisms and so on.

【2】Case report：

【3】We report on a case of a 47 year-old male who presented with abdominal pain in the right upper quadrant. Abdominal examination objectified a painful bulk in this location. Abdominal CT-scan showed a mass surrounded by huge inflammatory changes in the fat tissue (omentum). The patient underwent surgical operation and a 10 centimetres in diameter mass was removed. No postoperative complication was recorded.

【4】Conclusions： Histological examination found a necrosed omental lipoma. We discuss the possible diagnosis.

【5】key words： Lipoma · omentum · omental infarction· liposarcoma·leiomiosarcoma · fibrosarcoma Primary tumours of the greater omentum are very rare. Ultrasound allows the detection and charac-terization of such lesions， but determination of their precise anatomical location is usually difficult by US. Computed tomography determines the omen-tal origin of the tumour. Thus， when US reveals an abdominal tumour of unknown origin， the possibility of an omental tumour， although rare， must be kept in mind and CT should be performed.

【6】CASE REPORT

【7】We report on a case of a 47 year-old male patient that complained of a 4-days abdominal pain to the right upper abdominal quadrant. No nausea or vomiting was referred. The patient had a previous record of diabetes， hyperuricemia， high blood pressure， disli-pemia and congenital blindness.

【8】Physical examination revealed a temperature of37.7°C and the abdominal examination found a 10centimetres painful bulk in the right upper quadrant. No abdominal tenderness was present. Laboratory routine test found 13.000 leukocytes/uL， 79.1%neu-trophyles， glucose 338 mg/dL， creatinine 1.5 mg/dL and fibrinogen 1446 mg/dL. Urine sediment analy-sis was normal. Abdominal CT-scan showed some inflammatory changes in the right hypochondrium and right flank . The initial diagnosis was omental infarction， so the patient was admitted to the hospital and was put under antibiotic treatment(cefepime 2gr ev/12 hr and metronidazol 1.5 gr ev/24hr). Colonoscopy was performed and showed no pathological findings. The symptoms did not ease off after one week of treatment and a control CT-scan showed that the initial findings had worsened， so the patient was subjected to exploratory laparotomy. A 17x8x6 centimetres mass in the omentum was encountered in the right upper quadrant. Several small bowel loops were stuck on the mass but were easily separated. No postoperative complication was recorded and the patient was discharged 4 days after operation.

【9】Histological exam of the specimen revealed the presence of a pseudocystic mass containing hematic liquid and the presence of normal adipocytes. The clinical and histological diagnostic was consistent with infarcted omental lipoma .

【10】DISCUSSION

【11】Omental masses can histologicaly correspond to sev-eral entities， for instance， epiploic tumors， omental infarction， acute diverticulitis， acute appendicitis， traumatisms and so on.

【12】Epiploic tumors are very uncommon， and there can be several histologic types： leiomyosarcoma， fibrosarcoma， haemangiopericitoma， liposarcoma， leiomyoma， spindle cell sarcoma， lipoma and others. Thus， only about 200 cases have been published in the literature . Ultrasonography and CT-scan findings in cases of omental infarction are similar as in the cases of Omental liposarcomas and mesotheliomas. These can present as abdominal painless masses and other vague symptoms and signs. Theratoma of the epiplon can histologicaly contain any kind of tissue， but specifically teeth or bone . It can also simulate an epiploic appendagitis or an omental infarction when it's located adjacent to the colon or in the omentum. Omental lipoma is usually non-symptomatic and it’s usually an incidental finding in autopsies， although it can get torsioned and produce an acute abdomen. It could be easily diagnosed by means of ultrasonography (a well defined homogeneous hyperechogenic mass) or CT-scan and they can be easily enucleated.

【13】Omental infarction was first described by Bushin1.896. It’s a well described entity in adults of all ages(mean 40 year-old). They are mostly diagnosed as acute appendicitis because of their identical symptoms and always lead the patient to the operating room. The aetiology remains unknown although it is said that there could be an embryologic variant of the omental vascularization that could make it more likely to suffer an infarction 3，51.Occasionally， a bulk can be found in the abdominal examination and ultrasonography or CT-scan can be very useful in the diagnostic pro-cess. The literature suggests that omental infarction is a benign entity that can be managed conserva-tively. Puyalert et al  described the conservative management in 7 adults with clinical symptoms and ultrasonography findings of omental infarction and concluded its feasibility. Nevertheless， surgical exci-sion of the affected omentum is the definitive treat-ment， solving abdominal pain in 100% of the cases with low or non-existent complications .

【14】Epiploic appendagitis is an entity that should also take part in the process of differential diagnosis. One hundred and ten cases of epiploic appendagitis in 1960 and 276 cases in 1968 were described. This increase in the incidence of epiploic appendagitis could be explained by the extended use of modern techniques such as ultrasonography and CT-scan. This entity can appear at any age (maximum incidence： 40year-old). The symptoms are usually referred to lower hemiabdomen， but nausea， vomiting， diarrhea and fever are not very frequent， instead. Only occasionally an abdominal bulk can be found. It frequently presents as acute abdomen， being diagnosed as acute diverticulitis in 2.3 to 7.1% of the cases and as acute appendicitis in0.3 to 1% of the cases. The complementary methods of choice are ultrasonography and CT-scan but even with these， sometimes it is impossible to distinguish between epiploic appendagitis， omental infarction and acute diverticulitis. In those cases in which it is not possible to view the colonic wall adjacent to the diverticle in CT-scan the radiologist usually describe the findings as an acute appendagitis. Doppler colour analysis could be helpful in these patients . Nevertheless， the course with conservative management is similar in both cases 

【15】Acute appendicitis should also be borne in mind. Swelling of the appendix or the peri-appendicular fat tissue in ultrasonography or CT-scan frequently confirms the diagnosis.

【16】Tuberculous peritonitis is a less frequent entity but not less important. Difuse involvement of the omentum found in CT-scan or ultrasonography could suggest omental infarction. However， lymphadenopathies， mesentery involvement， thikness of the intestinal wall or loculated ascitis should also be found to support this diagnosis .

【17】The most frequent metastasizing tumor is ovarian carcinoma， although peritoneal metastasis could be due to any abdominal tumor. It could also simu-late epiploic appendagitis or an omental infarction but other signs of malignancy should be present. Abdominal trauma should also be taken into account but in this case， the diagnosis is clear because of the previous record .

【18】Mesenteric paniculitis is shown in ultrasonography as non-compressible hyperechogenic mass； Symptoms in omental infarction are very alike . Urachal cyst is a rare abnormality that occurs in a persistent part of the urachus. The cyst can be symptomatic when it gets infected， causing mesogastric abdominal pain. The loca-tion of the cyst (extraperitoneal) and its relation to the urine bladder may suggest the correct diagnosis 

【19】CONCLUSSIONS

【20】We can conclude from the reviewed literature， on the one hand， that omental lipoma has basically been described in newborn and very young children On the other hand， we can also state that big lipomas in adults usually appear in the mesentery. Both of them frequently present as acute abdomen due to occlusion or torsion.

【21】The case that we report on is a big lipomatous mass in an adult with an unusual way of presenting. The patient had a previous record of congenital blindness and dislipemia and though we cannot establish a direct relationship between these two facts and the surgical findings， it is worthy to mention such a coincidence.

【0】Background：

【1】Strongy loidiasis is a worldwide infection， infecting approximately 100 million people in more than 70 coun-tries. It is common in Southeast Asia， Latin America， Papua New Guinea and some parts of the United States. Malnutrition， cancer， organ transplantation，hemodialysis and prolonged use of corticosteroids increase the risk of this opportunistic infection. Undiagnosed and untreated， its mortality rate can be high.

【2】Case Report： We present a 36 year old Black man with history of malignant hypertension and glomerulonephritis who had chronic eosinophilia and vague， poorly localized abdominal pain and tenderness. He received three deceased donor kidney transplants， two of them failed and the third one succeeded. However， after transplantation， his abdominal pain and discomfort increased， became anorexic， lost weight and developed fever and lethargy Duodenal aspirate examination was positive for strongyloides stercoralis. Immunosuppressant medications were discontinued and he was treated with thiabendazole. In spite of treatment， his condition deteriorated and he expired.

【3】Conclusions： Due to low sensitivity of stool and serological examinations， diagnosis of strongyloidiasis often is delayed. A high index of suspicion and prompt diagnosis and treatment are essential in decreasing the morbidity and mortality of this infection. Before organ transplantation， every attempt should be made to find the cause of peripheral blood eosinophilia and in endemic areas and among patients coming from countries where the in-fection is known to exist， organ recipients and donors should be screened for parasitic infections including strongyloidiasis

【4】Key words： transplant· strongyloides · hyperifection

【5】Strongyloides stercoralis is a soil nematode  that is endemic in tropical and subtropical areas of the world， infecting approx-imately 100 million people in Southeast Asia， Latin America， Puerto Rico， southeastern and occasionally northern areas of the United States . Overcrowded conditions and a high de-gree of migration from tropical areas of the world are respon-sible for the prevalence of this nematode in some metropoli-tan areas. Once the parasite has gained access to the host， it may reside there for decades. Hyperinfection with this oppor-tunistic infection might occur in a variety of circumstances in which cell mediated immunity is depressed， like malnutrition， malignancy， human immunodeficiency virus infection(HIV)， and patients who have received organ transplantation .

【6】Case Report

【7】The patient was a 36 year old Black man with history of arterial hypertension who was first hospitalized with several months history of abdominal pain and distention. He was noted to be hypertensive with cardiomegaly and retinal hemorrhages. Laboratory studies showed BUN 110 mg/dL， serum creatinine16 mg/dL， C3 75 mg/dL， hematocrit 34% and erythrocyte sed-imentation rate 47 mm/hr. Urinalysis showed 3 to 4 red blood cells per high power field and 2 to 3+ protein. Peripheral blood examination showed 31% eosinophils. Abdominal films showed small kidneys and multiple examinations of the stoo. for ova and parasites were negative. He was diagnosed to have ma-lignant hypertension and membranoproliferative glomerulone-phritis and his eosinophilia was thought to be related to he-modialysis. Because he was uremic， an arteriovenous fistula was established and he was placed on maintenance hemo dialysis. Over the next four years， he was hospitalized twice， once with a urinary tract and a second time with a respirato ry tract infection. Later on he received two deceased donor kidney transplants that failed and so a third transplant was attempted. Post-transplant， he was treated with immunosup-pressants that included azathioprine， prednisone and cyclo-phosphamide. The kidney transplant functioned well and pred-nisone dose was gradually tapered down.

【8】Following kidney transplantation， he continued to have mild abdominal pain that was diffuse， transient， not localizable and associated with anorexia， weight loss and vomiting cof-fee ground material. Eight months later， the pain became more intense and he was hospitalized. His abdomen was distend-ed， bowel sounds were decreased and his stool was positive for occult blood. Laboratory examination showed， white blood cell count(WBC) 10800， with 8% eosinophils， BUN 97 mg/dL， creatinine 2.2 mg/dl and glucose 420 mg/dL Plain x-rays of the abdomen showed distended bowels but no evidence of bowel perforation. Initially， he was treated conservatively and he showed signs of improvement but later he developed fever and progressive lethargy. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) fluid exam-ination showed， cloudy fluid， with 191 WBCs/cmm， 95% neu-trophils and 5% lymphocytes. He was treated for meningitis but all cultures came back negative. Chest x-ray was sugges-tive of pneumonia and a radiogram of the upper gastrointesti-nal tract was suggestive of diffuse thick infiltrative folds in the stomach and small intestine. These changes were thought to be parasitic in origin and therefore an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (EGD) was done. Gastric and duodenal aspirates were obtained and they were positive for Strongyloides ster-coralis larvae. Immunosuppressive medications were stopped and he was treated with thiabendazole but he continued to deteriorate and he expired a few weeks later. Permission for post-mortem examination was not granted.

【9】Discussion

【10】Strongyloides is a genus containing around 50 species that are obligate Gl parasites of vertebrates. It infects mammals， rep-tiles， birds and amphibians. Two species of strongyloides in-fect humans， S Stercoralis and S fulleborni . The latter is pri-marily seen in African primates but it can also infect humans. Strongyloides stercoralis is a soil parasitic infection that afflicts millions of people around the world. It was first described in French soldiers in Vietnam who had chronic diarrhea and it took 50 years to describe its life cycle . Strongyloides stercoralis usually resides in the duodenum and proximal jeju-num. The female parasite produces eggs that are embedded in the intestinal mucosa and are capable of reproducing parthoge-netically (Asexually) and produce first stage rhabditiform larvae that are 180 to 380 micrometer long， with a short rhabditoid esophagus and a prominent genital premodrium . These larvae pass through the stool， change into second， third and sometimes fourth stage filariform larvae， that may develop into free living adult males and females. The larvae penetrate the unbroken skin， enter the blood stream， travel to the lungs， ascend the trachea， enter the Gl tract， penetrate the mucosa and live in-between the enterocytes. Sometimes， larvae， that have reached the third stage， directly penetrate the intestinal mucosa， enter the blood stream and reach oth-er organs (Autoinfection). In doing so they carry intestinal bacteria on their surfaces and cause septicemia and menin-gitis (Hyperinfection). This repeated endogenous cycle leads to chronic infection that can last for decades . This condi-tion usually manifests itself by anorexia， nausea， poorly lo-calizable abdominal pain and distention， diarrhea and some-times bowel obstruction. Skin involvement is not uncommon and may be in the form of a serpiginous， migratory， urticarial rash， termed larva currens. Skin of buttocks， groin and trunk is more commonly affected than the skin covering the head and extremities. Lung involvement is usually asymptomatic but it may cause cough，dyspnea， pulmonary infiltrates， hemorrhage and bacterial abscess formation . With hyperinfection and disruption of intestinal mucosal integrity， paralytic ileus，peri-tonitis， septicemia  and occasionally massive Gl bleeding may ensue . Immunocompromised states， like HIV， mal-nutrition， malignancy ， severe nephrotic syndrome，organ transplantation， corticosteroid use and residence or travel to endemic areas should heighten level of suspicion for the pres-ence of this infection .

【11】Kidney disease， including nephrotic syndrome due to min-imal change disease  and acute interstitial nephritis have been reported in association with strongyloidiasis. In one case， minimal change disease was proven by kidney bi-opsy and the disease remitted once the infection was treat-ed with Ivermectin .

【12】Strongyloidiasis should be suspected if there are suggestive clinical signs or symptoms， eosinophilia or suggestive serolog-ical findings. Eosinophilia， though a frequent marker of par-asitic infection， may not be present in severely immunocom-poromised patients and therefore its absence does not exclude the possibility of Strongyloides. Definitive diagnosis is based on the microscopic detection of larvae in the stool. However， in uncomplicated infections the worm load is low and the stool examination may be negative. Repeated stool examinations increase the chance of finding infectinglarvae. Direct smear of feces in saline-Lugol iodine solution， Baermann concentra-tion， formalin-ethy. acetate concentration， Harada-Mori filter paper culture and agar nutrient plate culture are some of the techniques used to enhance discovery of the parasite . Examination of the duodenal fluid for larvae has more sensi-tivity than stool examination. The parasite may also be found in the pleural and peritoneal fluid， mucinous cysts， lymph nodes， sputum and urine. Serological studies， including ELISA have a high sensitivity but a low specificity for strongyloi-des stercoralis infection . Recently a novel real time PCR for the universal detection of strongyloides species was de-scribed  that is highly specific (100%) and may be helpful in some clinical settings.

【13】Treating strongyloidiasis， like other worm infections， is a dif-ficult issue partly because of the unreliability of stool exam-ination results， low specificity of serologic testing and partly due to unfamiliarity of physicians， particularly in non-endem-ic areas . Treatment with Ivermectin 200 mcg/kg， two dai-ly doses， is considered to be the treatment of choice， with a cure rate as high as 100% . It can be given orally， rectally， intravenously or subcutaneously . Other drugs like thia-bendazole and albendazole have been used as well. A ran-domized trial of a single dose of Ivermectin (200 mcg/kg) vs. albendazole (400 mg daily ×3) among 301 children infect-ed with strongyloides stercoralis in Zanzibar showed a cure rate of 83 vs. 45%. In another study involving cancer pa-tients， thiabendazole was effective in 74% of patients infect-ed with strongyloidiasis . Ivermectin is a semi synthetic derivative of the avermectin B1， it is metabolized by the liv-er through cytochrome P450-3A4， but it does not significant-ly affect the activity of CYP 450-3A4 and CYP2D6 or CYP2C9. It is highly protein bound and therefore it is not dia-lyzable.Thiabendazole， albendazole and mebendazole are me-tabolized by the liver and excreted by the kidney. Due to this， they should be used with caution in patients with kidney and liver disease. Regardless of which regimen is used to treat the patient， close follow up of the patient is mandatory to ensure that the infection is eradicated.

【14】Strongyloidiasis has been described with all organ transplants， including heart， lung， liver， intestine， pancreas， bone marrow， but mostly it has been reported in kidney transplant patients. It can infect both donors and recipients. Every effort should be made before harvesting or transplanting organs in endemic ar-eas or in suspicious circumstances to rule out parasitosis and particularly strongyloidias is . Prolonged corticosteroid use， either in the early post-transplant period or during treat-ment of rejection episodes， may reactivate dormant strongy-loidiasis and promote its proliferation in infected hosts . Cyclosporine may have protective effect  while tacroli-mus increases the risk of infection. In a study in sprague-Daw-ley rats infected with strongyloides ratti， cyclosporine， given orally or subcutaneously， decreased the stool concentration of strongyloides by almost 50% and It neither synergized nor antagonized the effect of thiabendazole .

【15】Our patient most likely had the infection at the time he was transplanted. Following transplantation， his condition deteriorated and although strongyloidiasis was diagnosed and treated promptly and his immunosuppressant medica-tions were discontinued， he did not improve and he expired.

【16】Unexplained peripheral blood eosinophilia， immunocompro mised state， prolonged use of steroids， travel to endemic ar-eas and especially organ transplantation should increase phy-sician suspicion for this infection . Close collaboration with infectious disease specialists is mandatory and very help-ful. Failure to treat this infection promptly and adequately can be associated with a mortality rate that could reach as high as 40 to 70% . In suspicious circumstances， empiric ther-apy can be justified .

【17】Conclusions

【18】Strongyloidiasis is a serious problem for immunocompromised and transplanted patients. Every attempt should be made to identify the cause of eosinophilia in transplant donors and re-cipients. This is particularly important in endemic areas and also in non-endemic areas where there is a large immigrant population. Once the infection is identified， immunosuppres-sion should be reduced until the infection is treated.

【0】ABSTRACT Background： Among trauma cases， the third most common cause of death from trauma is abdominal injury. Urbanization and industrialization led to events of violence which have increased the incidence of abdominal injuries. These injuries are real emergencies and put an enormous strain on all concerned in its management. Despite injuries being one of the important causes of injury and death， minuscule consideration has been given to its interventions， strategy to halt these injuries and the management of the sufferers. This study was conducted to highlight the trends of abdominal trauma and to determine the causes and injury patterns and their clinical profile. Aims & Objectives：To study the various organs injured in cases of abdominal trauma. Study various factors and clinical presentation in abdominal injuries. Material & Methods： Prospective observational study， carried out in the Department of General Surgery， SRTR GMC Ambejogai， Maharashtra， India. Detailed history regarding the site of trauma， nature of object assaulted the patient was inquired. All the patients with suspected abdominal injury were examined thoroughly，and baseline findings were recorded. All required investigation was carried out. Data were collected from case records， and analyses were done with the help of Microsoft Excel. Result： During the study， 100 cases were included and analyzed.72% of cases of abdominal injury were of blunt abdominal trauma. The most common age group was between 21-30years (54%). Almost 70% of cases reached the hospital within 5 hrs after injury. The most common organ injury was the small intestine (28%) and Spleen (26%). Conclusion： Among the study group， patients were mostly from 21 to 30years of age group. The blunt abdominal injury was the commonest type. Abdominal pain， vomiting and abdominal distension were the most common clinical findings. Small bowel and spleen were commonly injured organs. Chest injury was commonly involved in the associated injury. CT scan of the abdomen was the most sensitive organ to detect the exact nature of the intra-abdominal injury.

【1】Trauma is a major contributor to mortality and morbidity rates among the economically productive workforce of a popula-tion. Trauma ranks along with atherosclerotic arterial diseases and malignancy as a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Injury continues to be the leading cause of death in the first four decades of life. Abdominal injuries are on the increase in both developed and developing countries， and they remain a major source of morbidity and mortality. Abdomen is third in the list of most commonly injured regions in trauma. Abdominal trauma can be either blunt or penetrating. Although blunt ab- dominal trauma predominates to be the most common mode of an abdominal injury penetrating abdominal trauma remains one of the commonly encountered emergency surgical practice conditions. S Blunt Abdominal Traumas (BAT) account for90% of these injuries (compared to penetrating). Usually in the polytrauma abdominal injury associated with others. Their frequent association with other traumas requires an adequate clinical evaluation to avoid additional morbidity and mortal-ity. High-speed vehicles， decivilization of the human race， terrorism， and sports are just a few of the predisposing factors of trauma. Major trauma multiple organs and systems of the human body Evaluation of a patient with abdominal trauma can be a most challenging task that a surgeon may be called on to deal with.

【2】Abdominal injuries may be parietal or visceral injuries. Vis-ceral injuries may be intraperitoneal or retroperitoneal. Liver， spleen， stomach， small bowel， duodenum， large bowel， pancreas， kidney， ureter， and the retroperitoneal vascular are the organs included in this study. The pelvic organs are excluded. Delay in the presentation at the hospital after an injury， injury to the multiple organs， excessive blood loss and the ominous reputa-tion for high morbidity and mortality are just a few of the many reasons which make this topic a fascinating one.  Abdominal trauma contributes significantly to the morbidity and mortal-ity of trauma patients. In spite of injuries being one of the most important causes of injury and death in the developing world， minuscule consideration has been given to interventions designed to halt these injuries and the management of the suf-ferers. This study was conducted to highlight the demographic trend， clinical presentations and investigations of abdominal trauma.

【3】Aims and objectives

【4】·To study the various organs injured in cases of abdominal trauma.

【5】·Study the factors， like time of presentation after injury， age， symptoms， clinical presentation.

【6】·To study the incidence of other associated injuries.

【7】Materials and Methods

【8】The present study was carried out in the Department of General Surgery， SRT Rural Government Medical College， Ambajogai， Maharashtra， India. This was a cross-sectional observational study. The data was collected by direct interview with the pa-tient or patient relatives accompanying the patient and obtaining a detailed history. All the patients with suspected abdominal injury were examined thoroughly， and baseline findings were recorded. Investigations： All the protocol investigations were done in every case，i.e. Abdominal Xray， CT Scan， USG， Com-plete blood count， LFT， KFT etc.， were done. Thorough assess-ments for injuries and initial resuscitation of the patients were done. Documentation of patients， related to clinical findings and demographic information， treatment procedures were recorded on a specially prepared Detailed history regarding the site of trauma，nature of object assaulted the patient was inquired.

【9】Results and observation

【10】During study period medical records of 100 cases were included and analyzed as per inclusion and exclusion criteria.

【11】In the present study， we observed that incidence of abdominal trauma was common in the age group of 21-30 years in both types of injuries， i.e. in blunt， it was (42%) while in penetrating it was (12%). Musau P et al.  reported 53.8% of abdominal trauma cases belonged to the 21-30 years age group. This study almost correlates with the present study. Whereas Kala S et al. has reported 28% of cases in 21-30 years. Haque MA et al. have reported 29.9% of abdominal trauma cases in the age group of 11-20 years. In the majority of the studies， the most commonly involved age group was 21-30 years. The mean age of patients in this study was 29.3 years which was comparable with Gholipur S et al.  and Chalya PL et al.  studies.

【12】In our study amongst male abdominal trauma was more com-mon in comparison with a female (Blunt 54% and penetrating18%). The male to female ratio was 2.6：1. Male to female ratio reported in various studies Gholipur S et al.  study， Chalya PL et al.  study， Gad MA et al.  study， Asuquo M et al. study， Mehta N et al.  study， Manohar K et al.  study， Musau P et al.  study， is 4：1，3.2：1， 4.4：1， 5.3：1， 3.7：1， 4：1，12.3：1respectively. The gender discrepancy with males outnumbering females seen in our study because males are the earning mem-bers of the family and are most exposed to outdoor activities in contrast to females， who tend to stay a home engaged in house-hold activities. The incidence of blunt abdominal trauma was72%. The incidence reported in other studies， Asuquo M et al. was 39.58%， Gad MA et al.  was 69.4%， Musau P et al. was 33.75%. As compared to other studies， the incidence of abdominal trauma was higher. This may be because of the small sample size. The incidence of penetrating abdominal trauma in our study was 28%. The incidence reported by Chalya PL et al.  was 22.2%， by Gad MA et al.  it was 30.6%. As compared to other studies the incidence of trauma was low. The ratio of penetrating to blunt abdominal trauma in our study was2.5：1. The ratio reported in other studies， Musuo P et al.  study， Manohar K et al.  study， Gad MA et al.  study was 2：1， 1.63：1 and 2.26：1， respectively. The ratio reported in the present study was following Musau P et al.  study and Gad MA et al.  studies.

【13】It was evident that the abdomen's pain was the predominant presenting symptom in patients in abdominal trauma (Blunt 68%and penetrating 26%) followed by vomiting. Out of all patients with blunt abdominal trauma， most patients (50%) presented casually within 5 hours. At the same time， most patients (20%) with penetrating injury arrived at casualty within 5 hours after trauma. It was evident that the small bowel was the most com-monly involved (22% in blunt trauma and 6% in penetrating injury)， hollow viscus in abdominal trauma. The spleen was the most commonly (26%) injured solid organ inblunt trauma， while mesentery was the most commonly (6%) injured soft tissue or-gan in penetrating abdominal trauma in the present study. Some patients required more than one procedure due to two or more intra- abdominal organ injury. Few patients in whom abdominal-ray were normal but had a perforation of hollow viscera， which was detected on CT scan abdomen. This indicates that the CT scan is more sensitive to plain abdominal radiograph in cases of abdominal trauma. CT scan abdomen and CT scan thorax showed 100% sensitivity for detecting intra-abdominal and tho-racic pathology in our study. FAST was done in 76 patients and detected pathology in 64 patients and was normal in 12 patients in our study (Sensitivity 84%). Kulkarni S et al.  studies2015， Mehta N et al.  studies 2010 reported the same findings as our study. The most common injured organ in penetrating abdominal trauma was the small bowel. In the study reported by Asuoquo M et al.  studies， 2010 small bowel was the most commonly injured viscera followed by omentum. In the study reported by Manohar K et al.  2010 jejunum was the most commonly injured viscera. Thus the findings in our study are following other studies. The spleen was the most common injured solid organ in our study 2015， Srihari V et al.  studies2015， Manohar K et al.  studies 2010. Thus the finding re-ported in our study was following the studies mentioned above. In the studies reported by Kala SK et al.  studies， 2010 study liver was the most common organ injured. Chest injury was the commonest extra-abdominal injury associated with abdominal trauma in our study， followed by skeletal injury and head injury. A similar pattern of extra-abdominal injuries associated with abdominal trauma was observed in other studies.

【26】Conclusion

【27】The most common type of abdominal injury was blunt abdomi-nal trauma. Patients among the age group of 21-30 years were the most common age group. Most of the cases reached the hospital within 5 hrs after injury. Abdominal pain， vomiting and abdominal distension were the most common clinical findings. Small bowel and spleen were commonly injured organs in study populations. CT scan of the abdomen was the most sensitive organ to detect the exact nature of intra-abdominal organ injury. Early diagnosis of the extent of injury by appropriate imaging in-vestigations and early interventions are crucial in management.

【28】The outcome profile of this study could improve diagnostic and therapeutic strategies to reduce the mortality associated with these injuries.

【0】Background：

【1】Primary thyroid lymphomas are rare diseases that continue to produce diagnostic and therapeu-tic dilemmas. Among these， Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) represents the more com-mon subtype while Burkitt lymphoma (BL) is unusual. Distinguishing between BL and DLBCL is critical as the two disease require different therapeutic management. Diagnostic accuracy is there-fore essential to obtain patient safety.

【2】Here， we described the second case of Burkitt Lymphoma of the thyroid gland reported in the English literature， investigate the differential diagnosis and explore the diagnostic approach that might be used when neoplasia with morphological features intermediate between BL and DLBCL happens on pathologist's practice.

【3】Case Report：

【4】A 56-year-old women presented to our attention for the evaluation of a rapidly growing neck mass causing compressive symptoms. Ultrasound examination demonstrated two hypoechogenic nodules within a diffusely enlarged thyroid gland. Histological analysis showed cells resembling DLBCL， as well as starry sky pattern and immunohistochemical pattern suggestive of BL. The final diagnosis of BL was confirmed by FISH analysis that demonstrated c-myc-IgH rearrangement with t(8；14) translocation.

【5】Conclusions：

【6】This study demonstrates that no single parameter alone (such as morphology， genetics analysis or immunophenotyping) can be used as gold standard for the diagnosis of BL， but a combination of several diagnostic techniques is necessary for an optimal practical approach. Since treatment reg-imens for BL and DLBCL differ significantly， we believe that our study should be useful to suggest the correct diagnostic algorithm to be used when a case of BL， with unusual localization and an-biguous morphological features， is encountered in routine setting.

【7】key words： atypical Burkitt lymphoma· lymphoma of the thyroid gland·diagnosis of atypical BL

【8】BACKGROUND

【9】Primary malignant lymphoma of the thyroid gland is an un-common malignancy， representing approximately 1-5%of all thyroid malignancies . It is often associated with au-toimmune disorders such as Hashimoto's thyroiditis . Primary thyroid lymphoma is predominantly seen in mid-dle-aged to elderly women. Almost all primary thyroid lym-phomas are of B-cell origin， including marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of the mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) type and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). DLBCL accounts for 50-70% of cases； Burkitt lymphoma (BL) is exceptional .

【10】BL is one of the most aggressive malignancies in the human body . It is rapidly deadly if untreated， but it is curable with intensive chemotherapy.Diagnostic accuracy is there-fore essential to obtain patient safety.

【11】The WHO classification defines BL by the presence of a c-myc translocation resulting in the deregulation of c-myc protein expression. The majority of work in studying the breakpoints has focused on the t(8；14) translocation. In en-demic BL， the breakpoints on chromosome 8 occur in non-coding regions 5 to c-myc exon l， and the breakpoints on chromosome 14 occur usually in the IGHjoining regions at sites that are possible targets for somatic hypermutation， which occurs during germinal center B cell development. These translocations deregulate c-myc expression， driv-ing cells through the cell cycle and activating antiapoptotic pathways. To our knowledge this is the second case of pri-mary BL of the thyroid gland documented in English liter-ature  and the first in which the translocation t(8；14) has been molecularly demonstrated.

【12】CASE REPORT

【13】A 56-vear-old caucasian woman was admitted to“SS Annunziata”Hospital of Chieti because of tracheal com-pressive symptoms. One month before admission， the thy-roid gland began to enlarge rapidly causing dysphagia， short-ness of breath and voice hoarseness. Physical examination was remarkable for diffuse neck swelling complicated by right laterocervical lymph nodes enlargement.

【14】Laboratory findings at that time was as follows： normal blood count and electrolytes concentration； decreased level of se-rum albumin； alfa-globulin and erythrocyte sedimentation rates (VES： 45 mm/h， range 1-15) slightly elevated. Thyroid function test demonstrated mild hypothyroidism (free T4，1.29 ng/dl；TSH <0.001 punit/mL) with associated high level of anti-thyroglobulin antibodies (657.20 UI/mL). Serological examination were negative for HIV-virus， human T-cell lym-phoma virus type 1 (HTLV1) and hepatitis viruses B and C.

【15】Ultrasound examination showed a diffusely enlarged thy-roid gland extending to right cervical soft tissue with dis-placement of trachea and diffuse structure modification. Within the left lower pole and the right upper pole of the gland， two markedly hypoechogenic nodules (measuring4.7 mm and 4.4 mm in their maximum diameter， respec-tively) were observed. They showed taller-than-wide shape， irregular margins and poor intranodular vascularisation. No calcifications were detected.

【16】99mTc scintigraphy revealed no-tracer-uptake in the thyroidal left lobe and isthmus and a minimal uptake of tracer in the lower right pole ofthe gland . An urgent comput-erized tomography (CT) scan of the neck was subsequently obtained， which showed a large cervical mass arising from thyroid and extending to right cervical soft tissue with dis-placement of trachea. Malignant lymphoma has been sus-pected. Despite of FNA might be an appropriate first test for diagnosing thyroid lymphoma， in this case fine-needle aspiration has not been performed. Because of acute air-ways distress and respiratory emergency， the decision was made to carry out thyroidectomy to simultaneously obtain tracheal decompression and tumor debulking ，

【17】Macroscopic features

【18】Macrescopically thyroid gland was diffusely enlarged and55 g in weight. The cut surface， within an uniformly brown-ish parenchyma， showed two white ill-demarcated nodules measuring 4 cm and 4.5 cm in their maximum diameter placed in the right and left lobe respectively.

【19】Microscopic features

【20】Histopathological examination of the thyroid showed diffuse proliferation of monotonous， medium- to large-sized lym-phoid cells with round to irregular nuclei， clumped chro-matin， multiple small centrally located nucleoli and scant cytoplasm resembling blasts . The neoplastic cells were intermingled with plasmocitoid cells and macro-phages containing apoptotic debris which configured the morphological aspect of"starry sky" pattern . APT Up to 10 per 10 high-power fields mitotic features were seen. The contiguous thyroid epithelia was destroyed by cells with enlarged eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and large nuclei (Hurthle cell metaplasia) and by lymph folli-cles containing reactive germinal centers.

【21】Immunohistochemistry

【22】Immunohistochemically， the proliferating cells were CD20+， CD10+， CD79a+， Bcl6+， CD3-， CD23-， CD138- and Bcl2-. Kappa and Lambda chains were not ex-pressed. MIB-1 index was estimated to be nearly 100%. Lymphoid tissue adjacent to the tumor ar-eas showed an admixture of T and B cells， such as nor-mal lymph follicles. These findings strongly suggested the diagnosis of atypical Burkitt lymphoma associated with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.

【23】Molecular analysis

【24】Chromosomal translocation of c-myc gene involving both c-myc and IgH genes-t(8；14) (q24；q32)-has been dem-onstrated in tumor cells by fluorescence in situ hybridation(FISH) using LSI IGH Tricolor Dual Fusion Rearrangement Probe (Vysis， Stuttgart， Germany). The test is designed to detect chromosomal breakage at J or switch region in the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus (14q32). One hundred nuclei have been analyzed； a c-myc/IGH fusion signal was detected in 72% of them， which demonstrated one orange， one green， and one orange/green fusion signal pattern. c-myc 8；14 specific translecation supported the diagnosis of high grade BL.

【25】Therapy and Follow-up

【26】Three days after surgery， patient underwent a total body TC that showed a 2 cm focal， hypodense area on Ⅳ liver segment compatible with liver metastasis. Microscopic and immunohystochemical examination of bone marrow aspira-tion and biopsy showed no evidence of disease. Aggressive chemotherapy with central nervous system prophylaxis was then performed.

【27】DISCUSSION

【28】Lymphomas are subdivided into Hodgkin Lymphoma (HL) and non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL). HLs involves limph nodes predominantly (approximately 95%)， whereas 30% of NHLs present in extranodal sites . Within NHL， Burkitt Lymphoma (BL) is listed in the World Health Organization(WHO) classification as a high-grade malignant lymphoma， characterized by neoplastic germinal center B cells prolif-eration . Accordingly with clinical setting of occurrence， BL can be distinguished into three epidemiologic variants：endemic BL， that represents the most common malignan-cy in African children； sporadic BL， which is seen through-out the world and affects mainly children and adolescent； immunodeficiency-associated BL， that is often the initial manifestation of HIV infection .

【29】Primary thyroid lymphoma is rare and represents a hetero-geneaus group of diseases with a wide spectrum of histo-logical subtypes .

【30】At the time ofdiagnosis， most patients with lymphoma show rapid enlargement of thyroid gland， accompanied by nonspe-cific signs and symptoms related to neck compression such as horseness， dysphonia and dyspnea . Thyroid function tests are frequently normal or suggestive of hypothyroidism.

【31】Imaging findings show unilateral nodule， bilateral nodules within the gland or diffuse thyroid enlargement which are indistinguishable from a broad spectrum of disorders. Often， biopsy or surgery represent the most common methods for final diagnosis .

【32】Patients with chronic thyroiditis are at higher risk for the development of primary malignant lymphoma of the thy-roid gland， since the chronic antigen stimulation that take place in autoimmune disorders may led to a population of lymphocytes which are more inclined to neoplastic trans-formation . Even if rare， thyroid lymphoma should al-ways be kept in differential diagnosis with goiter or other neoplastic nodules； however， the differential diagnosis is fre-quently difficult because the clinical history， the physical ex-amination， the functional tests and the ultrasound are not specific for lymphoproliferative disorders .

【33】Among primary lymphoma of the thyroid gland， BL is very rare； the main diagnostic challenge is to distinguish it from DLBCL. Distinguishing between BL and DLBCL is critical as the two disease require different therapeutic management. BL is rapidly fatal if untreated， but it is curable with intensive prophylactic intrathecal chemotherapy and systemic chemo-therapy that crosses the blood-brain barrier， because of the high risk of involvement of central nervous system. In con-trast， the protocol used for DLBCL typically consists of ci-clophamide，doxorubicin， vincristine， prednisone (CHOP) with the monoclonal anti B-cell antibody rituximab .

【34】Unfortunately， clinical practice shows the existence of“grey zone” cases which have morphological and immunopheng-typical features intermediate between BL and DLBCL and which cannot be certainty classified among one of these categories .

【35】Morphologically BL tumour cells are mature medium sized B-cells， similar to germinal centre cells of B-cell follicles， showing a diffuse monotonous pattern of growth. The tu-mour has an extremely high proliferation fraction as well as high fraction of apoptosis. A"starry sky" pattern is usu-ally present， which is imparted by numerous benign mac-rophages that have ingested apoptotic tumour cells. Cells strongly express CD10， CD20， CD38 and Bcl6 while they are usually negative for Bcl2 (or weakly positive in less than20% of the cases). Nearly 100% of the cells are positive for MIB-1. t(8；14)(q24；q32) translocation has been found in80-90% of cases .

【36】Histological pattern of DLBCL is different and character-ized by the proliferation of medium-large neoplastic B-cell consisting of centroblastic， immunoblastic， T-cell/histiocyte-rich and anaplastic morphological variants. The neoplas-tic cells usually express pan B-cell markers (CD19， CD20， CD22， CD79a)， rarely CD38 and CD138. The proliferation fraction detected by MIB-1 is usually above 40% and CD10was rarely positive .

【37】In DLBCL there in not a specific translocation and up to30% of cases show abnormalities of the 3q27 region involv-ing the BCL6 gene .

【38】In this study， we reported a rare and problematic case of atypical Burkitt lymphoma of the thyroid gland， showing large cells resembling DLBCL， as well as starry sky pattern and immunohistochemical pattern suggestive of BL and whose definitive diagnosis was supported by the detection of c-myc-IgH rearrangement .

【39】Primary molecular alteration of BL is the deregulation of c-myc oncogene， due to the translocation of genetic materi-al between chromosome 8 and the immunoglobulin heaw chain (IgH) locus on chromosome 14：t(8；14)(q24；q32).However，c-myc/IGH fusion gene has also been observed in a proportion (5-15%) of patients with DLBCL .

【40】In this context we would precise that unquestionably FNA and adjuncts are recommended as the first test to diagnose thyroid lymphoma but， giving the significant percentage of primary cell lymphoma cases (50-60%) for which FNA re-sults are suggestive but not diagnostic， surgical procedure may still be required in many cases . Since our pa-tients showed respiratory emergency， we decided to per-form immediate thyroidectomy to simultaneously obtain tracheal decompression and tumor debulking.

【41】On the basis of our experience but with the limitation of this single case， we believe that no single parameter (such as morpholegy， genetics analysis or immunophenetyping alone) should be utilized as unique gold standard for the diagnosis of BL. Vice versa， a combination of several diag-nostic techniques is required to achieve diagnostic accuracy in case of lymphoma presenting intermediate morphology between BL and DLBCL. Achieving diagnostic accuracy is essential to address patients to the best therapy and to im-prove their oncological outcome， preventing either under-treatment and over-treatment .

【42】CONCLUSIONS

【43】It's our opinion that this case report should be useful when a case of BL， with unusuallocalization and ambiguous mOI-phological features， is encountered in routine setting.

【0】Background：

【1】Olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB)， also known as esthesioneuroblastoma， is a rare malignant head and neck can-cer thought to originate from the olfactory epithelium. It typically invades contiguous structures at presenta-tion. We report a very rare case of multifocal and ectopic ONB.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 41-year-old man presented with left nasal obstruction and occasional left epistaxis associated with head-ache. Endoscopic examination of the nasal cavities and computed tomography suggested bilateral polypoid masses. Histopathological diagnosis after endoscopic resection established bilateral olfactory neuroblastoma of the ethmoid sinuses. The patient received postoperative radiotherapy. He remains free of disease 4 years aftertreatment.

【4】Conclusions： To the best of our knowledge this is the second documented case of multifocal ectopic olfactory neuroblasto-ma. Clinicians should consider ONB in the differential diagnosis of bilateral synchronous nasal and paranasal masses to avoid delayed diagnosis. Endoscopic resection of ONB could be an option in selected cases.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Endoscopy·Esthesioneuroblastoma， Olfactory · Nasal Surgical Procedures· Nose Neoplasms·Paranasal Sinus Neoplasms Olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB)， also known as esthesioneu-roblastoma， is thought to arise from the specialized olfactory epithelium at the nasal roof and rarely originates in a differ-ent location. It represents about 5% of the cases of malignant nasal and paranasal sinus (NPS) tumors .

【6】At presentation， ONB typically extends by direct infiltration to adjacent structures， including the orbit， the skull base， and the contralateral nasal cavity. This feature， combined with its unspecific clinical presentation， often leads to a bad progno-sis. To date， there are neither well-defined treatment guide-lines nor a universally accepted staging system. The main prog-nostic factors are clinical stage， lymph node metastasis， and Hyams' histopathological grade.

【7】We report a very unusual clinical case of multifocal noncon-tiguous ectopic ONB. To the best of our knowledge， this is the second published case report of multifocal ONB.

【8】Case Report

【9】A 41-year-old white man presented with left nasal obstruction and occasional left epistaxis associated with headache begin-ning about 1.5 years before admission. Endoscopic examina-tion revealed a polypoid mass completely obstructing the left nasal cavity and on the right side a polypoid mass originat-ed from the middle meatus filling the nasal cavity. The rest of the examination results were unremarkable and no associat-ed cervical lymph nodes were found.

【10】Computed tomography (CT) showed a left nasal polypoid mass extending from the ethmoid sinus with partial opacifi-cation of the left maxillary sinus， and on the right side com-plete opacification of the ethmoid， maxillary， and sphenoid sinuses. There appeared to be no invasion of the cribriform plate， orbit， or skull base. Radiological findings suggested bi-lateral polyps .

【11】The patient underwent endoscopic resection. Complete bilater-al ethmoidectomy with wide middle meatal antrostomy as well as right sphenoidectomy and tailored left lamina papyracea re-section were performed because of suspicion of left sinonasal inverted papilloma. No postoperative complications occurred.

【12】Hematoxylin-eosin staining of the tumor showed a lobular growth pattern and round cells surrounded by neurofibrillary material . Immunohistochemical staining for syn-aptophysin， chromogranin， neuron specific enolase， and S-100protein proved to be positive， revealing the histological diag-nosis of bilateral Hyams' grade ll ONB of the ethmoid sinuses.

【13】A magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan was carried out 1month after surgery， confirming postoperative changes with no evidence of intracranial or orbital extension. Positron emis-sion tomography-CT (PET-CT) showed no distant metastases or local uptake . The patient was staged Kadish stage B and Dulgerov stage T1NOM0 bilaterally. He subsequently re-ceived postoperative 3-D conformal radiotherapy on the pri-mary site. The total dose was 60 Gy， which were divided into2 Gy/fraction. During the 48-month follow-up the patient has remained clinically and radiologically free of disease recurrence.

【14】Discussion

【15】Olfactory neuroblastoma， also known as esthesioneuroblasto-ma， is the most prevalent of the malignant neuroectodermal NPS tumors. It occurs in about 5% of the cases of malignant NPS neoplasms .

【16】ONB occurs at any age， from 3 to 90 years， with a bimodal dis-tribution in the second and sixth decades of life without any sex predilection . It was first described by Berger et al. in 1924 and has also been termed as the “great impostor"by Ogura and Schenck  due to its histopathological features that often require further histochemical， immunochemical， and ul-trastructural investigations， and due to the biological features， which range from indolent to highly aggressive growth . It is thought to arise from specialized sensory neuroectodermal olfactory basal cells from the upper nasal cavity， but its ori-gin is still controversial . ONB arises from the olfactory mu-cosa and when found in other locations other than the roof of the nasal cavity it is considered to be ectopic. Some of the alternative origin hypotheses， like Jacobson's vomero-nasal or-gan or autonomic ganglia， support the concept of ectopic ori-gin of ONB. Ectopic ONBs are particularly rare and have been previously reported in 21 cases， such as atypical nasal cavity locations， paranasal sinuses， nasopharynx， petrous apex， pi-tuitary gland， sphenoclival region， and pterygopalatine fos-sa . Only 1 multifocal synchronous ONB case besides ours has been documented in the literature . The present case should be regarded both as multifocal and ectopic， giv-en the tumor's origin in both ethmoid sinuses.

【20】Histological features include the characteristic nests of small， round， blue cells with rosette or pseudorosette formation and neurofibrillary matrix. Immunohistochemical staining is pos-itive for neuron-specific enolase， S-100 protein， synaptophy-sin， chromogranin， NFP， and CD 56. S-100 staining is typically limited to the sustentacular cells situated along the periph-ery of the lobules. Our case was tested for the first 4 markers， which were all positive. These immunohistochemical studies as well as electron microscopy may be necessary for differ-ential diagnosis， especially for high-grade tumors， which may be undistinguishable from other small round cell cancers . Hyams' grading system proposes 4 levels of differentiation with different histological features . Most ONBs are included in Hyams’lower grades l and Il (62%) \]， as was our case.

【21】Clinical manifestations may be similar to the ones observed in benign pathology， especially at a low-stage of disease or if bilateral pathology is present. Therefore， delay between the onset of symptoms， diagnosis， and treatment is common， which accounts for the bad prognosis and outcome of these patients . ONB typically invades the orbit， the skull base， and the paranasal sinuses， often being locally advanced (61%) and showing cervical lymph node metastases in 5% of cas-es at presentation . Neck masses eventually appear in25-35% of patients. Distant metastases at onset have been reported in 6.6% of the cases， with bone and lung metasta-ses being the commonest .

【22】Tumor staging is best established by the combination of CT and MRI. CT shows a homogenous or heterogeneous contrast-enhanced mass with areas of necrosis， T1-weighted MRI a hypointense mass， and T2-weighted MRI intermedi-ate to high intensity . Cysts along the margins of in-tracranial lesions are typically found in Kadish stage C ONB. Intralesional calcification may be considered pathognomon-ic . Hyperostosis of adjacent bones is also typically seen. Distant metastases have been successfully diagnosed with PET.

【23】Kadish et al. proposed 3 clinical staging categories - A， B， and C - depending on whether the tumor is localized in the nasal cavity (A)， nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses (B)， or extends beyond these structures (C) . Morita et al. modified this by adding stage D， which includes those cases with regional or distant metastases . The staging system of Dulguerov et al. is TNM-based  after radiological findings， but neither of them is universally accepted . None of the staging sys-tems is adequate for ectopic ONB， as shown by our patient， who presented with 2 ectopic tumors arising directly from the ethmoid sinuses without a nasal cavity origin or further ex-tension， both being staged as T1 with the Dulguerov classi-fication. Using the Kadish system， our case could be staged as B or even as A due to its lack of nasal cavity involvement， based on its ectopic localization.

【24】Treatment of ONB includes combinations of surgery， radiation， and chemotherapy， with no well-defined guidelines. Surgery with postoperative radiotherapy is the most accepted treatment mo-dality in all different stages， with the best survival rates (65%)， followed by radiotherapy as the only treatment . Craniofacial en bloc resection is the most frequently used technique and has long been considered to be the standard treatment. However， Devaiah and Andreoli stated that endonasal endoscopic surgery is a valid treatment option with comparable outcomes to open surgery in selected cases with no local invasion， showing even better survival rates . Folbe et al. presented one of the larg-est studies of ONB treated with endoscopic resection， including The low 5-year overall survival rate of 45% is due to recurrence of ONB， but improves in low-grade tumors. Wormald's review of the ectopic cases of ONB does not show any differences in treatment between ectopic and localized ONB . Hence， the main prognostic factors are clinical stage， Hyams' grade of dif-ferentiation，and lymph node metastasis status .

【25】Clinical and radiological follow-up has been suggested to be warranted for the remainder of the patient’s life.

【26】Conclusions

【27】To the best of our knowledge， this is the second reported case of multifocal ectopic non-invasive olfactory neuroblastoma . Clinicians should consider ONB in the differential diagnosis of bilateral nasal and paranasal masses to avoid delayed diagno-sis. Endoscopic endonasal surgery of selected NPS tumors does not compromise oncologic results and provides lower complica-tion rates with possible complete resection at the same time.

【0】ABSTRACT Spontaneous spinal epidural hematomas are rare and potentially disabling neurological emergencies. It leads to devastating neurologic outcomes， and most patients do not recover completely. The clinical presentation is diverse and includes a severe acute attack， radiating pain at the back， interscapular， or neurological deficits. We report a case of a young woman， 24-year-old， that was admitted to our department for sudden non-traumatic cervical spinal cord compression syndrome (Type A of the American Spinal Cord Injury Association "ASIA A")， including intense cervical back pain， sensory loss， and tetraplegia. Her past medical history was unremarkable. The MRI confirmed a cervical mass responsible for the spinal cord compression， and the emergent surgical intervention allowed us to evacuate acute C3-C7hematoma. Unfortunately， the patient never recovers from the neurologic deficit despite the emergent management of her case followed by functional musculoskeletal rehabilitation for two years.

【1】KEYWORDS Spinal Cord Compression， Hematoma， Epidural， Spinal， Cervical Vertebrae， case report

【2】Introduction

【3】Spontaneous spinal epidural hematomas are the idiopathic ac-cumulation of blood within the spinal canal's epidural space， causing symptoms varying from general back pain to complete paraplegia . It is a very rare cause of acute spinal cord com-pression and is estimated to occur every year in approximately0.1% of 100，000 individuals . MRI is the radiological investi-gation of choice. Fifty percent of spontaneous spinal epidural hematoma patients do not fully recover， and 30% of patients pre-sented with ASIA A classification did not improve with surgery. We present a case of a 24-year-old woman who never recov-ers from her ASIA A spontaneous cervical epidural hematoma despite rapid surgical evacuation in an emergency setting， 48hours of the tetraplegia onset.

【4】Case report

【5】A 24-year-old woman was admitted to our department for sud-den intense cervical back pain and tetraplegia within 48 hours. The patient denies neck trauma， and her past medical history was unremarkable. The physical examination revealed super-ficial and deep sensory palsy with the sensibility level at C4. The osteotendinous reflexes were abolished in all 4 limbs and acute urinary retention. There was no fever， and the patient was in general good health status. This cervical spinal cord com-pression is classified as ASIA A . The cervical MRI performed in emergency showed a posterolateral right epidu-ral masse that is heterogeneous in T1-weighted， hypointense in T2-weighted， and compressing the dural sheath from the 3rd to the 7th cervical vertebrae . These findings were sug-gestive of an epidural tumour lesion. The patient underwent surgical decompression the same day. Patient under general anaesthesia and in a supine position， we did laminectomy at C4-C5-C6 and got directly on a bunch of clotted blood in direct contact with dura sheath. This large extradural hematoma was completely evacuated. A subsequent search for a hemorrhagic defect proved was unsuccessful.
