【20】AHI： Apnea-Hypopnea Index

【21】decreased significantly with treatment in both groups of patients. This reduction was more significant in the group with adequate treatment compliance. In a study of Hussain et al. regarding long-term compliance with continuous positive airway pressure treatment， it was found that there was a significant reduction in ESS scores with treatment and this reduction was greater in compliant patients . Another study concluded that a 44%reduction in ESS scores was obtained with CPAP therapy within the first two weeks and the lowest mean ESS score was observed at six months331

【22】Since there are no validated satisfaction surveys assessing device compliance， usually surveys indicating the quality of life are used for this purpose . Balachandran et al. prepared a CPAP perception questionnaire for predicting patient compli-ance. They showed a significant correlation between questions and compliance with one-month CPAP treatment . In our clinic， we are using a five-point scale (very bad， bad， average， good and very good) to evaluate the general satisfaction levels of the device. This is not an international or widely used scoring system， but according to our experience gives valuable informa-tion about patient satisfaction. All patients were assessed with this general satisfaction questionnaire. As expected， patients'satisfaction with continuous positive airway pressure devices increased with increasing treatment compliance. This condition was supported by the fact that the Apnea-Hypopnea Index and

【23】ESS scores at 1st month were lower in the group with adequate treatment compliance. This also shows the efficacy of PAP ther-apy. Similar results are supported by various studies in the literature.

【24】The side effects experienced by the patients are one of the foremost reasons for withdrawal of the treatment. The most significant side effects are mask related side effects and the type of mask used in conjunction with PAP therapy J. Compli-ance with treatment generally decreases in cases with a higher incidence of complaints， especially about the mask J. Borel et al.  reported that the use of nasal masks was the first type of mask to enhance treatment compliance. It has also been reported that side effects associated with the mask also affect compliance with PAP therapy and occur in approximately 30-70% of patients . In our study， all patients had used a nasal mask， and so there were no differences regarding the type of mask used. However， some complaints， which we thought to be related to the general characteristics and quality of the materials， were significantly important in terms of treatment compliance. Among them， the most common complaints were skin irritation due to mask， device noise and morning headache.

【25】Limitations

【26】Our study has some limitations. First， it has a retrospective and single-centre design. The relatively small sample size of the current study indicates the need to validate the findings in a larger patient cohort. Despite these limitations， we believe that our results propose a need for further studies. Since the vast majority of the population was male， our findings cannot be extrapolated， female individuals.

【27】Conclusion

【28】As a result， we can say that patient-reported device side effects to decrease the compliance rates. On the other hand， increasing OSAS severity is positively correlated with device compliance. Another striking result of our study is that with increasing CPAP device use， which is the most effective treatment method in ob-structive sleep apnea syndrome disease， the efficiency of treat- ment and patient satisfaction are increased significantly. These results may lead us to encourage our patients for the increasing usage of the CPAP device.

【0】Background：

【1】Rheumatoid nodules develop mostly subcutaneously， they are less common in other organs. Recent studies have described formation of rheumatoid nodules or growth acceleration of existing nodules in relation to the treatment. The development or growth acceleration of rheumatoid nodules is known to be related to the treatment with methotrexate， etanercept， infliximab and leflunomide.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 59-year-old female patient was treated 9 years for seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. She took hydroxychloroquine， sulfasalazine， methotrexate and etanercept successively. Until then， the patient had suffered no rheumatoid nodules (not even subcutaneous). Isolated rheumatoid nodules were formed in her lungs when treated with leflunomide. The patient has been monitored after discontinuation of leflunomide treatment for the period of 20 months and only a mild progression of her lung disease has occurred.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Isolated rheumatoid nodules were formed in the lungs of our patient during leflunomide treatment. In addition to methotrexate， etanercept and infliximab， leflunomide can probably also cause the formation and growth acceleration of rheumatoid nodules.

【6】Key words： Rheumatoid arthritis· rheumatoid nodules· lungs· leflunomide

【7】BACKGROUND

【8】Rheumatoid nodules belong among the most frequent extra-articular manifestations of rheumatoid arthri-tis (RA). In most cases they occur subcutaneously， they are less frequent in other organs. In lungs they are detected on chest x-ray images approximately in 1% of patients， however computer tomography scans detect them more often . Formation of rheumatoid nodules or growth acceleration of exist-ing nodules related to treatment has been recently described. Development or growth acceleration of rheumatoid nodules has been reported in relation to treatment with methotrexate ， etanercept ， infliximab ， and it has been recently published in relation to the administration of leflunomide . We have observed a patient suffering isolated rheumatoid nodules in the lungs that were detected during her treatment with leflunomide.

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】A 59-year old woman was diagnosed with seroposi-tive rheumatoid arthritis in 1996. The patient was treated with antimalarial drugs (hydroxychloroquine)， temporarily with glucocorticoids， after that with sulfasalazine (2g/day) and later with sulfasalazine in combination with methotrexate (15 mg once per week). Right from the beginning of her disease，she was diagnosed with hypothyroidism resulting from autoimmune thyroiditis. The activity of the disease has not been adequately controlled during the whole period. In 2001， a total hip prosthesis of the right hip joint was implanted to the patient (methotrex-ate discontinued before surgery)； after surgery the patient was treated only with sulfasalazine. In 2002， the patient was treated with etanercept in the amount of 25mg twice a week， and the treatment was ter-minated after 9 months - the course of the disease remained unchanged. No pathological changes of the lungs were found during an x-ray taken 12 months after the treatment commencement and 3 months after the termination of etanercept treatment. From the beginning of 2003 the patient was treated with leflunomide as usual taking a maintenance dose of 20mg/d. In 2003， a left knee prosthesis was implanted to the patient. The pre-operative examination included a chest skiagram with a normal lung finding. An x-ray examination made thirteen months after the commencement of leflunomide treatment showed circular disseminated foci in both lungs whose scope was specified by a CT scan . Multiple ovoid localised foci ranging from 4 to 15mm were described in both lungs. A videothoraco-scopic examination both in the upper and bottom lung lobe showed small round yellowish foci that were placed subpleurally.

【11】One nodule (15x9x20 mm) was resected and histo logically examined. It was a nodule made of mostly necrotic tissue whose peripheral parts showed kary-orhectic disintegration of nuclei. Focal scarring with antracotic pigment was detected in the central area of the formation. A granulomatous reaction with a palisade of CD-68 positive macrophages was detected in the periphery of the formation. Giant multinuclear cells of Langhans type were not detected. Smaller， mostly lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates and scarring were located around the formation. No indication of vasculitis was found on the detected blood ves-sels. Special Ziehl - Nielsen staining did not show any mycobacteria， and no mycotic infectious agents were detected in the PAS reaction and by Grocott stain. The histological finding corresponded to the rheumatoid nodule .

【12】Objectively， the patient did not have any subcutane-ous rheumatoid nodules and did not suffer from any arthritis symptoms during the last year. Despite that high erythrocyte sedimentation rates and rheumatoid factor values persisted； the C-reactive protein (CRP) values from last examinations were lower.

【13】Other laboratory results：ESR： 83 mm per hour，hae moglobin： 115g/l， CRP 22.8g/l， rheumatoid factor313 IU/ml (Standard 0-25)， ANA， ANCA antibodies， HbsAg and HBC antibodies were negative.

【14】We have re-introduced methotrexate in the amount of15mg once per week in combination with hydroxy-chloroquine 200mg/day. We have reduced the dose of leflunomide to 10mg/day and gradually discontinued the treatment.

【15】No sign of the pulmonary involvement progression were detected at the control CT scan. The follow-ing laboratory parameters improved： ESR： 30mm per hour， blood count： Hb： 135g/l， CRP：10.4 mg/l. The patient later took only 12.5mg of methotrexate once per week plus non-steroid antirheumatics. For the period of 20 months of the pulmonary monitor-ing the patient continued to be asymptomatic with respect to pulmonary signs， and the pulmonary find-ing did not change considerably. Nevertheless， the latest CT scan indicated a small pleural exudate on the right side and a slight growth of some pulmonary nodules. Minor calcifications were detected in some pulmonary nodules.

【16】DISCUSSION

【17】Rheumatoid pulmonary nodules were formed in our patient during the leflunomide treatment. Our patient is interesting because of the following reasons：

【18】1) Isolated formation of nodules in the lungs and a lack of subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules：

【19】2) In the past she was treated with medicines that are known to cause potentially the development of new or growth acceleration of the existing rheumatoid nodules (methotrexate， etanercept)；

【20】3) Formation of pulmonary nodules during the leflu-nomide treatment：

【21】4) Monitoring of the course of the pulmonary involve-ment for the period of 20 months.

【22】Predilective factors for the rheumatoid nodules de-velopment are： positive rheumatoid factor， severe course of the disease， genetic predispositions as well as smoking . Rheumatoid pulmonary nodules are less frequently reported in women compared to men. Our patient has suffered a severe form of the disease with high titres of the rheumatoid factor. It is interesting that she did not suffer any subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules. We can only speculate whether the lung damage could have had an impact on the development of rheumatoid nodules because of any reasons just as a tissue damage caused by a chronic trauma in the area of the elbows is considered to be a factor causing predilective localisation of rheuma-toid nodules. Antracotic pigment in the nodule centre could indicate that.

【23】In the beginning， the patient was treated with metho-trexate， however the treatment was already terminated for the first time 3 years ago and repeated x-ray exami-nations of the chest carried out later were normal. Any connection with the etanercept treatment is also not probable. No nodules were found in the lungs after 9months of treatment with etanercept， and the skiagram taken 3 months after the termination of etanercept treatment was also normal. Rheumatoid nodules in the lungs were detected by chance after 13 months of treatment with leflunomide. Subcutaneous rheuma-toid nodules during the leflunomide treatment were formed approximately 6 months after the treatment commencement . It is a question whether， in the case of our patient， the development of pulmonary nodules was related to the leflunomide treatment in any way or whether it was an independent mani-festation of the disease. However， this fact must be taken into consideration after publishing the studies on the development and growth acceleration of rheumatoid nodules after leflunomide treatment. This suspicion has been also supported by the fact that， in the past， when the patient was treated with3 other DMARDs and later also with etanercept no rheumatoid nodules were formed and there were no other extra-articular manifestations.

【24】The pathogenetic mechanism of the formation and acceleration of rheumatoid nodules after lefluno-mide treatment has been unclear. A co-incidence of several factors has been assumed and an important role is given to insufficient elimination of high con-centrations of rheumatoid factor from the lungs. The hypothesis indicates that the insufficient elimination is caused by a reduced number of monocytes and a defect of their function caused by the effect of leflu-nomide . It is also unclear whether and up to which degree the subclinical lung damage by leflunomide can have an impact on the creation of lung nodules even though the clinically significant damage of the lungs by leflunomide has been rather rare .

【25】Rheumatoid pulmonary nodules are often asymp-tomatic as in our patient and they are mostly benign. Nodules can regress or grow spontaneously， or new nodules may develop or complications can occur. Pleural involvement can cause pleural exudate， pneu-mothorax， bronchlopleural fistula with empyema. We consider the small unilateral pleural exudate in our patient that occurred 20 months after detecting the pulmonary involvement to be an inflammatory reaction caused because of pleura erosion by any of subpleural nodules. In some of them， their close connection to pleura has been obvious already dur-ing the videothoracoscopic examination and the repeated CT scan.

【26】The growth acceleration and formation of new rheu-matoid nodules in relation to the treatment is charac-terised by certain autonomy of joint findings. Mostly it takes place in the case of considerable improve-ment of or disappearance of arthritis ， and the situation is similar in lung involvements . The treatment with infliximab caused improvements of joint findings but it did not have any effect on the immunopathology of rheumatoid nodules . It sug-gests that inflammation in synovialis and in nodules is mediated by a different mechanism. It seems that CD4+ T lymphocytes play a major role in the lung manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis which will， undoubtedly， affect the future pharmacotherapy in these forms.

【27】CONCLUSIONS

【28】In addition to methotrexate， etanercept and infliximab， leflunomide can probably also cause formation and growth acceleration of rheumatoid nodules.

【0】Background：

【1】Chronic neutrophilic leukemia (CNL) is a rare disease and can be characterized by dysplastic changes (CNL-D) only in very few cases. It has never been described after treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma (HL).

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 41-year-old woman， previously treated with chemo-radiotherapy for HL， presented with absolute neutrophilia， anemia and thrombocytopenia. All circulating neutrophils displayed Pelger-like fea-tures， with round-shaped nuclei. In addition， an evident clumping of chromatin into blocks sepa-rated by clear zones was observed in a significant percentage of Pelger-like neutrophils. Electron microscopy confirmed these findings. Bone marrow showed trilineage dysplasia. CNL-D was diag-nosed. Nine mon ths later， transformation into acute myeloid leukemia (M1 of FAB classification) was observed， with immunophenotype characterized by the expression of CD34， CD33， CD13， CD117 and HLA-DR. The patient died with a clinical picture of therapy-resistant disease.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Therapy-related myelodysplasia and acute leukemia can be observed after treatment for HL. We describe the first case of CNL-D following therapy for HL. CNL is frequently characterized by a fa-tal clinical course， and the presence of myelodysplastic features worsen prognosis. Thus， it is im-portant to recognise this clinical entity in order to develop appropriate therapeutic strategies.

【6】key words：

【7】acute myeloid leukemia· chronic neutrophilic leukemia · electron microscopy·Hodgkin lymphoma · neutrophils· pseudo Pelger neutrophils

【8】The WHO classification of the myeloproliferative neoplasms recognizes 8 entities： chronic myeloid leukemia， chronic eosinophilic leukemia， polycythemia vera， primary myelo-fibrosis， essential thrombocythemia， mastocytosis， myelo-proliferative neoplasms (unclassifiable)， and chronic neu-trophilic leukemia (CNL) .

【9】CNL is a rare entity generally characterized by a sustained mature neutrophilia， hepatosplenomegaly， a high leukocyte alkaline phosphatase (LAP) score， lack of detectable BCR-ABL transcripts， elevated serum B. and uric acid levels. In order to diagnose CNL， other diseases or causes of neutro-philia have to be excluded 

【10】A variant type of CNL has been reported in a few cases. Zoumbos et al. first described a type of CNL associated with myelodysplastic features， which they termed CNL-D.In addition， among the 4 cases of CNL reported by Zittoun et al.， 2 were characterized by myelodysplastic features ， and cases that could be classified as CNL-D were reported by Cervantes et al. ， and Ota et al. Evolution into acute myeloid leukemia (AML) of M1 or M2 FAB subtype was reported in most of those patients.

【11】CNL still is a rare disease and Elliot  suggested that con-tinued reporting of all cases of this entity must be encour-aged. CNL-D seems to be rarer， and knowledge of new cases could be helpful in order to understand its real importance.

【12】We recently reviewed our clinical files concerning second-ary acute myeloid leukemias， and a case of AML developed from CNL-D was found. Interestingly， the patient had been treated with chemo-radiotherapy for Hodgkin Lymphoma(HL). To the best of our knowledge， cases of CNL follow-ing treatment for HL have not yet been reported.

【13】CASE REPORT

【14】The patient was a 4l-year-old female with a previous histo-ry of stage IIIA HL (nodular sclerosis histology). She had been treated with 6 courses of the ABVD regimen ， fol-lowed by involved-field radiotherapy (30 Gy cumulative dose). Complete remission was obtained and the patient underwent follow-up， which included periodic execution of computed tomography and/or ultrasound， complete blood counts and serum chemistries. All test results were normal throughout follow-up. Seven years after chemo-radiothera-py treatment， and l year after the last medical investigation， the patient presented with anemia (Hb8g/dl)， low platelet count (12x10/1)，leukocytosis (WBC 15x10°/1)， with differ-ential： neutrophils 70%，lymphocytes 20%， monocytes 5%， eosinophils 5%. Blood films， stained with May-Grunwald-Giemsa， were examined by light microscopy： the whole neu-trophil population showed a pseudo Pelger (or Pelger-like) morphology， with round-shaped nucleus and abnormal chro-matin clumping .Other specimens were stained for myeloperoxidase and PAS using standard methods ， and LAP by means of a commercial kit (Sigma). Neutrophils showed a normal pattern of myeloperoxidase and PAS， and an intermediate LAP score . A trephine bi-opsy was also carried out. The bioptic sample was fixed in Myelodecreagent A (Bio-Optica) for 2 hr， decalcified in EDTA for 2 days， embedded in paraffin， and cut into 3-5um sections. The morphological evaluations， carried out af-ter hematoxylin-eosin and Giemsa stainings， showed trilin-ear dysplastic changes . Bone marrow sam-ples from a myeloaspirate confirmed the dysplastic changes， granulocytic hyperplasia and no excess blasts. After conventional karyotyping and PCR assays， there was no evidence of chromosomic anomalies， nor BCR-ABL posi-tivity. Peripheral blood and bone marrow samples were also subjected to ultrastructural studies of leukocytes fixed in paraformaldehyde and glutaraldehyde， postfixed in osmi-um tetroxide， embedded in Epon-Araldite， and examined under a Siemens Elmiskop 102 electron microscope . This method allowed observation of several ultrastructural anomalies of neutrophils， including abnormal chromatin clumping， Pelger-like morphology of the nucleus， and ab-normal granules .

【15】After excluding other possible causes of neutrophilia or leukemoid reactions， such as infection， myelofibrosis， 14，000×).

【16】intoxication， severe hemorrhage， acute hemolysis， and neoplasia infiltrating the bone marrow ， CNL-D，ac-cording to Zoumbos et al.，  was diagnosed.

【17】Because of the lack of a specific treatment ， the pa-tients underwent therapy with recombinant erythropoietin(60，000 U/week， subcutaneously， for 9 months) and low-dose cytarabine (10 mg BID subcutaneously， for 7 days every month；6 courses). A reduction in WBC values (3x10°/1) was obtained， but neutrophils still showed Pelger-like features. Anemia and thrombocytopenia did not show any signifi-cant improvement， and red cell transfusions were necessary.

【18】Nine months later， WBC increased to 12x10°/l， and blasts up to 18% appeared. Both marrow aspirate and bone marrow biopsy showed infiltration by 50% blasts that were myelo-peroxidase-positive and alpha-naphtyl-acetate esterase-neg-ative.Bone marrow samples were subjected to flow cytomet-ric assays， using a monoclonal antibodies panel including CD13， CD33，CD34， CD117，HLA-DR，CD14， CD64， CD16， CD11b， CD15， CD56， CD7， CD3， CD5， CD19，CD10，CD20， and CD38 (all purchased from Becton Dickinson). A three-color method was carried out using a FacsCalibur cytometer(Becton Dickinson). At least 30，000 events were acquired， and data were analyzed by the Cell-Quest software (Becton Dickinson). Blasts were positive for CD34， CD13， CD33， CD117，CD38， HLA-DR. PML/RARd，and AMLl/ETO，and CBF/MYH11 fusion genes were negative.

【19】Transformation into AML， M1 FAB subtype  was there-fore diagnosed. The patient underwent induction therapy with the daunorubicin plus cytarabine regimen (daunoru-bicin 45 mg/m² for 3 days plus cytarabine 200 mg/m²for 7days with continuous i.v.infusion) ， but she died of pneu-monia 3 months later without obtaining disease remission.

【20】DISCUSSION

【21】The current case is characterized by the onset of CNL 7years after cheme-radiotherapy for HL. A relationship be-tween these 2 events is likely because the increased risk of myelodysplasia and secondary leukemia in treated HL is well known . Interestingly， the interval between treatment for HL and CNL onset in our patient was 7 years， and there-fore is very close to the 5.8 year mean interval calculated in the study by Abrahamsen ， and within the 5-9 year in-terval found to be at higher risk for secondary AML after therapy for HL . In addition， the therapeutic regimen used in our case (chemo/radiotherapy) has been found to be associated with an increased risk for secon dary AML in HL， as well as female sex . However， among the cas-es of CNL (with or without dysplastic features) so far de-scribed in the literature， an association with treatment for HL has never been previously reported.

【22】CNL seems to have poor prognosis. Reilly  performed a survival analysis of 33 cases of patients felt to have true chronic neutrophilic leukemia' and suggested an overall medi- an survival of 30 months and a 5-year survival of 28%. The most frequent complication of CNL， which leads to death， is fatal cerebral bleeding ， but a spontaneous leukemic transformation cannot be excluded .CNL-D shows a worse prognosis， and transformation into AML has been seen in the majority of cases described thus far .

【23】CNL， and its variant presentation CNL-D， have to be care-fully differentiated from reactive neutrophilias， leukemoid reactions and chronic myeloid leukemia ； therefore， both clinical and laboratory criteria have to be taken into consideration before diagnosing CNL. Although the vari-ant type of CNL， termed CNL-D， shows dysplastic features that can be found by morphological criteria， we also used ultrastructural criteria to improve our diagnosis and pro-vide clear evidence for this peculiar clinical entity. In par-ticular， abnormal chromatin clumping was clearly demon-strated by electron microscopy.

【24】CONCLUSIONS

【25】To date， because of the rarity of the disease， no therapeu-tic standard has been determined in CNL. However， alloge-neic stem cell transplantation has been employed in young patients， with good results . Therefore， cases of CNL should be reported with regularity， in order to gain a better understanding of the nature of this rare disease. In partic-ular， dysplastic changes should be investigatedin order to recognize eventual cases of CNL-D. Thus， the combination of morphology and ultrastructural assays could be used as diagnostic tools to improve diagnosis .

【26】Finally， because of the poor prognosis of this disease， par-ticular efforts should be made to design effective therapeu-tic schedules.

【0】Background：

【1】Primary retroperitoneal mucinous cystadenoma (PRMC) is a rare benign tumor that occurs in the retroperito-neal space. PRMC is difficult to preoperatively diagnose， and final diagnosis requires surgical resection.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 39-year-old female was referred to our hospital with a chief complaint of tension and pain in the left flank. Imaging findings revealed a large， thick-walled unilocular cystic mass dorsal to the descending colon and ven-tral to the left kidney. Moreover， a content-rich mural nodule measuring 20 mm was detected on the cau-dal wall of the cyst， which was suspected to be malignant. The tumor was successfully resected. The cystic wall was composed of thick， scarred fibrous tissue， and the inner surface was lined with a single layer of mu-cinous epithelium with little atypia. The mural nodule mainly comprised necrotic tissue with no epithelium. Serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) level was high (109 U/mL) preoperatively， but it returned to nor-mal levels postoperatively. Importantly， CA19-9 expression was also confirmed using immunohistochemistry To the best of our knowledge， this is the first case of PRMC with elevated serum CA19-9 levels confirmed by immunohistochemistry.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】PRMC is only diagnosed by surgical resection. Ifimaging studies indicate signs of malignancy， surgeons should not hesitate to surgically confirm the diagnosis.

【6】MeSH Keywords： CA-19-9 Antigen· Case Reports ·lmmunohistochemistry· Retroperitoneal Neoplasms

【7】Abbreviations：

【8】PRMC - primary retroperitoneal mucinous cystadenoma； CA19-9-serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9； CT - computed tomography； CEA - carcinoembryonic antigen； MRI - magnetic resonance imaging Primary retroperitoneal mucinous cystadenoma (PRMC) is a rare cystic lesion initially reported by Bassini in 1889 . PRMCs are found mainly in women with indefinite abdominal symp toms such as pain or distension， or incidentally detected in the imaging studies for other purposes. The histogenesis is still unclear since there is originally no epithelial tissue in the retroperitoneum. Surgical resection is necessary for both di-agnosis and treatment to avoid dissemination by percutane-ous biopsy， especially when there are radiological signs sug-gesting malignancy， such as mural nodule or calcification .

【9】Herein， we report a case of PRMC with a mural nodule along with high serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) lev-els in a 39-year-old female patient. This is the first report of PRMC with evidence of CA19-9 expression confirmed by immunohistochemistry.

【10】Case Report

【11】A 39-year-old female presented with a chief complaint of left-sided abdominal tension and pain. She had a medical history of a left ovarian cyst that was surgically removed when she was 19 years old. She began to have left-sided abdominal dis-tension and pain in October 2017， and because the symptoms sustained， she visited a nearby hospital. Computed tomography (CT) showed a large left retroperitoneal cystic lesion with a mu-ral nodule. Therefore， she was referred to our hospital for fur-ther evaluation and treatment in December 2017.

【12】Her height was 161 cm and weight was 44 kg. Her blood pres-sure was 95/65 mmHg， heart rate was 64 beats/minute， and body temperature was 36.8°C The abdomen was soft and slightly distended on the left side with a palpable and mo-bile mass. No tenderness and skin changes were observed. Laboratory study results showed elevated serum CA19-9 level(109 U/mL)； other tumor markers \[carcinoembryonic antigen(CEA)， CA-125， squamous cell carcinoma antigen， and cytoker-atin 19 fragment) were within normal limits. Complete blood count and serum chemistry results were normal.

【13】Abdominal contrast-enhanced CT revealed a well-circum-scribed unilocular cystic lesion with a thick capsule measuring11x8x15 cm， located dorsal to the descending colon and ventral to the left kidney without any obvious invasion. A mural nod-ule measuring 20 mm was observed on the caudal wall ofthe cyst， but without enhancement . On magnetic reso-nance imaging (MRI)， the content of the cystic lesion showed slightly high intensity on T1-weighted image and high intensity on T2-weighted image， which was suggestive of hematoma. The mural nodule showed low intensity on both T1- and T2-weighted images . Overall， we suspected a malignant cystic lesion located in the left retroperitoneum owing to the presence of the mural nodule and high serum CA19-9 level. We chose to resect the tumor without biopsy to avoid dissemina-tion. Considering the large size and possibility of malignancy， laparotomy rather than laparoscopic surgery was chosen.

【14】No intraperitoneal dissemination or distant metastasis was ob-served during surgery. The left ovary was absent by previous medical history of oophorectomy and the fallopian tube was normal. The tumor was located in the adipose tissue dorsal to the descending colon， and it was attached to neighboring tissues such as the mesocolon， left ovarian vessels， and left ureter. We resected the tumor with a part of the Gerota's fascia， left ovarian vessels， and descending colon en bloc， because the marginal vessels of the descending colon were inseparable from the tumor. The colon was reconstructed by functional end-to-end anastomosis using the Endo GIA Tri-StapleM. The left ureter was successfully preserved by preoperatively inserting a temporary stent.

【15】Macroscopically， the resected specimen was a cystic lesion with a mural nodule on the caudal wall of the cyst . It was 13x8x3 cm in size and 815 g in weight. The content was yellowish seromucinous fluid without any blood component. There was no invasion into the descending colon， which was resected en bloc. Histopathological findings revealed that the cystic wall was composed of thick， scarred fibrous tissue and the inner surface was lined with a single layer of mucinous epithelium with little atypia . The mural nodule was mainly necrotic tissue with blood cells and no epithelial cells. Immunohistochemistry results were negative for estrogen re-ceptor (ER) and PAX8， and positive for CA19-9 . No ovarian stroma was observed. In accordance with our findings， PRMC was diagnosed.

【16】The postoperative course of the patient was uneventful， and she was discharged on the 17th postoperative day. The se-rum CA19-9 level on the 38th postoperative day was normal(26 U/mL). The patient was free of recurrence to date.

【17】Discussion

【18】PRMC is a rare tumor. Cheng et al. reported 113 retroperitoneal tumor cases， in which only 1 case was diagnosed as PRMC compared to the most common case diagnosis of liposarcoma(n=34) . Typically， no epithelial tissue exists in the retroperi-toneum. PRMC is generally considered to arise from teratoma， ectopic ovarian tissue， invagination of the mesothelium with subsequent mucinous metaplasia， or remnant of embryonic genitourinary tissue. However， the definitive causative fac-tors remain unknown.

【19】In our case， the tumor was less likely to have originated from ovarian tissue because the left ovary was completely removed in a previous surgery and no remnant ovarian tissue was found intraoperatively； moreover， the specimen showed no ovarian stroma and immunohistochemistry result was negative for ER.

【20】CA19-9 is a well-known tumor marker with little specificity and is upregulated in pancreatic， biliary， lung， uterine， and ovarian cancers. In addition， norma. tissues， such as the bile duct， pancreatic duct， and endometrium， express CA19-9 . For example， in a reported case of abdominal mesothelioma， elevated serum CA19-9 levels were observed . Therefore， the etiology of elevated serum CA19-9 levels remains unex-plained in our case.

【21】To the best of our knowledge， PRMC with high serum CA19-9levels has never been reported to date. Moreover， our case demonstrated CA19-9 expression using immunohistochemistry， which is extremely rare for PRMC. Kamiyama et al. reported that 12 out of 63 cases showed malignant mural nodules and serum CEA and CA19-9 levels tended to be higher . The signs of malignancy have been reported to be mural nodule， irreg-ular capsule， and calcification of the capsule. However， these signs are also observed in cases of PRMC， which makes the preoperative diagnosis even more difficult .

【22】PRMC arises in the retroperitoneum and becomes symptomatic only when the tumor reaches a certain size. The main symp-toms are abdominal pain and distension， but no specific symp-tom has been reported. Displacement of adjacent organs， such as ureter， kidney， and colon， causes pollakiuria and constipa-tion， which may then sometimes become the chief complaints. The risk factors for PRMC have not yet been elucidated， but it has been recommended to include it in the differential diag-nosis and to conduct imaging studies for middle-aged women with recurrent abdominal symptoms 

【23】Diagnosis of PRMC is suggested mainly by imaging studies， but no specific findings have been reported to date. Most PRMCs consist of well-circumscribed unilocular masses with isodensity in the retroperitoneum ， but these findings are nonspecific. Rajiah et al. suggested a useful classification of primary retroperitoneal masses. First， these masses can be di-vided into solid and cystic masses， and then further subdivided into neoplastic and non-neoplastic masses . In our case， the tumor was classified as a cystic and neoplastic mass. The differential diagnosis includes masses originating from the ep-ithelial tissue (e.g.， PRMC)， mesothelial tissue (e.g.， mesothe-lioma)， germ cell (e.g.， teratoma)， cystic change in a solid neo-plasm (e.g.， sarcoma)， and other origins (e.g.， lymphangioma， epidermoid cyst， and tailgut cyst). Lastly， the diagnosis can be narrowed by some clinical information.

【24】In our case， the mural nodule was detected in the preopera-tive imaging studies but was finally diagnosed as mainly ne-crotic tissue， possibly from an old hematoma， without any ep ithelial component.

【25】Conclusions

【26】We reported a case of PRMC with a mural nodule and high se-rum CA19-9 levels. To the best of our knowledge，this is the first report that demonstrated PRMC with CA19-9 expression by immunohistochemistry. If the lesion is found to be malig-nant， the treatment strategy must be adjusted accordingly.

【0】Background：

【1】Cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy is the standard therapy for unresectable and recurrent esophageal cancer. Cisplatin-based chemotherapy often causes adverse effects， such as nausea， vomiting， and renal dysfunction， which may necessitate dose modification or treatment prolongation. Therefore， novel combination therapies are urgently needed to improve the efficacy and overcome drug toxicity in this setting.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 77-year-old man with advanced esophageal cancer received cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy as neoadjuvant chemotherapy. On day 8 of administration， the patient had lightheadedness， diaphoresis， and nausea and be-came unconscious and developed severe hyponatremia. We diagnosed the patient with cisplatin-induced syn-drome of inadequate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH). Subsequently water restriction was started， and treatment with a salt-added diet and 3% hypertonic saline infusion was initiated. The hyponatremia improved and the patient was discharged on day 16 of administration. Therefore， neoadjuvant chemotherapy was dis-continued， and surgical treatment was performed. However， the tumor recurred and chemotherapy was re-quired. The patient developed severe hyponatremia while receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy； hence， folinic acid， fluorouracil， and oxaliplatin therapy (FOLFOX) were administered as an alternative treatment. The patient completed the FOLFOX therapy without developing SIADH.

【4】Conclusions

【5】The cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy is currently the standard chemotherapy regimen for esophageal cancer. However， SIADH is a known adverse effect when using cisplatin. In patients with esophageal cancer， oxalipla-tin appears to have a lower risk of SIADH than cisplatin， suggesting that oxaliplatin can be a therapeutic op-tion for patients with esophageal cancer who are at high risk of SIADH.

【6】Keywords： Cisplatin· Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma · Hyponatremia · Oxaliplatin Cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy is the standard therapy for un-resectable and recurrent esophageal cancer . Cisplatin-based chemotherapy often causes adverse effects， such as nausea， vomiting， and renal dysfunction， which may necessitate dose modification or treatment prolongation . In general，esopha-geal cancer patients have a lower performance status and poor-er nutrition than patients with other cancer types. Therefore， novel combination therapies are urgently needed to improve the efficacy and overcome drug toxicity in this setting. Some patients may benefit from switching to folinic acid， fluorouracil， and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) therapy， especially those with impaired renal function or challenges with high-volume infusions . A rare adverse effect of cisplatin is syndrome of inadequate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH) . Here， we present a case of SIADH in a patient with esophageal squamous cell cancer who was receiving cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy and later successfully continued treatment with FOLFOX therapy.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 77-year-old man presented to the clinic with pharyngeal discomfort over the previous 2 months. An upper gastroin-testinal endoscopy revealed an esophageal tumor in his tho-racic esophagus. The patient was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma after a biopsy and was referred to our hospi-tal. His medical history included myocardial infarction， stroke， and diabetes. His medications included aspirin， azilsartan， amlodipine besilate， indapamide， carvedilol， rosuvastatin calci-um， glimepiride， sitagliptin phosphate hydrate， and voglibose. The patient did not use diuretics. Imaging studies showed no distant metastases， and a final diagnosis of cT3N0M0 stage ll cancer was made. The standard care for esophageal can-cer  is to operate after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). Cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy (cisplatin 80 mg/m?， 5-fluoro-uracil 800 mg/m2) was commenced as NAC. Hyperhydration(3000 mL/day) with mannitol and magnesium sulfate support were provided before he received cisplatin on day 1. The pa-tient was given 200 ml of 20% mannitol injection on day 1only. On day 8 of administration， the patient had lightheaded-ness， diaphoresis， and nausea and became unconscious； blood test results showed a decrease in serum sodium levels from134 mEq/L to 106 mEq/L (135-146 mEq/L). Urine osmolality was 612 mOsm/L (50-1300 mOsm/kg)， serum osmolality was229 mOsm/L (275-290 mEg/L)， fractional excretion of sodi-um (FENa) was 1.1%， urine Na concentration was 79.7 mEg/L， serum arginine vasopressin (AVP) was 1.2 pg/mL， and serum uric acid level was 2.6 mg/dL (3.6-7.0 mg/dL). The results of other investigations are shown in Table 1. We diagnosed the patient with cisplatin-induced SIADH as there were no abnor-malities on head and chest computed tomography (CT). There was also no evidence of adrenal， thyroid， cardiac， renal， or liv-er dysfunction or signs of dehydration. Subsequently， water restriction was started， and treatment with a salt-added diet and 3% hypertonic saline infusion was initiated. The patient was discharged with gradual improvement in serum sodium levels to 130 mEq/L on day 16 of administration. Thoracic and abdominal contrast-enhanced CT and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy showed a marked reduction in the size of the esoph-ageal lesion after NAC. Positron emission tomography-CT (PET-CT) also showed a decrease in fluorine-18-deoxyglucose (FDG) accumulation (from 22.33 to 18.69 times the standard uptake value \[SUV\])， which we considered to be a minor clinical re-sponse . It was determined that continuing NAC was not possible because of marked hyponatremia； therefore，1 month later， the patient underwent thoracoscopic esophagec-tomy， laparoscopic gastrointestinal reconstruction， and 2-field lymph node dissection with a pathological diagnosis of stageⅢ T3N2M0 well-to-moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Four months after the surgery， a thoracoabdominal contrast-enhanced CT showed a soft tissue shadow extend-ing from the cervical anastomosis to the superior mediasti-num. PET-CT showed an accumulation of FDG at the esopha-geal anastomosis (19.67 times the SUV) and the cervical lymph nodes ， as well as at the mediastinal lymph nodes， right pleura， and 10h rib. The patient was diagnosed with recurrent esophageal cancer， right pleural dissemination， mediastinal lymph node metastasis， and rib metastasis. We decided to start the FOLFOX therapy (folinic acid 200 mg/m?， fluorouracil 2800 mg/m?， and oxaliplatin 85 mg/m²) as the patient developed marked hyponatremia with cisplatin/5-flu-orouracil therapy preoperatively. The serum sodium concen-tration was maintained above 130 mEg/L after 1 course， and the patient was able to continue treatment without develop-ing SIADH. Serum sodium concentration and creatinine levels before and after chemotherapy are shown in Figure 3. The pa-tient did not develop SIADH， but contrast-enhanced CT after4 courses of chemotherapy showed an enlarged lesion， which indicated disease progression. Chemotherapy was discontin-ued， and the patient received best supportive care.

【11】Discussion

【12】SIADH associated with advanced cancer is a common electro-lyte abnormality. The frequency of SIADH (Na <130 mEq/L) has been reported to be 3.7% in patients receiving chemothera-py . SIADH is thought to be mainly induced by platinum-based drugs， such as cisplatin， or by electrolyte abnormalities caused by vomiting， diarrhea， and massive infusions com-monly associated with chemotherapy . There are 2 possi-ble pathophysiological mechanisms for cisplatin-induced hy-ponatremia- SIADH and renal salt wasting syndrome (RSWS) due to dehydration and renal dysfunction. The pathogenesis of RSWS is thought to be a tubular disorder caused by cispla-tin， but the exact mechanism of action is not clear and there are no established diagnostic criteria. It is characterized by ob-vious signs of dehydration and renal dysfunction， resulting in marked sodium diuresis . SIADH is thought to be caused by impaired electrolyte absorption at Henle’s loop， increased hy-dration to prevent renal damage during cisplatin administration， and accelerated antidiuretic hormone secretion (ADH) secre-tion due to vomiting and pain.

【13】The concept of SIADH was proposed by Schwartz et al in 1957. It is a syndrome in which abnormal secretion of ADH causes water retention， resulting in hyponatremia . There have been reports of SIADH caused by vincristine， cyclophosphamide，and cisplatin as well as other antineoplastic agents . The SIADH diagnostic criteria include： 1) preserved adrenal， thyroid， renal， and cardiac function， with no cirrhosis， diuretics， and dehydra-tion； 2) urine osmolality >100 mOsm/L； 3) serum osmolality<280 m0sm/L；4) serum sodium concentration <135 mEq/L；5) FENa >0.5%； and 6) urine sodium >30 mEq/L . In some cases， the diagnostic criteria include a serum ADH concentra-tion greater than the measurement sensitivity . However， an abnormal serum ADH concentration is not characteristic of SIADH alone and thus has no diagnostic value . In this case， we investigated the possibility of both RSWS and SIADH as causes of hyponatremia. The patient had no apparent fea-tures of dehydration or renal dysfunction. Hyponatremia im-proved after treatment with water restriction and sodium correction. Therefore， the main reasons for the development of SIADH could have been excessive hydration to prevent re-nal dysfunction during cisplatin administration and the use of oral diuretics.

【14】The usefulness of cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy as NAC for stage ll and Ill advanced esophageal cancers has been previ-ously reported . In this case，cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy was administered as NAC and caused marked SIADH. Therefore， NAC was discontinued after 1 course and the patient under-went surgica. treatment. Although chemotherapy was indicat-ed for early postoperative recurrence， the risk of cisplatin-re-lated SIADH recurrence was considered high. There is a case of SIADH after treatment with cisplatin in which the patient was able to continue treatment with carboplatin instead of cisplat-in . With regard to the available chemotherapy regimen for esophageal cancer， the PRODIGE5/ACCORD17 trial compared FOLFOX-radiotherapy (RT) and cisplatin/5-fluorouracil-RT ther-apy in patients diagnosed with stage I-IA cancer and eligi-ble for radical chemoradiotherapy and concluded that progres-sion-free survival was similar with both regimens， but FOLFOX might be more convenient . That case study also suggest-ed that FOLFOX-RT may be an alternative to cisplatin/5-fluo-rouracil-RT. In addition， the E-DIS trial， performed for patients with unresectable or recurrent esophageal squamous cell car-cinoma， showed comparable results between the FOLFOX and cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy . In a study that compared the cisplatin/TS-1 and oxaliplatin/TS-1 therapy in patients with unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer， 13.4% and4.4% of patients in the cisplatin/TS-1 and oxaliplatin/TS-1groups had hyponatremia， respectively . Cisplatin-induced SIADH is considered to be caused by impaired electrolyte re-absorption at Henle's loop and water overload due to large amounts of hydration ， and it seems to occur less frequently with oxaliplatin since it does not require large amounts of hy dration. However， even when using oxaliplatin， careful atten-tion should be paid， as there have been reports of SIADH even with this regimen .5-fluorouracil and platinum-based reg-imens were considered preferable in this case because of the response to the preoperative cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy. Switching from cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy with cisplatin to FOLFOX therapy with oxaliplatin allowed our patient to con-tinue treatment without subsequent development of SIADH. Oxaliplatin has several advantages over cisplatin， including that it does not require large amounts of hydration and can be performed on an outpatient basis. However， there is cur-rently little evidence regarding the treatment of esophageal cancer， and great caution is required when using this drug.

【15】Conclusions

【16】The cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy is currently the standard chemotherapy regimen for esophageal cancer； however， SIADH is a known adverse effect when using cisplatin， as seen in the present case. To the best of our knowledge， there is no report of SIADH caused by cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy wherein the patient could continue chemotherapy without SIADH by switching to FOLFOX therapy with oxaliplatin. Oxaliplatin ap-pears to have a lower risk of SIADH than cisplatin， suggesting that oxaliplatin can be a therapeutic option for patients with esophageal cancer who are at high risk of SIADH.

【17】Data Availability Statement

【18】All data generated or analyzed during this study are included in this article and its supplementary material files. Further en-quiries can be directed to the corresponding author.

The SIADH diagnostic criteria include： 1) preserved adrenal， thyroid， renal， and cardiac function， with no cirrhosis， diuretics， and dehydra-tion； 2) urine osmolality >100 mOsm/L； 3) serum osmolality<280 m0sm/L；4) serum sodium concentration <135 mEq/L；5) FENa >0.5%； and 6) urine sodium >30 mEq/L . In some cases， the diagnostic criteria include a serum ADH concentra-tion greater than the measurement sensitivity . However， an abnormal serum ADH concentration is not characteristic of SIADH alone and thus has no diagnostic value . In this case， we investigated the possibility of both RSWS and SIADH as causes of hyponatremia. The patient had no apparent fea-tures of dehydration or renal dysfunction. Hyponatremia im-proved after treatment with water restriction and sodium correction. Therefore， the main reasons for the development of SIADH could have been excessive hydration to prevent re-nal dysfunction during cisplatin administration and the use of oral diuretics.

【14】The usefulness of cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy as NAC for stage ll and Ill advanced esophageal cancers has been previ-ously reported . In this case，cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy was administered as NAC and caused marked SIADH. Therefore， NAC was discontinued after 1 course and the patient under-went surgica. treatment. Although chemotherapy was indicat-ed for early postoperative recurrence， the risk of cisplatin-re-lated SIADH recurrence was considered high. There is a case of SIADH after treatment with cisplatin in which the patient was able to continue treatment with carboplatin instead of cisplat-in . With regard to the available chemotherapy regimen for esophageal cancer， the PRODIGE5/ACCORD17 trial compared FOLFOX-radiotherapy (RT) and cisplatin/5-fluorouracil-RT ther-apy in patients diagnosed with stage I-IA cancer and eligi-ble for radical chemoradiotherapy and concluded that progres-sion-free survival was similar with both regimens， but FOLFOX might be more convenient . That case study also suggest-ed that FOLFOX-RT may be an alternative to cisplatin/5-fluo-rouracil-RT. In addition， the E-DIS trial， performed for patients with unresectable or recurrent esophageal squamous cell car-cinoma， showed comparable results between the FOLFOX and cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy . In a study that compared the cisplatin/TS-1 and oxaliplatin/TS-1 therapy in patients with unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer， 13.4% and4.4% of patients in the cisplatin/TS-1 and oxaliplatin/TS-1groups had hyponatremia， respectively . Cisplatin-induced SIADH is considered to be caused by impaired electrolyte re-absorption at Henle's loop and water overload due to large amounts of hydration ， and it seems to occur less frequently with oxaliplatin since it does not require large amounts of hy dration. However， even when using oxaliplatin， careful atten-tion should be paid， as there have been reports of SIADH even with this regimen .5-fluorouracil and platinum-based reg-imens were considered preferable in this case because of the response to the preoperative cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy. Switching from cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy with cisplatin to FOLFOX therapy with oxaliplatin allowed our patient to con-tinue treatment without subsequent development of SIADH. Oxaliplatin has several advantages over cisplatin， including that it does not require large amounts of hydration and can be performed on an outpatient basis. However， there is cur-rently little evidence regarding the treatment of esophageal cancer， and great caution is required when using this drug.

【15】Conclusions

【16】The cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy is currently the standard chemotherapy regimen for esophageal cancer； however， SIADH is a known adverse effect when using cisplatin， as seen in the present case. To the best of our knowledge， there is no report of SIADH caused by cisplatin/5-fluorouracil therapy wherein the patient could continue chemotherapy without SIADH by switching to FOLFOX therapy with oxaliplatin. Oxaliplatin ap-pears to have a lower risk of SIADH than cisplatin， suggesting that oxaliplatin can be a therapeutic option for patients with esophageal cancer who are at high risk of SIADH.

【17】Data Availability Statement

【18】All data generated or analyzed during this study are included in this article and its supplementary material files. Further en-quiries can be directed to the corresponding author.
