【0】Background：

【1】Intravesical administration of Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (B CG) has been used effectively for treatment of superficial carcinoma of the bladder. Although well tolerated in the majority of patients adverse local and systemic side effects have been described.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We report the case of a 58 year old man who developed granulomatous prostatitis and interstitial pneumonitis following intravesical instillation of B CG for recurrent superficial bladder cancer. Prostate biopsies showed tuberculoid granulomatous inflammation， whereas mycobacterial cultures of sputum were negative. A high resolution computed tomography scan revealed interstitial fibrosis with reticular pattern. The patient received antituberculous treatment and corticosteroids with complete remission.

【4】Concluslons：

【5】This was a rare presentation of granulomatous prostatitis and interstitial pneumonitis following immunotherapy with BCG. Both a hypersensitivity reaction and an infection mechanism should be considered in this particular case.

【6】Key words： BCG vacclne ·bladder neoplasms · prostatltls · pneumonltls

【7】Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) is an attenuated strain of Mycobacterium bovis that has been used effectively in the treatment of patients with superficial bladder cancer. BCG has been shown to eradicate residual tumour in more than 60% of patients with papillary disease and in over 70% of patients with carcinoma in situ . The intravesical instillation of BCG induces local as well as systemic immunological response that is required to effectively eradicate cancer cells . Although the majority of the patients tolerate BCG intravesical treatment well， anumber ofadverse effects have been described. Patients usually experience low grade fever， dysuria， heamaturia and malaise. More serious complications include granulomatous prostatitis， pneumonitis and hepatitis and sepsis. We report a case of granuloma-tous prostatitis and interstitial pneumonitis following intravesical BCG instillation that required antiturb-erculous treatment and corticosteroids for cure.

【8】CASE REPORT

【9】A 58-year old， non-smoking， immunocompetent man was referred to our clinic for assessment of granulomatous prostatitis. Eight years previously he was diagnosed with papillary tumour of the bladder for which he underwent transurethral resection and received chemotherapy with complete remission. Five years later the patient presented with hematuria and repeated cystoscopy with bladder biopsy showed recurrence of carcinoma in situ. The patient was then treated with suspensions of 81 mg of BCG in50 ml of saline instilled into the bladder at 6 weekly intervals. After the sixth dosage he developed night fevers (39°C) and polyarthralgia. His erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was 74 mm/h， C-reactive protein (CRP) was positive and was noted to have slightly elevated Prostatic Specific Antigen (PSA) of 4.3 ng/ml (normal values 0-4 ng/ml). Transrectal ultrasound of the prostate demonstrated a 2.1x0.7 cm hypoechoCIIlic lesion in the right zone. Prostate biopsies revealed chronic inflammatory infiltration with formation of tuberculoid granulomatous struc-tures .

【10】Upon physical examination he had bibasilar inspira tory rales， whereas all other systems were normal. His family history was negative for cancer or other chronic conditions， whereas from his past medical history the only thing of interest was an operation performed ten years previously for a left varicocele. Routine blood tests and thyroid function tests were normal. His oxygen saturation (SaO2) was 97%. Mantoux test was performed with positive result (20 mm). Mycobacterial cultures of sputum and urine were negative. A bronchoscopy with trans-bronchial lung biopsy and bronchoalveolar lavage(BAL) demonstrated lymphocytosis and activated T helper cells (33%). Biopsy specimen revealed areas of interstitial inflammatory infiltration . Cytology specimens were negative for tumour and cultures for fungi and acid fast bacilli were also n亡ga-tive. Pulmonary function tests (PFT) with diffusion were normal. Chest radiography displayed peripheral microreticulonodular opacities in the middle and lower lung fields. A chest high resolution computed tomography (CT chest HR) scan identified areas with interstitial fibrosis . CT scan of abdomen was normal and gallium citrate scan was negative for active lung disease.

【11】The patient was started on aregimen of oral rifam-picin (600 mg daily)， isoniazid (300 mg daily) and ethambutol (1200 mg daily) for two months and continued rifampicin and isoniazid to complete a six-month course， but refused to start corticoste-roids. One month after the beginning of antituber-culous treatment the urologists repeated intravesi-cal treatment with BCG at three monthly intervals. Six months later the patient underwent transrectal ultrasound of prostate that was normal with disap-pearance ofthe right side lesion whereas cystoscopy revealed no signs of relapse. The patient remained well until five months later when he visited our clinic again complaining of gradually worsening dyspnoea on exertion. A marked decrease in diffu-sion (Dco=71.5%) was noted but a new CT chest HR showed no significant changes compared to the previous one. The patient still declined treat-ment with corticosteroids. Four months later， his dyspnoea was much worse and the patient revisited our clinic. A new PFT revealed a further decrease in diffusion (Dco=67.6%). A repeated CT chest HR showed worsening compared to the previous one， with appearance of honeycomblung in all lung fields and bronchiectasic areas in the middle lobe. the lingula and the upper parts of the lower lobes. The patient finally agreed to begin treatment and he was started 40 mg prednisone daily with complete resolution of dyspnoea. Two months later a new CT chest HR was markedly improved and a repeated PFT showed increase in diffusion (Dco= 83.4%). The patient remains well and is now on 20 mg pred-nisone daily.

【12】DISCUSSION

【13】Immunotherapy with intravesicular BCG for patients with superficial transitional carcinoma ofthe bladder is associated with side effects of moderate severity that are generally well tolerated. In the multi-center series reported by Lamm et al  granuloma-tous prostatitis was observed in 1.3% of the patients whereas serious complications defined as hepatitis or pneumonitis occurred in 0.9% with affected patients presenting with fever， chills， night sweats， malaise， dyspnoea and cough. Local side effects occur either as an inflammatory reaction to BCG instillation or due to an infection secondary to contact with BCG contaminated urine 

【14】In this report， we describe a case in which a patient treated with intravesical BCG because of transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder developed prostatic tuberculosis and interstitial pneumonitis. In granu-lomatous prostatitis PSA levels are often elevated and ultrasound typically shows diffuse hypoechoic areas . This was the case in our patient， with tuber-culoid granulomas on prostate biopsy confirming that attenuated mycobacteria are the causative factor for these lesions.

【15】Concerning the pulmonary involvement， it is un-settled whether a hypersensitivity reaction due to BCG antigens or an actual pulmonary infection due to haematogenous spread of mycobacteria provokes lung reaction . There is in fact some consensus that both mechanisms play a role . According to some authors， the reticulonodular opacities on chest radiographs， lymphocytosis on BAL with elevated T一AT T4/T8 ratio on BAL， the detection of interstitial pneumonitis on lung biopsy， a favourable response to corticosteroids in selected patients and the ab-sence of granulomatous inflammation on the lung biopsy specimens are regarded as the main features of pulmonary localization of hypersensitivity reactionFor this reason， recommended treatment for patients with M.bovis infections in the acute setting is a combination of isoniazid plus rifampicin for three to six months with the addition of prednisone 40 mg daily .

【16】Although an actual infectious process cannot be excluded regarding the pulmonary involvement in our patient， we have evidence for a hypersensitiv-ity reaction. The findings on CT chest HR were consistent with diffuse interstitial pneumonitis and mycobacterial cultures were negative. In addition， increased activated alveolar lymphocytes on BAL analysis and the rapid recovery of the patient with corticosteroids are also suggestive of a hypersensi-tivity mechanism.

【17】CONCLUSIONS

【18】In conclusion， we have reported an interesting case of granulomatous prostatitis following intravesical BCG therapy. The patient received antituberculous treat-ment for his prostatitis with full recovery. However， during antituberculous treatment he developed in-terstitial pneumonitis. In this regard， corticosteroids appear to be the appropriate treatment as was in our patient.

【0】ABSTRACT Background-Nerium oleander (common oleander grown as an ornamental plant) and Cerbera Thevetia(yellow oleander grows wildly on the roadside). All parts of these plants， including nectar， are potentially lethal. Suicidal poisoning by the products of these plants is a toxicologic emergency in tropical and subtropical regions. They contain cardiac glycosides， namely Oleandrin， Oleandrigenin， Nerifolin， ThevetinA， and ThevetinB， which act like digoxin in addition to gastrointestinal symptoms. Ingestion of oleander results in nausea， vomiting， abdominal pain， diarrhoea， dysrhythmias， and hyperkalemia. Cardiac toxicity includes a variety of ventricular dysrhythmias and A-V Blocks， muscular twitching， tetanic spasms， lockjaw， coma and respiratory paralysis. The cause of death is usually cardiogenic shock and respiratory arrest. Some cases have been reported with acute kidney injury and hepatic damage. Case report- We have successfully managed 3 cases of acute oleander poisoning. All three patients were young and did not have comorbid conditions. 2 patients presented with mainly abdominal pain and vomiting and had hyperkalemia. The third patient had symptomatic bradycardia and several episodes of vomiting. Most cases can be managed by Multidose activated charcoal and supportive care with IV fluids and symptomatic treatment. However some patients require respiratory support， atropine and pacing for symptomatic bradycardia. Insulin-dextrose is the most effective method of treating hyperkalemia. Calcium chloride is contraindicated in this instance. Specific management is digoxin-specific Fab fragments. Emergency physicians may encounter these cases and should have sound knowledge about symptoms and management. Oleander poisoning should be considered in the differential for any young patient presenting with bradycardia.

【1】KEYWORDS oleander， toxicity， cardiac dysrhythmias， hyperkalemia， multidose activated charcoal， temporary pacing， acute kidney injury

【2】Introduction

【3】Nerium oleander (common oleander grown as an ornamental plant)l  and Thevetia peruviana (Cerbera thevetia12， yel-low oleander grows widely on sides of roads)  are orna-mental plants found all over India. All parts of the plant are poisonous-， including nectar. Even food cooked over the fire made with dried twigs can lead to accidental poisoning1. Seeds and leaves are common toxic principles. They cause gastroin-testinal irritability and cardiotoxicity. Gastrointestinal effects are due to direct irritant effects. Increased vagal tone is the reason for cardiac effects.

【4】They also cause hyperkalemia and skeletal and respiratory muscle paralysis. The most common cause of death is cardiac dysrhythmias and bradycardia， leading to circulatory failure.

【5】We are presenting here 3 cases of acute oleander poisoning， which we have treated successfully.

【6】Case Reports

【7】Case 1： A male patient of 28 years presented with repeated vom-iting and abdominal pain after 2 hours of intentional ingestion of 5-8 leaves of Nerium odorum crushed and mixed with jaggery. At presentation， his vitals were pulse-60/min regular rhythm with low volume， B.P-100/60 mm Hg， respiratory rate-24/min， room air saturation 95%. The only initial finding was congestion of oral mucosa. Gastric decontamination was performed with stomach wash and multidose-activated charcoal.

【8】Intravenous proton pump inhibitors and antiemetic and intra-venous hydration were initiated. He has been closely monitored with continuous cardiac monitoring and 12th hourly serum elec-trolytes. His serum potassium was 5.6meq/dl on the second day. Potassium correction is given with insulin-dextrose and salbutamol nebulization. The rest of the hospital course was uneventful. The patient was discharged after five days with follow-up advice.

【9】Case 2： A 32-year-old female presented with vomiting and abdominal pain 3 hours after the consumption of approximately3-5 seeds of yellow oleander intentionally. At the presentation， she was dehydrated with a weak pulse. Pulse rate-70/min reg ular rhythm， B.P-90/60mm Hg， respiratory rate-30/min，room air saturation-96%. Her serum chemistry revealed potassium of6meg/dl without any ECG abnormalities. She received similar treatment. Close ICU monitoring was initiated. She developed hyperkalemia several times， which has been corrected. The patient was discharged on day 7 with follow-up advice.

【10】Case 3： A 35-year-old female presented with vomiting， dizzi-ness， and blurring of vision 12 hours after the intentional con-sumption of 12 seeds of yellow oleander. At presentation， her pulse-40/min， weak regular rhythm， B.P-80/50 mm Hg，respi-ratory rate was 28/min and room air saturation-90%. Her ECG showed sinus bradycardia. She also had similar treatment to that of the first patient. Atropine 1mg was given intravenously and repeated three times. Her heart rate and blood pressure im- proved transiently after each dose of atropine but started falling again. Because of her symptomatic bradycardia， she required pacemaker therapy. Her vitals improved after pacing and re-mained stable. Her blood investigations were unremarkable except for potassium 5.2 meq/dl. She was symptomatically bet-ter on day 2， and the pacemaker was detached. Her heart rate gradually improved to 70/min and her blood pressure to 110/70mm Hg on day 3. She was advised to follow up regularly and was discharged on day 7.

【11】Discussion

【12】Nerium oleander is a large evergreen ornamental shrub with long， lanceolate leaves and clusters of whitish or pinkish flower-. Yellow oleander is an ornamental shrub (that grows to about 30feet in height) belonging to the family Apocynaceae with longish(about 15 cm long) leaves yielding a milky sap and yellowish funnel-shaped flowers1. The fruit is diamond or clam-shaped and has 2 to 4 seeds in its stony inner section. The concoction of the leaves and root are used in Indian traditional medicine. The root is used as an abortifacient-. Bark extracts have been investigated as cytotoxic agents in chemotherapy. All parts of the plant are toxic， including the nectar and food cooked over the dried branches of the tree can also cause poisoning as tox-ins are not destroyed by heat1. They contain various cardiac glycosides， namely oleandrin， neriin， nerifolin， peruvoside， ru-voside， cereberin， thevitinA， thevitinB13. The cardiac glycosides have carbohydrate or sugar moiety attached through an oxygen bridge to carbon 3 of the A' ring of the steroid. They act like digoxin and inhibit sodium-potassium ATPase123. The toxic dose is 5 to 15 leaves or 15 grams of root for common oleander. About 8 to 10 seeds or 15 to 20 grams of yellow oleander1 is considered toxic.

【13】Symptoms generally begin within 10 to 20 minutes of inges-tion. A tingling or burning sensation in the fingers and toes is usually seen first， followed by sweats and chills， generalized paraesthesia， dry mouth， and numbness. The following signs and symptoms are seen：

【14】1\. GIT： Nausea， vomiting， diarrhoea. Numbness of the tongue occurs sometimes.

【15】2\. CVS： Increased ectopy and conduction delay leading to bradycardia， supraventricular tachycardia with AV block. Ventricular fibrillation is potentially lethal. Shortened QRS-T interval， T wave flattening/inversion， irregular ventricu-lar rate， increased PR interval， etc.， have also been reported. Smoke from a burning oleander the plant can cause dizzi-ness， vomiting， and cardiac dysrhythmias. Bradycardia and heart block are the most frequently reported cardiac abnormalities.

【16】3\. CNS： Delirium， lethargy， dizziness， drowsiness. Occasion-ally there may be seizures and coma.

【17】The most typical manifestations associated with yellow olean-der poisoning include bradycardia with AV block， hypotension， lethargy， dizziness， and GI distress. Convulsions， electrolyte disturbances， hypertension， and coma have also been reported. Mydriasis may occur. Numbness and burning sensation in the mouth may develop. The sap of the yellow oleander tree may cause blistering or dermatitis on contact1. Subendocardial and perivascular haemorrhage with focal myocardial oedema has been found during autopsies. Some authors reported acute kid-ney injury and hepatic failure.

【18】Table 1 Toxic parts and doses

| Species  | Fatal dose  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Species  | Leaves  | Seeds  | Root  |
| Pink oleander  | 5-15  | 一  | 15 gm  |
| Yellow oleander  | 10-15  | 8-10  | 20 gm  |

【20】Table 2 Management of oleander poisoning

| Decontamination  | Gastric lavage  | Indicated within the first 2 hours  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decontamination  | Multidose activated charcoal  | Prepare slurry with and administer orally or through Ryle’s tube theinitial dose of 1 gram/kg followed by 0.5 gram/kg 8th hourly  |
| Gastrointestinal  | Vomiting and abdominal pain  | Proton pump inhibitors  |
| Supportive  | Hypotension and shock  | IV crystalloids and vasopressors as needed  |
| Cardiac  | Bradycardia  | Atropine and pacing as per ACLS protocol  |
| Cardiac  | Tachycardia  | Rate-limiting drugs as per protocol  |
| Metabolic  | Hyperkalaemia  | High-dose insulin-dextrose therapy Use calcium cautiously-canprecipitate tachycardia  |
| Metabolic  | Acute kidney injury Metabolic acidosisRefractory Hyperkalaemia  | haemodialysis  |
| CNS  | Seizures  | Phenobarbitone  |

【22】Cardiac glycosides of this plant are best identified by radioim-muno assay.

【23】Initial assessment and management are similar to other poisonings. No definite criteria are available for risk stratification’. Continuous ECG monitoring is necessary to de-tect dysrhythmias’； more prolonged monitoring is appropriate in patients with severe poisoning. Supportive care. Correction of dehydration with normal saline is essential， and antiemetics are used to control severe vomiting. Hypokalemia worsens toxicity due to cardiac glycosides， and hyperkalemia is life-threatening. Both must be corrected. Hyperkalemia is due to an extracellular shift of potassium rather than an increase in total body potas-sium. It is best treated with insulin-dextrose infusion(adminis-ter 0.2 unit/kg of regular insulin with 200 to 400 mg/kg glucose). Intravenous calcium increases the risk of cardiac dysrhythmias and is not recommended in treating hyperkalemia. Serum mag-nesium should be corrected as it can worsen cardiac glycoside toxicity. Gastric lavage is part of the standard care for poison-ing with many substances. Yellow oleander seed fragments can stay in the stomach for many hours after ingestion. One study reported that multidose activated charcoal has a survival advantage over single-dose activated charcoal. There is pharma-cological evidence that MDAC increases the plasma clearance of cardiac glycosides. In severe cases， bradyarrhythmias are commonly managed with atropine， isoprenaline， and temporary cardiac pacing. Tachyarrhythmias have a poor prognosis and are more challenging to treat. Lidocaine (1 milligram/kg) is the preferred antiarrhythmic； the role of intravenous magnesium(2-4gm IV) is uncertain.

【24】Digoxin-specific antibody fragments effectively revert life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias and are the only specific treat-ment available； prospective observational studies show a benefi-cial effect on mortality. High cost and lack of availability limit the widespread use of digoxin-specific antibody fragments in developing countries. Digoxin Fab fragments are indicated if the potassium concentration exceeds the upper limit of the normal range (5 mEq/L) in association with other severe symptoms. Some investigators recommend the empiric administration of 10 vials of digoxin-specific Fab. One study has suggested Fructose-1， 6-diphosphate (FDP) as a novel antidote for yellow oleander-induced cardiac toxicity. The mortality ranges from 10-to 17%for in- hospital patients. Hemodialysis is ineffective in removing cardiac glycosides. However， it helps manage refractory aci-dosis. Certain steroid compounds such as spironolactone and pregnenolone-16alpha-carbonitrile， have decreased glycoside toxicity by increasing biliary excretion. Although not yet tried in humans， these agents could be tried as a treatment modality.

【25】Conclusion

【26】Early presentation and timely intervention can decrease compli-cations and mortality from life-threatening dysrhythmias. Seeds of yellow oleander are more toxic than the leaves. Management includes supportive therapy with gastric lavage， multidose acti-vated charcoal， fluid and electrolyte management and atropine of bradyarrhythmias. Severe cases of poisoning and those pre-senting late might require transcutaneous pacing. Most patients can be managed without digoxin-specific Fab fragments.

【0】Background：

【1】Invasive mucinous carcinoma arising in ectopic axillary breast tissue is an uncommon diagnosis. While some published medical literature makes recommendations regarding the management of ectopic primaries， many of these recommendations are outdated. We therefore hope to provide general guidance with the manage-ment of this rare entity.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We report a case of a 70-year-old woman with primary invasive mucinous carcinoma of ectopic breast tissue. A literature study was performed on primary ectopic breast carcinoma. This case report with review of the lit-erature was performed to provide rationales for a more conservative treatment based upon current data and treatment paradigms.

【4】Although the diagnosis of primary ectopic breast carcinoma is uncommon， the presence of a suspicious nod-ule along the mammary ridge should alert the clinician to consider the possibility of this diagnosis. A mammo-gram and ultrasound of the nodule were performed and the suspicious nodule was biopsied， confirming the diagnosis. Breast conservation was performed with standard nodal evaluation.

【5】Conclusions：

【6】The management of primary ectopic breast carcinoma should be based upon current breast conservation tech-niques of orthotopic breast cancer. Current data suggest that standard treatment paradigms remain applica-ble to this rare clinical entity.

【7】MeSH Keywords：

【8】Adenocarcinoma， Mucinous· Breast Cancer·Breast Neoplasms · Mammary Carcinoma·Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy Ectopic breast tissue (EBT) can be defined as encompassing both supernumerary and aberrant breasts . EBT is demon-strable in about 0.2-6% of the entire population .For the sake of this discussion， EBT will be used to describe all breast tissue found distant to and/or noncontiguous with the nor-mal anatomic breast.

【9】Primary carcinoma of EBT is uncommon， making up only 0.3%of all breast neoplasms ， with mucinous carcinomas repre-senting a small fraction of these rare lesions. Since the pub-lished medical literature on ectopic breast cancers remains lim-ited， and contains outdated guidelines for management， this case report is presented to provide general guidance on how to manage this rare entity.

【10】Case Report

【11】A 70-year-old gravida 1， para 1， post-menopausal African American woman presented to an outside institution com-plaining of a superficial right axillary mass that she first no-ticed 6 months prior to initial presentation. A mammogram was performed at an outside institution and found to be un-remarkable. This was followed with a dedicated mediolateral oblique mammographic view of the ipsilateral breast and an ultrasound of the right axilla， which revealed a solid hyper-vascular， hypoechoic nodule protruding into the skin， measur-ing 1.0×0.6 cm . Differential diagnosis at the time included occult primary breast carcinoma， metastatic breast cancer， and various lesions of intradermal origin. She under-went an excisional biopsy of the axillary skin nodule， which demonstrated a 0.9-cm invasive mucinous breast carcinoma. The pathologic differential diagnosis at the outside facility in-cluded metastatic breast carcinoma versus primary adnex-al tumor， with consideration given to a breast primary tumor.

【12】Immunohistochemical analysis found that the tissue was estro-gen receptor (ER)-positive at 99%， progesterone receptor (PR)-negative at <1%， HER2/neu-negative by fluorescence in situ hy-bridization， and negative for CK5/6， p63， and GCDFP-15. She was clinically staged according to American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) 7th edition as pT1b，cN0， cM0. Her initial eval-uation included a computed tomography (CT) of her chest， abdomen， and pelvis， which demonstrated no other lesions.

【13】Her past medical and surgical history was unremarkable. She underwent yearly screening mammograms since the age of40. Her family history was contributory for breast cancer in her mother at age 62， breast cancer in her daughter at age 47， and prostate cancer in her brother at age 71.

【14】With positive margins on her initial excisional biopsy， the pa-tient was referred to our institution. Pathology review con-firmed the primary lesion as not being a metastatic focus or a small superficial lymph node， in part due to the absence of lymph node tissue and presence of surrounding healthy breast tissue adjacent to the cancer. The patient underwent a wide local excision of her surgical scar along with the subcutane-ous tissue， and lymphatic mapping/sentinel lymphadenecto-my . The sentinel lymph nodes felt clinically benign intraoperatively， and no enlarged lymph nodes were noted in-traoperatively . Pathology demonstrated addition-al grade 1 invasive mucinous carcinoma within the residu-al subcutaneous EBT excised， but all margins were negative at a distance of 20.3 cm. There was no sentinel lymph node involvement， lymphovascular invasion， in situ component， or skin involvement on final pathology Postoperatively， she was prescribed external beam whole-breast radiotherapy of 46Gy， in 23 fractions， with a tumor cavity boost of 14Gy in 7 fractions. She was prescribed adjuvant endocrine therapy， and referred to genetics because of her significant fam-ily history of malignancy. The patient was seen 6 months post-operatively with no evidence of recurrence on examination.

【15】Discussion

【16】Embryology

【17】Between the 5th and 6h week of embryonic development， the mammary ridges ("milk lines") begin to form as 2 ventral bands mammography noted no primary within the breast， while axillary ultrasound demonstrated a subcutaneous nodule that was subsequently noted to be a primary ectopic breast carcinoma.

【18】of thickened ectoderm extending from the base of the forelimb(future axilla) to the hindlimb (inguinal region) . Ifthese fail to undergo complete regression soon after formation， polymastia (ac-cessory mammary glands) or polythelia (accessory nipples) occurs. Although the axilla is the most frequent site ， EBT can be found in multiple locations in up to one-third of patients .

【19】Clinical symptoms and manifestations

【20】EBT is embryologically identical to normal anatomic breast tissue and is subject to normal hormonal responses， making it susceptible to the same diseases and neoplastic degener-ation  as orthotopic breast tissue. Most patients first notice EBT as a soft， nontender mass in 1 or both axillae . Although most EBT is asymptomatic ， hormonal and cos-metic changes can be associated with menses， puberty， or preg-nancy  and cause distension and mild pain ， most fre-quently during the menstrual cycle .

【21】Incidence and histology

【22】Primary ectopic breast carcinoma (PEBC) of the axilla is rare and accounts for only 0.3% of all breast cancers . The axilla is the most common site of PEBC， ranging from 58% to 71% of cases. Mucinous carcinoma (MC)， a rare histologic breast can-cer subtype， is characterized by extracellular mucin that dissects into the stroma ， and accounts for<2% of all inva-sive breast cancers . In a series by Nihon-Yanagi of 64patients with ectopic breast carcinoma， only 7.8% of patients had mucinous carcinoma， making the incidence of mucinous PEBC <0.2% of breast cancer cases. Other histologic subtypes found included invasive ductal carcinomas (75%)， medullary carcinomas (7.8%)， and apocrine carcinomas (6.3%) . 【23】Diagnosis

【24】Due to the low incidence and misidentification of PEBC， the delay in diagnosis  averages 40.5 months ， with lesions often mistaken for another disease such as a skin tag， nevus， hidradenitis， or lymphadenopathy . EBT usually presents only a cosmetic concern ， but this can be severe and a source of embarrassment. Nevertheless， it is subject to the same in-fluences as orthotopic breast tissue； inflammatory and neo-plastic conditions must be considered .

【25】PEBC can present in several ways， ranging from normal-appear-ing ectopic breast tissue to a lesion having ulceration， bleed-ing， discolored skin， crusting， or associated discharge . The presence of a subcutaneous mass along the mammary line should prompt the clinician to consider the possibility of PEBC and the presence of suspicious nodules warrants histolog-ic evaluation . After surgical or needle biopsy confirms PEBC， some authors recommend further imaging to rule out meta-static disease or ipsilateral breast involvement . A review of the literature suggests that ectopic breast tissue can be bi-lateral ， and therefore contralateral evaluation should be strongly considered  via examination of the contralat-eral axilla， both breasts， and surrounding nodal basins .

【26】Mammograms， in particular， may be negative because of the location of PEBC， while ultrasound may be of limited utility be-cause of its frequent subcutaneous location. This can make the diagnosis uncertain and necessitate fine-needle aspiration(FNA) or core-needle biopsy . In mucinous carcinoma of the breast， diagnosis may be challenging because of the like-lihood of sampling areas of mucin that lack epithelial cells .

【27】In a series of 26 patients undergoing resection of EBT， only3.8% were found to contain a carcinoma . While some au-thors suggest early prophylactic resection of ectopic breast tissue in any patient who presents with EBT for its oncolog-ic， emotional， and anesthetic benefit ， the low rate of PEBC may not justify the morbidity of such an approach. If the presence of EBT is painful or symptomatic， particularly during menses ， complete excision can be performed for its cos-metic advantage and possible improvement of symptoms . Prospective data regarding the benefit of such an approach is lacking and informed consent is imperative.

【28】Others argue that given the lack of high-level evidence， resec-tion of all asymptomatic EBT should be weighed against the risks of surgery  and recommend monitoring EBT with self-breast examinations and frequent follow-up visits . In a series of 28 patients who underwent prophylactic excision， there was a 39.2% postoperative complication rate fol-lowing excision of ectopic breast tissue， mostly related to poor scar formation followed by intercostobrachial nerve injury and presence of residual tissue. The high complication rate， howev-er， suggests that patients with ectopic breast tissue should in-stead be counseled and conservatively managed .Operative intervention in the axilla can also pose a risk of contracture and potentially lower the sentinel node identification rate .

【29】Imaging evaluation

【30】Mammography is usually not helpful in screening for PEBC be-cause of its location in the high axilla ， although oblique and exaggerated craniocaudal views may compensate for this location and visualize ectopic breasts . Ultrasonography may also visualize ectopic breast tissue in the axilla and guide treatment based on radiologic features. Up to 21.2% of muci-nous carcinomas of the breast are not detected on mammo-gram . Most commonly， ectopic breast tissue carcinomas are sonographically hypoechoic， while mucinous carcinomas as a whole differ by having complex cystic and solid components， as well as internal hyperechoic features with hypoechoic peripheral shadows . Heterogeneity and irregular margins on sonography confer a worse prognosis .

Even among cases having extensive metastatic disease from PEBC， there are no reports of ipsilateral breast metastases

【34】Currently， staging does not differentiate PEBC from orthotopic breast cancer， with the T classification based upon the max-imal diameter of the PEBC Since EBT has a tendency to be more superficial， ectopic breast carcinoma is more like-ly to involve the skin and be classified as a T4 lesion al-though the largest series in the literature demonstrates that small skin-involved lesions have similar prognoses as those without such involvement . Despite the more favorable prog-nostic factors in MC ， authors have concluded that nod-al status and adjuvant therapy appear to be more significant predictors of prognosis than histologic type . 【41】Treatment

【42】Due to its rarity and paucity of data， there is little published medical literature on management of axillary PEBC，but standard breast cancer paradigms still apply. Historically， PEBC was treated with excision of the ectopic breast tissue carcino-ma， radical mastectomy， and radiation to the chest . As far back as 1961， Cogswell and Czerny found no oncologic benefit to performing a radical mastectomy over excision of the axillary tumor and tail of the breast， and axillary lymphad-enectomy . Given that histological data confirms that these are breast cancers， we believe the best treatment practices of orthotopic breast cancer should be applied to PEBC .

【44】Patients with hormone receptor-positive PEBCs should be of-fered adjuvant hormone therapies because of its reduction of contralateral breast cancer  and recurrence rate ad-vantage， also seen for mucinous tumors such as that report-ed here . There is little reason to believe that PEBC without ipsilatera. breast involvement necessitates adjuvant irradiation beyond the tumor site and axilla， and all available evidence suggests that radiotherapy need not be used on the ipsilateral breast .

【46】Axillary dissection can result in significant morbidity. In 1 se-ries， physical and psychological complications were reported in most (73%) patients who underwent axillary dissection . There are few reports describing the use of sentinel lymphadenectomy in the treatment of ectopic breast cancer 32，44，45J. In this case re-port， we were able to utilize sentinel lymphatic mapping along with sentinel lymphadenectomy in identifying 3 sentinel lymph nodes， avoiding the potential morbidity of axillary lymphade-nectomy. Because sentinel node biopsy is successful in both breast cancer  and melanoma  (among other malig-nancies)， from a variety of anatomic locations， there is no bi-ologic reason to believe that this would be different for PEBC

【47】Thorne et al. used sentinel lymphadenectomy to isolate the lymphatic drainage of accessory breast tissue on the anterior abdominal wall. They reported more accurate staging and sug-gest utilizing lymphatic mapping and sentinel lymphadenec-tomy for PEBC . PEBC is found to be close to the normal anatomic breast in 93% of cases ， which makes use of radio-nuclide potentially more challenging because of the proximity of the primary injection site to the location of the nodes with shine-through from the primary， potentially obscuring the low-er gamma counts from nodes. However， this proximity should also make the lymphatic drainage patterns somewhat predict-able， and use of blue dye remains practical， as in this case. We therefore believe that the use of the sentinel lymph node tech-nique， using blue dye such as Lymphazurin， is safe and fea-sible in patients with early-stage PEBC. 【48】Surveillance

【49】There are no specific surveillance guidelines for PEBC， but fol-low-up involving serial examinations should be maintained. The American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) clini-cal practice guidelines  and NCCN Guidelines  for breast cancer follow-up and management after primary treatment can be used in patients treated for PEBC， and standard bilateral mammographic screening should be performed annually. The site of the resection， however， is likely to be primarily ame-nable to physical examination， with imaging required only in the event of a physical examination finding.

【50】Conclusions

【51】Due to its rarity， management guidelines for invasive muci-nous carcinoma of ectopic axillary breast tissue are lacking.

【52】Once the diagnosis of PEBC is confirmed， multi-disciplinary treatment should be employed based upon current breast can-cer guidelines. The limited published data also suggest that radiotherapy should be limited to the tumor cavity and ipsilateral axilla. 【0】Background：

【1】Invasive mucinous carcinoma arising in ectopic axillary breast tissue is an uncommon diagnosis. 【4】Although the diagnosis of primary ectopic breast carcinoma is uncommon， the presence of a suspicious nod-ule along the mammary ridge should alert the clinician to consider the possibility of this diagnosis. A mammo-gram and ultrasound of the nodule were performed and the suspicious nodule was biopsied， confirming the diagnosis. Breast conservation was performed with standard nodal evaluation.

【5】Conclusions：

【6】The management of primary ectopic breast carcinoma should be based upon current breast conservation tech-niques of orthotopic breast cancer. Current data suggest that standard treatment paradigms remain applica-ble to this rare clinical entity.

【7】MeSH Keywords：

【9】Primary carcinoma of EBT is uncommon， making up only 0.3%of all breast neoplasms ， with mucinous carcinomas repre-senting a small fraction of these rare lesions. Despite its propensity for early lymphat-ic involvement， metastatic spread to the ipsilateral breast has not been reported . There is little reason to believe that PEBC without ipsilatera. breast involvement necessitates adjuvant irradiation beyond the tumor site and axilla， and all available evidence suggests that radiotherapy need not be used on the ipsilateral breast .

【46】Axillary dissection can result in significant morbidity. In 1 se-ries， physical and psychological complications were reported in most (73%) patients who underwent axillary dissection . Currently， lymphatic mapping and sentinel lymphadenectomy are standard practice and highly accurate . There are few reports describing the use of sentinel lymphadenectomy in the treatment of ectopic breast cancer 32，44，45J. In this case re-port， we were able to utilize sentinel lymphatic mapping along with sentinel lymphadenectomy in identifying 3 sentinel lymph nodes， avoiding the potential morbidity of axillary lymphade-nectomy. Because sentinel node biopsy is successful in both breast cancer  and melanoma  (among other malig-nancies)， from a variety of anatomic locations， there is no bi-ologic reason to believe that this would be different for PEBC

【47】Thorne et al. used sentinel lymphadenectomy to isolate the lymphatic drainage of accessory breast tissue on the anterior abdominal wall. They reported more accurate staging and sug-gest utilizing lymphatic mapping and sentinel lymphadenec-tomy for PEBC . PEBC is found to be close to the normal anatomic breast in 93% of cases ， which makes use of radio-nuclide potentially more challenging because of the proximity of the primary injection site to the location of the nodes with shine-through from the primary， potentially obscuring the low-er gamma counts from nodes. However， this proximity should also make the lymphatic drainage patterns somewhat predict-able， and use of blue dye remains practical， as in this case. We therefore believe that the use of the sentinel lymph node tech-nique， using blue dye such as Lymphazurin， is safe and fea-sible in patients with early-stage PEBC. When blue dye is in-jected， intradermal injection may be required because of the subdermal nature of the lesion in the axilla； injection into the axilla would stain much of the tissue and make sentinel node identification difficult. Should radionuclide be desired，resec-tion of the primary would be required prior to the search for sentinel nodes， to prevent shine-through and allow for detec-tion by the gamma probe adjacent to the area of the PEBC .

【48】Surveillance

【49】There are no specific surveillance guidelines for PEBC， but fol-low-up involving serial examinations should be maintained. The American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) clini-cal practice guidelines  and NCCN Guidelines  for breast cancer follow-up and management after primary treatment can be used in patients treated for PEBC， and standard bilateral mammographic screening should be performed annually. The site of the resection， however， is likely to be primarily ame-nable to physical examination， with imaging required only in the event of a physical examination finding.

【50】Conclusions

【51】Due to its rarity， management guidelines for invasive muci-nous carcinoma of ectopic axillary breast tissue are lacking.

【52】Once the diagnosis of PEBC is confirmed， multi-disciplinary treatment should be employed based upon current breast can-cer guidelines. We believe that early-stage PEBC can be treat-ed with wide local excision， sentinel lymph node biopsy， and axillary dissection if required. The limited published data also suggest that radiotherapy should be limited to the tumor cavity and ipsilateral axilla. The patient should be prescribed hormonal therapy and/or chemotherapy， depending on the tumor charac-teristics， all consistent with standard breast cancer guidelines.

【0】Background：

【1】Fabry disease is an X-linked disorder. Due to deficiency of the enzyme o-galactosidase A， neutral glycosphin-golipids (primarily globotriaosylceramide) progressively accumulate within lysosomes of cells in various organ systems， resulting in a multi-system disorder， affecting both men and women. Misdiagnosis and delayed diag-nosis are common because of the nature of Fabry disease.

【2】Case Report： We report a case of Fabry disease with a p.R301X (c.901 C>T) mutation in a 39-year-old man who was being treated for chronic sclerosing glomerulonephritis for 2 years. Family screening tests showed that the proband's mother， sister， and daughter had the same mutation with different phenotypes. Levels of o-galactosidase A were low in the proband and his mother and sister. Cornea verticillata and heart involvement were present in multiple family members. Agalsidase alfa treatment was started in patients where indicated.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Pedigree analysis is still a powerful， readily available tool to identify individuals at risk for genetic diseases and allows earlier detection and management of disease.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Codon， Nonsense · Fabry Disease · Heart Diseases· Kidney Failure， Chronic GLA gene produces enzyme o-galactosidase A and is present on the long arm of chromosome Xq22.1. Due to deficiency of the enzyme a-galactosidase A， neutral glycosphingolipids (primari-ly globotriaosylceramide) progressively accumulate within lyso-somes of cells in various organ systems. Globotriaosylceramide gradually accumulates in endothelial cells， vascular smooth muscle cells， pericytes， renal epithelial cells， myocardial cells， and neurons， which leads progressively to cellular dysfunction， necrosis， apoptosis， inflammation， and fibrosis .

【6】Demonstration of deficient activity of o-galactosidase in plas-ma or leukocytes and showing GLA mutation are the primary diagnostic tools in men . Female patients may have en-zyme activity within the normal range； therefore， they should have their status determined by genotyping (analysis of the GLA gene mutation).

【7】The first clinical manifestations of the disease appear in child-hood， and renal， cardiac， and cerebrovascular complications usually arise in adulthood. The clinical features of FD are ac-roparesthesia and pain crises， angiokeratomas， gastrointesti-nal symptoms， and corneal dystrophy. In later stages of dis-ease， proteinuria， renal failure， left ventricular hypertrophy， arrhythmias， and stroke develop .

【8】Misdiagnosis of the FD is an important problem. Sometimes it takes years between beginning of the symptoms and correct diagnosis. The Fabry Outcome Survey study showed that the mean time was 14.5 years for men and 16.8 years for wom-en . In another study， the recognition of the underlying diagno-sis was delayed by 14 years in men and 19 years in women . Therefore， it is important to examine the index cases. There are cases in which the clinical indicators of FD overlap with those of some rheumatic disorders， such as familial Mediterranean fe-ver . Retrospective studies found a significant delay in diag-nosis of Fabry disease in ~40% of men and-70% of women .

【9】Phenotypic variability in the same family， in terms of involved organs and severity， was previously defined for M51l muta-tion . It has been defined in 8 Italian patients aged 22-58years. Six patients were female. The proband was a 22-year-old female patient who had been suffering from recurrent fe-ver of unknown origin， burning pain located in the hands and feet， and gastrointestinal disturbances. It took 10 years after the appearance of the first clinical manifestations to diagnose FD. The other female patient had cardiac involvement with dys-pnea and arrhythmias. A 28-year-old man with no enzymatic activity showed serious cerebrovascularinvolvement， although the other patient， a 58-year-old man， was completely asymp-tomatic. One of the daughters of the 58-year-old man had no enzymatic activity. She showed cerebral involvement and was also diagnosed with multiple sclerosis based on the presence of lesions of the corpus callosum on MRI.

【10】This study reports the clinical， biochemical， and molecular char-acterization of 4 members of the same family. The proband was being treated for chronic sclerosing glomerulonephritis for 2 years. Four members of the family showed the exonic p.R301X (c.901 C>T) nonsense GLA gene mutation， which is a disease causing mutation associated with the atypical phe-notype . The p.R301X (c.901 C>T) mutation has pre-viously been reported in families with FD， but here we report the clinical history of a family that highlights a phenotypic vari-ability in terms of involved organs and severity .

【11】Case Report

【12】The proband was a 39-year-old man who was treated for chronic sclerosing glomerulonephritis over 2 years. Recently， he began to complain of fatigue， hypohidrosis， and Raynaud's phenom-enon. His physical examination showed angiokeratoma， grade3/6 systolic murmur on apex， and cornea verticillata. Laboratory evaluation showed hemoglobin 13.9 g/dl， white blood cell count6.73×10/pL， platelet count 1.96x105/pL， erythrocyte sedimen-tation rate 6 mm/h， blood urea nitrogen 51 mg/dL creatinine3.21 mg/dl， 24-h urinary protein 3.3 g/day， and other parame-ters were in the normal ranges. Echocardiography showed left ventricular hypertrophy， mitral regurgitation (grade 1-2/4)，and tricuspid regurgitation (grade 1/4). Electrocardiography was in normal range. At the time of intake his family history was un-remarkable. We evaluated the patient with suspicion of FD. The patient had a pathogenic p.R301X (c.901 C>T) mutation and showed enzymatic activity of o-galactosidase 6.56 nmol/mgh(normal range： 32-60 nmol/mgh)， which was below the nor-mal value. Agalsidase alfa treatment was started.

【13】Genetic and biochemical tests were extended to the proband's family members. These analyses showed that the proband inherited the p.R301X (c.901 C>T) mutation from his moth-er. She was a 63-year-old woman with enzymatic activity of5.8 nmol/mgh (normal range： 32-60 nmol/mgh) and with symptoms not clearly related to FD. She was taking 50 mg/day L-thyroxine for hypothyroidism and 50 mg/day metoprolol for palpitations. Her past medical history showed that she had acroparesthesia and neuropathic pain in her thirties. She be-gan to have cardiac symptoms in the third decade. Physical examination showed blood pressure of 160/90 mmHg， grade2/6 systolic murmur on apex， angiokeratoma， and cornea ver-ticillata.Echocardiography showed significant left ventricular hypertrophy， electrocardiography showed normal sinus rhythm， and 24-h urinary protein was 31 mg/day. There was no neu-rological or renal involvement.

【14】The proband's sister's enzymatic activity was 12.8 nmol/mgh(normal range： 32-60 nmol/mgh). She began to complain of hyperhidrosis， palpitations， and neuropathic pain in her third decade of life. Physical examination showed blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg， grade 2/6 systolic murmur on aorta， angio-keratoma， and cornea verticillata. Echocardiography showed significant left ventricular hypertrophy and mitral regurgita-tion， and 24-h urinary protein was 712 mg/day.

【15】Cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was normal in all patients. Agalsidase alfa treatment were started in the moth-er because of heart involvement， and in the sister for heart and kidney involvement in addition to low enzymatic activity.

【16】The proband's 6-year-old daughter’s genetic test showed that she had the same mutation and her enzymatic activity was in the normal range - 46.20 nmol/mgh(32-60nmol/mgh). She does not have any symptoms associated with FD.

【17】All patients gave written informed consent to participate in this study.

【18】Peripheral blood samples were collected， using EDTA as an an-ticoagu lant， for detection of a-galactosidase A activity and ge-netic analysis. c-Galactosidase A activity was measured by fluo-rometric assay， as described by Blau et al.  in an external laboratory (Duzen Laboratory， Ankara) . Fabry disease was indicated when o-galactosidase A activity in blood was <32nmol/mgh (normal range 32-60 nmol/mg.h). We also performed mutation analysis with an automated sequencing method that screened all 7 exons of GLA. The MiSeg next generation sequenc-ing (NGS) platform (Illumina， San Diego， CA， USA) was used for GLA gene sequencing analysis. The manufacturer's standard procedure was used while extracting genomic DNA using the QIAamp DNA Blood Midi Kit (Qiagen， Hilden， Germany). IGV 2.3(Broad Institute) software was used for visualization of the data.

【20】Discussion

【21】The estimated incidence of FD in the general population is 1in 117 000 . Newborn screening initiatives have found a high prevalence of the disease， as high as 1 in ~3100 new-borns in Italy .

【22】To date，>600 mutations have been described in the exons and introns of the GLA gene， and discrimination between patho-logical and neutral mutations is difficult . Classically， clinical mani-festations are more severe in male hemizygous subjects than in female heterozygotes. Recently， it was found that FD can also severely affect women， but progression of the disease to organ failure generally takes longer and the severity of symp-toms are more variable than in men . For this reason， ac-curate follow-up is required for female patients， independent of enzymatic activity levels.

【23】Misdiagnosis of the FD is common； it takes years (14-19 years) between beginning of the symptoms and correct diagnosis . In our case， the patient was being treated for chronic scleros-ing glomerulonephritis for 2 years， which is a relatively short time. Fabry disease may not be diagnosed until development of end-stage renal failure in patients with proteinuria. The fre-quency of FD was 0.04% (2/5408) in men and 0% (0/3139) in women， and then 0.02% (2/8547) in all patients undergo-ing dialysis in the Japan Fabry Disease Screening Study . In Spain， 3650 samples from hemodialysis patients (18.5% of all patients undergoing hemodialysis in Spain) were tested and 11 new unrelated cases of Fabry disease (4 males and 7females， 0.003%) were diagnosed . The prevalence of FD was detected as 0.17% in Turkish hemodialysis patients .

【24】Although the average presentation age is 6-8 years in males， the proband's symptoms began in his late thirties. His moth-er's and sister’s symptoms also began at about the same age. His 6-year-old daughter does not have symptoms. Suspicion， careful physical examination， and past medical history (includ-ing acroparesthesia， heat and cold intolerance， and hypohidro-sis) are very valuable.

【25】In the M51l mutation， there were reports of cardiac， cerebral， and gastrointestinal involvement， but the kidneys are pro-tected . Another study evaluating intrafamilial phenotypic variability in 4 families (GLA gene mutations； p.R220X， p.C52Y， p.C172Y， p.R342X) with FD showed that renal and cardiac in-volvements， angiokeratoma， and acroparesthesia are common findings . Cerebral involvements are found only in p.C52Y and p.R342X mutations. In our patient's p.R301X mutation， ce-rebral and gastrointestinal involvement were absent.

【26】European renal best practice recommends screening patients for Fabry disease when there is unexplained chronic kidney disease in men younger than 50 years and women of any age. In men， the activity of a-galactosidase A can be measured in plasma， blood cells， or dried blood spots. In women，mutation analysis is necessary， as enzyme measurement alone can miss over one-third of female Fabry patients . Our proband pa-tient was a 39-year-old man who was being treated for chronic sclerosing glomerulonephritis. His sister had renal involvement.

【27】Cardiac symptoms， including left ventricular hypertrophy， ar-rhythmia， angina， and dyspnea， are reported in 40-60% of pa-tients with FD . The prevalence of Fabry disease in primary cardiology practice with strictly defined otherwise unexplained LVH was 4% in males. Systematic screening is recommended in all men older than 30 years with LVH of unknown etiology for FD， even in the absence of obvious extracardiac manifesta-tions . Many characteristics of Fabry disease cardiomyop-athy， with regard to electrocardiography and cardiac imaging， have been claimed. None of the criteria were specific enough(90%) to be used for definitive diagnosis of Fabry disease.

【28】Cerebrovascular manifestations result from multifocal small-vessel involvement and may include thromboses， seizures， paroxysmal hemiplegia， or hemianesthesia. Sensory neurons in spinal ganglia and small myelinated and unmyelinated fi-bers are preferentially affected. As a result of these features and the frequent presence of lesions in MRI scans， FD is of-ten misdiagnosed as multiple sclerosis . Fabry disease may explain~1% of all strokes in young people， including 3-5% of cryptogenic strokes. Early recognition of FD may help to initi-ate appropriate treatment to decrease the risk of subsequent complications .

【29】The European Fabry Working Group consensus recommends enzyme replacement therapy as soon as there are early clini-cal signs of kidney， heart， or brain involvement for classically affected men. Classically affected women and men with non-classical FD should be treated as soon as there are early clin-ical signs of kidney， heart， or brain involvement， while treat-ment may be considered in women with non-classical FD with early clinical signs that are considered to be due to FD .

【30】Conclusions

【31】In conclusion， our findings confirm the intrafamilial phenotyp-ic variability in patients who have the same mutation. In the light of previous studies and results of the present report， it appears that heterozygous women could be affected as se-verely as man and should not be considered as asymptomat-ic carriers. Pedigree analysis remains a powerful， readily avail-able tool to identify individuals at risk for genetic diseases.

【0】ABSTRACT Dental implantology is one of the areas that are growing lately. With the development of new materials， new techniques and possibilities appear to ensure the integrity of the dentomaxillofacial apparatus from a functional and physiognomic point of view in a short time. Immediate loading of the dental implant allows the restoration of function， especially the physiognomic one in a very short time. Purpose： This study aims to report the management of immediate loading in the frontal， maxillary area. The All-on-four concept allows an immediate loading and temporary prosthesis of the patient， regardless of the jaw (upper or lower)， on the same day that the implants were inserted. Immediate loading all on 4-all on six it is a viable and future solution in total edentulous.

【1】KEYWORDS immediate loading， all-on-4， totally edentulous patient

【2】Introduction

【3】Technological advances in the development of new materials and new techniques in implant therapy allow us to obtain excellent results in prosthetic restoration on implants. The final aesthetic result defines success or failure in implant therapy. On the other hand， even if the aesthetic aspect is a priority， we must not neglect the functional aspect.The doctor tends to go beyond the subjective evaluation of the patient who besides aesthetics， is concerned with： phonation， social image， social inhibitions， various disabilities.

【4】The edentulous patient is a case that requires the restoration of functions as soon as possible. If the patient is partially dentate or has inadequate prosthetic work and the therapeutic solution includes extraction of all remaining teeth and removal of inade-quate prosthetic work， the therapeutic solution must come in a for as short a time as possible.  For these reasons， the all on 4/ all on 6 variant with immediate loading is from our point of view a therapeutic solution to consider. In order to obtain good results， however， both the doctor and the technician must under- stand the morphology of the maxillary bones， take into account the alveolar mucosa， to determine together the ideal position of the implant horizontally and vertically. It takes 3-6 months in which the implants are covered by the gums； this period may increase in areas where bone grafts have been performed (e.g. sinus lift) .

【5】Thanks to the Swedish school we know that the long-term success of dental implants can only be achieved if they are os-seointegrated，i.e. if they have direct contact with the bone； as a result， the immediate loading was considered inappropri-ate because it led to the interposition of fibrous tissue between the implant and the bone. Excessive micromovements at the bone-implant interface threaten the stability of the implant and disrupt bone tissue formation， leading to stem cell differentiation into fibroblasts rather than osteoblasts. With the evolution of implantology， the concept of "immediate loading" is gaining ground， and the two surgical stages are replaced with a single surgical stage by using transmucosal components connected to the implant.

【6】Case report

【7】The 65-year-old patient presents with a partially extended eden-tate in the upper jaw， wanting a fixed restoration of the im-plant. Considering the precarious situation of the remaining teeth ， it is decided to extract them and insert 4 implants. The radiological examination highlights a generous bone supply so that the loading is decided immediately after the insertion of the 4 implants. Before extraction， the maxillary prosthesis is used to mark the size of the lower third of the face on the skin. Remove the remaining teeth， insert 4 implants in positions 15，1.2， 2.2 and 2.5. Apply multi-unit-abutments angled over the implants in order for the orifice through which the prosthetic work will be screwed to be located palatine. With a standard tray， an impression is taken by the closed tray method， and an in-dividual tray is made. Position the direct impression abutments with which the screwing direction of the future pros-thetic restoration is checked. The gypsum impression is taken with an open tray ， and implant analogues are applied. Apply on the front implants two titanium abutments which will adapt  so that the patient can close his mouth in a centric relationship； the size of the lower floor of the face was previously recorded. The prosthesis made preopera-tively by erasing the remaining teeth from the gypsum model is perforated at the level of the frontal implants； the prosthesis is applied on the prosthetic field and then in the created holes self-curing acrylate is applied. The respect of the vertical di-mension of the face is verified， the patient closes in maximum intercuspation， and after taking the acrylate， the intermaxillary relations are registered. Then the prosthesis is unscrewed from the 2 front implants  and fixed in the moulded model based on the gypsum appliance with an open tray. The two titanium abutments are applied in the prosthesis for the dis-tal implants ， and then the prosthesis is reinforced with a thin metal band . The final prosthesis is applied in the oral cavity ， and a control radiograph is performed  to verify the correct screwing of the titanium abutments in the multi-unit-abutments. The occlusion is checked both in maxi-mum intercuspation and in lateral movements to eliminate any premature and interfering contact . The patient comes for a daily check-up for a week to check for occlusion.

【8】Discussion

【9】The All-on-four concept allows an immediate loading and tem-porary prosthesis of the patient， regardless of the jaw (upper or lower)， on the same day that the implants were inserted. Implants may or may not be post-extraction. The All-on-four concept involves the insertion of 2 anterior vertical implants and two inclined implants in the distal area， a concept developed by Paulo Malo. Moreover， at the jaw， they will allow the use of long implants， 13-15 mm， which through the bicortical support will ensure a torque of minimum 40 N / cm necessary in immediate loadingJ.

【10】Research has shown that if implants have characteristics that ensure good primary stability， limiting micromovements to 50-150 um， called tolerated movements， in implants，loaded earlier than 3-6 months， as required by the classical protocol， no fibrous tissue appears. However， tissues appear if micromovements occur above the value of 100-150 um， due to insufficient primary stability or excessive load， causing the interposition of fibrous tissue. To obtain primary stability that allows immediate loading， the torque required to remove the implants should be 40-45N / cm. The torque decreases from day 15 to day 21， which corresponds histologically to a maximum of bone resorption.

【11】Stability gradually recovers from day 30 to 45， which histo-logically corresponds to an increase in bone apposition. His-tological and biomechanical evidence shows that peri-implant bone undergoes rapid and intense resorption between 2-4 weeks of functional loading when primary stability decreases until it reaches a critical value. Performing prosthetic work during this period endangers the stability of the implant and may cause failure. If animmediate prosthetic load is made it should be done in the first 2-3 days after implant insertion when the primary sta-bility of the implant is sufficient to oppose the forces that seem to screw/unscrew the prosthetic abutments/prostheses. Stability gradually recovers from day 30 to 45， which from a histological point of view corresponds to an increase in bone apposition. Performing prosthetic work between days 3-30 endangers the stability of the implant and can cause failure.

【12】Experimental studies have shown that the application of axial forces / of different angles on inclined implants causes bend-ing forces and pressure on the bone but which are annihilated by binding to other axially inserted implants. It is inserted in front of the mentonier hole/maxillary sinus， and the implant protrudes from the bone in position PM2. It requires the bone thickness to be 5-6 mm so that the implants have a diameter of4mm. If we do not have this thickness， it must be evaluated whether the reduction in crest height will ensure the desired thickness and bone height between canines： minimum 10 mm at max. and 8 mm at the mandible .

【13】At the level of the jaw， they can be inserted with/without sinus lift. Achieving a sinus lift is beneficial because the in-sertion is done under visual control， and the passage through the sinus cortices will significantly increase the stability of the implant. The inclination towards the occlusal plane is 30-45degrees. However， no higher than 45°. 4 implants are inserted in the jaw， and 6 in the maxillary， with a small number of implants obtaining a passive adaptation of the metal structure， is easier， and so is hygiene. In this case， because of bone availability only for implants were implants： all the implants were 4mm diameter， the length was 13 mm for frontal implants and 15 mm for distal implants (Nobel Biocare@).

【14】The distribution of the implants forms a prosthetic polygon enlarged by the distal inclination； A relative parallelism is re-quired for to obtain a passive adaptation of the prosthetic work：this is achieved by applying on implants multi-unit-abutments of 0 °， 17 ° and 30° angles with different threshold heights de-pending on the thickness of the gum. Identical to this concept with the success rate of other oral rehabilitation on im-plants， 98%. In order to obtain such a success rate， in the oral rehabilitation with four implants of the total edentulous， it is im-portant to take into account： bone quality， length implants， the thickness of the implants. It is very important that the prosthetic work is inserted in the first 48-72 hours and the abutments are tightened with the necessary torq (approx. 15 N / cm) . No intervention is performed on the abutment-implant assembly during the osseointegration period of 6-8 weeks .

【15】The degree of bone atrophy will dictate the fixed / mobile work. The prostheses used in the immediate loading can be made entirely of acrylate or acrylate and a metal structure， with-out requiring scientific data to determine which is better. The prosthesis must rigidly and firmly join the implants and dis-tribute the forces evenly.

【16】Implant failure in immediate loading is caused by prosthetic causes such as： Lack of precision / passive adaptation， occlusal causes， decimation of prosthetic work， prosthesis fracture，longin.

【17】Conclusion

【18】Immediate loading allows the patient to restore in a very short time both masticatory and physiognomic and phonetic function. In the case of all on 4 -all on 6， we may consider therapeutic solution to think the first time when we have a total edentate.

The prosthesis made preopera-tively by erasing the remaining teeth from the gypsum model is perforated at the level of the frontal implants； the prosthesis is applied on the prosthetic field and then in the created holes self-curing acrylate is applied. The respect of the vertical di-mension of the face is verified， the patient closes in maximum intercuspation， and after taking the acrylate， the intermaxillary relations are registered. Then the prosthesis is unscrewed from the 2 front implants  and fixed in the moulded model based on the gypsum appliance with an open tray. The two titanium abutments are applied in the prosthesis for the dis-tal implants ， and then the prosthesis is reinforced with a thin metal band . The final prosthesis is applied in the oral cavity ， and a control radiograph is performed  to verify the correct screwing of the titanium abutments in the multi-unit-abutments. The occlusion is checked both in maxi-mum intercuspation and in lateral movements to eliminate any premature and interfering contact . The patient comes for a daily check-up for a week to check for occlusion.

【8】Discussion

【9】The All-on-four concept allows an immediate loading and tem-porary prosthesis of the patient， regardless of the jaw (upper or lower)， on the same day that the implants were inserted. Implants may or may not be post-extraction. The All-on-four concept involves the insertion of 2 anterior vertical implants and two inclined implants in the distal area， a concept developed by Paulo Malo. Moreover， at the jaw， they will allow the use of long implants， 13-15 mm， which through the bicortical support will ensure a torque of minimum 40 N / cm necessary in immediate loadingJ.

【10】Research has shown that if implants have characteristics that ensure good primary stability， limiting micromovements to 50-150 um， called tolerated movements， in implants，loaded earlier than 3-6 months， as required by the classical protocol， no fibrous tissue appears. However， tissues appear if micromovements occur above the value of 100-150 um， due to insufficient primary stability or excessive load， causing the interposition of fibrous tissue. To obtain primary stability that allows immediate loading， the torque required to remove the implants should be 40-45N / cm. The torque decreases from day 15 to day 21， which corresponds histologically to a maximum of bone resorption.

【11】Stability gradually recovers from day 30 to 45， which histo-logically corresponds to an increase in bone apposition. His-tological and biomechanical evidence shows that peri-implant bone undergoes rapid and intense resorption between 2-4 weeks of functional loading when primary stability decreases until it reaches a critical value. Performing prosthetic work during this period endangers the stability of the implant and may cause failure. If animmediate prosthetic load is made it should be done in the first 2-3 days after implant insertion when the primary sta-bility of the implant is sufficient to oppose the forces that seem to screw/unscrew the prosthetic abutments/prostheses. Stability gradually recovers from day 30 to 45， which from a histological point of view corresponds to an increase in bone apposition. 【13】At the level of the jaw， they can be inserted with/without sinus lift. Achieving a sinus lift is beneficial because the in-sertion is done under visual control， and the passage through the sinus cortices will significantly increase the stability of the implant. The inclination towards the occlusal plane is 30-45degrees. However， no higher than 45°. 4 implants are inserted in the jaw， and 6 in the maxillary， with a small number of implants obtaining a passive adaptation of the metal structure， is easier， and so is hygiene. In this case， because of bone availability only for implants were implants： all the implants were 4mm diameter， the length was 13 mm for frontal implants and 15 mm for distal implants (Nobel Biocare@).

【14】The distribution of the implants forms a prosthetic polygon enlarged by the distal inclination； A relative parallelism is re-quired for to obtain a passive adaptation of the prosthetic work：this is achieved by applying on implants multi-unit-abutments of 0 °， 17 ° and 30° angles with different threshold heights de-pending on the thickness of the gum. Identical to this concept with the success rate of other oral rehabilitation on im-plants， 98%. In order to obtain such a success rate， in the oral rehabilitation with four implants of the total edentulous， it is im-portant to take into account： bone quality， length implants， the thickness of the implants. It is very important that the prosthetic work is inserted in the first 48-72 hours and the abutments are tightened with the necessary torq (approx. 15 N / cm) . No intervention is performed on the abutment-implant assembly during the osseointegration period of 6-8 weeks .

【15】The degree of bone atrophy will dictate the fixed / mobile work. The prostheses used in the immediate loading can be made entirely of acrylate or acrylate and a metal structure， with-out requiring scientific data to determine which is better. The prosthesis must rigidly and firmly join the implants and dis-tribute the forces evenly.

【0】Background：

【1】The prevalence of gingival overgrowth in renal transplant recipients maintained on cyclosporine A remains as essential and still unexplained problem for the patient， physician and periodontist. Clinically significant gingival overgrowth may be associated with inflammation， pain， tooth migration， mastication and cosmetic disorders and it may cause physiological and psychological morbidity. Tacrolimus is a new immunosuppressant， a therapeutic alternative to CsA and has no adverse effect on the gingival tissues.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We reported on a case of five patients after renal transplantation with severe CsA - induced gingival overgrowth and different treatment modalities. Two of them underwent periodontal therapy and surgical treatment - gingivectomy. The next three patients were converted from CsA to tacrolimus. Hygiene instructions to all patients were given. After 2 years in surgery treated patients gingival overgrowth， degree and inflammation level were lower but still present. In patients converted to tacrolimus treatment almost complete regression ofthe gingival overgrowth without surgical intervention were observed.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Both periodontist and patient have an important role to play in improving oral hygiene and gingival health. Cyclosporine-induced gingival overgrowth is effectively ameliorated by conversion from CsA to tacrolimus while surgical intervention provides only temporary remedy.

【6】key words： cyclosporine A · gingival overgrowth·tacrolimus · periodontal treatment·gingivectomy Cyclosporine A (CsA)， a potent immunosuppres-sive agent， has been used for over 25 years to pre-vent organ rejection after allogenic transplantation. It selectively blocks the activation of T helper and cytotoxic lymphocytes by inhibiting production of interleukin-2 and interferon-y. The use of cyclospo-rine is associated with several side effects. Gingival overgrowth (GO) is one of the most frequent and well recognized complication in renal， heart and liver transplant recipients. It occurs in varying de-gree and intensity in 20% to about 80% of patients treated with CsA . The overgrowth begins at the interdental papilla and then affects the entire gingivae and extends coronally growing to a serious problem. It develops always when teeth are present， on all tooth surfaces， more often from the side of oral vestibule than oral cavity. It causes unsightly appearance， pain and discomfort. In some cases the overgrowth can be so severe that interferes with mastication， occlusion， speech and can have psychological implications for affected patients. Gingival disfigurations also restrain patients from keeping their oral cavity in proper hy-gienic state， which results in a grater risk of inflam-mation and caries . Gingival overgrowth can exist in various clinical presentations ranging from non-inflamed， firm and fibrous， to hemorrhagic and inflamed. CsA-induced gingival overgrowth was first reported by Starzl in 1980 and then first described in a dental magazine in year 1983. Since then many further studies have investigated many potential risk factors of CsA- induced gingival overgrowth. But the mechanisms underlying this pathology are still not fully elucidated . It remains unclear why only some patients are susceptible to gingival overgrowth while others are unaffected. Different therapeutic methods such as plaque control， initial periodontal treatment， and surgical treatment (ie. gingivectomy or flap operation) were applied for gingival over-growth.

【7】Tacrolimus (FK506) was introduced as a new immu-nosuppressive agent for use in organ transplants in1987. Tacrolimus is used as an alternative to cyclo-sporine and has demonstrated high clinical efficacy in prevention of graft rejection in solid organ trans plant. Both drugs have similar mechanisms of action， clinical effectiveness but differ slightly in side effects In patients treated with tacrolimus， gingival overgrowth is not observed. A significant reductions of gingival overgrowth in patients after conversion from CsA to tacrolimus without any supplementary surgical procedure were described.

【8】In the presented paper two treatment modalities：conversion of cyclosporine A to tacrolimus， and continued CsA administration together with and surgical treatment and periodontal therapy were compared.

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】The study compares two different treatment thera-pies on clinical improvement and reduction of CsA induced gingival overgrowth. We presented five pa-tients after renal transplantation with severe degree of gingival overgrowth， two women and three men labeled A，B， C， D， E. The patients were 23-57 years old. The transplant procedure was performed between18-99 months before last dental examination. In all of the patients both vertical and a horizontal extension of GO were significant. Clinical characteristic of patients is provided in Table 1. All the patients received CsA together with azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil and corticosteroids. Also concomitantly calcium channel blockers were administered (amlodipine or verapamil)， drugs which can independently induce or/and intensify GO .
