【12】Two patients： A and B - women， developed clinically severe gingival overgrowth connected with severe in-flammation. Both hygiene index-API% and bleeding index -SBI% were high. So that the patients required periodontal treatment. Photographs A1， A2， B1， B2show clinical status of gingival overgrowth. Before treatment appropriate antibiotic prophylaxis was ad-ministered. Scaling， root planning and gingivectomy were performed. Then precise hygiene instructions were given and in the further treatment solution of 0.12%chlorhexidine (Corsodyl or Eludril) mouthrinses or chlorhexidine gel (Parodium or Elgydium) topically applied was prescribed in the maintenance treatment. Surgical treatment was performed in these two patients， at the time when tacrolimus was being introduced in our center， and its impact on gingivae was not clear.

【13】The next three patients - men， C， D and E revealed more severe GO than the women. They had better hygiene， only gentle inflammation of the overgrown gingivae so SBI% and hygiene indices were lower. The gums were hard and fibrous are showed on pho-tographs C1， D1， E1. These patients were switched to tacrolimus treatment， because of late acute renal allograft rejection in 1 patient and hiperlipidemia in1 patient and only because of gingival overgrowth in one patient. These conversions were decided and carried out in accordance with the protocol used by the transplant team. The day after cessation of CsA， tacrolimus was started at dose of 0.075mg/kg b.m. administered twice a day. Trough level of tacrolimus was maintened between 8-10ng/ml. No changes were made to the other immunosupressive drugs. The pa-tients also received instructions and reinforcement to improve oral hygiene by topically using 0.12%chlorhexidine. All the patients continuously received amlodipine or verapamil.

【14】After implementing periodontal therapy in patients A and B significant decrease in all clinical parameters(API% index， SBI% index， GO score) was observed. The photographs B3， B4 and B5 show the status just after periodontal therapy and one month later in patient (woman) B. Patients A and B were subjected to surgical excision of gingivae. Within a short period after surgical treatment the gingival overgrowth be-came more and more apparent. Patient B required repeated surgical excision. After 2 years both in patient A and B gingival overgrowth and gingivitis were still present -as shown on photographs A3 and A4 (patient A) and B6 (patient B). GO scores were， however， lower than before the periodontal treatment， the degree of oral hygiene was insufficient， dental plaque was present in almost all sites. Gingival over-growth caused ailments comparable to those before the surgical treatment.

【15】On photographs C2 and C3 clinical status of gingivae of patient C only 6 months after conversion is pre-sented. At this time the reduction of GO was more advanced in a horizontal than in a vertical extension of GO and the gums were smooth.

【16】In the last two patients converted to tacrolimus treat-ment (named D， E) almost general regression of GO was observed. Photographs D2 and E2 show gingival conditions for patient D and E respectively two years

【17】DISCUSSION

【18】Gingival enlargement in transplantation patients consti-tutes problems and difficulties for dentist， mainly due to unknown complex nature of this pathology and the different risk of complications that might be occur during systemic therapy. Specific cooperation of transplanta-tion team and periodontist is essential. Both periodontist and patient have an important role to play in improving oral hygiene and gingival health. Hygiene training and motivation program should be introduced .

【19】after conversion. Both in sites around anterior and posterior teeth the gingiva achieved a satisfactory morphology. But in some interdental papillae weak anatomic irregularities persisted. The hygiene condi-tion was proper， without any bleeding. The patients also felt almost totally relieved from GO.

【20】The periodontal and surgical therapies were insuffi-cient to reduce CsA -induced gingival overgrowth in the described patients. Surgical procedure remained the only way to ameliorate CsA-induced GO before the tacrolimus era. As a matter of fact this treatment led to an improvement in gingival conditions but pathology was still present. The GO relapsed and required re-peated surgical treatment. Some investigators reported that plaque and gingival inflammation were important determinants for the incidence and development of GO. The degree of oral hygiene has been decidedly in relation to the most severe degree of GO. On the other hand it was concluded， that intensive plaque control.removal of local irritants were of some benefit for the gingival condition， but did not prevent GO in some CsA treated patients . It was also shown that periodontal treatment including gingival curet-tage or gingivectomy has been effective in decreas-ing GO through the elimination of the inflammatory component of the overgrowth . Patients underwent surgical treatment very often showed relapse of GO in different time after operation .

【21】On the contrary to the surgical procedures the conver-sion of CsA based treatment to tacrolimus resulted in gradual and effective decrease in gingival hyperplasia to reach total regression in the presented patients. This resolution was observed 3 months after conversion of Fiqure E2. Patient E： status two years after conversion to tacrolimus treatment.

【22】therapy， despite continued administration of calcium channel blockers， which used concomitantly with CsA intensified gingival overgrowth . Similar results of tacrolimus treatment were presented by other researchers. CsA-induced gingival overgrowth is now recognized as an indication for conversion to tacrolimus. Thus， when it is possible， CsA withdrawal and conversion to tacrolimus treatment in transplant recipients who developed GO should be performed by the transplant team.

【23】CONCLUSIONS

【24】Tacrolimus treatment is an effective and safe way to eliminate gingival overgrowth. Surgical therapy removes gingival hyperplasia only temporarily and does not stop inflammation in described patients. Chronic periodontal inflammation in kidney graft recipients may be a risk factor of cardiovascular disease

【0】Background：

【1】Lichen sclerosus (LS) is a chronic autoimmune dermatosis characterized by white， sclerotic， atrophic plaques. Classic LS commonly occurs in the anogenital region， while extragenital lichen sclerosis typically occurs on the trunk and proximal extremities. Bullous lichen sclerosus is a rare variant that can occur in both genital and extragenital LS. Flaccid bullae can form， which may become hemorrhagic and produce a characteristic appear-ance clinically.

【2】Case Report： In this report， we describe the case of a 63-year-old female patient who presented for evaluation of a rapid-ly growing， erythematous， scaly growth on her back/shoulder that was biopsied and found to be hemorrhagic bullous LS. We will discuss the clinical and histologic features of this case as well as treatment of bullous LS， which in this case was a topical high-potency corticosteroid.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Bullous LS has been poorly studied due to the rarity of the condition， with limited investigation of the clinical and histopathologic characteristics of bullous LS and the available treatment options. Although rare， extragen-ital LS with hemorrhagic bullous features is an important variant of LS that should be considered to ensure ap-propriate diagnosis and treatment.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Administration， Topical ·Blister · Lichen Sclerosus et Atrophicus· Skin Abnormalities Lichen sclerosus (LS) is a chronic autoimmune disorder of un-known etiology characterized by white， sclerotic， atrophic plaques. Classic LS commonly occurs in the anogenital region and can be asymptomatic or present with dryness， pruritis， and pain. Extragenital lichen sclerosis may also occur， com-monly on the back， chest， abdomen， and proximal extremi-ties. Extragenital lesions may present as bullous lichen scle-rosus， a rare variant of LS. Bullous LS has been poorly studied due to the rarity of the condition， with limited investigation of the clinical and histopathologic characteristics of bullous LS and the available treatment options. Apart from a few case reports， there is limited published information regarding this entity and its treatment. We will discuss the clinical and his-tologic features of bullous LS in this case as well as treat-ment of bullous LS.

【6】Case Report

【7】We describe the case of a 63-year-old female patient who pre-sented for evaluation of a rapidly growing， erythematous， min-imally symptomatic， scaly growth on her back/shoulder that erupted 6 months ago and had rapidly grown since. The pa-tient noted occasional pruritis over the site of the lesion but was otherwise asymptomatic. The patient reported no previ-ous trauma to the site and no personal or family history of skin cancer. Her medical history was significant for hypothy-roidism that was well-controlled with levothyroxine.

【8】On physical exam， the patient had an erythematous，scaly， well-demarcated， 4.3x5.1 cm plaque on the right upper back and shoulder . No other lesions were noted on exam. Due to concern for malignancy， a shave biopsy of this thin plaque was performed. The biopsy revealed compact hyperkeratosis， effacement of underlying rete ridge architecture， epidermal at-rophy， and numerous extravasated erythrocytes with super-ficial perivascular lymphocytic inflammation. A subepidermal cleft was noted in the central portion of the lesion with partial homogenization of the underlying dermal collagen . Hemorrhagic bullous lichen sclerosus was diagnosed based on clinical and histological presentation.

【9】Treatment was initiated with betamethasone 0.05% ointment twice daily for 8 weeks. At the follow-up visit， the lesion had markedly improved， with partial resolution of the hemorrhagic blister . Treatment was continued for an additional 4months with betamethasone twice daily， with application for3 weeks followed by a 1-week break. Follow-up at 6 months showed almost complete resolution， with an atrophic white plaque replacing the hemorrhagic blister . At final follow-up at 15 months， the lesion was completely resolved， with only an atrophic white patch remaining with re-pigmen-tation at the edges of the lesion .

【10】Discussion

【11】Lichen sclerosus was first clinically described in 1887 by Hallopeau， with the histopathological features characterized shortly thereafter by Darier . Although numerous studies and guidelines have been published regarding anogenital LS， extra-genital LS remains poorly studied， with few established guide-lines for treatment. Although LS can occur at any age in both sexes， it predominantly occurs in postmenopausal females in the fifth and sixth decades of life. Most LS cases occur in the anogenital region (85-98%)， while the remaining 15-20%occur in extragenital regions， primarily the back， chest， abdomen， and proximal extremities . Unlike anogenital LS， extragenital LS does not have malignant potential. LS lesions may initially be-gin as polygonal， white， elevated papules that eventually prog-ress to plaques that become atrophic and wrinkled . While classic LS often presents with pain and severe pruritis， extra-genital LS is often minimally symptomatic or asymptomatic.

【12】The underlying etiology and pathogenesis of LS has yet to be elucidated， although multiple mechanisms have been impli-cated. The prevailing theory based on current research is that autoimmunity in predisposed individuals leads to the devel-opment of both anogenital and extragenital LS . A study of350 women with LS found that 21.5% had at least 1 autoim-mune disorder at the time of diagnosis， with the most prev-alent disorder being autoimmune thyroiditis . In the same study， 42% of patients with LS had autoimmune antibodies.

【13】Specific antibodies that have emerged in the pathogenesis of LS are IgG1 and IgG2 autoantibodies against extracellular ma-trix protein 1 (ECM1)， a membrane glycoprotein found in the basement membrane.These autoantibodies have been found in 75% of patient with LS. ECM1 interacts with perlecan， a ma-jor proteoglycan in the basement membrane. This interaction shows the important role of ECM1 in the binding of dermal col-lagens and elastic fibers . These autoantibodies are thought to disrupt these interactions， resulting in the dermatopatho-logical findings of LS. The flaccid bullae that develop in bullous LS may be due to an exaggerated response of this mechanism， with the disruption of the basal layer leading to instability of the basement membrane. Another proposed mechanism for the formation of bullae is the development of edema of the papillary dermis secondary to dermal lymphocytic infiltration and inflammation， which interferes with supporting collagen fi-bers and flattens the rete ridges . This combination of base-ment membrane disruption and inflammation results in blis-ter formation with minimal trauma.

【14】Due to the relative rarity of extragenital LS， there are no ran-domized，controlled studies for treatment of LS， and treatment recommendations are mainly based upon prior case reports. First-line treatment consists of topical corticosteroids， com-monly clobetasol propionate 0.05%， a super-potent steroid， once or twice daily for 2 weeks . Topical calcineurin inhibi-tors may be used for both initial treatment and maintenance therapy following initial treatment. A double-blind study com-paring clobetasol and pimecrolimus in patients with vulvar LS found that both effectively decreased inflammation， but clo-betasol was more effective than pimecrolimus .

【15】Extragenital LS is typically less responsive to topical steroids and calcineurin inhibitors compared to anogenital LS， and ad-ditional therapies are often required. Phototherapy has been found to be effective in certain patients， with case reports spe-cifically showing clinical improvement with narrowband UVB， UVA1， and psoralen-UVA (PUVA) .

【16】This case was a unique example of an almost completely hem-orrhagic bullous lichen sclerosus lesion treated effectively with a high-potency topical corticosteroid. Although relatively rare， extragenital LS is an important variant of LS that should be considered to ensure appropriate diagnosis and treatment.

【0】ABSTRACT Background and aim： The International Myeloma Group Uniform response criteria for multiple myeloma mandates the normalization of serum-free light chain ratio (SFLCR) and absence of clonal plasmacytosis to report stringent complete treatment response(sCR). This requirement， in addition to the criteria for clinical response (CR)， implies that SFLCR is a more sensitive indicator of residual disease than serum immunofixation electrophoresis (SIFE). This study aimed to analyze the relationship between SFLCR and SIFE in patients with monoclonal gammopathies. Methodology： This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted in a referral laboratory in India. Records of 716cases of confirmed monoclonal gammopathies， including results of serum protein electrophoresis (SPE)， SIFE and SFLC assay， at various stages of treatment， were analyzed. The reference range for the SFLC ratio x：入 was 0.26-1.65. The results of the SFLC assay were categorized as concordant or discordant with established diagnosis based on correct or incorrect identification， respectively， of the dominant light chain by the k：入 ratio. Results： The percentage of samples with normal SFLCR in the presence of truly positive SIFE (21.5%) was substantially more than those with concordant abnormal SFLCR and negative SIFE(4.88%). The false negative rate of k：入 ratio in the detection of lambda chain lesions (55%) was higher than that for kappa light chain lesions(20%). Conclusion： Normal SFLCR cannot exclude residual disease in monoclonal gammopathies. Results should be interpreted cautiously while assessing response to treatment in such cases.

【1】KEYWORDS Serum free light chain assay， Serum protein electrophoresis， Serum immunofixation electrophoresis， Monoconal gammopathy

【2】Introduction

【3】Monoclonal proteins in monoclonal gammopathies can vary widely in terms of concentration as well as chemical structures. Laboratory testing strategy continues to evolve for quicker and more accurate detection of this heterogenous group of mono-clonal proteins. The International Myeloma Working Group guidelines recommend serum free light chain (SFLC) assay for investigative workup in addition to electrophoretic tests and bone marrow examination . SFLC assay detects and quanti-fies K and 入 free light chains (FLCs) by using antibodies against epitopes normally hidden in the intact immunoglobulin. The normal c：A ratio is 0.26-1.65. An abnormal ratio represents an ex-cess of monoclonal light chains. A major advantage of the SFLC assay is its sensitivity in detecting concentrations of free mon-oclonal light chains as low as <1 mg/L. In contrast， the lowest concentrations of monoclonal protein that serum protein elec-trophoresis (SPEP) and serum immunofixation electrophoresis(SIFE) can detect are 1，000 mg/L and 150 to 500 mg/L，respec-tively . In addition， a serum-based assay also eliminates the need for 24-hour urine collection and variability due to re-nal threshold or renal functions associated with urine-free light chain quantification .

【4】According to the International Myeloma Working Group(IMWG) Uniform Response Criteria for Multiple Myeloma， the K：A ratio must be normal along with absent clonal plasmacyto-sis to document a stringent complete treatment response(sCR). This is in addition to the criteria for clinical response(CR)， which requires negative immunofixation on serum and urine， the disappearance of any soft tissue plasmacytomas and <5%plasma cells in the bone marrow. Including a normal x：A ratio as one of the requirements for sCR suggests that SFLCR is the most sensitive indicator of residual disease and implies that SIFE can be negative for monoclonal protein in the presence of abnormal SFLCR but not vice versa. Therefore， this study seeks to ana-lyze the relationship between SFLCR and SIFE in patients with monoclonal gammopathies.

【5】Materials and Methods

【6】This was a retrospective cross-sectional study conducted in a referral laboratory in India. After excluding samples with biphe-notypic presentations， records of 716 confirmed cases of mono-clonal gammopathies at various stages of treatment with their corresponding SPEP/SIFE and SFLCA results were analysed af ter approval from the institutional review board. SPEP was per-formed by agarose gel electrophoresis using Sebia HYDRASYS2 SCAN FOCUSING system with fractionation into five major fractions： albumin， alpha-1 globulins， alpha-2 globulins， beta globulins and gamma globulins. SIFE was also performed in the Sebia HYDRASYS 2 SCAN FOCUSING system. The pro-teins， separated by electrophoresis on alkaline buffered agarose gels， were incubated with individual antisera. After removing the non-reacted proteins， the immunoprecipitates were stained with acid violet or amido black. The electropherograms were evaluated visually for the presence of specific reactions with the suspect monoclonal proteins. SFLC levels were measured using Freelite assay from The Binding site on the Optilite analyser plat-form. For FLC kappa， the reference range was 3.3-19.4 mg/L； for FLC lambda， it was 5.71-26.3 mg/L； and for FLC ratio(K：A)， it was 0.26-1.65. An established diagnosis of monoclonal gam-mopathy was used as a reference. An abnormal SFLC ratio was considered concordant if the dominant light chain identified by the x：A ratio matched with the diagnosis and discordant if otherwise.

【7】Results

【8】The distribution of cases according to the immunoglobulin type is given in Table 1. IgG kappa was the commonest monoclonal immunoglobulin type observed. Out of 8 observations of non-secretory myelomas， 7 corresponded to kappa chain restriction and 1 corresponded to lambda chain restriction. SIFE identified the original M protein in 625 samples. Table 2 shows the SIFE and SFLC ratio comparison with the total data. A substantial percentage of samples had a normal SFLC ratio in positive SIFE(21.5%). The concordance of SIFE was significantly higher than that of the SFLC (x：入) ratio(P<0.001). Further analysis of SFLC ratio results regarding correct light chain identification revealed that the false negative rate for detection of lambda chain lesions is higher than that for kappa light chain lesions， the two rates being 55% and 20%， respectively.

【9】Discussion

【10】In our study， the percentage of samples with a normal SFLC ratio but positive SIFE was higher than those with a negative SIFE and abnormal SFLC ratio. This corroborates with the observation of Singhal et al.， who had similar findings in their study on pa-tients with secretory IgG and IgA myeloma . They reported a sensitivity and specificity of 66% and 69% respectively for SFLC on evaluation against SIFE. Our data analysis further revealed a high false negative rate of K：入 ratio for lambda chain lesions(55%)， with the corresponding rate for kappa chain lesions being20%. This is in agreement with a previous study by Singh et al.， which also reported the FLC k：入 ratio to be falsely negative in about 27% of the samples having a detectable monoclonal Ig by electrophoretic methods. Furthermore， the false-negative rate was higher for lesions with lambda light chains (31.2%) than those with kappa light chains (23.7%).

【11】FLCs can vary widely regarding the amino acid sequence of epitopes and may not react appropriately with the polyclonal antibodies in the calibrator. As such， the antigenic epitopes pro-duced in an individual patient may not be recognized by the antibodies in the kit . Another cause of falsely low serum FLCs is antigen excess leading to the saturation of all possible binding sites on the detection antibodies . False-negative re-sults with SFLCA can also occur if the monoclonal cells produce only an intact monoclonal Ig without a detectable increase in the monoclonal free light chain.

【12】Lambda chains have a comparatively greater tendency than kappa chains to dimerize， which can block the access of Binding site antibodies to their target epitopes and cause under detec-tion of lambda chain lesions by K：入 ratio. This was investigated by Singh et al.， who compared the results of serum and urine protein electrophoreses with the results of SFLCA. They found that 25% of patients with lambda light chain lesions had a nega-tive serum K：入 ratio in the presence of detectable light chains in urine . Another plausible explanation is that the production of lambda chains is inherently less than kappa chains； as such， much higher concentrations of monoclonal immunoglobulins need to be formed to result in abnormal lambda dominant SFLC ratio . Many previous studies on multiple myeloma patients have found a significantly higher number of cases with kappa light chain dominance as opposed to those with lambda chain dominance . A high false negative rate of K：A ratio for lambda chain lesions can also be due to the overproduction of polyclonal kappa light chains in lambda chain monoclonal gammopathies.

【13】Conclusions

【14】Our data shows that a normal SFLCR cannot be counted as evi-dence for the absence of monoclonal gammopathies. SFLCA is associated with significant limitations due to both assay-related analytical issues as well as intrinsic properties of monoclonal proteins. This should be considered while interpreting the re-ports for response assessment in myeloma patients.

【0】Background：

【1】The eustachian valve is rarely involved in bacterial endocarditis. Patients who present with bacteremia and ev-idence of organic septic emboli should raise the suspicion of endocarditis as a possible differential diagnosis. This case series describes 2 unique cases of eustachian valve endocarditis (EVE) in patients who had a history of intravenous drug use； although 63% of EVE is caused by Staphylococcus aureus， the causative agent in our first case was methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE)， which is only the third reported case of EVE caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis. Of note， the previous 2 cases of MRSE EVE were also found to be associated with cardiovascular hardware.

【2】Case Reports：

【3】The first case of the series describes EVE by MRSE with an endovascular graft acting as the nidus of infection. Second case of EVE was caused by methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus epidermidis (MSSA)， the source of bac-teremia being a rectovesicular abscess.Although initial transthoracic echoes were negative in both cases， sub-sequent transesophageal echoes were able to detect vegetations on the eustachian valves. Treatment includ-ed 4-6 weeks of culture-directed antibiotic therapy for both of our cases.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】EVE may be an under-diagnosed sequelae of staphylococcal bacteremia， especially in the intravenous drug abuse population， further reinforcing the importance of systemically visualizing all cardiac valves， including the eustachian valves， while performing echocardiography

【6】Keywords： Echocardiography·Echocardiography， Transesophageal· Endocarditis · Endocarditis， Bacterial·

【7】Staphylococcus epidermidis

【8】Abbreviations： EVE - eustachian valve endocarditis； MRSE -methicillin-resistant Staphytococcus epidermid- is； MSSA - methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus； IVC -inferior vena cava；RA- right atrium；

【9】TTE - transthoracic echocardiogram； TEE -transesophageal echocardiogram； HCV - hepatitis C virus； BPH - benign prostatic hyperplasia； CRP- C-reactive protein The eustachian valve is located at the junction of the inferi-or vena cava (IVC) and the right atrium (RA) in approximately25% of individuals . On imaging， its appearance is that of an elongated， membranous structure extending from the IC to the border of the fossa ovalis . It is relatively easily vi-sualized on routine transthoracic echocardiogram； however， it is rarely involved in bacterial endocarditis， with only a handful cases reported since it was first described in 1986， which was actually diagnosed at autopsy . The main predisposing fac-tor is intravenous drug use and the most common causative agent is Staphylococcus aureus . Pacemaker wires， history of rheumatic heart disease， and indwelling vascular lines/cathe-ters/devices are important causes as well . Here， we de-scribe recent experience with EVE at our academic medical center， including 1 case of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE) infection， making this only the third report-ed case of EVE to have been caused by S. epidermidis. The first2 cases of MRSE EVE were found to be associated with intra-cardiac hardware .

【10】Case Report

【11】Case 1

【12】A 62-year-old man with past medical history of hypertension， methamphetamine abuse， and aortic dissection s/p endovas-cular graft repair (1 month prior) was admitted due to sudden onset of severe left lower extremity pain. CT angiography of the lower extremities showed popliteal occlusion， for which the patient underwent emergency embolectomy. Of note， he had an acute embolic stroke just 10 days prior， but a trans-thoracic echocardiogram (TTE) had failed to show an embol-ic source at that time.

【13】Initial labs on admission showed leukocytosis and mild throm-bocytosis.EKG showed no new interval changes compared to prior tracings. Initial (and repeat) blood cultures were posi-tive for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis， with high suspicion for involvement of thoracic aorta vascular graft (which was placed 1 month prior). Multiple septic em-boli were thought to explain acute limb ischemia and recent stroke. As such， transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) was pursued given persistent bacteremia and strong suspicion for a cardioembolic origin. TEE showed a large， echogenic， mo-bile mass measuring 1.7x1.3 cm attached to the eustachian valve along the RA wall， consistent with valvular vegetation. It is also possible that this vegetation ad-hered to， and obscured on echocardiogram， an underlying Chiari Network adjacent to the EV， which could be the prima-ry locus of this patient's endocarditis. However， there was no evidence of atrial septal or ventricular septal defect to suggest EV vegetations as a cause of systemic embolism. Subsequent CT chest imaging showed acute intramural thrombus or he-matoma spanning the entire aortic stent graft， possibly due to an endoleak， which was the likely source of thromboembo-lism. The thrombus and vascular graft were likely the source of infection as evidenced by the persistent staphylococcal bacteremia. Similarly， the bacteremia was likely the cause of the EV vegetation due to hematogenous spread as opposed to spontaneous formation of a vegetation on the EV leading to graft infection. The thrombus and vascular graft were also probably infected in the setting of persistent staphylococcal bacteremia. Cardiothoracic surgery did not offer any surgical management in this case given deteriorating overall clinical condition and multiple uncontrolled comorbidities. His subse-quent hospital course was complicated by ventilator-associ-ated pneumonia. Due to inability to achieve source control of infection， namely the endovascular graft， the patient contin ued to deteriorate despite antibiotic therapy. Unfortunately， he died on day 12 of hospitalization.

【14】Case 2

【15】A 57-year-old man with past medical history of HCV infection(on treatment with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir)， rectal prolapse in 2011， intravenous drug abuse， and BPH who presented to the emergency department for rectal bleeding of 2 weeks du-ration. In addition， he had left knee pain and swelling for 10days， to the point where he required crutches to ambulate. He also mentioned burning with micturition and fever for the last 5 days. Of note， he had an indwelling Foley catheter， which was placed 1 month prior to admission due to acute retention deemed secondary to BPH. He failed a voiding tri-al 1 week prior to admission， hence the catheter was not re-moved. Vitals at initial assessment were as follows： blood pres-sure 151/67 mmHg， pulse 105 beats per minute， temperature38.4℃， respiratory rate 18/minute， and an oxygen saturation of 95% on room air. Physical exam findings were grossly un-remarkable apart from trace pitting edema bilaterally. An EKG showed sinus tachycardia with evidence of possible left atrial enlargement with broad， notched P waves. Initial laboratory results showed a WBC count of 12.9x103/mm3， Platelet count625 000 (reference range： 150-328)， ESR-97 mm/hr (reference range： 0-20 mm/hr)， and CRP 21.30 mg/dl (normal <0.8 mg/dl). Urinalysis revealed 121 WBCs/hpf and positive leukocyte es-terase； urine drug screen was negative. X-ray films of the chest and left knee were unremarkable. The next day， urine cultures came back positive for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus au-reus (MRSA) and blood cultures came back positive for methi-cillin-sensitive S.aureus (MSSA). Left knee arthrocentesis was promptly performed and cultures subsequently grew MSSA.

【16】This patient was initially treated with left knee open arthroto-my including irrigation and debridement by Orthopedics； and Cefazolin was started as well. Given MSSA bacteremia， a trans-thoracic echocardiogram (TTE) was ordered to rule out infec-tive endocarditis. No vegetations were visualized but the mi-tral valve was found to be mildly thickened. Five days later， in light of persistent bacteremia and ongoing fevers， the deci-sion was made to obtain a TEE， which revealed a large，echo-genic mobile mass measuring 1.7×1.3 cm attached to the eu-stachian valve along RA wall . This was deemed to be evidence of EVE. To locate a definitive source of MSSA， a CT abdomen/pelvis was ordered， which did show a rectovesicular abscess， measuring 7.2x4.7×8.5 cm in size， with involvement of seminal vesicles and prostate. Subsequent percutaneous drainage was performed by interventional ra-diology and the fluid aspirate culture grew MSSA. Clinically， the rectovesicular abscess was thus deemed to be the prima-ry source of his bacteremia. Blood cultures following drainage of the abscess remained negative. It was recommended that the patient complete a total of 6 weeks of cefazolin therapy from the first day of negative blood cultures. CT surgery did evaluate the patient during hospitalization but decided that there were no indications for surgical management. Hence， he was eventually discharged with medical management. He did well on the 6 weeks of antibiotics without the need for read-mission. He is alive and doing well at this time.

【17】Infective endocarditis refers to bacterial or， rarely， fungal in-fection of the endocardium. The EV， a remnant of the right si-nus venosus valve， located at the junction of the IVC and RA， can rarely become a focus of infection . These 2 cases il-lustrate the importance of orderly evaluation of the EV during echocardiography in all patients with suspected endocarditis， as well as careful evaluation of atrial septal patency due to risk of cerebral and/or systemic embolization from right-sided com-plications. This systematic approach would help prevent miss-ing EVE during routine studies， as recent studies have shown that EV involvement may be more common than previously thought . The literature suggests that both TTE and TEE provide similar information for the diagnosis of EVE； however， more recent literature have suggested that TEE is a more sen-sitive diagnostic tool than TTE with regards to detected EVE， al-though it is generally most practical to start with TTE.

【18】In addition， TEE would be an important diagnostic tool if there is a lack of clinical response to antibiotic therapy to detect possible complications such as abscesses， fistulas， valve per-forations， prolapse， aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm formation， or papillary muscle/chordal rupture. Importantly， TTE is less sensitive for detecting these features of so-called“paraval-vular involvement."

【19】EVE usually follows a benign clinical course， resolving with a4-6-week course of culture-directed antibiotic therapy from first negative cultures. The choice of antibiotics for Staphylococcus epidermidis remain similar to the choice of antibiotics for Staphylococcus aureus， with vancomycin being the preferred treatment for methicillin-resistant (MRSA) strains and penicil-linase-resistant penicillins or“anti-staphylococcal penicillins”such as nafcillin or the first-generation cephalosporin cefazo-lin being the preferred treatment for MSSA. Surgical manage ment is reserved for vegetations that do not resolve with anti-microbials and for hemodynamically compromising vegetations.

【20】Our cases illustrate the importance of thoroughly evaluating the valves， including EV， during echocardiography in all pa-tients with suspected endocarditis or cardiac embolization， as well as careful evaluation of atrial septal patency. This sys-temic approach would help prevent missing EVE during routine studies. Importantly， TEE is a more sensitive tool than TTE to diagnose EVE. Thus， TEE should be considered when right-sid-ed endocarditis is suspected but TTE is negative， especially in the setting of persistent bacteremia， presence of risk factors， or evidence of single or multiple septic emboli. In addition， an ongoing poor clinical response in known cases of endocardi-tis should prompt a TEE to rule out complications such as ab-scesses， fistulas， valve perforations， prolapse， aneurysm/pseu-doaneurysm formation， or papillary muscle/chordal rupture.

【21】Case 1 describes only the third reported case of EVE to have been caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis， with the 2 prior cases having infected intracardiac hardware and this case hav-ing MRSE infection of the vascular graft.

【22】Our case series also highlights the significance of recognizing the risk factors of endocarditis， including eustachian valve en-docarditis. In such instances， it is essential that all valves are interrogated thoroughly in a systematic way， including the eu-stachian valve， especially when there is a high suspicion for infective endocarditis.

【0】ABSTRACT Ebola Viral Haemorrhagic Disease (EVD) is a bio-hazard and a bioterrorism with a global health impact. It is currently one of the public health emergencies which requires a multidisciplinary approach in its diagnosis and management， hence， necessitating an emergency preparedness response. The role of Haematology in the management of EVD cannot be over-emphasized. This is evidenced by the haematological findings in peripheral blood samples of victims of Ebola outbreaks. The key findings which include peripheral blood pancytopenia (severe leucopenia with degenerating neutrophils and atypical lymphocytopenia， severe thrombocytopenia with coagulopathy evidenced by excessive bleeding and anaemia)， depressed cell-mediated immunity (decreased T-cell and CD8+ HLA-DR+ activation)， unresponsive peripheral blood monoclonal cells， high viral antigenaemia and elevation of the serum nitrous oxide levels are evidences of impaired immune system. These findings play key roles in the diagnosis， monitoring， and prognostication of the disease outcomes.

【1】This study was a critical evaluation of EVD and the roles of haematology and immunology in the diagnosis and palliative treatment of the disease.

【2】Introduction

【3】EVD is one of the biohazards of worldwide public health impor-tance terrorizing humankind today. Its outbreaks and sporadic emergences often hit the African continent， especially the sub-Saharan Africa， which happens to be the primary endemic zone. The pathogenesis of Ebola virus infections is largely uncharacter-ized because most outbreaks occur in remote African communi-ties where suspected specimens collection and processing are dif-ficult. Ever since its discovery in 1976， over twenty outbreaks of the disease have been recorded. Apart from the challenging poor social and environmental determinants of health in Africa that account majorly for this disease outbreak， limited access to both diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in both resource-rich and resource-limited countries have a detrimental effect on case ascertainment as well as patient care. These limitations have contributed to delay in diagnosis and in differentiating EVD from other clinically similar disease conditions.

【4】The diagnostic and other laboratory tests play a vital role in confirming and excluding suspected cases， monitoring of disease progression and complications and discharge planning. These help in decision-making that will ultimately separate the con-firmed cases quarantine the suspects； provide optimal care for the patients and judicious allocation of resources. However， the dearth of diagnostic and specialized laboratory tests to track EVD trajectory is a significant challenge in the risk assessment and management. This limitation was responsible for the initial failure to contain the EVD outbreak of West Africa between 2013and 2016， and an outbreak rated as the largest ever recorded in history resulting in substantial global response.

【5】The acronym haemorrhagic' connotes the significance of haematology in the diagnosis and treatment of EVD. The earliest targets of the Ebola virus infection are the blood cells (trilineage blood cells) and the immunological system. This is evidenced by anaemia due to excessive blood loss through the cutaneous region and orifices (i.e，epistaxis， hyperaemia， ear bleeding， etc.)； leukopenia (absolute neutropenia and reactive lymphocytope-nia) and haemorrhagic disorder due to thrombocytopenia， vas-culopathy and coagulopathy. The key immunological dis-orders include depression of cell-mediated immune system ev-idenced by decreased T-cell count， decreased cytotoxic T-cell(CD 8+) and depressed CD8+HLA-DR+ activation. Other im-munological findings include unresponsive peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs)evidenced by reduced expression of cytokines， Fas antigen and Fas ligand of infected and uninfected population， increase viral mRNA load and antigenaemia with increasing severity. This study is a critical appraisal of EVD and the roles of haematology as a non-microbiological approach in diagnosis， monitoring and prognostication of the disease tra-jectory. It also aimed to demystify the term"Haemorrhagic"in the coded name"Ebola Viral Haemorrhagic Disease" by giving insights into the haematological and immunological components which contribute to clinical diagnosis and surveillance of the disease.

【6】Materials and Methods

【7】Published articles on Ebola viral haemorrhagic disease were sought using Medical Study Headings and grouped according to the following categories： epidemiology， a brief history of EVD and the seroepidemiological evidence-based relevance， the roles of Haematology in Diagnosis and Surveillance of EVD and finally the topic discussion. About 34 references related to the research questions were critically reviewed from the search databases from 1990 to 2018. Due Ethical clearance diligence was followed and this was in keeping with guidelines of the Helsinki  and Good Clinical Practice.

【8】Epidemiology

【9】Ebola viral disease is a fatal haemorrhagic illness which has gained public health relevance over the last four decades glob-ally. This infectious disease is unique in its occurrence based on the fact that it is predominantly found in low-income coun-tries of sub-Saharan African region where poor environmental sanitation and poverty are common compared to high-income countries. The first outbreak was in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in 1976， which has recorded a total of ten out-breaks till date The current outbreak in DRC， described by the World Health Organization as the'second-worst ever' outbreak with the high-est confirmed (incidence) cases since the inception of the Ebola outbreak in DRC in 1976. The current outbreak has recorded over four hundred and forty-one  confirmed cases， as well as two hundred and thirty two ， confirmed Ebola-related deaths giving a Case Fatality Rate of 53% as of December 7，2018. The West African outbreak in 2014-2016 was described as the most complex outbreak of the disease (i.e.， a condition described as bioterrorism) since its inception in 1976 with over twenty-eight thousand cases  recorded in six significant countries namely Guinea， Liberia， Sierra Leone， Nigeria， Mali and Senegal.

【10】It is worthy of note the global implication of the West Africa Ebola outbreak. Its outbreak was unprecedented in scale and limitation. About three European countries (Italy and United Kingdom which recorded one confirmed case respectively and Spain which recorded three confirmed cases) and the United States of America (4 confirmed cases) joined among the nations that had the impact of the West African Ebola outbreak . As at March 2015， about twenty-seven thousand， four hundred and one  confirmed cases and ten thou-sand， one hundred of ninety-four  Ebola-related deaths were recorded giving rise to a case fertility rate of 37%. The implication is that two out of every five confirmed cases of Ebola viral fever died in the West African outbreak between2014 and 2016. This case-fatality rate was relatively less than that recorded between 1976 to 2008 in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Gabon， which ranged from 68% to 88% . When comparing the two case fatality rates (i.e.， West African outbreak and that of DR Congo)， it will be easy to con-clude that the current Ebola viral strain in DRC appears to be more virulent than the West African strain of 2014-2016. How-ever， in terms of devastation and invasiveness， the West African outbreak was more devastating and invasive by killing over eleven thousand  people within two years (i.e.，about407 deaths per month compared to approximately 52 deaths per month，p<0.05).

【11】Nigeria， Africa's most populous nation， with a population size of 199，000 000 people， based on recently estimated popula-tion size by the National Population Commission， was not left out in the Ebola epidemic scourge of 2013-2016. About six countries were affected by the West Africa Ebola outbreak ， out of which three countries were significantly affected namely Guinea， Liberia， and Sierra Leone， while the three less significantly affected countries were Nigeria， Mali and Senegal. Nigeria， being a densely populated nation， created a significant concern due to the emergence of Ebola outbreak both at the local and international levels.

【12】However， containment limited the disease outbreak to 20 con-firmed cases and eight fatalities bringing the case fatality rate to about 40%. The Nigerian index case was imported by a United-based businessman who contracted the deadly virus dur-ing a brief stop-over at Monrovia for a funeral of a close relative， who died of Ebola. He flew into Nigeria by the commercial air-line after the refusal of medical advice on quarantine in Liberia. On 20 October 2014， the World Health Organization declared Nigeria Ebola-free； 42 days after a total of 20 individuals were confirmed infected with EBOV， of whom eight died.

【13】The Nigerian scenario of the Ebola outbreak was unique be-cause of the proper documentation of both genetic and contact tracing data. This made complete transmission chain recon-struction possible with detailed clinical information available to the patient. All these factors were responsible for the case ascertainment and containment which ultimately led to the re- duced case fatality rate compared to other severely affected West African countries mentioned earlier . The re-search study design by Folarin et al. was more in keeping with a high evidence-based observational study (probably retro-prospective cohort study) as it has to do with a systematic review of all the measures put in place to ensure proper data collection with minimal bias compared to that by Onyeonoro et al. which was more of a case study， where such details were ab-sent History of EVD andd seroepidemiological evidence-based relevance Ebola virus disease (EVD)， previously known as Ebola haem-orrhagic fever (EHF) is one of the most fatal of the viral haem-orrhagic group of diseases. It is usually severe and often fatal in humans and nonhuman primates such as monkeys，gorillas， and chimpanzees. The first outbreak of EVD was in Yambuku， Zaire in September 1976 (about 42 years ago) involving a nun. A package containing a shiny， blue thermos flask was sent to the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp， Belgium through a Belgian doctor， who was based in Zaire (now the Democratic Republic of Congo). The blood sample was collected from a nun， a missionary from Belgium， who had fallen mysterious illness unknown to the doctor. Peter Piot， a 27-year old scientist and medical school graduate who was training as a microbiol-ogist， was the person who received the sample and when he looked at the microscope， he saw a gigantic-worm like structure resembling one other virus-the Marburg virus. Yambuku was the location of the old Catholic mission hospital where the nun worked. About three hundred deaths were recorded following this outbreak. The viral disease was to be named Yambuku virus but was later changed to Ebola because of fear of stigmatisation in the area. It was later named Ebola which was the name of the nearest river to the area. Ebola viral disease was quoted as a disease of poverty， and dysfunctional health function by Piot on his second visitation to Yambuku in 2014.

【14】EVD is caused by infection with the virus of the family Filoviridae， genus Ebolavirus. It is a filamentous， single-stranded negative-sense RNA virus .

【15】The host cell receptor of Ebola virus entry into the cell is the cholesterol transporter Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Once in-side the cell， the viral RNA polymerase (L Protein) begins to copy the  strand RNA to make (+) strand transcripts that mimic the structure of messenger RNA and are translated by host ribosome. Ebola is known to replicate in reticuloendothelial cells such as the spleen， mononuclear phagocytic cells， endothelial cells， hep-atocytes. Five subspecies of Ebola virus have been identified out of which four have been documented to cause disease inhumans. They include Ebola virus (Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) with case fatality rate of 90%； Sudan virus (Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV) with50% case fatality rate； Tai Forest virus (Tai Forest ebolavirus， also known as Cote dTvoire ebolavirus (TAFV) which was identified in 1994； Bundibugya virus (Bundibugya ebolavirus (BDBV)；and Reston virus (Reston ebolavirus (RESTV) caused by infected cynomolgus monkeys that were imported from Resto， Virginia and Texas， USA. It has the potential of about 82% case fatality rate in non-human primates. In the course of EVD transmis-sion， the natural reservoir host is unknown. However， in Africa， fruit bats， especially， the Hypsignathus monstrous， Epomops franqueti and Myonycteris torquata are the presumed natural hosts for EVD. The migratory fruit bat Eidolon helvum found in Ghana and Nigeria is a potential reservoir of EVD.

【16】While EBOV， BDBV，SUDV and TAFV occur in an animal host which are native to Africa， EBOV， SUDV and BDBV have been associated with most EVD outbreaks in Africa .

【17】The epidemiologic triangle of transmission of the virus is from wildlife to man through contact with infected fruit bat， or via intermediate hosts such as monkey， ape， or pig which got in-fected by contact with fruit bat saliva or faeces.  A man may become infected through contact with infected animal while slaughtering or by consuming blood， milk， raw or undercooked meat of the infected animal. The portal of transmission from person to person is through direct contact with blood， secretions or other bodily fluids of an infected person， or from contact with contaminated sharp object or equipment in the environment. We can classify the direct mode of transmission of the virus in the community via human-to-human transmission， with infection resulting from direct contact (i.e.，broken skin or mucous mem-brane) with the blood， secretions， organs or other bodily fluid of infected people .
