【19】Democratic Republic of Congo

【20】The indirect mode of transmission is through contact with the environment contaminated with such fluids. A typical case scenario is in burial ceremonies in which the mourners have direct contact with the body of the deceased person. Men who have recovered from the disease can transmit the virus through their semen for up to 61 days after recovering from the illness. The presence of Ebola virus in breast milk raises the possibility of direct mother-to-child transmission. The virus can remain in breast milk even after clearance from the blood. The virus is relatively absent in urine and clean environment.

【21】There is a whole lot of difficulty in early detection and confir-mation of Ebola outbreak due to challenges in sample collection and transportation from the suspected Ebola patient. There is apathy in sample collection from suspected patients using inva-sive methods. However， diagnosis can be made using venous blood， oral fluid (which contains saliva and crevicular fluid)， tissue and skin biopsy .

【22】The skin has a low prevalence of the virus. The oral fluid consist of several components such as saliva and crevicular fluid rich in plasma-derived IgG and IgM  A suitable fluid device for collecting oral fluid is OraSure or Epitope.

【23】The role of hematology in diagnosis and surveillance of EVD

【24】Ebola virus is a biosafety level-4 agent and cannot be diagnosed in a clinical diagnostic laboratory， but by using research labora-tories through several types of tests. There are two methods of diagnosis of EVD：

【25】1\. Microbiologic and

【26】2\. Non-microbiologic techniques.

【27】The microbiologic technique uses the current diagnostic algo-rithm for laboratory-confirmed cases and these include：

【28】·Reverse Transcriptase Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR)

【29】·Confirmation by antigen detection Test or

【30】· Detection of IgM antibody in the blood

【31】The use of RT-PCR is a more effective and reliable diagnostic method of detecting Ebola virus in patient serum， plasma and whole blood. It is used in rapid diagnosis of EVD in an outbreak setting and for assessment of the viral load. However， this method is not readily available as it is only found in a few designated research laboratories in resource-limited countries. Samples from suspected patients are sent for confirmation in laboratories which use RT-PCR machines and it takes a long time to get the results.

【32】Other microbiological methods of diagnosis， which could be classified under immunological techniques include the antibody-capture enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA)， antigen detection test， serum neutralization test， electron microscopy and virus isolation by cell culture on vero E6 cells (ATCC CRL-1586) or human embryonic kidney 293 cells (ATCC CRL-1573). The non-microbiological technique of diagnosis， which is a haematological approach includes the use of Wright-stained peripheral blood-film and immunophenotyping of patient lym-phocytes obtained at different stages following the disease on-set. The last two non-microbiological methods of diagnosis are purely haematological. The Wright-stained peripheral blood film at the fatal stage (i.e.， during the acute phase) shows re-duced and dysfunctional platelet from the peripheral blood， a condition known as thrombocytopenia. This is evidenced by bleeding from a venipuncture site， conjunctival bleeding， pe-techiae， ecchymosis， epistaxis， gingival bleeding， gastrointestinal bleeding (i.e.， hematemesis， bloody diarrhoea) and intracranial haemorrhage. This condition accounts for the haemorrhagic (bleeding) disorder of EVD， hence the term，"Ebola viral haem-orrhagic disease." Another key factor that could account for a bleeding disorder is coagulopathy； hence a coagulation profile may show deranged prothrombin time (PT)， prothrombin ratio(PTR)， international normalized ratio (INR) and partial throm-boplastin time (PTT). Although the bleeding disorder mimics that of clinical Disseminated Intravascular Coagulopathy (DIC)， this has not been proven with an evidence-based study. The bleeding disorder marks the terminal phase of EVD.Other haematological findings which will aid in diagnosis include the morphological changes in peripheral blood lymphocytes into plasmacytoid lymphocytes， plasma cells and lymphoblasts； the fragmentation of nuclear lobes of the neutrophils and the for-mation of pseudo-Pelger Huet cells which are neutrophils with dumbbell-shaped bilobed nuclei .

【33】Discussion

【34】The management of EVDremains challenging due to unavailabil-ity of routine laboratory analytics in outbreak settings. However， it is worthy of note that it is associated with a high prevalence of haematological， immunological and biochemical abnormalities， even in mild cases. This study showed that haematolog-ical findings such as thrombocytopenia and bleeding disorder as the most frequent abnormalities in EVD. This was in keep-ing with studies by Hunt et al.  were 45% out of 104confirmed cases were thrombocytopenic. Apart from the thrombocytopenia which is a common finding， EVD presents with other atypical haematological features in peripheral blood of the victims， which could vary from person to person. In a study by Sanchez et al.  peripheral blood pancytopenia(trilineage cytopenia) was a significant haematological finding in the viral haemorrhagic infection， while haemoconcentration(raised haematocrit) and granulocytosis characterized patient population seen by Hunt et al. The striking contribution of Haematology in the diagnosis of EVD was evidenced by the morphological findings of the peripheral blood of Ebola victims：the dysplastic neutrophils (i.e.， pseudo-Pelger Huet cells) and the plasmacytoid lymphocytes could serve as early markers for diagnosis， surveillance and monitoring EVD progression in settings where confirmatory tests may not be readily available.

【35】One of the fundamental roles of every public health specialist， especially the epidemiologist， is to break the transmission chain of the infectious disease to halt the spread of the disease. This strategy is used globally to curb the spread of infectious disease， especially in low-income countries where they are the leading cause of death. Ebola can be defeated with domestic and international collaborative efforts in sub-Saharan Africa using knowledge generated from the surveillance data of the disease in the region. This could be exemplified in the collaborative efforts of the CDC and WHO in curbing the burden or prevention of the Ebola outbreak in West Africa. 

【36】The first public health approach in actualising this is by deal-ing with disparities， inequities and inequalities that create gaps among us. One of the strategies of creating a healthy nation is by dealing with inequities. There should be a collaborative effort by the global community to respond to the Ebola outbreak as a global problem and not an African problem. It is a communi-cable disease and there is no limitation to its spread. The spread of Ebola viral disease to the United States， United Kingdom， Spain and Italy in 2016 was evidence of the global implication of the disease. This has gone a long way to refute the old narrative that 'Ebola Viral Disease'is an African problem.

【37】EVD is a public health emergency and so requires an emer-gency preparedness response， just like other natural disasters， using the ideal health protective tools. A public health protec-tion arm with high-level surveillance and auditing units for EVD must be established in the ministry of health of the“all at-risk countries". This will help in disease tracking and periodic eval-uation of outcomes to improve the quality of management of index cases.

【38】The Nigerian framework for an emergency response to vi-ral haemorrhagic diseases， evidenced by the emergence of the national centre for disease control and prevention (NCDC) is strongly recommendable. The NCDC crafted the local Ebola Emergency Operations Centre (EOC). This centre is made of a response team that co-ordinates Ebola response. The function of this team includes surveillance， case management，infection control， social mobilization， laboratory services and point of entry management and co-ordination. Before an outbreak， the team should establish a functional incidence management system and mobilize resources to facilitate emergency response through the dissemination of National EVD Emergency pre-paredness plan.

【39】The level of hygiene and sanitary practices should be at their peak to ensure complete break in the chain of the epidemiologi-cal transmission. Effort should be made to make the antiviral agent and vaccines available in all the vulnerable areas as part of emergency preparation strategy There is a need for public health enlightenment campaign and engagement of state institu-tions to ensure strong buy-in from all stakeholders. They should also provide technical support to states in term of strategy and technical support to strengthen EVD outbreak preparedness.

【40】The standard infection control precautionary measures must be strictly adhered to. A Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) while the collection of the specimen or handling the suspected or confirmed patient is mandatory. According to WHO， the PPE specification as recommended by Occupational risk department include the NPT3-type facemask， water-tight goggles， triple ni-trile gloves， helmet and impermeable waterproof leg covering. All PPE materials used are single-use and disposed of once re-moved. The government should， as a matter of urgency， consider legislation of control of the sale of potential reservoirs for culinary in market places. This validity of this study could be verified based on its high-level evidence-based multi-centricity which could be the strength of the study， while the small study population size and failure to stratify the haematological find-ings in the various sub-species of Ebola virus could be possible weaknesses. These weaknesses must be addressed holistically in further studies.

【41】In Conclusion， the Ebola outbreak is a public health emer-gency and requires emergency prepared response team to fore-stall future occurrence. It has a significant global implication claiming several lives in low- and high-income countries. It represents a public health disaster of global significance and requires prompt response and management. The environmen-talists， epidemiologists， microbiologists， haematologists， physi-cians and other health care providers have a role to play with regards to its management to mitigate the consequences follow-ing the outbreak. The public health approach towards its con-trol or prevention includes food security， environmental sanita-tion， immunisation， healthcare， reducing the risks of wildlife-to-human transmission， human-to-human transmission and sexual transmission through the adoption of safe sex until the semen tests negative. The role of haematology in diagnosis， prognos- tication and palliative care of the disease complications cannot be over-emphasized. This is even more important in resource-constrained settings where facilities for confirmation of EVD are not readily accessible. It is therefore strongly recommended that all peripheral blood samples which show evidence of thrombo-cytopenia or pancytopenia in suspected patients with bleeding disorders be subiected to a confirmatory test for the viral haem-orrhagic disease.

【0】Background：

【1】Coumadin is the standard oral anticoagulant used in a variety of clinical conditions. Coumadin in-hibits the vitamin-K dependent gamma-carboxylation of coagulation factors II， VII， IX， X and the anticoagulant proteins C and S. Rarely， skin necrosis occurs when the resultant initial procoagu-lant state in the first few days of starting coumadin leads to thrombosis and formation of blood clots tin the dermal capillaries. This in turn causes skin necrosis due to interruption in blood sup-ply to the skin.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We are presenting the case of a 64 year-old female admitted for acute respiratory distress second-ary to newly-diagnosed pulmonary embolism. The patient was started on therapeutic doses of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and coumadin. After 5 days of treatment， the patient started complaining of pain and numbness in both upper extremities. Overnight， this rapidly progressed to manifest hemorrhagic bullae with necrotic areas. This was immediately recognized as coumadin-induced skin necrosis. Coumadin was stopped immediately. Vitamin K was administered and local wound care was provided. Therapeutic LMWH was continued. The skin lesions began to show im-provement after 3 days.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】In coumadin-induced skin necrosis， the patient initially presents with pain and erythema， followed by petechial lesions which progress to become purpuric. Hemorrhagic bullae with necrosis and es-char formation may soon develop. Once it is suspected， coumadin should be stopped and the pa-tient should be given Vitamin K and FFP to reverse the effects of coumadin.

【6】key words： coumadin· skin necrosis · low molecular weight heparin· pulmonary embolism

【7】BACKGROUND

【8】Coumadin is the standard oral anticoagulant used in a vari-ety of clinical conditions. Coumadin inhibits the vitamin-K dependent gamma-carboxylation of coagulation factors II， VII， IX， X and the anticoagulant proteins C and S. Rarely， skin necrosis occurs when the resultant initial procoagulant state in the first few days of starting coumadin leads to throm-bosis and formation of blood clots tin the dermal capillaries. This in turn causes skin necrosis due to interruption in blood supply to the skin. Skin necrosis usually develops with initial large doses of coumadin (>10 mg/day) without bridging with heparin in the initial few days. Early recognition of this com-plication is very important because a delay in the diagnosis may lead to serious complications such as limb amputation.

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】Our patient is a 64 year old Caucasian female with PMH of morbid obesity， obstructive sleep apnea， chronic obstructive pulmonary disease， diabetes， hyperlipidemia and hyperten-sion who was sent to our institution from the nursing home because of acute respiratory distress. At our emergency de-partment， the patient was immediately intubated. ABGs showed respiratory acidosis with a pH of 7.30 and pCO2 of64. A-a gradient was increased at 400. The patient was afe-brile but tachycardic at a rate of 110 beats per minute. CXR showed small bilateral pleural effusions. CBC showed leu-kacytosis of 13.2， normacytic anemia with a hemoglobin of 10.5 mg/dL， and normal platelets. The patient’s blood urea nitrogen and creatinine are within normal limits. Brain natriuretic peptide was only 124， troponin I was 0.01， but D-dimer level was elevated at 2036. Urinalysis wa normal. Initial assessment was respiratory failure secondary to COPD exacerbation and possible health-care associated pneumo-nia. The patient was started on steroids and antibiotics. CT angiography of the chest showed a small filling defect with-in a peripheral left upper lobe vessel. The patient was start-ed on therapeutic doses of enoxaparin. Venous Doppler of both lower extremities were negative for any deep venous thrombosis. On the 3 hospital day， the patient was started on 2.5 mg of coumadin， which was increased to 5 mg on the6 hospital day since the patient’s INR was still subtherapeu-tic. On the 7 hospital day， the patient started complaining of pain and numbness of both hands. Overnight， she devel-oped erythematous and necrotic bullous lesions on the up per extremities . INR was 2.3.

【11】Coumadin-induced skin necrosis was immediately suspect-ed. Coumadin was stopped and hematology consult placed for further evaluation. The patient was given 10 mg of vita-min K， and enoxaparin was continued. Venous and arteri-al imaging of the upper extremities were done. It was nega-tive for any venous thrombosis or arterial insufficiency. The necrotic lesions started improving 3 days after the discon-tinuation of coumadin. Furthermore， the patient was extu-bated on the 11" hospital day and was observed in the gen-eral medical floor for one day before she was transferred to a subacute rehabilitation facility.

【12】DISCUSSION

【13】Coumadin is an oral anticoagulant used in a variety of clin-ical conditions. Its mechanism of action involves the inhi-bition of vitamin K-induced gamma carboxylation of coag-ulation factor II， VII， IX， X and anticeagulant proteins C and S. Skin necrosis is a rare and unpredictable but well recognized complication associated with coumadin use. This typically develops during the first few days of couma-din therapy， and usually with doses >10mg/day. It occurs in0.01% to 0.1% of patients started on coumadin. This devel-ops secondary to the paradoxical transient hypercoagula-ble state produced by the suppression of the activity of the anticoagulant protein C within the first few days of couma-din use. Coumadin inhibits protein C and factor VII stron-ger than the other coagulation factors during its initial stag-es of therapy. This can be attributed to the short half-lives of these two proteins - 1.5 to 6 hours for factor VII and 8hours for protein C. The resultant hypercoagulable state leads to thrombosis and blood clots the in the dermal cap-illaries which causes skin necrosis due to interruption in the blood supply to skin. For this reason coumadin should be overlapped with parenteral anticoagulants for 4-5 days. Protein C deficiency is present in only one third of patients who develop coumadin-induced skin necrosis. Breasts， but-tocks，abdomen， thighs， extremities are common sites of in-volvement because of the large amount of subcutaneous tis-sue in these areas.

【14】Coumadin-induced skin necrosis typically develops in mid-dle-aged， peri-or post-meopausal， obese females treated with coumadin for deep venous thrombosis or pulmonary em-bolism. The patient usually complains of intense pain and paresthesias in the affected areas. Lesions usually begin as an area of erytherma which progresses to form ecchymoses， petechiae and hemorrhagic bullae with necrosis of the skin and subcutaneous tissue.

【15】The common differential diagnosis of coumadin-induced skin necrosis are pyoderma gangrenosum， necrotizing fas-ciitis， cellulitis， ecthyma， and Fournier's gangrene (when lesions occur in the penis).

【16】The initial diagnosis of coumadin-induced skin necrosis is based on clinical grounds. A high index of suspicion is re-quired for diagnosis and intervention. Coumadin should be immediately discontinued once it is suspected. Vitamin K and fresh frozen plasma should be administered to reverse the effects of coumadin. Unfractionated or low molecular weight heparin should be started to prevent further clot-ting and necrosis. Activated protein C use should be also be considered. Proper local wound care with topical anti-biotics and frequent dressing is an important part of treat-ment. Some wounds can heal without surgical intervention， but many patients need surgery for debridement and skin grafting. Early wound care consult， surgery and plastic sur-gery consult should also be obtained as needed. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy should be considered as an important ad-junctive therapy in patients at high risk for developing sig nificant morbidity and mortality. Its use has been detailed in a few case reports.

【17】CONCLUSIONS

【18】In coumadin-induced skin necrosis， the patient initially presents with pain and erythema， followed by petechial le-sions which progress to become purpuric. Hemorrhagic bullae with necrosis and eschar formation may soon devel-op. Once it is suspected， coumadin should be stopped and the patient should be given Vitamin K and FFP to reverse the effects of coumadin.

【0】Background： Lymphatic circulation in the thorax enters the systemic blood flow at the subclavian vein. Instances where diversion occurs leads to complications such as pleural effusion. A rare complication of lymphatic diversion results in fluid accumulation in the bronchial tree， causing plastic bronchitis. The following case is the first ever report of plastic bronchitis presenting with pneumopericardium.

【1】Case Report： A 24-year-old female presented to our Emergency Department with an asthma exacerbation. After initiating bronchodilators， a chest radiograph (CXR) showed extensive subcutaneous emphysema， pneumomediastinum， and pneumothorax with atelectasis of the left lung. Chest tomography supported the CXR findings， as well as a finding of pneumopericardium. A thoracostomy tube was placed and a mediastinal window and pericardial window procedure were performed in an attempt to relieve the pressure upon the collapsed lung. Despite these invasive procedures， there was minimal improvement of lung volume with further respiratory deterioration； the patient eventually required mechanical ventilation. Bronchoscopy was performed， which evacuated a white chalky and rubbery substance that created a mold of the bronchial airways. Following the bronchoscopy， the patient's respiratory status improved， requiring less ventilator support， and that patient was successfully extubated.

【2】Conclusions： This case highlights the most crucial management of a patient presenting with pneumomediastinum， pneumo-thorax， and pneumopericardium due to plastic bronchitis. Plastic bronchitis should be high on the list of dif-ferential diagnoses. The management of plastic bronchitis with bronchoscopy is supported by the fact that no invasive therapy such as thoracostomy tube or mechanical ventilator alleviated the problem， however， bron-choscopy removed the worm-like cast lodged within the lumen of the bronchial tree.

【3】MeSH Keywords： Bronchitis · Bronchoscopy· Pneumopericardium

【4】Lymphatic circulation in the thorax traverses from the lymphatic system to the subclavian vein， returning into systemic circula-tion. Abnormal flow is often retrograde from the thoracic duct to the lung parenchyma . Instances where the drainage is diverted leads to complications such as pleural effusion， or even more rarely， bronchitis within the spectrum of pulmonary lymphatic perfusion syndrome . Patients prone to diversion of lymph fluid are those with congenital cardiac anomalies or pulmonary diseases such as asthma. Plastic bronchitis is a rare disorder in which the lymphatic fluid collects in the bron-chial airway forming a rubbery substance obstructing airflow characterized by large， rigid airway plugs， often more cohe-sive than ordinary mucus plugs . In a large university center， researchers discovered 14 cases in a pool of over 205 000 pa-tients， portraying the rarity of the disease . We present the first ever reported case of plastic bronchitis in a patient who was found to have a pneumopericardium.

【5】Case Report

【6】This is a case of a 24-year-old previously healthy female pre-senting to the hospital with complaints of shortness of breath with neck fullness that acutely worsened prior to arrival. She began feeling ill approximately 1 week prior to her visit， with upper respiratory tract infection with occasional chest tight-ness. In the Emergency Department， a chest radiograph showed extensive pneumomediastinum，pneumothorax， and subcuta-neous emphysema. Follow-up chest tomography confirmed the pneumomediastinum， emphysema， as well as pneumopericar-dium . The patient received a chest tube， and peri-cardial window and mediastinal window procedures. Despite chest tube placement， the left upper and lower lobes remained collapsed. Fiber optic bronchoscopy was performed which re-vealed extensive bilateral mucous plugging with findings de-scribed as plastic worm-like substance following the tracks of the airway mostly in the left upper lobe， left lower lobe， and right upper lobe .

【7】Discussion

【8】Mucosal or alveolar capillary barrier injury causes cast for-mation by protein-rich material， and endobronchial lymph or exudative airway inflammation . These casts were com-posed of material with proteins， mucus， neutrophils， and eo-sinophils depending on the type of group . Type 1 inflam-matory casts consist of fibrin and inflammatory cells such as eosinophils， whereas type 2 acellular casts consist primarily of mucin. Type 2 generally occurs in children with congenital heart disease 8，9J. Type 1 is often associated with an acute

【9】Subcutaneous emphysema； red arrows，

【10】Pneumomediastinum； blue arrow， Pneumopericardium.

【11】presentation versus the chronic or recurrent presentation of type 2 . One case reported in the literature demonstrated plastic bronchitis secondary to silicosis， and the casts consisted of silica laden macrophages .

【12】The management of plastic bronchitis consists largely of me-chanical evacuation of the casts acutely with bronchoscopy and preventing recurrence. A large case series of plastic bron-chitis patients found that extraction via bronchoscopy is the only effective treatment . Prior to extraction， the treatment includes bronchodilators， corticosteroids， mucolytics， and mac-rolide antibiotics . One case report found that steroid treat-ment dissolved the secretions . In cases where clots can-not be mobilized， chest physiotherapy might be an option. Dissolving the clots can be achieved by either inhaled mu-colytic or fibrinolytic agents such as tissue plasminogen ac-tivator (tPA) . Another study utilized thoracic duct stents to prevent abnormal or retrograde flow back to the pulmo-nary circulation . One group found that utilization of com-plete parenteral low-fat nutrition decreased the amount of cast formation .

【13】Conclusions

【14】This case presents a rare cause of dyspnea in a young healthy patient without pre-existing comorbidities， and illustrates the severe complications of plastic bronchitis. In the event a dyspneic patient is found to have extensive pneumomedias-tinum， pneumopericardium， pneumothorax， or subcutaneous emphysema， unexplained by usual causes such as trauma， then plastic bronchitis should be included as a differential di-agnosis. This is especially true if there is no improvement of lobar atelectasis after chest tube insertion. Asthma can cause plastic bronchitis with type 1 cast formation. It is important to distinguish classic asthma exacerbations from exacerba-tions with cast formation as the treatment will vary consid-erably. Although there were many possible treatment options discussed in this case report， patients rarely improve without the extraction of casts by bronchoscopy.

【0】Background：

【1】Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) is a rare disease. Infectious mononucleosis-like symptoms due to Epstein-Barr virus reactivation in adulthood are also rare. Here， we aimed to report a case of Epstein-Barr vi-rus reactivation presenting with relapsing infectious mononucleosis-like symptoms with liver failure in com-mon variable immunodeficiency with chronic hepatitis B virus infection.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 36-year-old Japanese woman with chronic hepatitis B virus infection developed relapsing fever， lymphade-nopathy with marked splenomegaly， and ascites 6 months after treatment with propagermanium， a nonspecif-ic immune modulator， and subsequent treatment with entecavir and pegylated interferon sequential therapy. Although the hepatitis B virus load was controlled， Epstein-Barr virus deoxyribose nucleic acid was detected in her serum. Seven months later， her symptoms improved following corticosteroid treatment. Prior to sequential therapy， she developed pneumonia 4 times in 2 months and exhibited consistent hypoimmunoglobulinemia before corticosteroid treatment. Further examinations showed low amounts of switched memory B cells， and absence or barely detectable levels of isohemagglutinins. Subsequently， she was diagnosed with common vari-able immunodeficiencv.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Epstein-Barr virus reactivation with relapsing infectious mononucleosis-like symptoms can occur following im-mune modulation therapy in patients with common variable immunodeficiency， and this can affect the pa-tient's primary disease. Therefore， immunoglobulin screening along with the consideration of CVID in all pa-tients is required before immune modulation therapy is planned.

【6】Keywords： Common Variable Immunodeficiency·Epstein-Barr Virus Infections · Hepatitis B·Proxigermanium Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is extremely common world-wide， and approximately 90% of adults are infected before 30years of age . Following primary infection， EBV persists for the remainder of an individual's life. It can reactivate under physical and psychological stress and in individuals with a va-riety of autoimmune diseases and cancers . Moreover， re-activation sometimes results in severe or fatal outcomes .

【7】Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) is a primary im-munodeficiency disease characterized by hypogammaglobu-linemia， recurrent infections， and various complications， with a prevalence of 0.001-3.374 per 100 000 population， and the prevalence tends to be higher in countries with a high Human Development Index . It is very rare for patients with CVID to present with relapsing infectious mononucleosis (IM)-like symptoms.

【8】Propagermanium (PG) is an organic germanium that is used to treat chronic hepatitis B in Japan owing to its immune mod-ulatory effects； it can reduce levels of hepatitis B e (HBe) an-tigen， hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribose nucleic acid (DNA) polymerase， and alanine aminotransferase (ALT)， as well as increase the HBe antibody titer . In recent years， attempts have been made to use PG for the treatment of various dis-eases owing to its multiple effects， including anti-inflamma-tory， antitumor， and antiviral effects .

【9】Here， we report a case of relapsing IM-like symptoms associ-ated with liver insufficiency due to the reactivation of EBV af-ter PG treatment in a patient with chronic HBV infection ac-companied by CVID.
