High glucose levels can harm connective tissue by altering extracellular matrix components and affecting how cells operate . MS problems have hitherto received less attention than vascular consequences of DM， which have been the subject of substantial study. This study was done to discover how common MS disorders are among diabetics in Mo-rocco， what causes them， and how they relate to other diabetes complications such as micro-and macrovascular issues.

【8】Methods

【9】This study was carried out for one year at the Bhima Bhoi Medi-cal College & Hospital， Balangir. After agreeing， patients with Type 2 DM were enrolled in this cross-sectional study. The World Health Organization's standards for diagnosing diabetes mellitus， which call for a fasting plasma glucose level of ≥126mg/dL (7.0 mmol/l) ， were used as the eligibility criteria. Patients with a history of hand injuries， central or peripheral nervous system diseases， chronic rheumatic diseases， end-stage renal diseases， and thyroid conditions were disqualified from participating.

【10】All of the study participants' demographic data， including their age， gender， and body mass index (BMI)， were recorded. In addition， clinical information was logged， such as the pa-tient's lipid profiles， haemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) levels， type and duration of diabetes (measured in years)， and anti-diabetic med-ication. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) criteria were also used to define dyslipidemia . According to ADA guide-lines from 2008 ， diabetes was only deemed to be controlled if the haemoglobin A1c level was less than 7%. Retinopathy， nephropathy， and neuropathy are examples of microvascular consequences of diabetes mellitus (DM). There have also been reports of macrovascular complications (coronary artery disease， peripheral arterial disease， and history of stroke).

【11】We obtained descriptive statistics， such as proportions for categorical variables and mean values for continuous variables. The Chi-square test was used to determine whether the relation-ship between the prevalence of MS problems and various factors was statistically significant. In order to evaluate the multivari-ate connections between MS problems and various variables， a multiple logistic regression analysis was performed. Statistical significance was defined as a p-value of 0.05. The Statistical Package for Social Sciences was used to conduct the statistical analysis .

【13】308 people with diabetes mellitus participated in the study. 53IPa years， 44 to 63 years old was the patients' median age. In ad-dition， 46 percent of the population were men， and 54 percent were women.

【15】Retinopathy， nephropathy， and neuropathy together ac-counted for 28%，16%， and 12% of these patients. There were14 patients (4.5%) with DM macrovascular problems (coronary artery disease， peripheral arterial disease， and history of stroke). Additionally， while three diseases in the same patient were un-common， one disorder was observed in 25.8% of patients and two disorders in 5.1% of patients， respectively (3.5 percent). The prevalence rates according to demographic and clinical charac-teristics of patients are shown in Table 2.

【16】Age over 50 and dyslipidemia were the only variables in the multivariate analysis that were substantially linked to an increased prevalence of one or more MS diseases. Age above50 was a risk factor for both SC and OA. Additionally， a longer diabetes history seems to increase the risk. Patients with diabetes for more than ten years were more likely to suffer hand problems. OA was more prevalent in women. Nephropathy and being overweight appeared to be strongly linked to OA. Dyslipidemia was substantially linked to a higher risk of SC and hand diseases.

【17】Discussion

【18】Numerous research has evaluated MS problems in diabetic pa-tients. In the past， research mostly evaluated specific elements， primarily anomalies in the upper limb in MS. Furthermore， the connection between MS problems and dyslipidemia has been disregarded. However the current study looked at a number of variables， including vascular problems and dyslipidemia， that are linked to an increased prevalence of MS diseases in Type 1DM and Type 2 DM.

【19】This study found three significant results. Second， the onset of various MS symptoms was substantially correlated with age above 50 and dyslipidemia. Thirdly， no association between haemoglobin A1c level and musculoskeletal problems was discovered.

Over one-third of the enrolled patients had one or more mus-culoskeletal problems. Several earlier investigations have found a prevalence of between 36 and 75 percent of diabetes individ-uals . The inclusion of both type 1 and type 2 DM may have contributed to the lower prevalence of MS complications in the current study. Age over 50 and dyslipidemia were dis-covered to be related to musculoskeletal diseases in the current investigation. which is consistent with earlier investigations.|14.151

In 15.3 percent of cases，shoulder capsulitis was found. An higher prevalence of hand deformities Sa was linked to long-term diabetes and dyslipidemia. Accord-ing to earlier reports， the occurrence varied between 26 and 64percent 16，171.

Higher levels of diabetic complications occur when diabetes is poorly controlled. Certain rheumatic disorders may get worse as a result of poor glycemic control. Diabetes manage-ment should be based on pharmacotherapy， food， and a regular， suitable physiotherapy programme. In order to decrease the frequency and severity of complications， we advise all diabetic patients to include an appropriate exercise regimen in their dia-betes management， under the supervision of their doctor.

source_info.text:
【0】Background：

【1】Phosphorous is an essential component of cell structure and physiology， and is required for energy conserva-tion and expenditure. Severe hypophosphatemia can lead to profound dysfunction and injury affecting most organs and can be life-threatening. It can also compromise weaning of mechanically ventilated patients. Long-term assisted ventilatory care in ambulatory or inpatient settings is an expanding medical service for patients with various forms of persistent or progressive incapacitating diseases. Hypophosphatemia， caused by respi-ratory alkalosis， has been reported in critical-care settings， but its occurrence in medically stable patients re-quiring long-term respiratory support has not been thoroughly investigated.

【2】Case Report： We report the case of a ventilated patient in a chronic vegetative state displaying progressive hypophospha-temia spanning over 3 months， with plasma levels gradually declining to 0.8 mg/dL Evaluation did not reveal conditions leading to diminished phosphate absorption or enhanced urinary phosphate excretion， but it iden-tified respiratory alkalosis related to a recent increase in target minute-volume ventilation in the adaptive sup-port ventilation (ASV) mode as the cause of hypophosphatemia. Despite the very low plasma phosphate level， the patient was asymptomatic， probably because this type of hypophosphatemia may not represent physio-logically significant intracellular phosphate depletion. The respiratory alkalosis resolved upon decreasing the target minute-volume ventilation settings， and serum phosphate was normalized.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Since blood gases are not routinely monitored in respiratory and hemodynamically stable patients on long term respiratory support， hypophosphatemia may herald the development of significant respiratory alkalosis. Assessment of acid-base balance is thus warranted in patients receiving long-term ventilation， especially in those developing hypophosphatemia.

【5】Keywords： Alkalosis， Respiratory· Hypophosphatemia ·Respiration， Artificial

【6】Phosphorous is an essential component of cell structure， phys-iology， and is required for energy conservation and expendi-ture. Severe hypophosphatemia can be life-threatening，lead-ing to profound dysfunction and injury affecting most organs. Central nervous system derangement， cardiac failure，rhabdo myolysis， and hemolysis are only a few examples of the poten-tially devastating sequelae of severe hypophosphatemia .

【7】The average total body phosphorous content in adults is about700 g， the majority of which is incorporated in the skeletal hy-droxyapatite matrix， while only about 10% plays a role in or-gan physiology， mostly as a principal intracellular phosphate ion (PO -). Normal extracellular and serum phosphate concen-tration of 2.5-4.5 mg/dl (0.80-1.45 mmol/l) largely reflects the balance between intestinal absorption and renal excretion of phosphate. To a lesser extent， release of phosphate from bone and deposition during bone turnover also contributes to se-rum phosphate concentration. Compound interacting mech-anisms govern these physiological processes， including vita-min D metabolites， parathyroid hormone \[PTH\]， and fibroblast growth factor \[FGF\]23 .

【8】Long-term assisted ventilatory care in ambulatory or inpatient settings is an expanding medical service for patients with var-ious forms of persistent or progressive incapacitating diseas-es， and for some patients needing a protracted rehabilitating and weaning process ， many of them recently associated with COVID-19 disease . We have operated a long-term as-sisted ventilatory care division for 21 years，and currently are treating over 200 inpatients in 6 units， with an age range of3 months to 100 years. Adaptive support ventilation (ASV) is a highly convenient mode of respiratory support for patients requiring long-term assisted ventilatory care ， and about80% of our adult patients (>18 years old) are presently treated with this mode of ventilation (Hamilton Medical AG， Rhaziins， Switzerland). This technology provides a closed-loop controlled ventilator mode， designed to decrease patients'work of breath-ing. It requires the determination of the patient’s ideal body weight (IBW)， extrapolated from height and gender. The level of required support is defined by the healthcare team， where100% support is IBWx100 ml minute ventilation. A sophisticat-ed algorithm calculates the tidal volume and respiratory rate and the pressure support/control to achieve minimal work of breathing， taking into account the respiratory mechanics data from the ventilator monitoring system (resistance (R)， compli-ance (C)， time constant (RxC)， auto-PEEP).

【9】Based on our clinical judgment and goals regarding weaning， once the patients are medically stabilized， particularly regard-ing their hemodynamic and respiratory status， we do not rou-tinely assess their acid-base status， but instead monitor their ventilation status principally by their oxygen saturation by a pulse-oximeter and end-tidal CO， using a capnograph.

【10】Hypophosphatemia caused by respiratory alkalosis has been reported in critical-care settings ， but its occurrence in sta-ble patients requiring long-term respiratory support has not been thoroughly investigated. Herein we report the unusual presentation of severe progressive hypophosphatemia as the sole manifestation of concealed respiratory alkalosis in a pa-tient in a chronic vegetative state ventilated using the ASV ventilator mode.

【11】Case Report

【12】A 53-year-old female patient suffering from advanced pro-gressive multiple sclerosis reached a vegetative state and had been treated in our long-term assisted ventilatory care facili-ties for over 5 years with the use of the ASV mode (Hamilton C1 ventilator). Other medical problems included an episode of Guillain-Barre syndrome，epilepsy， obesity， hypothyroidism， and non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus. She has been treat-ed with levothyroxine， prednisone， metformin， glargine insu-lin， duloxetine， apixaban， levetiracetam， as well as a canna-binoid preparation (for spasticity) and a calcium-vitamin D3preparation. She was enterally fed with EasyDaily 810 ml/day(Supplying 685 mg phosphorus/day； EasyLine， Caesarea， Israel). Hypophosphatemia was first noted in January 2021， and it gradually intensified over 110 days， reaching levels as low as0.8 mg/dL . However， her medical condition and rou-tine laboratory results remained stable， with the exception of a modest increase in total plasma Ca+ levels. Initial evalua-tion revealed vitamin D3 levels of 83.9 ng/mL (target range75-125 ng/mL)， and depressed parathyroid hormone (PTH)，10.5 pg/mL (normal range 18-80 pg/mL). Urinary 24-h phos-phate excretion was 15 mg/24 h (normal >400 mg/24 h) de spite the administration of phosphate supplements. Finally， blood gases revealed marked respiratory alkalosis with a pH7.50， pCO， 24 mmHg po， 94 mmHg， 0， saturation 98%， and HCO， 18.7 mmol/L.

【13】In retrospect， due to declining pressure support below 10 cmH，0and to decrease the work of breathing in the patient， who was not a candidate for weaning from the ventilator， her ASV pa-rameters were adjusted before the substantial decline of se-rum phosphorus level . Parameters were moved from70% support with a target minute-volume ventilation (MW) of4.3 L/min， to 90% support with a target MW of 5.5 L/min. The target MW was reduced accordingly， resulting in a normalized acid-base balance and transient hyperphosphatemia，which ter-minated upon cessation of phosphate supplements . Three weeks later， her phosphate level was 4.6 mg/dL， with a pH of 7.38， pCO， 34 mmHg and bicarbonate 20.7 meq/L

【14】Discussion

【15】Acquired hypophosphatemia is principally caused by altered phosphate absorption (for instance during malabsorption， vita-min D deficiency， or with the ingestion of phosphate-binders)， or by enhanced phosphaturia (most often caused by hyperpara-thyroidism， and rarely by malignancy-related enhanced levels of FGF23) . Intracellular translocation of phosphate is an ad-ditional often overlooked cause of reduced plasma phosphate levels . It may result from enhanced cellular consumption of phosphate， as happens during refeeding of malnourished patients. Phosphate redistribution with intracellular translo-cation of phosphate may also be triggered by alkalosis， as it activates phosphofructokinase and increases consumption of phosphorous for glycolysis and downstream formation of gly-colytic intermediate metabolites . Indeed， respiratory alkalosis is the most common cause of hypophosphatemia in hospitalized patients ， with a more modest， yet significant effect of metabolic alkalosis. Hyperventilation associated with panic disorders has been documented to cause hypophospha-temia ， and low plasma phosphate has been proposed as a clue suggesting this condition . Hypophosphatemia also accompanies other conditions characterized by intense work of breathing such as sepsis or recovery from ketoacido-sis， but causative mechanisms other than alkalosis may be in-volved as well . Hypophosphatemia is also found in mechan-ically ventilated patients with diminished work of breathing. Srinivasagam et al  reported that hypophosphatemia de-veloped within 24-36 h in 43% of acutely ventilated patients in a critical care unit， resolving upon discontinuation of ven-tilation. They also detected inappropriate phosphaturia while PTH levels were unaltered， suggesting a phosphaturic impact of respiratory alkalosis unrelated to PTH. This is in contrast with observations by Krapf et al ， who found that chron-ic respiratory alkalosis leads to renal PTH resistance， inhibit-ing phosphaturia and potentially generating hyperphospha-temia. Laaban et al  reported hypophosphatemia upon initiation of ventilation in 14 acutely ventilated patients with COPD， and also found a decline in urine phosphate in 2 of those patients. In another study， Watt and Silva  evalu-ated blood gases and electrolytes in 30 long-term ventilated tetraplegic patients (duration of ventilation ranging from 1 to30 years). They found that these patients were mildly hyper-ventilated (mean pH7.46). However， their average phosphate levels were within the normal range， and some had values below the 95% CI of a control group of tetraplegic self-ven-tilated patients. However， to the best of our knowledge， ad-ditional systematic assessment of phosphate balance among patients requiring long-term assisted ventilatory care has not been studied. Our patient presented with profound hypophos-phatemia. Although blood gases and pH were not determined prior to reaching the critically low phosphate levels， it is likely that iatrogenic hyperventilation already took place during the initial days of decline in serum phosphorus levels， with fur-ther exacerbation upon adjustment of the ventilator respira-tory parameters .

【16】The clinical significance of chronic hypophosphatemia related to respiratory alkalosis and intracellular phosphorous trans-location remains speculative. This type of hypophosphatemia most likely does not represent physiologically significant in-tracellular phosphate depletion. The clinical outcome of our patient supports this notion， as throughout the protracted pe-riod of severe hypophosphatemia there were no clinical or lab-oratory features indicating organ or tissue damage， such as cardiomyopathy，rhabdomyolysis， or hemolysis. Her vegetative state precluded the assessment of neurologic deterioration. However， concerns remain regarding decreased respiratory muscle strength caused by hypophosphatemia， particularly throughout scheduled disconnection and weaning from the respirator ， as currently practiced in our institution in con-valescing COVID-19 patients .

【17】Conclusions

【18】The current report calls into question our routine of not peri-odically monitoring blood gases， without which we are likely to overlook chronic respiratory alkalosis in patients on long-term assisted ventilatory care， which can lead to protracted hypophosphatemia. The central message of this case report is that the assessment of acid-base balance in such patients is indispensable even though their overall medical condition appears to be stable， especially when changing the setting of the ventilator. Hypophosphatemia might be an early indica-tor of evolving hyperventilation， and should particularly initi-ate prompt determination of blood gases.

【1】CIC-rearranged sarcoma (CRS) is a recently described subset of undifferentiated small-round-cell sarcomas of bone and soft tissue. DUX4 is the most common gene involved in CRS. Malignant cardiac effusion with subsequent cardiac tamponade is an oncologic emergent con-dition. 【12】response was stable disease for 8 months， after which lymph node metastases progressed. 【14】CRS is a recently recognized， genetically defined subtype of undifferentiated round-cell sarcoma that morphologically re-sembles the Ewing sarcoma family of tumors . However， un-like Ewing sarcoma， CRS arises mostly in deep or superficial soft tissue and rarely in flat bone . In our case， we were un-able to determine whether the left humerus was the prima-ry site of the tumor， even though the osteolytic lesion in the left humerus was the largest of the multiple lesions at the pa-tient's first visit.

【15】patient received a course of palliative radiotherapy to the left humerus， and his pain was immediately relieved. X-ray exami-nation showed bone formation after the irradiation. In addition to the radiotherapy， the patient was treated for advanced pri-mary bone sarcoma with the same palliative chemotherapeu-tic regimen that would be used in Ewing sarcoma. His clinical The patient in this case exhibited disease progression that was unlike that of more common sarcomas. In particular， cardiac tamponade caused by sarcoma is extremely rare， and there are no reported cases of CRS causing pericardial effusion. In the few reported cases of cardiac tamponade in sarcoma patients， it was caused by pericardial extension  or direct cardiac wall invasion . In the present case， we speculate that pericardial effusion may have arisen due to impaired lymphatic drainage secondary to lymphomatous involvement of the mediasti-nal lymph nodes， as seen in other advanced small-round-cell neoplasms in which lymph node metastasis is common， such as lung cancer， malignant melanoma， and malignant lympho-ma. Although previous reports showed that the frequency of lymph node metastasis in malignant soft tissue tumors was less than 5%， a higher incidence was observed in some sarco-ma subtypes ， including the newly recognized CRS subtype.

【16】CRS is considered to be a very aggressive tumor. In a review of 115 cases of CRS， Antonescu et al reported a 2-year over-all survival (OS) rate of 53% and a 5-year OS rate of 43%. These patients received multimodal treatment， including sur-gery， chemotherapy， and radiation， as is commonly applied in other small-round-cell sarcomas， such as Ewing sarcoma， but the response rates to these treatments were inferior compared with those of other round-cell sarcomas. In our case， irradia-tion effectively relieved pain caused by the humeral lesion. In addition， mediastinal irradiation successfully controlled the pericardial effusion until the end stage of the disease.

【17】Because CRS is a recently recognized sarcoma， the optimal treatment strategy in advanced CRS is still unclear. Radiation therapy may be useful for disease control， a possibility that warrants further investigation. Our case suggests that the progression pattern of CRS is very different from that of oth-er conventional sarcomas， which should be taken into consid-eration when choosing treatments.

【18】Conclusions

【19】This is the first case report of CRS causing cardiac tamponade as the initial symptom. Cardiac tamponade is a rare present-ing feature of sarcoma and may be misleading. Physicians and pathologists should include CRS in the differential diagnosis if the pericardial fluid in the context of cardiac tamponade con-tains atypical small-round cells.

【0】Background：

【1】Desmoid tumor (DT)， also known as aggressive fibromatosis or desmoid-type fibromatosis， is a rare disease. It can occur in anyone at any age， and is more likely to appear in female patients. DTs are sometimes associ-ated with familial adenomatous polyposis and rare syndromes such as Gardner syndrome. Arising from spe-cific cells， fibroblasts， they tend to develop in patients with a history of abdominal surgery and rarely produce metastases.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We present a case of a 41-year-old man who was referred for abdominal discomfort with no digestive or gen-eral symptoms. An abdominal CT scan revealed a mass in the left hypochondrium， corresponding to an in-traperitoneal tumor extending to left colon. Based on MRl， we suspected a gastrointestinal stromal tumor. Colonoscopy showed no intraluminal tumor in the colon. A PET-CT scan revealed tumor hypermetabolism and no metastases. The mass was diagnosed as a DT after percutaneous biopsy. Six weeks after diagnosis and as the tumor continued increasing despite pharmacological treatment， the patient underwent surgical pancreatic tail resection with splenectomy and left colonic segmentectomy. Histological examination revealed a 7.047-g DT with severe infiltration of pancreatic parenchyma and transmural colic barrier， with no high-grade differen-tiation and negative resection margins. The postoperative recovery was uneventful， and we proposed surveil-lance with MRI.

【4】Conclusions： The DT was surgically removed and patient remains under MRI surveillance. Other reported management ap-proaches consist of radiotherapy， tyrosine kinase inhibitors，anti-hormonal therapies/non-steroidal anti-inflam-matory drugs， chemotherapy， or close surveillance only. This is， to our knowledge， the largest and heaviest DT reported in the modern literature.

【5】Keywords： Colorectal Surgery·CTNNB1 Protein， Human · Fibromatosis， Aggressive·Gardner Syndrome·Radiotherapy

【6】Abbreviations： DT - desmoid tumor； CT scan-computed tomography scan； FAP - familial adenomatous polyposis；

【7】NSAID-non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug； ECOG PS - Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status Desmoid tumors (DTs) are rare tumors which develop from the connective tissue： well-differentiated mesenchymal fi-broblasts or myofibroblasts. DTs represent<3% of all soft tissue tumors and have an estimated incidence of 2-4 new cases per million population per year . Also known as ag gressive fibromatosis or desmoid-type fibromatosis， DTs are benign tumors which can develop anywhere in the body， in-vade surrounding tissues， and can be very difficult to con-trol because of their rapid growth. McFarlane was the first to describe a DT， which was located in the abdominal wall of a young patient in 1832 . The WHO classifies DTs as intermediate (locally aggressive) fibroblastic and myofibro-blastic tumors .

【8】DTs can localize intra- or extra-abdominally， mostly in the ab-dominal wall， and there is no evidence of their metastatic po-tential. DTs typically affect young adults between 20 and 30years of age . The clinical presentation of DTs ranges from fully asymptomatic to swelling， left hypochondrium pain，epi-gastric pain， nausea， vomiting， and back pain. The etiology of these tumors is not well understood and they have 2 typical presentations： sporadic， mostly associated with post-traumat-ic (postoperative) etiology  or associated with Gardner syn-drome， a subtype of familial adenomatosis polyposis (FAP).FAP develops in patients with mutations in the APC gene ； 20%of these APC mutations are de novo . In some rare cases， DTs are associated with the peripartum period.

【9】Specific factors have been identified as abnormalities in his-tological analysis showing fibroblastic proliferation and then confirmed by immunohistochemical staining for B-catenin， as the B-catenin gene (CTNNB1)， present in more than 75% of DTs cases， is mutated in FAP or Gardner syndrome .

【10】There is no standard of care for DTs， but the first-line pharma-cotherapy consists of selective estrogen receptor modulators such as Tamoxifen or Toremifene and non-steroidal anti-in-flammatory drugs (NSAID) as well as cytotoxic chemotherapy and sometimes radiotherapy . Treatment with oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor drugs such as Imatinib or Sorafenib has shown promising results . An emerging technique uses high-in-tensity ultrasound waves to remove small DTs. This non-inva-sive approach can be combined with other treatments 9，10.

【11】However， in the vast majority of symptomatic cases， surgery plays a major role in the treatment of DTs. In 25-60% of pa-tients who undergo surgery， DTs recur locally ， most fre-quently near the surgical resection. It is well accepted that the aim of surgery is to remove the entire tumor with RO re-section margins and minimize the risk of recurrence. Based on data from 495 patients with DTs， physicians at Memorial

【12】We report the largest case of pancreatic DT， diagnosed on22 November 2021， at the Geneva University Hospitals， Switzerland. The DT was removed surgically with negative re-section margins. We expand this case report with a literature review on DTs of the pancreas.

【13】The work has been reported in line with the SCARE 2020 criteria：Updating Consensus Surgical CAse REport (SCARE) Guidelines， International Journal of Surgery 2020；84：226-230.

【14】Case Report

【15】A 41-year-old male patient with no significant medical or sur-gical history apart from an asymptomatic megaureter and a bicuspid aortic valve presented to his family physician with nausea and diarrhea persisting for 1 week， 3 months prior to our consultation. He was prescribed simple symptomatic man-agement. Because of the persisting abdominal discomfort and postprandial nauseas， the patient was referred to the Division of Digestive Surgery of the University Hospitals of Geneva. We noted a visible bulking in the epigastric and left hypochondri-ac region. The mass was easily palpable and solid， without any signs of abdominal guarding. The patient was in good condition， height 178 cm， weight 77 kg， and ECOG PS 0. He reported no active smoking or alcohol consumption， no aller-gies， and no regular medication. The patient had no person-al or family history of desmoid tumor. The first abdominal CT scan  showed a massive intra-abdominal heteroge-neous tissue tumor located in the left hypochondrium and in-vading the left colon. We also observed a moderate amount of intra-abdominal free fluid and suspected the tumor to be a gastrointestinal stromal tumor. We then performed an MRI， which revealed that the left hypochondrium mass was mildly heterogeneous with T2 hypersignal and T1 hyposig-nal of unclear origin， with restricted diffusion， mild enhance-ment after contrast injection， and encapsulated， and was merg-ing with the tail of the pancreas and compressing the left colic flexure. Colonoscopy was normal apart from a severe extrinsic compression localized in the left colic flexure. To explore the potential malignancy and metastases of the tumor， a whole-body PET/CT scan was performed . It revealed a hy-permetabolic tumor of more than 20 cm extending from the left pancreas and invading the left colic flexure， and no other suspect hypermetabolic lesions. Histological and immunohis-tochemical images of a percutaneous biopsy were compati-ble with an active DT.

【16】The case was presented to our multidisciplinary care team， who opted for a conservative initial management with sulin-dac (NSAID) and close surveillance. One month after this de-cision， the patient presented with an increased abdominal cir-cumference and alternating diarrhea and constipation. A new MRI showed that the tumor had rapidly grown from 7 to more than 18 cm ， with T2 hypersignal and T1 hyposignal. The case was once again presented to our multidisciplinary care team， who suggested a surgical“en-bloc”resection.

【17】The patient underwent surgery 3 months after the initial CT scan. He underwent midline laparotomy and exploratory lap-arotomy， which revealed no suspect secondary lesions. The mass was bulging from the left hypochondrium and infiltrat-ed the left colic flexure and the spleen. We performed a me-ticulous adhesiolysis to isolate the whole tumoral mass， a left pancreatectomy， division of the pancreas with a 60-mm sta-pler Echelon\*(ohnson & Johnson)， with splenectomy and seg-ment resection of the left colic flexure with direct latero-lateral anastomosis. The mass was resected"en-bloc" and weighed 7.057 g . The surgery lasted 264 min， blood loss was estimated to be 300 cc， and the patient did not re-ceive any transfusion. Postoperative care was uneventful， with a standard application of the ERAS@ protocol of our institu-tion  and the patient was discharged on day 5.

【18】Pathology and immunohistochemistry examination of the re-sected mass revealed a DT measuring 40 cm. It consisted of elongated，thin，tapered cells of uniform appearance with pale cytoplasm，embedded in a collagenous stroma. There was no nuclear hyperchromasia， cytological atypia， or mitosis. Blood vessels were thin-walled， with perivascular edema and vascu-lar microhemorrhages .

【19】We observed nuclear B-catenin staining . Smooth muscle actin (SMA) was weakly positive and desmin was neg-ative. DNA sequencing revealed that the CTNNB1 (B-catenin) gene carried the p.T41A (c.121A>G) mutation. The tumor in-vaded almost the whole pancreatic parenchyma and infiltrat-ed the colonic wall， but circumferential resection margins and organ resection margins were negative.

【20】We proposed active close surveillance with MRI every 3-6months， because even with the negative resection margins the risk of recurrence seems to be proportional to the initial size of the tumor. The patient had 2 follow-up MRl scans at 6and 12 months after surgery， without any sign of recurrence and without hepatic， pancreatic， or colic nodules.

【21】Discussion

【22】A search of the English-language scientific literature yielded30 reports of DTs which developed at the expense of the pan-creas  . The mean age at diagnosis was 42.1years old and 61.3% of patients were male. The mean tumor size was 7.99 cm and， except for Bruce et al  and Alghamdi et al ， none of the reports specified the weight of the tumor； 26% of tumors were totally asymptomatic， and58% of patients had unspecific epigastric pain or discomfort. This case is， to our knowledge， the heaviest DT of the pancre-as ever reported in the English-language scientific literature.

【23】The road to clear diagnosis of DT is often long and winding- from clinical examination of unspecific symptoms through various imaging techniques to histological examination. As DTs are rare in routine practice， it is important to remember their frequent association with FAP， attenuated FAP， or Gardner syn-drome. Quintini et al  showed that 10-25% of patients with mutations in the APC gene develop DTs and that these tumors are an important cause of mortality after total colectomy. We recommend that patients diagnosed with DTs be referred to an experienced multidisciplinary team. Even if the guidelines are unclear， we strongly recommend a surgical approach for tumors larger than 10 cm， grow rapidly， or， most important-ly， are symptomatic. Surgeons should always strive to achieve negative resection margins， but even then， the recurrence of DTs is frequent (25-60%) . DTs can also be challenging to treat surgically， especially when located in tight spaces such as around the pancreas.

【0】Background：

【1】Desmoid tumor (DT)， also known as aggressive fibromatosis or desmoid-type fibromatosis， is a rare disease. It can occur in anyone at any age， and is more likely to appear in female patients. DTs are sometimes associ-ated with familial adenomatous polyposis and rare syndromes such as Gardner syndrome. Arising from spe-cific cells， fibroblasts， they tend to develop in patients with a history of abdominal surgery and rarely produce metastases.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We present a case of a 41-year-old man who was referred for abdominal discomfort with no digestive or gen-eral symptoms. An abdominal CT scan revealed a mass in the left hypochondrium， corresponding to an in-traperitoneal tumor extending to left colon. Based on MRl， we suspected a gastrointestinal stromal tumor. Colonoscopy showed no intraluminal tumor in the colon. A PET-CT scan revealed tumor hypermetabolism and no metastases. The mass was diagnosed as a DT after percutaneous biopsy. Six weeks after diagnosis and as the tumor continued increasing despite pharmacological treatment， the patient underwent surgical pancreatic tail resection with splenectomy and left colonic segmentectomy. Histological examination revealed a 7.047-g DT with severe infiltration of pancreatic parenchyma and transmural colic barrier， with no high-grade differen-tiation and negative resection margins. The postoperative recovery was uneventful， and we proposed surveil-lance with MRI.

【4】Conclusions： The DT was surgically removed and patient remains under MRI surveillance. Other reported management ap-proaches consist of radiotherapy， tyrosine kinase inhibitors，anti-hormonal therapies/non-steroidal anti-inflam-matory drugs， chemotherapy， or close surveillance only. This is， to our knowledge， the largest and heaviest DT reported in the modern literature.

【5】Keywords： Colorectal Surgery·CTNNB1 Protein， Human · Fibromatosis， Aggressive·Gardner Syndrome·Radiotherapy

【6】Abbreviations： DT - desmoid tumor； CT scan-computed tomography scan； FAP - familial adenomatous polyposis；

【7】NSAID-non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug； ECOG PS - Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status Desmoid tumors (DTs) are rare tumors which develop from the connective tissue： well-differentiated mesenchymal fi-broblasts or myofibroblasts. DTs represent<3% of all soft tissue tumors and have an estimated incidence of 2-4 new cases per million population per year . Also known as ag gressive fibromatosis or desmoid-type fibromatosis， DTs are benign tumors which can develop anywhere in the body， in-vade surrounding tissues， and can be very difficult to con-trol because of their rapid growth. McFarlane was the first to describe a DT， which was located in the abdominal wall of a young patient in 1832 . The WHO classifies DTs as intermediate (locally aggressive) fibroblastic and myofibro-blastic tumors .

【8】DTs can localize intra- or extra-abdominally， mostly in the ab-dominal wall， and there is no evidence of their metastatic po-tential. DTs typically affect young adults between 20 and 30years of age . The clinical presentation of DTs ranges from fully asymptomatic to swelling， left hypochondrium pain，epi-gastric pain， nausea， vomiting， and back pain. The etiology of these tumors is not well understood and they have 2 typical presentations： sporadic， mostly associated with post-traumat-ic (postoperative) etiology  or associated with Gardner syn-drome， a subtype of familial adenomatosis polyposis (FAP).FAP develops in patients with mutations in the APC gene ； 20%of these APC mutations are de novo . In some rare cases， DTs are associated with the peripartum period.

【9】Specific factors have been identified as abnormalities in his-tological analysis showing fibroblastic proliferation and then confirmed by immunohistochemical staining for B-catenin， as the B-catenin gene (CTNNB1)， present in more than 75% of DTs cases， is mutated in FAP or Gardner syndrome .

【10】There is no standard of care for DTs， but the first-line pharma-cotherapy consists of selective estrogen receptor modulators such as Tamoxifen or Toremifene and non-steroidal anti-in-flammatory drugs (NSAID) as well as cytotoxic chemotherapy and sometimes radiotherapy . Treatment with oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor drugs such as Imatinib or Sorafenib has shown promising results . An emerging technique uses high-in-tensity ultrasound waves to remove small DTs. This non-inva-sive approach can be combined with other treatments 9，10.

【11】However， in the vast majority of symptomatic cases， surgery plays a major role in the treatment of DTs. In 25-60% of pa-tients who undergo surgery， DTs recur locally ， most fre-quently near the surgical resection. It is well accepted that the aim of surgery is to remove the entire tumor with RO re-section margins and minimize the risk of recurrence. Based on data from 495 patients with DTs， physicians at Memorial

【12】We report the largest case of pancreatic DT， diagnosed on22 November 2021， at the Geneva University Hospitals， Switzerland. The DT was removed surgically with negative re-section margins. We expand this case report with a literature review on DTs of the pancreas.

【13】The work has been reported in line with the SCARE 2020 criteria：Updating Consensus Surgical CAse REport (SCARE) Guidelines， International Journal of Surgery 2020；84：226-230.

【14】Case Report

【15】A 41-year-old male patient with no significant medical or sur-gical history apart from an asymptomatic megaureter and a bicuspid aortic valve presented to his family physician with nausea and diarrhea persisting for 1 week， 3 months prior to our consultation. He was prescribed simple symptomatic man-agement. Because of the persisting abdominal discomfort and postprandial nauseas， the patient was referred to the Division of Digestive Surgery of the University Hospitals of Geneva. We noted a visible bulking in the epigastric and left hypochondri-ac region. The mass was easily palpable and solid， without any signs of abdominal guarding. The patient was in good condition， height 178 cm， weight 77 kg， and ECOG PS 0. He reported no active smoking or alcohol consumption， no aller-gies， and no regular medication. The patient had no person-al or family history of desmoid tumor. The first abdominal CT scan  showed a massive intra-abdominal heteroge-neous tissue tumor located in the left hypochondrium and in-vading the left colon. We also observed a moderate amount of intra-abdominal free fluid and suspected the tumor to be a gastrointestinal stromal tumor. We then performed an MRI， which revealed that the left hypochondrium mass was mildly heterogeneous with T2 hypersignal and T1 hyposig-nal of unclear origin， with restricted diffusion， mild enhance-ment after contrast injection， and encapsulated， and was merg-ing with the tail of the pancreas and compressing the left colic flexure. Colonoscopy was normal apart from a severe extrinsic compression localized in the left colic flexure. To explore the potential malignancy and metastases of the tumor， a whole-body PET/CT scan was performed . It revealed a hy-permetabolic tumor of more than 20 cm extending from the left pancreas and invading the left colic flexure， and no other suspect hypermetabolic lesions. Histological and immunohis-tochemical images of a percutaneous biopsy were compati-ble with an active DT.

【16】The case was presented to our multidisciplinary care team， who opted for a conservative initial management with sulin-dac (NSAID) and close surveillance. One month after this de-cision， the patient presented with an increased abdominal cir-cumference and alternating diarrhea and constipation. A new MRI showed that the tumor had rapidly grown from 7 to more than 18 cm ， with T2 hypersignal and T1 hyposignal. The case was once again presented to our multidisciplinary care team， who suggested a surgical“en-bloc”resection.

【17】The patient underwent surgery 3 months after the initial CT scan. He underwent midline laparotomy and exploratory lap-arotomy， which revealed no suspect secondary lesions. The mass was bulging from the left hypochondrium and infiltrat-ed the left colic flexure and the spleen. We performed a me-ticulous adhesiolysis to isolate the whole tumoral mass， a left pancreatectomy， division of the pancreas with a 60-mm sta-pler Echelon\*(ohnson & Johnson)， with splenectomy and seg-ment resection of the left colic flexure with direct latero-lateral anastomosis. The mass was resected"en-bloc" and weighed 7.057 g . The surgery lasted 264 min， blood loss was estimated to be 300 cc， and the patient did not re-ceive any transfusion. Postoperative care was uneventful， with a standard application of the ERAS@ protocol of our institu-tion  and the patient was discharged on day 5.

【18】Pathology and immunohistochemistry examination of the re-sected mass revealed a DT measuring 40 cm. It consisted of elongated，thin，tapered cells of uniform appearance with pale cytoplasm，embedded in a collagenous stroma. There was no nuclear hyperchromasia， cytological atypia， or mitosis. Blood vessels were thin-walled， with perivascular edema and vascu-lar microhemorrhages .

【19】We observed nuclear B-catenin staining . Smooth muscle actin (SMA) was weakly positive and desmin was neg-ative. DNA sequencing revealed that the CTNNB1 (B-catenin) gene carried the p.T41A (c.121A>G) mutation. The tumor in-vaded almost the whole pancreatic parenchyma and infiltrat-ed the colonic wall， but circumferential resection margins and organ resection margins were negative.

【20】We proposed active close surveillance with MRI every 3-6months， because even with the negative resection margins the risk of recurrence seems to be proportional to the initial size of the tumor. The patient had 2 follow-up MRl scans at 6and 12 months after surgery， without any sign of recurrence and without hepatic， pancreatic， or colic nodules.

【21】Discussion

【22】A search of the English-language scientific literature yielded30 reports of DTs which developed at the expense of the pan-creas  . The mean age at diagnosis was 42.1years old and 61.3% of patients were male. The mean tumor size was 7.99 cm and， except for Bruce et al  and Alghamdi et al ， none of the reports specified the weight of the tumor； 26% of tumors were totally asymptomatic， and58% of patients had unspecific epigastric pain or discomfort. This case is， to our knowledge， the heaviest DT of the pancre-as ever reported in the English-language scientific literature.

【23】The road to clear diagnosis of DT is often long and winding- from clinical examination of unspecific symptoms through various imaging techniques to histological examination. As DTs are rare in routine practice， it is important to remember their frequent association with FAP， attenuated FAP， or Gardner syn-drome. Quintini et al  showed that 10-25% of patients with mutations in the APC gene develop DTs and that these tumors are an important cause of mortality after total colectomy. We recommend that patients diagnosed with DTs be referred to an experienced multidisciplinary team. Even if the guidelines are unclear， we strongly recommend a surgical approach for tumors larger than 10 cm， grow rapidly， or， most important-ly， are symptomatic. Surgeons should always strive to achieve negative resection margins， but even then， the recurrence of DTs is frequent (25-60%) . DTs can also be challenging to treat surgically， especially when located in tight spaces such as around the pancreas.

【0】Background：

【1】Hyperammonemia as a cause of unconsciousness in adult patients is mostly related to liver dysfunction. However， elevated plasma ammonia without signs of liver failure can be associated with valproic acid (VPA)， an antiepileptic drug. We report two patients with acute unconsciousness， hyperammonemia and normal liver function in association with VPA.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 23-year-old female on chronic VPA therapy attempted suicide by taking 100 tablets ofVPA. She had elevated plasma ammonia (250 umol/L) and serum VPA concentration (3250 umol/L). After discontinuation of VPA her mental status improved together with normalization of plasma ammonia and serum VPA level. After restarting her chronic VPA therapy plasma ammonia level remained normal and serum VPA concentration within the therapeutic range.

【4】A 34-year-old male on chronic VPA therapy presented with acute unconsciousness and hyperammonemia (326 umol/L). He had stable VPA dosing and serum VPA concentration within the therapeutic range (354 umol/L). Following discontinuation of VPA we observed improvement of his mental status and decreasing of ammonia level. After we reinitiated VPA therapy， his mental status worsened again in correlation to increased ammonia level.

【5】Conclusions：

【6】Hyperammonemia with central nervous depression may develop in acute VPA overdose as well as in chronic VPA therapy with stable dosing without any obvious acute clinical event. In patients with unexplained unconsciousness measurement of plasma ammonia is an important screening test.

【7】Key words： valproic acid· unconsciousness · ammonia· liver function

【8】Valproic acid (VPA)， used as an antiepileptic drug， may be associated with the central nervous system depression due to hyperammonemia in the absence of liver dysfunction  even with VPA in therapeu-tic range. Hyperammonemia mostly occurs among1yP children as a manifestation of inborn errors of me-tabolism . In adults elevated plasma ammonia is usually due to liver failure， toxic ingestion of 5-fluoro-uracil， haematological malignancy， bleeding from the intestines or deficiency of urea-cycle enzymes. The presence of ammonia in the blood at only two times the upper limit of the normal range may cause central nervous system depression， resulting in lethargy， coma， and death. We report two patients where unconsciousness was due to hyperammone-mia in the absence of liver dysfunction. In the first case hyperammonemia appeared at increased serum VPA levels after acute VPA overdose， while in the second one ammonia levels were directly associated with administration of VPA that remained within the therapeutic range throughout the course.

【9】CASE REPORTS

【10】Case report #1

【11】A 23-year-old female on chronic antiepileptic therapy with VPA presented to the emergency department af-ter the ingestion of 30g of VPA (100 x 300 mg tablets) in suicide attempt. On admission her Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) was 6， respiratory rate 12 breaths/min-ute， pulse rate 65 beats/minute， temperature 35.9℃， blood pressure supine 105/60 mmHg and oxygen saturation 96%. Hepatocellular enzyme levels were normal， while plasma ammonia level and serum VPA concentration were elevated： 85 umol/L (normal range： 9-33 umol/L) and 3250 umol/L (therapeutic range： 345-690 umol/L)， respectively. Plasma ammo-nia had further increased to 250 umol/L by 12 hours. In the next 48 hours serum VPA and plasma ammonia gradually decreased and improvement of the patient's mental status was observed. After we restarted the patient's chronic VPA therapy， plasma ammonia re-mained normal and serum VPA concentration within the therapeutic range . The patient was discharged on her chronic VPA therapy.

【12】Case report #2

【13】A 34-year-old male with epilepsy presented to the emergency department due to acute unconscious-ness. There was no data about possible overdose of his chronic VPA therapy. On admission his GCS was 8， respiratory rate 16 breaths/minute， pulse rate83 beats/minute， temperature 37.2℃， blood pressure supine 100/70 mmHg and oxygen saturation 98%. Hepatocellular enzymes were normal. A computed tomography scan of the head and laboratory tests of cerebrospinal liquor were unremarkable. Searching for other possible causes of unconsciousness plasma ammonia level was obtained， that was 326 umol/L(normal range： 9-33 umol/L). The serum VPA level was 354 umol/L and had increased to 377 umol/L(therapeutic range： 345-690 umol/L) 11 hours af-ter admission. Following discontinuation of VPA the patient's mental status improved and plasma ammonia decreased to 9 umol/L 42 hours after ad-mission. On the third day we restarted the patient’s chronic VPA therapy. His mental status begun to worsen again in correlation to increased ammonia levels to 247 umol/L. Serum VPA levels remained within the therapeutic range. After discontinuation of VPA and replacing it with carbamazepine the pa-tient's mental status and ammonia levels normalized.

【14】DISCUSSION

【15】Hyperammonemia is a known metabolic side effect of VPA. In our first patient hyperammonemia was induced by acute VPA overdose with increased serum VPA concentration. After normalization of serum VPA and plasma ammonia， the patient’s symptoms improved. Serum VPA remained within the therapeutic range， even after restarting of the chronic VPA therapy. The second patient with hyperammonemia was on long-term VPA therapy， with stable dosing and serum VPA concentration within the therapeutic range. There were no signs of liver dysfunction and no data of possible additional toxic ingestion. Therefore， other causes of unconsciousness were initially considered， but were not proven by laboratory or imaging tests. Clinical observation and obtained serial ammonia and VPA levels during restarting the VPA therapy clearly pointed out that VPA was directly associated with am-monia level and the patient’s symptoms ， even that serum VPA concentration remained within the therapeutic range throughout the course.

【16】Presented cases confirm previous observations that there is no clear correlation between clinical course， serum VPA levels and ammonemia. Neurological symptoms are not directly associated with the degree of hyperammonemia， which may be asymptomatic， and serum VPA. Case series have demonstrated that severe neurological effects with coma predomi-nately develop when the peak VPA concentration is at least four-times the upper therapeutic limit . However， another case report illustrated high ammo-nia levels in a patient with coma but the peak VPA concentration within the therapeutic range . These observations suggest that multiple contributory factors might be responsible for neurological complications of VPA， including hyperammonemia， direct sedative effect， cerebral oedema， mitochondrial dysfunction and lactic acidosis . Hyperammonemia is believed to be the result of the impact of VPA's me-tabolites on the elimination of ammonia in the urea cycle. Depletion of L-carnitine， involved in the me-tabolism of urea-cycle enzymes， also plays its role. Hyperammonemic coma without associated liver failure is according to literature a rare complication of a chronic and stable VPA therapy， described primarily in patients with inborn errors of metabolism， such as ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency and occur- ring idiosyncratically during initial stages of therapy.Other contributing factors might be pro-tein-rich diet， physical exertion or combination of antiepileptic drugs . In our first patient hyper-ammonemia with increased VPA level could be due to transient enzyme saturation that was reversible.In the second patient with stable VPA therapy no acute precipitants of encephalopathy were documented. Pre-existing congenital abnormalities of urea-cycle enzymes that were asymptomatic or/and depletion of L-carnitine might contribute to hyperammonemia in association with the impairment of metabolic mecha-nisms. Underlying pathophysiology in our patient unfortunately was not investigated.

【17】Treatment of VPA-induced hyperammonemic en-cephalopathy includes discontinuation of VPA and supportive measures. Therapy with L-carnitine sup-plementation is recommended in acute VPA overdose with coma， hepatic dysfunction and increasing am-monia levels . However， there is little objective evidence for its routine use in VPA overdose . Methods of extracorporeal removal of VPA， hemodi-alysis and hemoperfusion， have been used in cases of severe intoxication， yet in the absence of controlled clinical trials their place in the management of VPA overdose is not clearly defined .

【18】CONCLUSIONS

【19】Unconsciousness due to hyperammonemia may oc-cur in acute VPA overdose as well as in clinically stable VPA treated patients and therapeutic VPA levels. Therefore， hyperammonemia may represent an unrecognised cause of mental status changes in VPA treated patients. Presented cases point out the importance of measuring plasma ammonia level as a screening test in patients presenting with unexplained unconsciousness. In addition， ammonia level should be evaluated in all VPA treated patients who develop an altered mental status.

【0】ABSTRACT Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava (LSVC) not very uncommon in the cardiovascular intervention. It often poses a problem during Permanent Pacemaker Implantation (PPM) due to abnormal anatomic course of the venous system. Here we have reported a series of 4 such cases.

【1】KEYWORDS Left Superior Vena Cava (LSVC)， Permanent Pacemaker Implantation (PPM)， Coronary Sinus (CS)

【2】Introduction

【3】Persistent left superior vena cava (LSVC) present in 0.5% of the general population， and up to 10% of those with established congenital heart disease. The true incidence is， however， un-known as this anomaly exists without affecting the systemic venous return.However， persistent LSVC has important im-plications in patients who undergo cardiac interventions such as placement of a transvenous pacemaker. This anomaly is also essential in patients with associated congenital malformations where it may pose difficulty during catheterization and surgery.

【4】Persistent left superior vena cava results from failure of in-volution of left anterior and left common cardinal veins. In the majority of the cases， it drains into the RA using the coronary sinus. In the remaining， it drains into the LA via the partially or completely unroofed coronary sinus. There is an increased likelihood of congenital heart disease if there is no right-sided superior vena cava or if the LSVC drains into the left atrium(LA).  The clinical suspicion of LSVC is by observing more considerable distension and double a wave in the left jugular compared to the right jugular vein. Other clues to the diagnosis are left paramediastinal venous crescent on chest x-ray， and an enlarged coronary sinus on echocardiography.

【5】Persistent LSVC is not the only cause of a dilated coronary sinus， however， with other etiologies including elevated right atrial pressure (most common)， coronary arteriovenous fistula， partial anomalous pulmonary venous return， or an "unroofed"coronary sinus affording shunt flow between the left atrium and coronary sinus. Transthoracic echocardiography reveals a dilated coronary sinus and diagnosis can be confirmed by use of saline contrast ("bubble study") echocardiography. The fol-lowing diagnostic criteria can be used with echocardiography： the presence of a dilated coronary sinus on two-dimensional echocardiography in the absence of evidence of elevated right-sided filling pressures；  enhancement of the dilated coronary sinus before the right atrium (RA) after contrast material infu-sion into a left-arm vein；  normal transit of contrast with RA opacification before the coronary sinus with contrast injected from the right arm. 

【6】Pacemaker implantation has been reported in patients via persistent left superior vena cava.  In this article， we present a series of cases in which pacemaker implantation was done in patients who were detected to have persistent left superior vena cava while undergoing pacemaker implantation. In all of these cases， the implantation was done successfully without any complication. These cases also highlight the importance of careful clinical and echocardiographic examinations during the preparative phase before taking these patients for surgery.

【7】Case report 1

【8】The 66-year-old male admitted with a recurrent episode of syn-cope. ECG revealed a complete heart block. He was put on temporary pacemaker in an emergency. After the initial evalu-ation， he was planned for permanent pacemaker implantation. The procedure was started after taking consent for the procedure. Puncture into the left subclavian vein by percutaneous approach was done. When the guidewire was tried to introduce through the puncture needle， it was initially felt with mild resistant. Ter-rumo wire was taken which passed through this puncture needle quickly and reached to the heart via left subelavian vein. At the fluoroscopy image， the wire did not seem to be in the right-side chambers of the heart as it usually does. It looked like left-sided superior vena cava (LSVC). 10 ml iso-osmolar dye was taken and pushed through the left brachial vein to achieve venogram image. It was visible now and confirmed the presence of left-sided superior vena cava. 7F sheath was introduced through a puncture needle， the guidewire was removed， and permanent lead was introduced. With the help of double-curved loop， the permanent lead for the right ventricle was screwed in a good position with good threshold and impedance. The procedure was completed successfully (Image 1a and 1b). Procedure time was 31 minutes.

【9】Case report 2

【10】A 52-year-old gentleman presented with repeated syncope with ECG evidence of advanced atrioventricular block. He was planned for DDDR permanent pacemaker implantation. Af- ter initial percutaneous puncture through a left subclavian vein， the guidewire seems to be run along the left side of the spine in AP view of fluoroscopy image. 10 ml isoosmal dye was taken and injected into the left brachial vein for venogram study. It was revealed that the gentleman had left superior vena cava. Terrumo wire was taken and passed into the right atrium and into inferior vena cava. Right ventricular screwing lead was passed with the help of S-shaped stylet and screwed in proper position with acceptable threshold and impedance. Right atrial ascrewing lead was screwed into the right atrium with the help of single curved stylet. The procedure was completed success-fully . The procedural time was 47 minutes.

【11】Case report 3

【12】42-year-old lady admitted for pacemaker implantation for Left Bundle Branch Block and repeated syncope. She had no history of chest pain. Coronary Angiogram was done outside， which revealed normal coronaries. Echocardiogram revealed normal Left ventricular ejection fraction. She was planned for Septal Pacing. After an initial percutaneous puncture， it was found that she has persistent left superior vena cava. Septal pacing was achieved without much difficulty， and permanent pacing lead was actively fixed with a satisfactory threshold (Image 3 a and 3b). The procedure was successful. Procedure time was 17minutes.

【13】Case report 4

【14】29-year-old gentleman admitted with recurrent syncope was found to have Complete Heart Block. He has dextrocardia. Echocardiogram revealed no structural abnormalities. He was planned for PPM implantation. After an initial puncture， it was found that He has persistent LSVC. Morphological Right ventric-ular Apical Pacing was achieved successfully. The procedural time was 1hour and 5 minutes.

【15】Review of the literature

【16】The first description of PLSVC perhaps dated long back remains a matter of debate in the medical literature (17th to 18th century). The first review on the topic of LSVC was published in 1850 by John Marshall . Despite numerous publications on PLSVC there has been very little in the literature specifically di-rected toward the potential importance of the incidental finding of PLSVC to an interventional cardiologist who is directly in-volved in pacemaker implantation. Incidental detection PLSVC during such procedure of pacemaker implantation has been re-ported previously. Increased detection in such cases may be due to the association of conduction disturbances and venous drainage abnormalities in population. Most of the time during such procedure operator switches to the right side， however， may not be possible always. There are different techniques re-ported for successful implantation through the left side. All these modifications (like making a loop in the pacemaker lead， stylet or large bore sheath to make the loop straight， use of venous ul-trasound，venogram) helps to tide over such difficulties. Here in this series， we had used several such modifications according to presenting a scenario， and successful implantation was done.

【17】Discussion

【18】Persistent LSVC always poses difficulty when approaching from the left side has been the choice during PPM implantation. In the first case (Image 1a and1b) it was very much trouble as the guidewire was not going beyond some point and it was felt with resistance. It may look like that subclavian vein has been punctured in a different place， or there might be obstruction. The course of the vein is different in the presence of LSVC， which is not understandable without venogram. After the venogram was done， it was obvious that LSVC rather than obstruction is the cause. Therefore the guidewire can be pushed in that direction without worrying about perforation. Placement of the RV lead is also difficult due to bend and loop in the venous course. Stylet needs to be curved twice to reach RV apex. Some may prefer the alfa helical loop or double-curved S-shaped loop. Placement of RA leads comparably easier than RV apical lead (as in the second case - Image 2). A single loop in the stylet may place the RA lead in the desired position without much difficulty. Septal pacing has always been difficult in terms of proper positioning116and needs to be confirmed by the different fluoroscopic view. In the 3 rd case， Septal pacing was done through LSVC and approved by several fluoroscopic views and ECG (Image 3a and3b). PPM implantation in dextrocardia is always challenging. Position of the chambers of the heart needs to be evaluated in details before such procedure undertaken. In the 4th case， it took longer time to position the pacing lead in RV apical position.

【19】Overall the procedure time in each of the above the cases were longer due to unpredictable and challenging anatomy. It in-creases the radiation exposure to patients and operator. The com-plication related to puncture (pneumothorax， bleeding， perfora-tion， arterial puncture) becomes higher due to difficult anatomic access in such cases. Preoperative evaluation thus becomes nec-essary in such cases. Presence of dilated coronary sinus (CS) may indicate the presence of LSVC. However， several other conditions may result in dilated CS. A preoperative venogram may delineate the confirmed presence of LSVC. But mandatory venogram in all cases may expose the patient to dye related com-plications (allergy，renal dysfunction， etc.). Right-sided venous access may alleviate problems of LSVC， but most of the patients are right-handed， and left-sided implantation is conventional. Therefore protocol-based approach may be required to avoid such difficulties.

【20】Conclusion

【21】operative echocardiogram， a high index of suspicion and pre-operative venogram may confirm the presence of LSVC. The right-sided approach may decrease the difficulties in the nega-tion of pacemaker lead in such cases. Increase fluoroscopic time， and radiation exposure is another aspect of PPM implantation in patients with persistent LSVC. Lastly， expertise approach might decrease overall complications in unpredictable cases.

【0】ABSTRACT Background： Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune rheumatic disease characterized by inflammation that affects the organs or systems in the body. Clinical manifestations of SLE are varied. Lymphocytes are one type of white blood cell (leucocyte) which play a role in the pathogenesis of SLE through the role of B cells and T cells. Lymphocyte count is also included in hematologic criteria of SLE and it is associated with the increase of organ damage index. Objective： To determine the lymphocyte count in the clinical manifestations of patients with SLE. Methods： This study was analytic research with cross-sectional design. The subjects were all newly diagnosed patients with SLE. The study was conducted at Wahidin Sudirohusodo Hospital and its network from May until July 2018. Results： Subjects who met the study criteria were 37， who were all women. The most common clinical manifestations were mucocutaneous with26 subjects (97.3%). Renal manifestations (p <0.001)， vasculitis (p=0.003) and constitutional symptoms (p=0.002) had significant correlation in patients with lymphopenia compared to patients who had normal lymphocyte levels (p <0.01). Subjects with >3 clinical manifestations had lower average lymphocyte count of 1018.03/ pl， while the subjects with≤ three clinical manifestations had an average lymphocyte level of 1949.44/ ul. This result was statistically significant， with p=<0.001. Conclusions： Renal manifestations， vasculitis， and constitutional symptoms were associated with lymphopenia. Lympophenia was commonly found in subjects who have more clinical manifestations.

【1】KEYWORDS SLE， lymphocyte count， lymphopenia， clinical manifestations

【2】Abbreviations

【3】·SLE： Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)

【4】·CNS： Central Nervous System

【5】·ACR： American College of Rheumatology

【6】· ANA： Anti Nuclear Antibody

【7】Introduction

【8】Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune rheumatic disease characterized by inflammation that affects the organs or systems in the body. This disease is associated with the deposit of autoantibodies and immune complexes which caused tissue damage. Clinical manifestations of SLE are varied， including the involvement of skin and mucosa， joints， blood， heart，lung，kidney， central nervous system (CNS)， and the im- mune system. Lymphocytes are one type of white blood cell(leucocyte) which play a role in the pathogenesis of SLE through the role of B cells and T cells. Lymphocyte count is also included in hematologic criteria of SLE， and it is also used as a parameter to measure the disease activity of SLE. Lymphopenia in SLE patients with an active disease has a significant pathological meaning. It can occur without leukopenia. It could be caused by the presence of lymphocytotoxic antibodies and lymphocyte apoptosis. Absolute lymphopenia correlates with disease ac-tivity. Patients with lymphocyte count less than 1500 cells/mm3at the diagnosis indicate a higher frequency of fever polyarthri-tis， kidney and central nervous system involvement. A study conducted by Faddah. S et al. in Egypt reported that lymphope-nia in patients with SLE was associated with the incidence of lupus nephritis， leukopenia， increase of disease activity index， and increase of organ damage index. Kosalka. J et al. stated that patients with lupus nephritis had an increase in B cell im-maturation， excessive activation of active memory T cells， B cells memory damage， and a decreased of inactive memory T cells. Those conditions were associated with lymphopenia in patients with active symptoms of SLE.

【9】Materials and Methods

【10】This study was an analytical study with cross-sectional design conducted at Wahidin Sudirohusodo Hospital in Makassar and its network hospital from May until July 2018.

【11】a) Population

【12】The population of this study were all inpatients and out-patients newly diagnosed with SLE. The diagnosis of SLE was made by using 4 of the 11 revised American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria in 1997， while the exclu-sion criteria were patients with SLE who had received high doses of corticosteroids， cytotoxic drugs， and immunosup-pressant drugs.

【13】b) Methods and data collection

【14】All subjects underwent history taking， physical exami-nations and additional investigations including complete blood tests， erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)， liver and kidney function， urinalysis， ANA profile， chest radiography， echocardiography， or abdominal ultrasound. Patients were divided into two groups based on the lymphocytes count. Group 1 consist of subjects with lymphopenia (lymphocytes<1500/ul) and group 2 was subject without lymphopenia(lymphocytes ≥ 1500/ul). Clinical manifestations were di-vided into nine manifestations， namely： mucocutaneous manifestations， musculoskeletal manifestations， renal mani-festations， haematology manifestations， neuropsychiatric manifestations， manifestations of vasculitis， serositis， and constitutional manifestations.

【15】c) Statistical analysis

【16】Data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for Social Science (SPSS) program version 22. The statistical analysis performed was the calculation of frequency distribution and Chi-Square statistical test， Exact Fisher and Independent T-test. Statistical test results were significant if the value of p <0.05.

【17】During the 3-month of the study period， we found 37 patients who were all women with SLE who met the inclusion criteria and were willing to participate. There were 25 patients (67，6%) with lymphopenia and 12 subjects  without lymphopenia. Table 1 shows that the mean age in this study was 26 ± seven years which range from 15-46 years. Based on laboratory re-sults， patients with SLE had average lymphocyte count 1244.6±785.5/ul， with the lowest count was 133/ul and the highest level was 3978/pl. The most common clinical manifestations were mucocutaneous manifestations in 36 patients (97.3%)， and the rarest was neuropsychiatric disorders which were only found in4 patients (10.8%).

【18】Table 2 shows the comparison of laboratory results between lymphopenia and non-lymphopenia patients. The value of ESRI was significantly higher in group 1 compared to group 2， which is 71.28 compared to 51.50. Leucocyte count was significantly lower in group 1 than group 2， which is 6306.40 compared to9536.67. Haemoglobin， urea， creatinine， and platelet levels did not show a statistically significant difference.

【19】Renal manifestations， vasculitis， and constitutional symp-toms in group 1 and group 2 showed a statistically significant difference， with p <0.01， as shown in Table 3. Other clinical manifestations did not have significant correlation， although it was found to be higher in patients with lymphopenia (p >0.01).

【20】Table 4 shows that subjects with> 3 clinical manifestations had lower lymphocyte counts than subjects with only three clinical manifestations， and this result was statistically signifi-cant with p=<0.001.

【21】Discussion

【22】The prevalence of SLE varies in each country. In Indonesia， there had been no report of it， but it was estimated more than 1，500，000cases. According to Wallace et al.， the risk ratio between women and male is 9：1. It is related to estrogen hormone in women.6According to a study conducted by Urowitz et al. in 1997， more than 80% of patients with SLE were exposed in reproductive age between 15 -40 years with an average age in 34.3 years.7 SLE exposures at the age of 45 or after menopause phase are rare. Those results are similar to our study in which the subjects were all women， and the average age of the subject was 26 ± 7； with the youngest age was 15 years old and the oldest was 46 years old.

【23】In our study， the average of lymphocyte count was1244.6±785.5/ul which is similar to study conducted by Oe-hadian et al. at Hasan Sadikin Hospital， Bandung in 2013， found the average lymphocyte count in SLE patients was1721±600/pl. These results can vary， depend on the sever-ity of disease activity in which low lymphocyte count represent severe disease activity in our subject. Both T cells and B cells will decrease indirectly proportional with the lymphocyte count； whereas， on the contrary， the levels of Natural Killer cells are increases. The decreased lymphocyte count can also be caused by various factors， such as secondary infection and nutritional status of subjects that were not excluded.

【24】The most common clinical manifestations were mucocuta-neous. It was similar to a study conducted by Cojocaru et al.， which found that more than 80% of patients with SLE had skin problems. According to Cervera et al.， cutaneous lesions can occur in more than 85% of patients with SLE. The most com-mon cutaneous disorder that found was malar rash. Most of the mucocutaneous abnormalities in SLE are triggered by expo-sure to ultraviolet or direct exposure to sunlight. Indonesia's location is right on the equator that receives continuous sunlight exposure throughout the year， and it could be an explanation to why the most common manifestations in this study were mucocutaneous.
