【32】In this study， we compared laboratory parameters，including haemoglobin，ESR， creatinine， leukocytes， and platelets in order to find out if there were any effects of lymphocyte count on those panels. It was found that there was a significant correla-tion between lymphopenia and ESR (p=0.014)，and leucocyte count (p=0.035). The average ESR levels of SLE patients with lymphopenia was 71.28 mm/hour， whereas according to Sto-jan et al. levels 50-70 mm/hour was classified into moderate activity category. The increase of ESR levels correlated with the increase of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index (SLEDAI) score which indicates a high disease activity. The average of leucocyte count in Group 1 significantly differ compared with Group 2， but the average of leucocyte count in subject with lymphopenia is still in the normal range. Pa-tients with SLE often have leukopenia， which is caused by the suppression of T lymphocytes resulting in decreased of Colony Forming Units (CFU) which plays a role in the pathogenesis of granulopoiesis failure in SLE. Subjects with lymphopenia had lower platelet count， but it is not statistically significant. One of the mechanisms that underlying thrombocytopenia in patients with SLE is the decrease of peripheral platelets caused by an-tiplatelet antibodies. Pathomechanism of antiplatelet antibody formation is similar to the formation of anti-lymphocyte autoan-tibodies through the hyperactive pathways of TH cells and B cells， and the decrease of Treg cells that cause the increased of autoantibodies formation. 

【33】Some literature had explained the association of lympho-cyte count and clinical manifestations， which one of them is renal manifestations. Faddah et al.'s study in 2013 explained the association of lymphopenia with lupus nephritis， Vila et al. in 2006 also found a statistically significant correlation be-tween lymphopenia and the incidence of lupus nephritis. Our study also found that renal manifestations have a significant association with lymphopenia (p<0.001). These results can be explained through the research conducted by Nakabayashi et al.， which found a high level of anti-T cell antibody， especially in proliferative glomerulonephritis. The increased incidence of lupus nephritis in lymphopenia was associated with mal-function of CD8+， T cell suppressor and NK cell suppressor activity in patients with SLE which is unable to regulate the synthesis of polyclonal immunoglobulins and the production of autoantibodies. Some of these autoantibodies will form im-mune complexes together with nucleosomes (histone DNA)， chromatin， C1q， laminin， RO (SS-A)， ubiquitin， and ribosomes which will form deposits in the mesangium， subendothelium， or subepithelial of glomerulus that resulted in tissue damage.

【34】Vasculitis also had a significant correlation with lymphopenia(p=0.003)， which is similar to study conducted by Drenkard et al. Vasculitis in SLE is classified into secondary vasculitis， where the pathogenesis is not known. Most of the hypothesis about the cause of vasculitis in SLE is immune complex depo-sition in the vascular endothelium. The effect of endothelial immune complex deposition activates a secondary inflamma-tory response which causes the formation of C5b-9 complement bonds which can destroy the basal membrane of blood vessels. That pathogenesis is associated with low lymphocyte count in

【35】SLE patients with vasculitis， in which the formation of immune complex deposition is associated with the increased of autoan-tibodies， including anti-lymphocyte autoantibodies， which re-sulted in lymphopenia. Constitutional symptoms also had a significant correlation with lymphopenia (p=0.02) which also associated with the degree of disease activity.

【36】Other manifestations such as mucocutaneous abnormali-ties， musculoskeletal， other haematology， neuropsychiatry， and serositis did not have significant correlation， but the prevalence was higher in patients with lymphopenia. These results are sim-ilar to study conducted by Faddah et al. In contrast， and Yu et al. reported that lymphopenia conditions in patients with SLE are associated with risk of lupus neuropsychiatric. Their study explained that anti lymphocytes antibodies， including anti-DNA and anti-ribosomal P antibodies， were frequently found in SLE patients. Anti-ribosomal P antibodies induced T cell apoptosis and cross-react with neuron cells.

【37】Various literature had explained the negative correlation be-tween lymphocyte count and clinical manifestations of patients with SLE. The lower the lymphocyte count， there will be more clinical manifestations that appear. In this study， we analyzed the average of lymphocyte count with the number of clinical manifestations that appeared to find out their correlation. The result showed a significant correlation， with p <0.001. It was also illustrated that lymphopenia is associated with the severity of disease activity， which is similar to study by Vila et al. and Yu et al. Lymphocyte apoptosis may result from activation-induced cell death via Fas and Fas ligand pathway or death by neglect-apoptosis of CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells that bear the CD28 molecule， which is a potent costimulatory signal for T-cell activation， which was found decrease in the peripheral blood of patients with SLE. It appears that CD28 mediated costim-ulation influences T-cell susceptibility to activation-induced cell death and may be involved in T-cell lymphopenia. Research by Yu et al. also found a significant correlation between lym-phopenia and target organ that involved； the more target organs are involved， it will be the number of clinical manifestations that appeared.

【38】The conclusion is renal manifestations， vasculitis and consti-tutional symptoms were associated with lymphopenia. Lym-pophenia is commonly found in subjects who have more clinical manifestations.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Depression is a multifactorial disorder， and novel biomarkers which might be predictive of depression are very intriguing as depression currently no biomarker of depression is available and it is heavily associated with increasing treatment resistance. Major depression is reportedly associated with inflammatory processes which include elevated levels of proinflammatory cytokines， decreased neurogenesis， which is followed by neuro progression (including pathological reorganization of the central nervous system)， mitochondrial dysfunction， and the dysfunction of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. There are observed lowered antioxidant concentrations and increased oxidative stress levels as well causing changes in activity and expression of various anti-inflammatory agents like Superoxide Dismutase (SOD)， the activity of which may be measured by various methods. Aim： To study the levels of the inflammatory marker Superoxide Dismutase enzyme (SOD) in individuals with depression and individuals without depression. Methods and material： The cross-sectional study was conducted at the Department of Psychiatry MGM medical college， Indore， India. A convenient sample of 60 patients with depression and 60 controls were recruited for one year. Patients attending Psychiatry OPD were assessed through semi-structured Performa consisting of socio-demographic variables and clinical variables， clinical rating scale which is Hamilton depressive rating scale， and Human Superoxide Dismutase ELISA kit. Appropriate statistical tests for continuous and categorical variables were applied； the value of statistical significance was kept as P <0.05. Result： The mean age of the case group i.e. was 31.9 years ±8.26years while that of the control group i.e. was 31.2 years ±7.32 years. The mean serum SOD for patients of depression is 1.52±0.24u/ml which is considered a high value as compared to serum SOD levels in controls which were 1.39±0.34u/ml， which is low. This value differed statistically significantly with a t-value of 2.98 and a p-value of 0.03. Conclusion：There is a greater prevalence of depression among the young population and there is also a slight male preponderance for depression. Contrary to the Western notion that marriage is a protective factor， about half of the study participants with depression were married. Serum Superoxide dismutase levels were significantly higher in depressed patients as compared to healthy controls making it a potential biomarker of depressive disorder in the future， which makes it a good perspective for further research.

【1】KEYWORDS depression， depression investigations， superoxide dismutase in depression

【2】The lifetime prevalence of major depression averages 11.1percent in low-income countries and 14.6 percent in high-income countries. The lifetime rates of major depressive disorder in childhood range from 0.6 to 4.8 percent with a median of 2.2percent.

【3】Depression is a multifactorial disorder whose aetiology in-cludes genetics， environmental， psychological， and biological factors. persistent sadness of mood， low energy levels， and anhedonia primarily characterise depression. Patients of depres-sion may present with a variety of deficits in sleep， appetite， psychomotor activity， and cognition . Studies have shown that the prevalence of lifetime and current MDD in India was5.25% and 2.68%， respectively. Prevalence was highest in the40-59 age groups， among females and those residing in cities with a population >1 million. Age， education， gender， residence and household income were found to be significantly associated with Depressive Disorder 

【4】Currently， there are no clinically relevant predictors of re-sponse for depression patients to one antidepressant compared to others despite contrary claims and recent pharmacological advancements， due to which clinicians have to wait for clinical response. Novel biomarkers that might predict depression and suicidal behaviour are very intriguing， as depression is heavily associated with increasing treatment resistance and increased risk for substance abuse and suicide. Of interest corresponding to the situation is noted that patients with autoimmune disorders have conspicuously high prevalence rates of depressive disor-der. Studies of the present literature supported the abnormal activation of cell-mediated immunity and other autoimmune pathways activation along with different immune biomarkers in the pathophysiological pathways underlying major affective disorders and suicidal behaviour .

【5】Major depression is reportedly associated with inflammatory processes， which include elevated levels of proinflammatory cytokines， decreased neurogenesis， which is followed by neuro progression (including pathological reorganization of the central nervous system)， mitochondrial dysfunction， and the dysfunc-tion of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. In addition， there are also observed lowered antioxidant concentrations and increased oxidative stress levels .

【6】An imbalance between the prooxidant and the antioxidant factors in favour of the prooxidant causes oxidative stress.Ox-idative damage to cells and organs is caused by free radicals(FR) (superoxide， hydroxyl radical) or nonradical molecules，like hydrogen peroxide， and their derivatives called reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reactive nitrogen species (RNS)， which are also expressed in the organism during the standard metabolism. However， if ROS and RNS are produced in large amounts and in the wrong place， they can cause oxidative modifications of lipids， proteins， and DNA. In addition， they can modify the cell membranes causing alteration in the function of receptors and altering enzymes and gene activity. Oxidative stress contributes also to aging .

【7】It is concluded in various studies that， as with many other human diseases， oxidative stress is implicated in many neu-ropsychiatric disorders， including schizophrenia， bipolar disor-der， depression， and Alzheimer’s disease. The brain has a huge amount of oxygen consumption and a lipid-rich environment， so it is highly susceptible to oxidative stress. Both increased production of reactive oxygen species and alterations in antiox-idant defences have been demonstrated in various studies of psychiatric patients. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) is the pri-mary and critical enzyme in detoxifying superoxide radicals and ROS， primarily generated in the most biological reactions of free radical formation. There are inconsistent data on this enzyme activity in patients with psychoses and other psychiatric disor-ders. Since psychotic disorders are heterogeneous disorders and due to their complex pathology， it is not surprising that different authors have found that SOD activity is increased， decreased， or unchanged in the same type of psychosis. 

【8】Superoxide Dismutase (SOD； EC 1.15.1.1) is an enzyme that catalyzes the dismutation of the superoxide radical， into either molecular oxygen or hydrogen peroxide， thus preventing per-oxynitrite production and further damage. Superoxide anion radical (O2.) can be formed by one-electron reduction of the molecular oxygen or by one-electron oxidation of the hydrogen peroxide. It is highly effective in the inactivation of some en-zymes， but it cannot directly oxidize unsaturated fatty acids. In biological systems， it is generated accidentally through the elec-tron transport chain systems in either the endoplasmic reticulum or in the mitochondria via electron leakage from the intermediate electron carriers onto oxygen； via auto-oxidation of redox-active chemicals via glycation of proteins and via thiol oxidation. By various mechanisms， superoxide is generated by oxidases， particularly the xanthine oxidase and NADPH oxidase of the phagocytic cells which are involved in providing an immune re-sponse towards pathogens. During the process of phagocytosis， neutrophils produce approximately 16 times more superoxide than that produced in resting cells. The superoxide produced in this manner allows the phagocytes to kill the various mi-croorganisms in the invading host. Vascular endothelial cells， fibroblasts，lymphocytes， and many other human cells release superoxide involved in intracellular signalling in various physi-ological conditions. Xanthine oxidoreductase (XOR)， which has a key role in purine catabolism， may exist in two forms， xanthine oxidase (XO) and xanthine dehydrogenase(XDH). Reoxidation of fully reduced XO produces two H2O2 and two superoxide radicals ， which may lead to the formation of toxic reactive species. However， the cell initially uses low concentrations of superoxide and hydrogen peroxide to mobilise the antioxida-tive system. Since superoxide is the primary ROS produced from various sources and mechanisms， its dismutation by SOD is extremely important for each cell. There are three forms of superoxide dismutase present in humans. First is the copper-and zinc-containing superoxide dismutase (CuZnSOD/SOD1)， which is localized predominantly in cytoplasmic and nuclear compartments as well as peroxisomes of all mammalian cells， the second one is the manganese superoxide dismutase (Mn-SOD/SOD2) localized within the mitochondrial matrix， and the third is the copper- and zinc containing SOD predominantly found in extracellular compartments (EC SOD/SOD3). CuZn-SOD is present in a eukaryotic cell. It can be inactivated by hydrogen peroxide， leading to the generation of either Cu (II)-OH or its ionized form Cu (II)-O.-. This enzyme can further catalyze the peroxidation of a wide variety of compounds.ER SOD is a homotetrameric glycoprotein with each subunit con- taining a copper and zinc atom which has a high affinity for the heparin sulfate and is known to scavenge the superoxide that is released from the cell surface. Besides EC SOD playing an important role in regulating extracellular superoxide levels， it is also important in the modulation of NO activity. EC SOD is highly expressed in blood vessels which consist of up to 70% of the SOD activity in both pulmonary and systemic arteries. Its expression is mainly regulated by cytokines that increase (IFNy) or decrease (TNFa and TGFB) EC SOD expression. In eukaryotic cells，MnSOD is located in the matrix of mitochondria which is produced constitutively and can also be induced by cytokines(IL-1， TNF) or endotoxin. In addition to cytokines， a wide range of reactive oxygen metabolites， which can be both inducible and basal levels， may induce MnSOD expression in different types of cells that may play a decisive role in the pathogenesis of oxida-tive stress-induced tissue injury . In conclusion， superoxide is one of the main ROS in the cell. As a consequence， superox-ide dismutase (SOD) serves a key antioxidant role. Depression is possibly accompanied by increased ROS production， which causes free radical damage of neurons， causing altered neuro-circuitry. To counter increased ROS， the expression of SOD can be increased .

【9】Methodology

【10】The case-control study was conducted for one year， from June2021 to May 2022 in the Department of Psychiatry， MGM Med-ical College， Indore， Madhya Pradesh， India. The Institutional Ethics Committee clearance was obtained before initiating this study. All patients fulfilling the inclusion criteria and who were present during the study period were enrolled for the study only after obtaining appropriate informed consent. The study re-cruited 154 participants by convenient sampling method based， out of which 34 declined to consent， so they were excluded from the sample. The final sample had 120 participants， which con-sisted of 60 depressed patients diagnosed with depression based on a clinical interview and diagnostic criteria described in the In-ternational Classification of Disorder (ICD 10). Inclusion criteria：Patients aged 18-45 belong to either sex and suffer from major depressive disorders according to the criteria in icd10. Only patients willing to give written， informed consent were enrolled in the study. Exclusion criteria： Patients below 18 years of age or above 45 years of age， suffering from any neurodegenerative disorder and currently on treatment with any anti-inflammatory drugs， antidepressants， antipsychotics， and mood stabilizers were excluded from the study because of the possibility of these drugs interfering with SOD levels.

【11】Study procedure

【12】Written informed consent was obtained after explaining the pro-cedure to the patient and the caregivers. Then， a semi-structured Performa was used to obtain socio-demographic details of the patients， such as age， gender， educational status， marital status， and occupational status. Hamilton depression rating scale was used subsequently. Blood sample (Venous blood) 5ml from both the case and controls will be collected with all aseptic precau-tions in a disposable syringe. After that， it will be transferred into a clot activator (red top) tube and kept for 30 minutes at room temperature. Then centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 10 min-utes， the serum will be drawn by a clean pipette into aliquots. Serum samples will be stored at -20 degree Celsius. The stored serum was later processed via a centrifuge machine， and the serum was analyzed for SOD with an Automated analyzer using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).

【13】Statistical analysis

【14】Statistical analysis was done using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 23.0. All values were expressed as mean± standard deviation. Continuous variables were assessed using the Independent t-test. In addition， a chi-square test was performed in order to test the relationship between categorical variables. A p-value <0.05 was considered to be statistically significant at a confidence limit of 95%.

【15】This is a novel study in Central India assessing the SOD of patients with depression with and without suicide attempts in120 patients. The mean age of the case group  i.e.， indi-viduals having depression， was 31.9 years The finding is similar to Kaplan and Sadock's Comprehensive textbook of Psychiatry10th edition. The mean age of the control group i.e.， indi-viduals without depression， was 31.2 years. For a consistent trend， we require a much larger sample for the study. As per the inclusion criteria， for the participants， the minimum age was18 years， and the maximum age was 45 years in both groups. The gender-wise distribution  revealed a male prepon-derance in both the groups， i.e.， in patients with depression and healthy controls. The males were 32(53.3%) out of 60 in the case group. As for the control group， male preponderance was noted again， with males representing 61.6% of the sample while females representing 38.3%. So the findings reported male domi-nance at 53.3% in patients presenting with a depressive episode， which is contrary to the findings that women have more preva-lence of depression worldwide and in corroboration with Raju et al. The difference in our findings can be explained by the possibility that in the community there might be more prevalence of depression among females but due to the social architecture of Indian society more males seek psychiatric care. Also， male depression affects families more seriously as they might be the family's sole breadwinners， making it more likely for men to seek care during the depression. The study ob-served a high percentage of married individuals constituting both groups； depressive patients (cases) and individuals without depression(controls). Among depressive patients， about 48.3%of individuals were married， while 31.6% were single. Of the remaining， 13.3% were separated， 5% were divorced， and 1%were widowed. Among the control group， 55% were married，35% were single， 6% were separated， 3.3% were divorced， and0% were widowed. Marriage is generally considered to be a pro-tective factor against depression. However， it has also been noted that this does not stand true for developing countries and in our study， we found that 46.7% of married participants were depressed as compared to 50% of single， separated， divorced and widowed participants. Indian culture can understand our findings. Most of the population gets married by the mean age of our study， which is 31.9 for the case group and 31.2 for the control group.  The finding can be explained in the light that in our culture， marriage is often arranged by parents regardless of the mental status of the children. Also， married life adds to the responsibilities of an individual， and this added burden might be a predisposing factor for depressive illness. Also， there is a possibility that depressed individuals are more commonly found to be married than married individuals with depression， as it is a social norm for an individual to get married right in their youth. It was revealed that serum SOD level positively correlates with the HAM-D scores in depressed patients with a Pearson correlation of 0.259， and this correlation is statistically significant with a p-value of 0.05.

【28】Patients with individuals in the Depression group  have shown higher mean serum SOD than the group of individ-uals without depression. The mean serum SOD for individuals with depression was 1.52 ± 0.24 u/mL， while for individuals without depression was 1.39 ±0.34 u/mL. The means differed significantly， with a t-value of 2.34 and a p-value of 0.02. The finding agrees with Tsai MC et al. ， who also reported that serum SOD levels were raised in individuals having depression as compared to individuals without depression. AJ Russo et al. also reported similar results with increased serum SOD in pa-tients with depression. However， our findings are contrary to the results of Herken et al.， which showed decreased levels of superoxide dismutase in depressed patients.

【29】HAM D scores correlated positively with the serum SOD levels. This correlation was statistically significant with a Pearson correlation of 0.259 and p-value of 0.05， which shows that the antioxidant factors can be studied as potential biomark-ers to assess the severity of depression.

【30】Conclusion

【31】There is a greater prevalence of depression among the young population and a slight male preponderance for depression. Contrary to the Western notion that marriage is a protective factor， about half of the study participants with depression were married. Serum Superoxide dismutase levels were significantly higher in depressed patients as compared to healthy controls making it a potential biomarker of depressive disorder in the future.

【32】In our study， there is a lack of longitudinal follow-up， which could have been utilized to compare serum SOD levels before and after an intervention. There is no arbitrary fixed reference value of serum SOD， so we could not draw any inference from the different values observed in cases and controls. There is also a lack of assessment of the serum SOD levels in context to differ-ent aspects of Depression like melancholy， somatic symptoms， insomnia， etc. Other inflammatory conditions could confound inflammatory marker SOD despite strict inclusion criteria. Al-though seemingly large for a study of such a design， the sample size was still small， and we relied on self-reported history of major depressive disorder as the source of information. Future studies could include other methods.

Superoxide anion radical (O2.) can be formed by one-electron reduction of the molecular oxygen or by one-electron oxidation of the hydrogen peroxide. It is highly effective in the inactivation of some en-zymes， but it cannot directly oxidize unsaturated fatty acids. In biological systems， it is generated accidentally through the elec-tron transport chain systems in either the endoplasmic reticulum or in the mitochondria via electron leakage from the intermediate electron carriers onto oxygen； via auto-oxidation of redox-active chemicals via glycation of proteins and via thiol oxidation. By various mechanisms， superoxide is generated by oxidases， particularly the xanthine oxidase and NADPH oxidase of the phagocytic cells which are involved in providing an immune re-sponse towards pathogens. During the process of phagocytosis， neutrophils produce approximately 16 times more superoxide than that produced in resting cells. The superoxide produced in this manner allows the phagocytes to kill the various mi-croorganisms in the invading host. Vascular endothelial cells， fibroblasts，lymphocytes， and many other human cells release superoxide involved in intracellular signalling in various physi-ological conditions. Xanthine oxidoreductase (XOR)， which has a key role in purine catabolism， may exist in two forms， xanthine oxidase (XO) and xanthine dehydrogenase(XDH). Reoxidation of fully reduced XO produces two H2O2 and two superoxide radicals ， which may lead to the formation of toxic reactive species. However， the cell initially uses low concentrations of superoxide and hydrogen peroxide to mobilise the antioxida-tive system. Since superoxide is the primary ROS produced from various sources and mechanisms， its dismutation by SOD is extremely important for each cell. There are three forms of superoxide dismutase present in humans. First is the copper-and zinc-containing superoxide dismutase (CuZnSOD/SOD1)， which is localized predominantly in cytoplasmic and nuclear compartments as well as peroxisomes of all mammalian cells， the second one is the manganese superoxide dismutase (Mn-SOD/SOD2) localized within the mitochondrial matrix， and the third is the copper- and zinc containing SOD predominantly found in extracellular compartments (EC SOD/SOD3). CuZn-SOD is present in a eukaryotic cell. It can be inactivated by hydrogen peroxide， leading to the generation of either Cu (II)-OH or its ionized form Cu (II)-O.-. This enzyme can further catalyze the peroxidation of a wide variety of compounds.ER SOD is a homotetrameric glycoprotein with each subunit con- taining a copper and zinc atom which has a high affinity for the heparin sulfate and is known to scavenge the superoxide that is released from the cell surface. Besides EC SOD playing an important role in regulating extracellular superoxide levels， it is also important in the modulation of NO activity. EC SOD is highly expressed in blood vessels which consist of up to 70% of the SOD activity in both pulmonary and systemic arteries. Its expression is mainly regulated by cytokines that increase (IFNy) or decrease (TNFa and TGFB) EC SOD expression. In eukaryotic cells，MnSOD is located in the matrix of mitochondria which is produced constitutively and can also be induced by cytokines(IL-1， TNF) or endotoxin. In addition to cytokines， a wide range of reactive oxygen metabolites， which can be both inducible and basal levels， may induce MnSOD expression in different types of cells that may play a decisive role in the pathogenesis of oxida-tive stress-induced tissue injury . In conclusion， superoxide is one of the main ROS in the cell. As a consequence， superox-ide dismutase (SOD) serves a key antioxidant role. Depression is possibly accompanied by increased ROS production， which causes free radical damage of neurons， causing altered neuro-circuitry. To counter increased ROS， the expression of SOD can be increased .

【9】Methodology

【10】The case-control study was conducted for one year， from June2021 to May 2022 in the Department of Psychiatry， MGM Med-ical College， Indore， Madhya Pradesh， India. The Institutional Ethics Committee clearance was obtained before initiating this study. All patients fulfilling the inclusion criteria and who were present during the study period were enrolled for the study only after obtaining appropriate informed consent. The study re-cruited 154 participants by convenient sampling method based， out of which 34 declined to consent， so they were excluded from the sample. The final sample had 120 participants， which con-sisted of 60 depressed patients diagnosed with depression based on a clinical interview and diagnostic criteria described in the In-ternational Classification of Disorder (ICD 10). Inclusion criteria：Patients aged 18-45 belong to either sex and suffer from major depressive disorders according to the criteria in icd10. Only patients willing to give written， informed consent were enrolled in the study. Exclusion criteria： Patients below 18 years of age or above 45 years of age， suffering from any neurodegenerative disorder and currently on treatment with any anti-inflammatory drugs， antidepressants， antipsychotics， and mood stabilizers were excluded from the study because of the possibility of these drugs interfering with SOD levels.

【11】Study procedure

【12】Written informed consent was obtained after explaining the pro-cedure to the patient and the caregivers. Then， a semi-structured Performa was used to obtain socio-demographic details of the patients， such as age， gender， educational status， marital status， and occupational status. Hamilton depression rating scale was used subsequently. Blood sample (Venous blood) 5ml from both the case and controls will be collected with all aseptic precau-tions in a disposable syringe. After that， it will be transferred into a clot activator (red top) tube and kept for 30 minutes at room temperature. Then centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 10 min-utes， the serum will be drawn by a clean pipette into aliquots. Serum samples will be stored at -20 degree Celsius. The stored serum was later processed via a centrifuge machine， and the serum was analyzed for SOD with an Automated analyzer using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).

【13】Statistical analysis

【14】Statistical analysis was done using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 23.0. All values were expressed as mean± standard deviation. Continuous variables were assessed using the Independent t-test. In addition， a chi-square test was performed in order to test the relationship between categorical variables. A p-value <0.05 was considered to be statistically significant at a confidence limit of 95%.

【15】This is a novel study in Central India assessing the SOD of patients with depression with and without suicide attempts in120 patients. The mean age of the case group  i.e.， indi-viduals having depression， was 31.9 years The finding is similar to Kaplan and Sadock's Comprehensive textbook of Psychiatry10th edition. The mean age of the control group i.e.， indi-viduals without depression， was 31.2 years. For a consistent trend， we require a much larger sample for the study. As per the inclusion criteria， for the participants， the minimum age was18 years， and the maximum age was 45 years in both groups. The gender-wise distribution  revealed a male prepon-derance in both the groups， i.e.， in patients with depression and healthy controls. The males were 32(53.3%) out of 60 in the case group. As for the control group， male preponderance was noted again， with males representing 61.6% of the sample while females representing 38.3%. So the findings reported male domi-nance at 53.3% in patients presenting with a depressive episode， which is contrary to the findings that women have more preva-lence of depression worldwide and in corroboration with Raju et al. The difference in our findings can be explained by the possibility that in the community there might be more prevalence of depression among females but due to the social architecture of Indian society more males seek psychiatric care. Also， male depression affects families more seriously as they might be the family's sole breadwinners， making it more likely for men to seek care during the depression. The study ob-served a high percentage of married individuals constituting both groups； depressive patients (cases) and individuals without depression(controls). Among depressive patients， about 48.3%of individuals were married， while 31.6% were single. Of the remaining， 13.3% were separated， 5% were divorced， and 1%were widowed. Among the control group， 55% were married，35% were single， 6% were separated， 3.3% were divorced， and0% were widowed. Marriage is generally considered to be a pro-tective factor against depression. However， it has also been noted that this does not stand true for developing countries and in our study， we found that 46.7% of married participants were depressed as compared to 50% of single， separated， divorced and widowed participants. Indian culture can understand our findings. Most of the population gets married by the mean age of our study， which is 31.9 for the case group and 31.2 for the control group.  The finding can be explained in the light that in our culture， marriage is often arranged by parents regardless of the mental status of the children. Also， married life adds to the responsibilities of an individual， and this added burden might be a predisposing factor for depressive illness. Also， there is a possibility that depressed individuals are more commonly found to be married than married individuals with depression， as it is a social norm for an individual to get married right in their youth. 【28】Patients with individuals in the Depression group  have shown higher mean serum SOD than the group of individ-uals without depression. The mean serum SOD for individuals with depression was 1.52 ± 0.24 u/mL， while for individuals without depression was 1.39 ±0.34 u/mL. The means differed significantly， with a t-value of 2.34 and a p-value of 0.02. The finding agrees with Tsai MC et al. ， who also reported that serum SOD levels were raised in individuals having depression as compared to individuals without depression. AJ Russo et al. also reported similar results with increased serum SOD in pa-tients with depression. However， our findings are contrary to the results of Herken et al.， which showed decreased levels of superoxide dismutase in depressed patients.

【29】HAM D scores correlated positively with the serum SOD levels. This correlation was statistically significant with a Pearson correlation of 0.259 and p-value of 0.05， which shows that the antioxidant factors can be studied as potential biomark-ers to assess the severity of depression.

【30】Conclusion

【31】There is a greater prevalence of depression among the young population and a slight male preponderance for depression. Contrary to the Western notion that marriage is a protective factor， about half of the study participants with depression were married. Serum Superoxide dismutase levels were significantly higher in depressed patients as compared to healthy controls making it a potential biomarker of depressive disorder in the future.

【32】In our study， there is a lack of longitudinal follow-up， which could have been utilized to compare serum SOD levels before and after an intervention. There is no arbitrary fixed reference value of serum SOD， so we could not draw any inference from the different values observed in cases and controls. There is also a lack of assessment of the serum SOD levels in context to differ-ent aspects of Depression like melancholy， somatic symptoms， insomnia， etc. Other inflammatory conditions could confound inflammatory marker SOD despite strict inclusion criteria. Al-though seemingly large for a study of such a design， the sample size was still small， and we relied on self-reported history of major depressive disorder as the source of information. Future studies could include other methods.

【0】Background： Congenital factor X deficiency is a rare inherited coagulopathy. Pregnancies in women with this disorder are of-ten associated with adverse outcomes， including miscarriage， premature labor， and hemorrhage during preg nancy and in the peripartum period. The literature on this disorder is sparse and shows a limited number of successful pregnancies in women with factor X deficiency.

【1】Case Report： In this report， we present the case of a successful pregnancy and term delivery by elective cesarean section in a 39-year-old primigravida with congenital factor X deficiency. Medical management followed the recommenda-tions of an interdisciplinary team comprising specialists in obstetrics， anesthesia， transfusion medicine，hema-tology， and neonatology. This high-risk pregnancy was successfully brought to term， and a healthy male neonate was delivered by elective cesarean section at 39 weeks' gestation. The patient's factor X deficiency (0.19 klU/L) was treated using 4 units of solvent-detergent-treated fresh frozen plasma (SD-FFP) 1 h before the cesarean section， leading to hemostatic levels of factor X and an uneventful intraoperative course. Postoperatively， the patient's factor X levels were controlled daily and corrected using SD-FFP as needed， with no clinically signifi- cant blood loss.

【2】Conclusions：

【3】SD-FFP can be used to manage congenital factor X deficiency in the peripartum period and maintain perioper-ative blood loss within normal limits.

【4】MeSH Keywords： Factor X Deficiency · Pregnancy Complications， Hematologic· Pregnancy， High-Risk Factor X is a vitamin K-dependent serum protease synthe sized in the liver . It is the first coagulation factor of the common pathway； once activated， it catalyzes the conver-sion of prothrombin to thrombin . Congenital factor X de-ficiency is a rare coagulation disorder with an incidence of1：1 000 000. The condition is inherited in an autosomal recessive fashion， with homozygous individuals usually show-ing a pronounced bleeding disorder. In heterozygotes， symp-toms can range from no bleeding diathesis to severe hemor-rhage in situations that involve hemostatic challenge， such as surgery or tissue trauma . Although the level of factor X deficiency is not always directly correlated with bleeding dis-order severity， lower factor X levels generally confer a higher risk for hemorrhagic complications .

【5】Menstruation， pregnancy， and childbirth make women with factor X deficiency more susceptible to clinically significant bleeding. In healthy women， factor X progressively increases during normal pregnancy . Starting from a normal value be-tween 50% and 150%， levels rise at 12-30 weeks’ gestation， peaking at an average value of 163%. A second rise occurs144 h postpartum， when levels can reach 173%. After this sec-ondary peak， levels decrease to preconception values within6 weeks . This physiological rise in factor X usually also oc-curs in women with mild-to-moderate factor X deficiency， and rarely in women with severe factor X deficiency.

【6】The relationship between coagulation factors and normal phys-iological changes in pregnancy is complex， and factor X defi-ciency has been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes， including miscarriage， premature labor， and hemorrhage dur-ing pregnancy or in the peripartum period . According to Spiliopoulus et al.， between 1960 and 2018 there were 31re-ported pregnancies in 19 women with factor X deficiency . Four of these 31 (13%) resulted in miscarriage， 4/31 (13%) were associated with vaginal bleeding during pregnancy， 6/31(22%) led to postpartum hemorrhage， and 8 of the successful preg-nancies (8/27； 30%) involved preterm delivery (<37 weeks) .

【7】In the present report， we present a successful pregnancy and term delivery by elective cesarean section in a 39-year-old pri-migravida with congenital factor X deficiency whose peripar-tum factor X levels were increased using solvent-detergent-treated fresh frozen plasma (SD-FFP).

【8】Case Report

【9】A 39-year-old nulliparous woman was referred to our tertiary care center because she had a known history of factor X defi-ciency. Her coagulation disorder was diagnosed at the age of 18 years during a routine preoperative assessment for an elec-tive tonsillectomy. Once discovered， the elective surgery was postponed and molecular diagnostics were performed. These showed that the patient was heterozygous for 2 mutations：MTHFR C677T and PAI-1 4G/5G. Subsequently， other family members were also tested， and it was found that both the patient's sister and nephew were heterozygous for the same mutations； all of these patients had factor X levels of 0.5 klU/L and were therefore diagnosed with mild factor X deficiency.

【10】When asked about her medical history prior to diagnosis of fac-tor X deficiency， the patient reported reoccurring heavy men-strual bleeding， without increased incidence of other signs and symptoms related to her factor X deficiency (i.e.，epistaxis， pete-chiae， hematoma formation， and bruising) and denied other chronic comorbidities. Moreover， no additional bleeding， apart from reoccurring heavy menstrual bleeding， was noticed between the time of diagnosis and the following medical procedures.

【11】At the age of 37 years， the patient underwent a tooth extrac-tion， which was monitored by a transfusion specialist. During that procedure， her coagulation test showed a prothrombin time (PT) of 0.51， an international normalized ratio (INR) of1.4， an activated thromboplastin time (aPTT) of 37.06 s， and a factor X level of 0.25 kIU/L， which prompted the transfusion specialist to recommend administering 10 mL/kg of FFP be-fore the procedure. The procedure was then carried out un-der local anesthesia. No intra- or post-operative complications were reported， and the patient was discharged from the hos-pita! the following day At the age of 38 years， the patient experienced her first preg nancy， which ended in miscarriage at 8 weeks. Due to heavy vaginal bleeding and lack of fetal cardiac activity， medical abortion was performed with 400 mg of misoprostol (Stada， VietNam-Singapore Industrial Park， Binh Duong， Singapore)， administered buccally. No bleeding complications were re-ported and the clinical course did not require administration of FFP or coagulation factors.

【12】The patient's second pregnancy occurred at the age of 39years and was closely monitored by the obstetrician and he-matologists with regular follow-up appointments. No bleeding complications occurred during the pregnancy. However， poly-hydramnion and gestational diabetes developed， with the lat-ter being well controlled with an appropriate diet. During the third trimester， a multidisciplinary team comprising specialists in obstetrics， anesthesia， transfusion medicine， hematology， and neonatology met and devised a thorough plan for safe delivery and postpartum period. The plan included scheduled admission to the hospital at 39 weeks， daily assessments of factor X levels with therapy adjusted accordingly， and term de-livery of the high-risk pregnancy by elective cesarean section.

【15】As scheduled， the patient was admitted to the hospital at 39weeks， weighing 90 kg and with BMI of 32 kg/m2. At that time， the first set of laboratory investigations was made . The patient's coagulation parameters included a prothrombin time of 0.48， an INR of 1.45， an acti-vated thromboplastin time of 36.5 s， and a factor X level of0.19 klU/L. Her levels of fibrinogen， factor ll， and factor VII were slightly elevated， and thrombelastography showed val-ues within the normal range .

【16】Based on the patient's factor X levels， risk of bleeding during obstetric procedures， and the fact that heavy bleeding cannot be fully predicted in cases like this， we decided that she should receive 4 units of SD-FFP 1h before the elective cesarean sec-tion. Two other therapeutic options were discussed： applica-tion of recombinant factor X or prothrombin complex concen-trate (PCC). Although recombinant factor X would have been our first choice， it is， unfortunately， not available in our coun-try. On the other hand， we decided against PCC due to its pos-sible thrombogenic effect， which is especially pronounced in pregnancy. Administration of SD-FFP resulted in factor X lev-els of 0.41 klU/L at the time of the procedure (Table 2， time point： preoperative). In addition， 2 units of packed red blood cells and 6 units of SD-FFP were placed on standby in case she developed bleeding complications during the procedure.

【17】Because the patient had hemorrhagic diathesis， neuraxial anes-thesia might have led to complications. For this reason， the pa-tient was given general anesthesia. Propofol (MCT Fresenius， Bad Homburg， Germany) and rocuronium (MSD， Kenilworth， NJ， USA) were administered intravenously， followed by anesthe-sia and rapid-sequence intubation. Sevoflurane (AbbVieNorth Chicago， IL， USA) was then used to maintain anesthesia， and the obstetricians proceeded with the delivery. Several minutes later， a healthy baby boy was delivered， with an Apgar score of 7/9 and a weight of 3450 g. After the baby was delivered， the anesthesia was augmented with i.v. sufentanil (Hameln， Germany). Intraoperatively， the patient received 15 IU of i.v. oxy-tocin (Syntocinon； Mylan， Canonsburg， PA， USA)， 0.2 mg of i.v. methylergometrine (Demergin； Demo， Germany)， and 800 mg of misoprostol (Stada，VietNam-Singapore Industrial Park， Binh Duong， Singapore)， administered rectally. The rest of the pro-cedure was performed as planned， with no bleeding compli-cations and no need to administer additional blood products.

【19】After an uneventful stay in the postoperative care unit， the pa-tient was discharged to the high-dependency unit (HDU) of the Department of Gynecology and Obstetrics. Over the next5 days， her factor X levels were assessed regularly ， and SD-FFP was adminis-tered as needed. Post-operatively， the patient received a total of 15 units of SD-FFP， with no significant blood loss. She and her healthy son were discharged from the hospital on day 7， with subsequent ambulatory follow-ups.

【20】Discussion

【21】The perioperative blood management approach used by our multidisciplinary team resulted in a successful term delivery and uneventful peripartum period in a patient with factor X defi-ciency， without significant bleeding or thrombotic complications.

【22】Factor X deficiency is a rare inherited coagulopathy， manifest-ed as various degrees of bleeding diathesis . The amount of factor X required to accomplish hemostasis is unknown， but levels of 10-35% are thought to be sufficient . In severe cases of factor X deficiency， bleeding complications can arise cases ending with massive hemorrhage necessitating hyster-ectomy . Moreover， data show a greater incidence of pre-term birth and neonatal death in pregnancies that reached the stage of fetal viability . In summary， women with factor X deficiency have a higher risk for greater hemorrhage during their menstrual cycle， unfavorable pregnancy outcomes， and peripartum bleeding.

【23】The first case of a pregnant woman with factor X deficiency was reported by Brody et al. in 1960 . Konje et al. commented on a young woman with this coagulopathy who developed retroplacental hematomas during pregnancy. During her hos-pitalization， she was treated with Bioproduct Laboratory fac-tor X and there were no complications during her delivery by a cesarean section . Kumar and Mehta described a factor X-deficient woman during her 4 pregnancies who was treated with prophylactic substitute of coagulation factors. Her preg-nancy and delivery ended with a positive outcome with no postpartum complications . Bofill et al. described a factor X-deficient patient in her early twenties who did not receive replenishment with coagulation factors， and the decision was made to treat her with FFP while she was in labor and during the first day after giving birth to her child； there was no sig-nificant blood loss and she delivered a healthy newborn . The present case management was similar to that reported by Venkatesh et al.， in which a young patient with severe fac-tor X deficiency underwent emergency cesarean section after a retroplacental bleed of approximately 50 mL was observed by ultrasound . The patient was at 37 weeks of gestation and was treated with FFP and i.v. tranexamic acid preopera-tively and in the early postoperative period after a healthy baby boy was delivered . In the present case， an elective cesare an section was planned at 39 weeks' gestation. Because the patient had low levels of factor X (0.19 kIU/L)， she was sched-uled to receive 4 units of SD-FFP 1 h before the cesarean sec-tion to elevate her levels of factor X above 50%. In the postop-erative period (during the next 3 days)， she received 15 units of SD-FFP. During the operation and in the postoperative pe-riod， her blood loss was within normal limits . She was discharged from the hospital after 7 days with a healthy baby boy.

【24】Due to limited reported data， there is no agreement regard-ing the recommendation for antenatal prophylaxis in all preg nant women with factor X deficiency. Each pregnant wom-an with factor X deficiency has a unique clinical course and should be managed and treated individually. Antenatal pro-phylaxis should be well planned in each pregnancy with se-vere deficiency， particularly for cases with obstetric complica-tions or bleeding during pregnancy. The hemostatic strategy during delivery should be planned individually considering the level of factor X， maternal loss of blood， and the obstetric pos-sibility of bleeding .

【25】The American Society of Anesthesiologists Task Force on Perioperative Blood Management states that FFP is indicated for correction of excessive microvascular bleeding (i.e.， coagu-lopathy) in the presence of an INR greater than 2.0 or for cor-rection of excessive microvascular bleeding secondary to coag-ulation factor deficiency in patients transfused with more than1 unit of blood volume (approximately 70 ml/kg) and when PT， INR， or PTT cannot be obtained in a timely fashion .

【26】Conclusions

【27】The present case involved a woman with severe factor X de-ficiency who was scheduled for a planned cesarean section. To optimize outcome and minimize the patient's risk for hem-orrhage， a multidisciplinary approach was used： factor Xlev-els were monitored during pregnancy， as well as in the pre-operative and early postoperative period， a predefined labor plan was devised， and intraoperative and early postoperative SD-FFP was used.

【0】ABSTRACT Cardiac surgery is one of the most commonly performed surgeries nowadays - thanks to improved extracorporeal circulation technique， improved postoperative care， and myocardial protection strategy. A cardioplegia solution was conceptualized to stop the heart for surgery and protect the heart. Various modifications of the cardioplegia solution have been made to make it more cardio-friendly. The following review article is a concise review of the evolution of various cardioplegia solutions and their various components.

【1】KEYWORDS cardioplegia， myocardial protection， cardiac surgery

【2】Introduction

【3】Once deemed untouchable， cardiac surgery has become rou-tine 1. One of the important factors for this transformation has been Improved myocardial protection during cardiac surgery. Various techniques of myocardial protection have evolved， like hypothermia， cardioplegia， intermittent cross-clamp fibrillation， ischaemic preconditioning and fibrillatory arrest. Since Melrose published the concept of diastolic cardiac arrest with potassium-containing cardioplegia solution 2， various researchers have been searching for the optimal and best cardioplegia solution for myocardial protection. Hypothermia (as Bigelow showed its cardioprotective role in canine models in 19503) alone was used earlier for cardiac surgery 4. Some studies have shown that myocardial protection by ischaemic preconditioning limits myocardial necrosis during CABG 5.6. On the other hand， phar-macological preconditioning/ hypothermic fibrillation does not offer good myocardial protection6. Intermittent cross-clamp fibrillation is a matter of debate. Earlier studies demonstrated the detrimental effect of fibrillation on the heart"， whereas recent authors again showed interest in fibrillatory arrest810. Among all these techniques， cardioplegia is regarded as the best method available for cardiac arrest as well as myocardial protection.

【4】Free oxygen radicals and intracellular calcium accumu-lation are the main culprits for ischemia-reperfusion injury in arrested hearts11. By creating electromechanical qui-escence of the heart， cardioplegia provides a clear opera-tive field&reduces myocardial oxygen demand， thus limiting ischemic12&reperfusionInjury.

【5】An ideal cardioplegia solution should achieve rapid diastolic arrest， provide good myocardial protection to limit ischaemia reperfusion injury， allow the return of the heart's normal elec-trical activity upon completion of the procedure and be non-toxic14

【6】Cardioplegic solutions cause diastolic arrest by 2 mecha-nisms：

【7】1) high potassium-containing solutions (extracellular plegia-blood plegia， St Thomas I & II， Celsior) reduce membrane po-tential and prevent repolarisation causing persistent membrane depolarization resulting in diastolic arrest. In addition， extra-cellular plegia does not create calcium or sodium gradient in extracellular fluid- hence maintaining equilibration and sub-sequent replacement is easier with them. Furthermore， adding calcium channel blockers or procaine reduces their washout by noncoronary flow15.

【8】2)Low electrolyte-containing solutions (intracellular plegia -HTK， via span) maintain low sodium of extracellular space， caus-ing hyperpolarization of the membrane and resulting in diastolic arrest. Due to Low sodium and calcium content， a large os-molar space is available- which is used to add other protective components like glucose， dextrose， mannitol or histidine with-out excessive hyperosmolarity. Also， a minimal extracellular calcium level will limit contraction or restrict ischemia-induced calcium entry.

【9】Cardioplegia may be administered by 1)antegrade (via aortic root or by individual perfusion of coronary arteries through coronary ostia)，2)retrograde (through coronary sinus) or 3) com-bined 1 routes. Antegrade plegia is commonly used as it is easier to administer and supplies all portions of the heart. In contrast， drawbacks of retrograde plegia are coronary sinus in-jury/ malposition of the cannula & incomplete protection of the myocardium (as only 70% of coronary venous blood drains into the coronary sinus)， leading to RV failure16. However， retro-grade plegia is beneficial in tight coronary ostial stenosis， Type

【10】Peg

【11】A aortic dissection， severe aortic regurgitation， etc. Combined antegrade and retrograde plegia are preferred in severe coronary artery disease17. During retrograde plegia administration， coro- nary sinus pressure should be below 50 mm of Hg to prevent maldistribution and/or coronary sinus injury. During antegrade root perfusion， 150ml/min/m2 BSA flow is maintained， and pressure is maintained below 75 mm of Hg. Direct ostial plegia should also be given cautiously to prevent ostial injury and later stenosis.

【12】Plegia solution may contain the patient’s blood from the CPB circuit ( Blood cardioplegia) as in Buckbergplegial8， Calafiore plegia19， Del Nido plegia20， or it may be administered with-out blood as in crystalloid plegia(St Thomas 2， HTK， Viaspan， CELSIOR)21.

【13】Cardioplegia temperature may be adjusted to be admin-istered as warm2223or tepid24， or cold2& may be adminis-tered continuously or intermittently26 in single or multiple re-peated doses. All crystalloid cardioplegias are administered cold (@4℃)， and blood cardioplegia can be administered ei-ther cold/tepid/warm1922，23，2425，26. The benefits of single-dose plegia are a)eliminates drawbacks of replegia like time wastage & surgical field reorientation， b)useful in minimally invasive cardiac surgery， and c)in Bentall/arterial switch oper-ation with unstable coronary ostial6， whereas benefits of inter-mittent/continuous plegia are washing out metabolites/toxic substances，providing continuous nutrition to arrested heart and maintaining uniform myocardial temperature-9.26.

【14】Table 1 shows the composition of various blood cardioplegia solutions & Table 2 shows the composition of various crystal-loid cardioplegia solutions. In contrast， Table 3 shows various crystalloid solutions used as base solutions for the preparation of cardioplegia.

【15】Melrose Solution

【16】A high potassium-containing solution was used for cardiac ar-rest. However high potassium itself， along with the hypertonic-ity of the solution， contributed to poor outcomes. Hence it was abandoned.

【17】Birmingham Solution 37

【18】Conti and colleagues developed it. The addition of glucose as a myocardium substrate led to the GIK solution's foundation.

【19】GIK/University Of Minnesota Solution 38

【20】This plegia solution was used extensively at the University of Minnesota (Minneapolis， MN) for many years. GIK solutions were prepared fresh to prevent insulin degradation. However， GIK solutions were insufficient for hearts with marginal LV function or for long periods of ischemia (> 120 min).

【21】St Thomas I 34

【22】St. Thomas I cardioplegic solution has been used worldwide since 1975. The plegia was prepared by adding a 20 ml solution containing potassium chloride 16 mmol/L， magnesium chloride16 mmol/L， and procaine 1 mmol/L to 1 L of Ringer'ssolution.

【23】St Thomas II 34

【24】In 1981， St Thomas I was modified with a significant reduction of calcium by 50%， omission of procaine， the addition of bicarbon-ate， a small reduction in the sodium and potassium content and adjustment of ph to 7.8， leading to the formulation of St ThomasⅡ solution， which was used all over the world then & is still used now. It is also used as a base mix for the cold blood cardioplegia solution proposed by Buckberg and colleagues. St Thomas II is usually given @4-6℃. Initially， 1000 ml is administered for a 70-kg adult， followed by 100 ml infusions intermittently every15 to 20 min， along with topical hypothermia to maintain the heart's temperature below 15℃.

【25】Buckberg Plegia

【26】Since Buckberg26 introduced the concept of plegia containing a patient's blood from the CPB circuit， it has been used in adult and pediatric cardiac surgery till today.

【27】The ratio of blood to crystalloid solution has been -4 parts blood to 1 part crystalloid cardioplegia. It was applied @ be-tween 4 and 6℃ to decrease myocardial temperature below15℃. The significant advantage of cold blood cardioplegia over crystalloid cardioplegia is that it is considered to provide oxy-gen and nutrients to the ischemic myocardium and offers op-timal buffering capacity. From cold blood plegia， the trend is shifted to warm blood cardioplegia1922232439 Modified Buckbergcardioplegia-is the dextrose-based solution in normal saline where potassium chloride acts as a depolarizing agent， and tromethamine performs buffering and citrate double phos-phate dextrose acts as a calcium chelator. It is delivered in a 4：1CPB blood-to-crystalloid ratio. The modified Buckberg cardio-plegia solution is modified to three distinct solutions： induction， maintenance and reperfusion. During the initiation of plegia， a dose of induction solution is given to arrest the heart， and after that， maintenance solution is administered every 15-20minutes during the course of the operation. Both are delivered at 4℃. The reperfusion“hot shot" is delivered at37°C just be-fore removal of the aortic cross-clamp. The reperfusion solution provides glutamate & aspartate to the heart.

【28】Del Nido Plegia

【29】Del Nido cardioplegia was developed by Pedro J. Del Nido and his team at the University of Pittsburgh in the 1990s20. Though It was invented for pediatric cardiac surgery， it is also being used successfully for in adult cardiac surgery32，33，40. The cardioplegia to autologous blood from CPB circuit ratio is 4：1. One single dose of 20 ml/kg is supposed to provide optimal myocardial protec-tion for 90 min. The administration pressure is 100-200 mmHg， and the administration flow is 200-300 ml/min. The potassium concentration is > 25 meq/l. The achieve myocardial tempera-ture is <15℃. Each ingredient plays an important role in the car-dioprotection strategy. Mannitol maintains Osmotic pressure&acts as a free-radical scavenger， MgSO4 is a Calcium channel blocker& improved myocardial recovery， NaHCO3 maintains PH， KCl is responsible for Myocardial depolarization， Lidocaine acts as a Sodium channel blocker& hyperpolarizing agent.

【30】Various modification has been made to the original Del Nido solution. NS solution27， Whole blood2or RL solution30 is used instead of Plasmalyte A solution with a comparable result.

【31】Calafiore Plegia

【32】Calafiore blood plegial is administered @ 10℃， and septal my-ocardial temperature is maintained @ 17-20C. For adults， 900ml is initially administered @ 300 ml/minute， followed by 200ml of the same solution after adequate intervals. It offers similar protection during CABG in acute coronary syndrome compared to traditional blood cardioplegia31.

【0】Background：

【1】POEMS syndrome is a rare systemic pathology of paraneoplastic origin that is associated with plasma cell dys-crasia. It is characterized by the presence of sensorimotor polyneuropathy organomegaly， endocrinopathy monoclonal gammopathy skin changes， and other systemic manifestations. The pathogenesis of the syndrome is unknown but over-production of vascular endothelial growth factor is probably responsible for most of the more characteristic symptoms.

【2】There is no standard treatment for POEMS syndrome and no randomized controlled clinical trials of treatment exist in the available literature. High-dose melphalan with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation should be considered for younger patients with widespread osteosclerotic lesions， and for patients with rap-idly progressive neuropathy.

【3】Case Report：

【4】This is the case of a 62-year-old Caucasian man who was admitted to our center presenting pretibial edema accompanied by significant weight loss and difficulty walking. POEMS criteria were present and an immuno-fixation test confirmed the presence of a monoclonal plasmaproliferative disorder. After autologous hemato-poietic stem cell transplantation， the monoclonal component disappeared and the patient’s clinical status im-proved markedly.

【5】Conclusions

【6】Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation following high-dose melphalan is an effective therapy for younger patients with widespread osteosclerotic lesions in POEMS syndrome.

【7】MeSH Keywords：

【8】Paraproteinemias· POEMS Syndrome · Polyneuropathies· Transplantation， Autologous·Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A

【9】POEMS syndrome (polyneuropathy，organomegaly， endocrinop-athy， monoclonal gammopathy， and skin changes)， also known in the literature as Crow-Fukase or Takatsuki syndrome， is a rare multi-systemic disorder associated with osteosclerotic my-eloma， a variant of plasma cell dyscrasia . The syndrome's most prominent clinical characteristic is polyneuropathy of sub-acute or chronic evolution， with marked motor predom-inance， which is almost always the reason the patients seek medical attention .

【10】In 1938， Scheinker was the first to describe the association between plasmacytoma and sensorimotor polyneuropathy . In 1956， Crow wrote a detailed description of 2 cases in which new osteosclerotic bone lesions and neuropathy coexisted， as well as edema in the ankles， feet， and legs， adenopathies in different regions， skin changes， and dulling or discoloration of the nails . Some years later， Bardwick et al.， coined the acronym POEMS by which it is known today， and which defines the syndrome's main characteristics. However， there are many other clinical manifestations not included in the name ， which is why Dispenzieri et al.  pro-posed a set of diagnostic criteria based on clinical findings in different patient series， that set out to encompass POEMS'entire symptomatic spectrum. Since then， these criteria have been updated several times . Currently， polyneuropathy and monoclonal gammopathy are the mandatory criteria for diagnosis， together with the presence of 1 of the other 3 main criteria and 1 of the 6 minor criteria.

【11】POEMS syndrome's pathogeny is complex and remains unclear. Diverse studies have stressed that patients present high lev-els of proangiogenic and proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-1B， TNF-o， or IL-6. These interleukins stimulate production of plasmacytoma-secreted vascular endothelial growth fac-tor (VEGF)， which has been found to be equally high in many POEMS patients . This factor， as its name indicates，targets endothelial cells， inducing the cell proliferation and increased capillary permeability responsible for most of the syndrome's characteristic manifestations. Several researchers have pro-posed that there may be a close relation between IL-6 levels and VEGF， and the diseases activity .

【12】At present， treatment of POEMS syndrome is not well estab-lished. The mode of therapy is based on whether the patient has limited or widespread sclerotic bone lesions. Radiotherapy is the treatment of choice in cases of single sclerotic bone le-sions or whenever the syndrome occurs within a limited area. In the case of widespread lesions， chemotherapy regimes based on alkylating agents (cyclophosphamide or melphalan) have been used alone or in combination with corticosteroids. which achieve clinical improvement in about 40% of patients . Plasmapheresis and immunoglobulins administered in-travenously have proved ineffective. In patients aged under70 years and free of contraindications， chemotherapy at high doses is the first option， followed by autologous hematopoi-etic stem cells transplantation (HSCT) .

【13】Here， we report a case treated with autologous hematopoiet-ic stem cell transplantation.

【14】Case Report

【15】This is the case of a 62-year-old male patient， a farmer， with antecedents of arterial hypertension， dyslipidemia， diabetes mellitus type 2， and bilateral carotid arteriopathy， who was hospitalized with intense fatigue and pretibial edemas， to-gether with considerable weight loss and general malaise. The patient also complained of increasing difficulty walking.

【16】Initial exploration substantiated his ambulation difficulty and identified surface sensitivity disorders in both legs， which were painful and proprioceptive， together with a reduction in bilateral tendon reflexes. Blood analysis discovered thrombosis (655 000platelets/ul； \[normal： 140 000-450 000/ul\])，increased plasma creatinine (2.3 mg/dl； mg/dl\]) and decreased vitamin B12 (176 ng/ml；ng/dl\]). Hormonal study found au-toimmune primary hypothyroidism (T4： 0.67 ng/dl ng/dl\]； TSH： 7.4 pUl/m! pUI/ml\]； anti-TPO antibodies：80 UI/ml \[<35UI/ml\]). A computerized tomography (CT) scan of the thorax and abdomen was made， which substantiated the presence of cardiomegaly， diverse mediastinal adenopathies， condensation at the base of the left lung with an associated small pleural effusion， slight pericardial effusion， slightly en-larged liver without evidence of any space-occupying lesion， discrete splenomegaly， and presence of non-predominant flu-id in the perihepatic space， right paracolic gutter， and pelvis.

【17】Due to the patient's clinical neurology， a neurophysical exam-ination was performed， which verified the existence of senso-rimotor-predominant demyelinating polyneuropathy.

【18】The patient improved initially and sustained a stable clini-cal evolution after diuretic treatment， normalization of the thyroid function， and corticosteroids at low doses， and was discharged from hospital. Some months later， the patient returned to hospital as previously arranged to complete diag-nosis， which confirmed a worsening of the edema and walk-ing difficulties after stopping the corticosteroid treatment. Furthermore， we observed hypertrichosis on the thorax， ab-domen， and upper and lower limbs， with increasing skin pig-mentation， which was striking ， together with sclero-dermiform dry hands with leukonychia. Analysis identified an exacerbation of renal insufficiency， as well as an increase in

【19】β2-microglobulin (6.58 mg/L mg/L\]) and hyperpro-lactinemia (472 pUl/ml pUl/ml\]). Bone scintigraphy was performed， which found no evidence of defined osteolyt-ic lesions， but did show a diffusely increased uptake affecting the whole skeleton， with a small area of slight focal increased uptake at the first sacral vertebra (S1) midline. When the CT bone window was examined， small sclerotic-appearing focal lesions measuring a few millimeters were identified that af-fected the axial skeleton， particularly the vertebrae (main-ly second dorsal and fourth lumbar vertebrae - D2 and L4). Sclerotic foci were also observed on the sternum and pelvic bones. An immunofixation test confirmed lamb-da light-chain restriction (69.07 mg/Lmg/L\]) and IgA monoclonal bands.

【20】Once the diagnosis of POEMS had been established， the pa-tient was treated with high-dose melphalan l.V. (200 mg/m²)， followed by autologous hematopoietic stem cells transplanta-tion (HSCT)， as the patient fulfilled the requirements for this procedure (age <70 years； disseminated bone lesions； absence of significant organ involvement). Six months after the pro-cedure， the patient showed a notable clinical improvement； the peripheral neuropathy had disappeared (normalization in neurophysical assessment) and so had the skin changes. In time， the rest of the clinical and analytical mani-festations went into remission， and this included the absence of the monoclonal component as shown by immunofixation testing. In later periodic check-ups， the patient remained clini-cally asymptomatic， without relapse of either plasma cell dys-crasia or related POEMS manifestations.

【21】Discussion

【22】The present case report of POEMS syndrome with widespread osteosclerotic lesions describes how the patient underwent a noticeable clinical improvement following autologous hema-topoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT).

【23】POEMS syndrome is a rare multisystemic disease that is diffi-cult to diagnose due to its low incidence， the diversity of af-fected organs and systems， and the variability of its clinical manifestations . Thus， diagnosis is often delayed and in this case diagnosis took 16 months. This situation coincides with most of the cases described in the literature， in which diagnosis took around 15 months after the first appearance of symptoms， even in health centers with ample experience with this syndrome .

【24】Polyneuropathy， which is a key criterion for diagnosis， is the syndrome's most frequent and disabling manifestation and its dominant paraneoplastic symptom. As in the present case， polyneuropathy is usually the first clinical manifestation to appear. This is a sensorimotor， demyelinating polyneuropathy that affects the lower limbs. Motor involvement follows the sensory symptoms. Both are distal， symmetric， and progres-sive， with a gradual proximal spread. Severe weakness occurs in more than half of patients and results in an inability to am-bulate . Thus， the present case presented typical clinical and electrophysiological findings.

【25】The presence of a monoclonal plasma cell disorder is a further diagnostic criterion. The monoclonal component is usually of immunoglobulin (Ig) type A， almost always with lambda light-chain restriction， differentiating the syndrome from multiple myeloma， in which light chains are of the kappa type. Another important difference between POEMS and multiple myelo-ma is that Bence-Jones protein is infrequent and that in bone marrow biopsies， plasma cell content is less than 5%. In the present case the biopsy was negative. The monoclonal com-ponent is usually low in quantity and sometimes almost unde-tectable in proteinograms. For this reason， when the presence of POEMS is suspected， immunofixation testing must be per-formed . In our patient， proteinograms were repeated-ly normal， so an immunofixation test was carried out that con-firmed the presence of lgA monoclonal bands and lambda light chains (69.07 mg/L mg/L). However， in about 15%of cases no monoclonal protein is detected even by immuno-fixation . In these cases， biopsy of a sclerotic， osteolyt-ic， or mixed bone lesion reveals a clone. Finally， there are rare cases in which there are no bone lesions； in such cases， blind iliac crest bone marrow biopsy often detects a small clone.

【26】With regard to bone affectation， the characteristic manifestation is single or various， pure or mixed， osteosclerotic focal lesions that show in radiography as a radiolucent central component ringed by a sclerotic margin， which differs from the pure os-teolytic appearance of classic myeloma. The lesions are found predominantly in the axial and proximal appendicular skeleton and may appear years before diagnosis. The cranium usually remains free of lesions . In the present case， multiple foci of osteosclerotic appearance were seen affecting various ver-tebral bodies， the sternum， and pelvic bone . In ad-dition to these manifestations， the patient fulfilled a number of the other diagnostic criteria established by Dispenzieri et al.， among which the most significant were hepatospleno-megaly， adenopathies， edema in the lower limbs， pleural and pericardia effusions， ascites， endocrinopathy (hyperprolac-tinemia)， skin changes (hypertrichosis and hyperpigmenta-tion)， and thrombocytosis As well as constituting a major diagnostic criterion， bone af-fectation is highly significant because its spread determines the therapeutic approach. Although no randomized controlled trials have been conducted in patients with POEMS syndrome， some case series have documented important clinical bene-fits from the use of intensive chemotherapy (high-dose mel-phalan) followed by autologous HSCT in the case of dissem-inated lesions . Jaccard et al.  reported the first case series of high-dose therapy and autologous HSCT in patients with POEMS syndrome， in which 5 patients received high-dose melphalan (140-200 mg/m?) followed by autologous HSCT. No deaths from drug toxicity occurred during mobilization or transplantation， and in all cases the treatment produced re mission of plasma cell proliferation associated with marked improvement in the patients' performance status， neurologic symptoms， and other manifestations of the syndrome. Clinical remission continued during the 36-month follow-up， and no patient experienced a relapse either of plasma cell dyscrasia or of related POEMS manifestations. In another study from the Mayo Clinic， 16 patients were treated with autologous HSCT； 14 evaluated patients achieved substantial neurologic improvement or stabilization of neuropathic deficits， and 5 of6 patients with a quantifiable serum M protein level achieved a hematologic complete response . Moreover， autologous HSCT also improved organomegaly， extravascular volume over-load， skin changes， and papilledema. However， HSCT was as-sociated with a high risk of transplant-related toxicities in the early post-transplant period. Six patients were admitted to the intensive care unit， 5 required intubation and mechanical ven-tilation during mobilization and transplantation， and 1 died115 days after HSCT.

【27】The largest series was a report of 59 patients with POEMS syn-drome treated with autologous HSCT using peripheral blood stem cells by the same Mayo Clinic group . Clinical improve-ment was nearly universal in these patients. They found that92% of patients achieved clinical responses， and the most rap-id responses were seen as soon as 100 days after transplan-tation. Maximal neurologic improvement was often not seen until 3 years afterward. After a median follow-up period of 45months， the 5-year overall and progression-free survival rates were 94 and 75%， respectively. Three patients died-1 patient died early， another died from relapse and disease progression4 years after transplantation， and a third died of lymphoma unrelated to POEMS syndrome. Of the 14 patients with pro-gressive disease post-transplant， none had clinical symptoms； instead， the progressions manifested as hematologic abnor-malities， radiographic findings， or increased VEGF levels.

【28】Other reports of autologous HSCT in POEMS syndrome have also described clinical improvement， with often dramatic

【29】In subsequent 24-month follow-up， our patient remained clin-ically asymptomatic， without relapse of either plasma cell dys-crasia or related POEMS manifestations. Moreover， no signifi-cant toxicity associated with the procedure occurred.

【30】Although this report only describes the case of a single patient， it agrees with other studies in supporting autologous hema-topoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) following high-dose melphalan as an important therapy for younger patients with POEMS syndrome who present multifocal bone lesions and/or diffuse plasmacytic bone marrow infiltration.

【31】Conclusions

【32】This case report describes an effective therapeutic option for patients with this serious but little known condition. Given that to date no standard treatment for this disorder has been estab-lished and there have been no randomized controlled clinical trials of POEMS syndrome treatment， therapeutic approaches can only be guided by the experiences recounted in the ret-rospective and observational studies available at the present time. In this context， the present case report coincides with and supports the results obtained in previous studies， which endorse HSCT in combination with an intensive chemothera-py regimen as one of the most active and effective therapies for the disseminated form of POEMS syndrome. Prospective treatment trials are needed to generate further evidence of the long-term clinical efficacy of HSCT for treating this syndrome.
