【5】Key words： sacrococcygeal teratoma · presacral teratoma · gynaecological laparoscopy Most teratomas occur in ovaries and testes of adolescents and originate from germ-cells. Teratomas can also be found in midline structures： sacrococcygeal， presacral， retroperitone um， postanal or even anterior mediastinum and pineal gland. Teratomas of non-gonadal location originate from embry-onic cells. Various theories try to explain the origin of terato-mas. The pathogenesis is generally thought to be a growth of primitive totipotential cells that have differentiated and ma-tured. According to the germ cell theory the totipotential cell is a “wandering germ cell" left behind during migration of embryonic germ cells from yolk sac to the gonad. According to the most popular theory the source of totipotential cells is a residual cell from the primitive streak and Hansen node of very early embryonic development. Normally， this primi-tive structure degenerates， however remains may persist in the sacrococcygeal region and develop into teratomas. There is also the theory that teratomas might be the result of twin-ning attempts .

【6】Familial form of presacral teratomas，inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern， has been reported. They differ from usual teratomas because of nearly equal sex prevalence， a low prev-alence of malignancy and a sacral defect .

【7】Primary presacral teratomas are extremely rare in adults. Teratomas of such localization appear in neonates and young adults. Sacrococcygeal teratomas are most commonly found in neonates， infants and children younger than four years. They appear with incidence of approximately 1：35，000-40，000 live births and a female to male ratio 4：1 . Most changes can be diagnosed prenatally， 50-70% are found during first few days of life， less than 10% are diagnosed beyond the age of two years . Malignant transformation has been found in ap-proximately 1% of teratoma patients comprising squamous cell carcinoma， adenocarcinoma， sarcoma and other malignancies. 【8】Tumours of sacrococcygeal location originate ventral or dorsal to the sacrum， they may grow posteroinferiorly into the gluteal area or anterosuperiorly into the lesser pelvis. Especially in the ventral location these tumours may grow to a large size as they develop into the retrorectal or presacral space 5.

【9】Altman et al. classifies sacrococcygeal teratomas. They marked out 4 categories by location. Type l are predominantly exter-nal tumours with minimal presacral component. Type ll pres-ents externally but with significant intrapelvic extension. Type Ill is still apparent externally but predominantly a pelvic mass extends into the abdomen. Type lV is a presacral mass with no external presentation. Our case conform type Ⅳ of Altman's classification， although most common in adults is type I .

【10】Case Report

【11】A 26-year-old woman， nulliparous， reported with abdominal pain occurring on the right side for about 11 months. 【13】MIEDNICA

【14】In April 2011 the patient was admitted to the Department of Operative Gynaecology. Abdominal pain was still reported. The abdomen was soft with mild lower abdominal tenderness on the right during examination. The gynaecological examination revealed normal size uterus， anteflexion， shifted to the left. The adnexa of uterus were without palpable changes. 【16】Discussion

【17】Sacrococcygeal teratoma might be asymptomatic in adults； usually it is detected by chance during imaging studies or clin-ical examination. Symptoms may be subtle and nonspecific as result of compression of adjacent structures： rectum， bladder or uterus . Such symptoms are： lower back and pelvic pain， constipation， sensation of incomplete evacuation， narrowed stools or incontinence. Frequent urination， dysmenorrhoea， nausea， vomiting， oedema and lower extremity paraesthesia have been observed . Cases of perinatal complications have been reported . In cases of external growth of the tu-mour overlaying skin might be puckered and discoloured .

【18】Differentiation between cystic changes in ovary and presacral re-gion is extremely difficult； it might even be a diagnostic challenge. In this area we can distinguish the following types of changes：congenital， inflammatory， neurogenic， osseous and miscellaneous. Conducting differential diagnosis should be considered： con-genital abnormalities， cystic changes in the ovaries， meningocele， rectal duplication， tailgut cyst， neurogenic tumours， osseous le-sions， renal cysts， Wilms’ tumour， soft tissue tumours such as lymphangioma， sarcoma， mucinous adenocarcinoma， cystic me-sothelioma， the Mullerian ducts cyst， epidermal cyst， enlarged lymph nodes and metastatic tumours of the uterus or ovaries. The most common tumours that develop in retro-peritoneal space are the lymph nodes modified by metastases.

【19】Differentiating presacral changes Currarino syndrome (Currarino anomaly CA) should also be taken into account. Syndrome is autosomal dominant disorder with mutation in homeobox gene HLXB9 located at the 7q36 locus. It is characterized by three main clinical features： presacral tumour， poorly developed sa-crum (sacral agenesis)， and malformations of the anus and rec-tum . The most common symptom is chronic constipation.

【20】In the case of accompanying inflammation the differential diagno-sis is even more difficult and may be misdiagnosed as high lying pararectal abscess， fistulas， granulomas or even tuberculosis .

【21】Imaging studies should include transvaginal and transrectal ultrasound， computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging， which are useful in identifying the exact location and suggest character of the tumour. Such diagnostics is helpful for determining the optimal surgical procedure. Laboratory tests levels of AFP， BhCG， CEA， Ca-125， CA19-9 and CA 15-3 should be done in case of suspicion of malignant transformation . Colonoscopy and sigmoidoscopy should also be considered.

【22】During childhood， 85% of the presacral cysts are benign， but the risk of malignant transformation increases with age. It must be remembered in the case of adults. The definitive di-agnosis is possible only after histopathological examination of the changes. Therefore the lesion should always be surgi-cally removed. Drainage or biopsy is not recommended .

【23】Due to the rarity of reported changes no firm guidelines exist. In the literature， depending on the anatomical con-ditions，descriptions of various surgical procedures are report-ed. They include anterior abdominal approach， post anal and combined access， also laparoscopic-assisted approach. If re-moval of the coccyx and the part of the lower sacrum is nec-essary sacral nerves should be preserved . In case of large tumours located in the abdominal cavity anterior abdominal approach was usually chosen and for changes with external extension posterior access. Reports of massive intraoperative haemorrhage associated with removal of the sacrococcygeal cysts forced changes in the surgical procedures . Bentley was the first to apply ligation of the median sacral artery be-fore attempted resection of the tumour. Then it was recom-mended to use of vascular clamp above the aortic bifurcation or encircling the distal aorta with a vasculartie. Although these techniques are logical and ensure safety， they require a lap-arotomy. When benefits of laparoscopy were realized， it was performed as assisting surgical procedure prior to the remov-al of the lesion from posterior sacrococcygeal approach. The median sacral artery was laparoscopically supplied， and then the tumour was removed via posterior approach， which sig nificantly reduced the number of complications， such as intra-operative haemorrhage . It resulted in more common usage of laparoscopy and combination of different surgical approaches. Just a few descriptions of procedures performed only by laparoscopy are reported. The first description of the laparoscopic removal of the retroperitoneal cyst comes from1995 . Since then， we find in the literature 3 further cas-es of presacral teratomas treated by laparoscopic surgery .

【25】Decision of laparoscopic surgery is certainly a challenge. 【0】ABSTRACT Spontaneous haemothorax is a clinical entity encompassing non traumatic accumulation of blood within the pleural space. Although hemothorax is often encountered in clinical practice， spontaneous hemothorax is an infrequent occurrence. Cases of spontaneous hemothorax have known to occur secondary to coagulopathy， malignancy， av malformations， pulmonary infarction and tuberculosis. The neoplasms known to be associated with hemothorax include schwannomas， Hepatocellular carcinoma and soft tissue tumors. lung carcinoma is a rare cause of hemothorax even in the setting of pleural extension. Here we highlight the importance of diagnosis spontaneous hemothorax in case of a primary lung malignancy.

【1】A 75 year old woman with no significant past medical history who presented to the ED with chest pain， was initially diagnosed with a pulmonary embolism. As a part of the work up for cause of pulmonary emboli in this otherwise IO healthy woman， a CT chest performed revealed an incidentally found right hilar lung mass and she was scheduled for an outpatient workup. A month later， she developed shortness of breath and presented to the ED before her scheduled appointment. A large pleural effusion was seen on the repeat CT chest. She underwent thoracocentesis， with pleural studies consistent with hemothorax. Eventually， she underwent endobronchial ultrasound with biopsy of lung mass. Based on the histopathology findings， she was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. We concluded that she likely experienced spontaneous hemothorax secondary to lung adenocarcinoma.

【2】To our knowledge there have been three other case reports of spontaneous hemothorax secondary to bronchogenic carcinoma. Cases of hepatocellular carcinoma with hemothorax have been known to have poor prognosis. Being uncommon， the prognostic implication of spontaneous hemothorax in primary lung malignancies has not been studied. Recognition of hemothorax in these patients can alter the course of management.

【3】Introduction

【4】While Hemothorax is a common entity found in clinical practice， the most common cause is trauma . Spontaneous hemotho- rax is a rare diagnosis， and spontaneous hemothorax secondary to cancer is an even rarer entity. The malignant causes for re-ported in the literature include schwannomas， hepatocellular carcinoma， choriocarcinoma and soft tissue tumours like an-giosarcoma . It is mostly seen secondary to rupture of pleural adhesions secondary to a pneumothorax. To our knowledge， there have been four case reports of spontaneous hemothorax secondary to bronchogenic carcinoma. Here we present a case of a 75-vear-old woman who presents to us with spontaneous hemothorax， eventually diagnosed to have primary lung adeno-carcinoma.

【8】Case presentation

【9】This is a 75-year-old female who presented to us with short-ness of breath.This patient came to our ED after being re-cently diagnosed with pulmonary embolism at an outside hos-pital. As a part of the workup for secondary causes， a CT scan chest revealed an incidentally found right lung mass with lym-phadenopathy. She was advised for an endobronchial ultra-sound with biopsy as an outpatient procedure. She was started on dabigatran for the PE and discharged.

【10】Meanwhile， at home， she developed shortness of breath about two weeks after discharge， before her scheduled EBUS. It pro-gressively worsened over 3-4 days. She was found to be hypoxic and tachypneic at pre-op testing for EBUS and was referred to the ED. In the ED， she had an oxygen saturation of 82% on room air， requiring supplemental oxygen via a nasal cannula which brought up her saturation to 95. She admits to having a poor appetite and reports 50lbs weight loss in the month prior to presentation to ED. she denies acute fever， chest pain， nausea， vomiting， dysuria or changes in her bowel habits. She had 50pack-year smoking history. After performing a chest CT in ED， she was found to have a massive right-sided pleural effusion and right lower lobe mass.

【11】A chest tube was inserted， draining 1.7 L of the grossly bloody fluid. Her pleural fluid studies are as presented in the table be-low： Pleural fluid cytology was positive for malignant cells. CK7positive CK20 weak blush TTF1 focal weak positive Napsin She underwent EBUS with biopsy and found to have adenocarci-noma on the histopathological exam. She was diagnosed with spontaneous hemothorax secondary to lung adenocarcinoma and referred to oncology

【12】Discussion

【13】Spontaneous hemothorax (SH) is a clinical entity encompassing non-traumatic accumulation of blood within the pleural space. It is defined as a pleural fluid with a hematocrit more significant than 50% of the patient's blood hematocrit . The most com-mon cause of spontaneous pneumohemothorax is the rupture of pleural adhesions in a spontaneous pneumothorax . SH， by itself， is very rare. Cases of spontaneous hemothorax have known to occur secondary to complications of anticoagulation therapy， coagulopathy， malignancy， arteriovenous malforma-tion， pulmonary embolism with infarction， and tuberculosis . The most common neoplasms associated with hemothorax in-clude schwannomas of von Recklinghausen disease， sarcomas， angiosarcomas， and hepatocellular carcinomas. Lung cancer is a rare cause of hemothorax， even in the setting of pleural ex-tension . The data on hemothorax secondary to neoplasia is limited to only case reports and case series. De France described the first case in 1974， who described two cases of spontaneous hemothorax， one secondary to choriocarcinoma and one sec-ondary to splenic artery rupture . Other notable cases worth mentioning include the occurrence of spontaneous hemothorax in cases of pleuropulmonary angiosarcoma  and carcinosar-coma . Describing the unusual cases of angiosarcoma and cystic chondroblastoma presenting as spontaneous hemothorax， Varsano et al. recognize the rarity of spontaneous true hemoth-orax as a presenting manifestation， especially of cancer . A review of databases including PubMed showed that there had been four case reports of bronchogenic carcinoma patients with spontaneous hemothorax， three of which were secondary to ade-nocarcinoma and one due to large cell carcinoma . The patients described by Kamiyoshihara  and Ausin et al. had a poor prognosis， with death within seven weeks and five weeks of diagnosis respectively， and suspected mechanism being an invasion of tumour into blood vessels. The mechanism of cancer-causing hemothorax remains unclear. Possible mecha-nisms could be torn adhesions， ischemic necrosis of lung tissue or tumour invasion of pulmonary vessels . In this case， there was no evidence suggesting pneumothorax or involvement of blood vessels. We believe in this case； hemothorax could be possibly secondary to surface vessels on the tumour.

【14】Conclusion

【15】Due to its rarity， we have limited understanding of spontaneous hemothorax in lung cancer. From the case reports cited so far， it appears that patients of lung cancer with hemothorax have a poor prognosis. The finding of hemothorax in these patients can serve as an essential prognostic or predictive marker and guide treatment. This makes the recognition of hemothorax important in this population1.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Mucosal melanoma is a subtype of Malignant Melanoma (MM). Urethral malignant melanoma is an extremely rare entity with a poor prognosis. It is associated with early recurrence and metastases. Methodology： It is a retrospective case report. Data was retrieved from the Human Information System (HIS)， an electronic data-based system of Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital and Research Centre. Case Discussion： We presented a case of MM of the urethra. Forty-year-old male presented with hematuria and mass in the penile urethra for 6 months. Cystoscopy and excision of the mass were performed which showed malignant melanoma. After complete pre-operative workup and multi-disciplinary team meeting， anterior urethrectomy and suprapubic cystostomy was performed. Adjuvant interferon was given. However， the patient presented with bilateral inguinal lymph node metastases which was detected on Positron Emission Tomography scan. He was offered radical treatment. He did not consent for the surgery. Patient died after 1 year of completion of treatment. Conclusion： With little knowledge reported， the management of urethral MM is still controversial. Proper planning and aggressive nature of treatment might help in curative management.

【1】KEYWORDS Malignant Melanoma， Mucosal Malignant Melanoma， Genifourinary Malignant Melanoma， Rare Urethral Cancer， Malignant Melanoma of Urethra

【2】Introduction

【3】Malignant Melanoma (MM) can affect any part of the body. There are two types of malignant melanoma， i.e. cutaneous MM and mucosal MM. Primary mucosal MM is a rare occurrence that constitutes 4% of all MM J. Mucosal MM can arise from all mucosal surfaces of the body； however， it mostly arises from the head and neck， female genital tract， anorectal region， and urinary tract . Melanocytes arise from neuroectodermal cells， and the urethra arises from the endoderm. Hence the incidence of malignant melanoma of the urethra is rare .

【4】The first case of urethral MM was reported by Reed . After that， some case reports and series have been published . The largest pool of data was published El-Safadi et al. in 2013 . The disease is more predominant in females. The clinical presentation of urethral MM is similar to that of urothelial carci-noma， resulting in a delay of diagnosis . Despite aggressive treatment of the disease， the prognosis of the disease remains poor.

【5】We reviewed the data from 1st January 2000 till 31st Decem-ber 2019. Two hundred seventy-one patients with a primary diagnosis of MM were registered at Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital and Research Centre. One hundred seventy-four patients had primary cutaneous MM while 97 patients had primary mucosal MM. Only one patient had MM of the urethra， which constitutes 0.36% of all MM and 1% of all mucosal MM. In this case， we present a case report of MM arising from the urethra discuss the clinical management of the disease.

【6】Case report

【7】Forty-six years old presented in the outpatient department with a history of hematuria and mass palpable in the last six months. He had an addiction to smoking 20 packs of cigarettes. He had no comorbidities and denied any family history of cancer. The abdominal examination was unremarkable. Cystoscopy and excision of the mass were performed， which showed a mass in the penile urethra. Histopathology slides showed nests and sheets of malignant neoplasm composed of spindle-shaped ep-ithelioid cells. There is moderate cytological atypia with pleo-morphic vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. Intracytoplas-mic melanin is also observed along with brisk mitotic activity as well as areas of necrosis. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for HBM45 and melan A， thus confirming malignant melanoma. After the surgery， a metastatic workup was per-formed， which was negative. Urethrogram was performed， which showed mucosal irregularity near navicular fossa and filling defect in bulbous urethra hinting towards the skip lesion of the known urethral malignant melanoma. Positron Emission Tomography scan (PET) confirmed urethrogram findings. How-ever， no FDG avid metastatic activity was observed. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scan showed soft tissue mass， which involves the vulvar part of the anterior urethra， with expan-sion and invasion into the corpus spongiosum. However， the membranous urethra and pelvic diaphragm had a normal ap-pearance. The patient was discussed in Multi-Disciplinary Team(MDT) meeting； the recommendation from MDT was to perform surgical resection followed by adjuvant interferon therapy.

【8】Anterior urethrectomy and suprapubic cystostomy were per-formed. The operative finding was a palpable tumour in the bulbar urethra. Histopathology was consistent with mucosal MM， and all of the margins were uninvolved with MM. The stage of the tumour was pT1. The patient remained stable during his post-operative period and was discharged on the fourth day of surgery. The patient was given adjuvant doses of interferon for three months. Then he was kept on surveillance.

【9】On his first visit after completion of therapy， bilateral in-guinal lymphadenopathy was appreciated on clinical exam-ination. PET scan showed bilateral FDG avid inguinal lym-phadenopathy. Ultrasound Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) con-firmed the metastatic MM of inguinal lymph nodes. After MDT recommendation， the patient was offered radical cystoprostatec-tomy with bilateral inguinal lymph node dissection. He refused further management and wanted to try herbal medications. Un-fortunately， he died after one year of surgical treatment due to metastases of the disease.

【10】Cutaneous MM is the commonest subtype of MM， comprising81% of all cases of MM. Involvement of male urethra by MM is an extremely rare entity. Urethral MM accounts for 0.2% of all MM while 4% of all urethral MM ， which can be seen in our reported case. The distal urethra is the most common site involved by MM ； in our case report， the distal urethra was involved.

【11】Our patient presented earlier than the reported mean age of diagnosis of mucosal MM . Male patients present slightly ear-lier than female patients . The most common symptoms are urethral mass， dysuria，local bleeding，hematuria， incontinence， vaginal bleeding， non-specific perineal pain， vaginal discharge and weight loss . Our patient presented with hematuria and urethral mass for six months. The mean duration of symp-toms reported is 21 weeks. However this patient presented late. Urethral MM are mistaken for either benign lesion including mucosal prolapse and chancre or malignant lesions .

【12】The pathogenesis of urethral malignant melanoma is still un-known， and several theories have been proposed. A possible mechanism is a metaplastic change in the squamous and glan-dular epithelium into pigment-producing cells (Melanocytes). Immunohistochemical markers are used in the diagnosis of MM as on the microscopic examination， and there is a wide histological spectrum of patterns. The most commonly used markers are S-100 protein and HMB-45. In our case report， we used HMB-45 for confirming the histological diagnosis of MM. HMB-45 is considered quite specific for melanocytic neoplasm.

【13】Majority of the times， patients present with metastases due to the aggressive biology of the disease. Despite radical man-agement， which involves radical surgery， chemotherapy， im-munotherapy and radiotherapy the prognosis remains poor. We did the same for the management of our patient； we started with the pre-operative workup to know the extent of the disease and the metastases if present. The curative surgery was performed with the achievement of RO resection of the tu-mour. Inguinal lymph node dissection is still debatable. Some suggest performing lymph node dissection at the time of pri-mary surgery . Inguinal lymph nodes are the first site of metastases in distal urethra MM. Although we did not perform inguinal lymph node dissection at the time of primary surgery and then on surveillance， the patient presented with inguinal lymphadenopathy， but the evidence from this case report is not enough in taking the decision of inguinal lymph node dissection. The optimal surgical treatment for this disease is still controver-sial.

【14】Mucosal MM is associated with early recurrence and early metastases， as is seen in our study. Despite surgical treatment and adjuvant therapy， the patient presented with early metas-tases. Metastases to inguinal lymph node occur due to spread through the deep lymphatic system. A palpabletumour at pre-sentation is a sign of advanced disease. It is observed in our patient that he presented late after six months of symptoms and had a palpable mass in the urethra； these two factors indicate the aggressive nature of the disease resulting in a poor progno-sis. In our case， we did have the chance of performing more extensive resection and offering further adjuvant chemotherapy or immunotherapy， but the patient did not consent for it.

【15】MM of the distal urethra in male is an infrequent entity. De-spite radical treatment， including surgery， chemotherapy， im-munotherapy and radiotherapy， the disease’s prognosis is still dismal. This case report will add information from this part of the world regarding the management of urethral MM.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： The pituitary tumour is the most common tumour found in the Sella region of the skull with varying prevalence. Although classified as benign， this tumour has a significant rate of morbidity and mortality. Case evaluation and disease courses require in determining therapy and prognosis for further cases. Material and Methods：This retrospective descriptive study used data collection methods derived from the medical records of patients with pituitary tumours at three hospitals in Makassar， South Sulawesi. Data collection was carried out based on diagnosis， gender， chief complaints， head (Computerized Tomography) CT scan results， Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) results， treatment， anatomic pathology results， and patient follow-up. Results： The results showed that five patients with pituitary adenoma who had the mean age of 45， three (60%) patients are male， and two (40%) are female. One patient(20%) with symptoms of endocrine disorders (acromegaly)， four (80%) patients with symptoms of the mass effect. Tumour size was measured volumetrically using the initial and the last follow-up MRI. We found that all detected masses were isointense with the most significant size 34 mm， the smallest size of 30 mm， and the mean previous tumour was 32 mm(SD=1.79). All patients underwent transsphenoidal (TSS) procedures. 60% showed a significant improvement in visual field abnormalities and headaches after surgery. A second TSS surgery performed in 1 patient (20%) found to have tumour persistence. Conclusions： TSS remains the treatment of choice for pituitary tumours. This study shows safe and effective TSS for pituitary tumours， provided surgeons with considerable experience and expertise perform it.

【1】KEYWORDS Acromegaly， Headache， Pituitary adenoma， Transsphenoidal surgery

【2】Introduction

【3】Pituitary tumours are the most common tumours found in the Sella region， which is 90-95%. Based on the study by Ezzat et al.  of 13 reviews on pituitary tumours， the prevalence of pituitary tumours varies from 1% to 40% in radiological studies and 1%-35% in post mortem (autopsy) studies. In an immuno-histochemical examination， the incidence is 25%-41%.

【4】These tumours most often found in women aged between 15-44 years ， and the most common type of tumour is a pituitary adenoma， which is 84.6% . In men， the mean size of a pituitary tumour is greater 23 mm compared to 15 mm in women. Larger tumours are found in the male because the diagnosis of pituitary tumours more slowly detected in men. Pituitary tumours are higher in incidence in the Negroid race than in the Caucasian and mongoloid races， but the exact cause of this condition still needs further investigation .

【5】Pituitary tumours usually develop slowly， benig mOuI P：n but areassociated with significant morbidity and premature mortal-ity . Pituitary tumours histologically resemble normal pi-tuitary glands. The number of hormones produced by the pi- tuitary gland increases with the development of the pituitary tumour. Besides，some cells are not functioning or "null" in the parenchyma that develops into adenomas. Pathogenesis of tu-mours is a multifactorial process， and the mechanism divided into three major groups ：

【6】1\. abnormalities of the genes that regulate the development and growth of the cell，

【7】2\. abnormalities of tumour suppressor genes and

【8】3\. disorders of genes that control cell death.

【9】Several genetic factors， including hormones， growth factors， and cell cycle regulators， work together on epigenetic events in the formation of pituitary tumours. Many researchers have reported methylated tumour suppressor genes. Many genes such as pituitary tumour transforming gene (PTTG)， pituitary-tumour-derived fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (Pdt-FGR2)， Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) damage inducible gamma pro-tein (GADD45G)， maternally expressed protein 3A (MEG3A)， zinc ginger protein pleiomorphic adenoma gene-like 1 (ZAC)， death-associated protein kinase (DAP kinase)， pituitary tumour apoptosis gene (PTAG) and p27 show its role in the formation of pituitary tumours. PTTG is closely related to the invasive and aggressive nature of pituitary tumours Four main groups， symptoms and signs of pituitary tumours can be classified as：

【10】a) Endocrine disorders； caused by overproduction or decreased hormone production causing an Addisonian crisis or sec-ondary amenorrhea.

【11】b) Mass effect on surrounding structures. Furthermore， hydro-cephalus is caused by suppression of the three ventricles which disrupt the flow of cerebrospinal fluid.

【12】c) Headache was due to stretching or compressing the Dura mater in the Sella or diaphragmatic， which is supplied by the trigeminal nerve branch.

【13】d) Accidental findings where 'accidental' tumours are found during the examination of other conditions.

【14】The dominant symptoms are endocrine and visual disor-ders. Visual disturbances that arise in the form of bitempo-ral visual field disorders due to suppression on the optic chiasm inferior. If the pressure is present for a long time， fundoscopy can show optic nerve atrophy .

【15】Adenomas that produce growth hormone show symptoms of acromegaly or gigantism， prolactin causes secondary amen-orrhea and galactorrhea， and Adrenocorticotropic Hormone(ACTH) causes Cushing's syndrome. Gonadotropin adenoma causes symptoms of gonadal dysfunction. While tumours that do not produce more hormones cause visual disturbances， al-though some cases report pan-hypopituitarism or apoplexy.

【16】Examination of pituitary tumours carried out with the fol-lowing studies ：

【17】1\. Radioimmune-assay examination to identify the hormone secreted.

【18】2\. MRI in the pituitary section， with sagittal and coronal re-construction， is the gold standard for pituitary examination.

【19】MRI examination revealed microadenomas as low-density focal lesions and macroadenomas as isointense and hyperintense lesions . CT scan can detect microadenoma up to 4mm in size. Macroadenoma provides a clearer picture with intravenous contrast， and it's more clear to see an extracellular extension with coronal scanning .

【20】Plain X-Ray examination shows enlargement accompanied by erosion of Sella turcica with prominent contours  .

【21】Management of pituitary tumours ：

【22】1\. Medication： In some type's dopamine agonists and soma statin， analogues can be given to adenomas that secrete growth hormone.

【23】2\. Radiotherapy： only performed if there is a subtotal tu-mour excision or if the postoperative endocrine examina-tion shows residue in the form of increased hormone secre-tion relapse occurs， but it's rare in macroadenoma. Total surgery is also performed to decompress the optic chiasm and optic nerye.

【24】A surgical technique using the transsphenoidal endoscopy f+approach is the choice of treatment because it's minimally inva-sive and allows the operator to access lesions on the cranial base . This technique does not require an oral/nasal incision， does not require a nasal speculum， good illumination and does not require nasal packing/tamponade for the nose because it does not result in postoperative epistaxis and is more directed towards the Sella turcica region .

【25】Transsphenoidal endoscopic surgery is performed by first checking the levels and function of hormones (especially thyroid to avoid complications in cardiovascular)， medical treatment in cases of macroadenoma with severe visual impairment， ad-equate radiological examination， examination of cortisol levels to avoid postoperative complications due to loss of ACTH， and administration of Hydrocortisone 100 mg during anaesthesia was administered .

【26】Material and Method

【27】This research is a retrospective， descriptive study. Data took the form of secondary data from medical records of patients at Hasanuddin University Hospital and Grestelina hospitals in Makassar， South Sulawesi， Indonesia， from January 2016， to December 2017， with a diagnosis of pituitary tumour. Data collected were diagnosis， gender， major complaint， head CT scan result， MRI result， treatments， anatomic pathology results， and patient follow-up.

【28】The chief complaint has divided the patients into four groups：

【29】1\. endocrine disorders (symptoms due to increased or de-creased hormone production).

【30】2\. mass effects (visual field disorders， hydrocephalus， and apoplexy).

【31】3\. Headaches，

【32】4\. tumours that found accidental when diagnosing other dis-eases.

【33】MRI results in the form of low-density lesions are classified as microadenoma， and isointense or hypertensive lesions are classified as macroadenoma. The results of the follow-up were group into three categories： improvement， worsening， and could not be determined (lost to follow-up).

【34】Result

【35】There were five patients with a diagnosis of benign pituitary ade-noma based on histopathological examination after transsphe-noidal endoscopic surgery.

【36】1\. Age and sex presentation The youngest age of patients diagnosed with benign pituitary adenoma is 38 years， and the oldest is 72 years . The mean age of 45 years with a standard deviation of 12，34 years. In 5 patients with benign diagnosis， pituitary adenoma obtained 3 (60%) are male， and 2 (40%) are female .

【37】2\. Presentation On the presentation， one patient (20%) with the symptom of endocrine disorders (acromegaly)， two (40%) patients with mass effect symptom (visual field disorders)， and two (40%) patients headache symptom .

【38】3\. Tumour size Tumour size was measured volumetrically us-ing the initial and the last follow-up MRI. We found that all detected masses were isointense with the most significant size 34 mm， the smallest size 30 mm， and the mean last tumour was 32 mm (SD=1.79) . CT scan results obtained slight hyperdense mass images with the largest size of 34.1 mm， the smallest size of 29.00 mm，and a mean of 31.16 mm (SD=1.97) .

【39】4\. Procedure Procedures given were mild pituitary gland TSS procedure in 4 patients (80%)， and severe pituitary gland TSS procedure in 1 patient (20%)，and none of the patients received medical therapy or radiotherapy. There are no postoperative complications reported .

【40】5\. Outcome Three patients (60%) showed a significant im-provement in visual field abnormalities and headache af-ter surgery， and 2 (40%) patients lost to follow-up . A second transsphenoidal (TSS) endoscopy surgery performed in 1 patient (20%) found to have tumour per-sistence. Pituitary hormone deficiencies increased after surgery. There are no complications after TSS surgery.

【41】Pituitary tumours were more common in males than in a female， our results difference with Mansour AA et al.， where they result in more common in a female than a male. Differences in gender domination of the pituitary adenoma in some literature may vary depending on hormonal secretion， patient age， tumour size. However， in Argentina and Saudi Arabia， the majority of pituitary tumours were dominated by a female .

【42】On the findings of clinical symptoms， the overall patient dom-inated by symptoms of mass effects and headaches. There is only one case with a clinical symptom of acromegaly， one of the clinical symptom of growth hormone (GH) cell adenoma. Although the findings on physical examination and comor-bidities are significant， the diagnosis of clinical symptoms in acromegaly can take a long time because the process is slow and is not realized by the patient or those around the patient .

【43】In patients with acromegaly symptoms， symptoms are experi-enced for four years before the patient undergoes the procedure. The findings in this study are contradictory to the theory that the symptoms of pituitary adenoma tumours dominated by in-creased pituitary hormone secretion. In contrast， symptoms such as pituitary lymphocytes， pituitary apoplexy， cranial nerve paral-ysis， temporal lobe epilepsy， hydrocephalus， and rhinorrhea are less frequent . Patients with acromegaly and Cushing’s dis-ease are at increased risk of hypertension and cardiovascular disease， diabetes， and obstructive sleep apnea. 60% of patients in our study had improvements symptoms after TSS surgery. Nomikos et al. assessing pituitary function in NFPAs before and after pituitary surgery in which only 9.7% of patients presented with headaches and 30，8% with visual field disorders .

【44】Non-functioning pituitary adenomas (NFPAs) are benignade-nohypophyseal tumours not associated with clinical evidence of hormonal hypersecretion . In this study， patients with NFPAs found in 80% of patients， and they came to the hospital because of visual field disorders and headaches. Visual disorders defects are the most common neuro-ophthalmological symptom， these symptoms because of tumour extent to the optic chiasma 一Nfpas majority found by incidental findings. However， with an increasing frequency of radiological evaluations of the Central nervous system (CNS) for another disease， pituitary adenomas are detected more frequently than in the past .

【45】The images on investigations (MRI and CT Scan) in all cases show the features that are following macroadenoma， namely isointense lesions on MRI examination with a size of more than10 mm and no tumour is calcified on CT Scan8. Patients with macroadenomas present with a deficiency of at least one pitu-itary hormone sequel from the compression normal anterior pituitary and or pituitary stalk .

【46】The primary treatment for many pituitary tumours is surgery those with neuro-ophthalmologic complaints and or tumours LtS affecting the optic pathway. Surgery is also urgently indicated for patients with apoplexy who develop neuro-ophthalmologic complaints. In our institution， tumours extent than 2 cm is needed surgery due to their propensity for growth in nearby structures. A Transsphenoidal hypophysectomy is a surgery method the most commonly used to remove a pituitary tumour that is relevant to literature 12.

【47】The success rate of transsphenoidal endoscopy varies be-tween 60% to 80%. Open surgery on a pituitary tumour is needed if there is a sub-frontal or retro clival extension of cancer. Postoperative care requires special attention to fluid balance， blood sugar levels， and hormonal status. Vision has improved but depends on the weight and duration of vision loss before surgery. Endocrine function sustained in 80% of patients with-out endocrine complaints before surgery， but if there is a loss of hormonal function and panhypopituitarism， hormone function cannot be supported. The need for radiotherapy is considered by examining residual tumours with MRI approximately two months postoperatively .

【48】The most common complication of pituitary tumour surgery with transsphenoidal endoscopy approach is cerebrospinal fluid leakage. Some clinicians recommend creating mucoperiosteal or mucoperichondrial flaps at the beginning of surgery to an-ticipate cerebrospinal fluid leakage， especially in tumours that have invaded the dura mater or arachnoid membranes. If no cerebrospinal fluid leak obtained， the flap would only create additional injury for the patient .

【49】All patients undergoing TSS surgery in Makassar are report-edly no complications. Yao et al.  reported that TSS en-doscopic therapy showed a lower operating time and hospital stay compared to the craniotomy approach . A minimally invasive endoscopic approach reduces the proportion of postop-erative complications such as cerebrospinal fluid leakage， septal perforation， and epistaxis compared to the microscopic approachJ.

【50】Recurrence of the pituitary tumours has been reported to occur in 10-40% of the patients， depending on adjunctive radio-therapy is accepted or not. Guadalupe Vargas et al. reported that tumour recurrence or persistence was detected in 27%，and all of these subjects underwent a second pituitary operation， mostly via the TSS approach. Adenoma regrowth associated with the presence of a tumour remnant after initial surgery which is a common occurrence in NFPAs 91. Reddy et al.  found the rate of pituitary tumours regrowth only for 6.9% in cases with complete tumour resection and 40% patients in whom tumour remnant had been left behind . In our retrospective study， we had no recurrence occur observed at 2-year follow-up， but further study required with more samples and longer follow-up.

【51】Conclusion

【52】TSS remains the treatment of choice for pituitary tumours. This study shows safe and effective TSS for pituitary tumours， pro-vided surgeons with considerable experience and expertise per-form it.

【0】Background：

【1】Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding is a symptom of a wide range of clinical disorders some of which are primarily not related to the gastrointestinal tract. This report highlights the diagnostic challenges encountered in the management of a case of metastatic choriocarcinoma that presented with features of upper GI bleeding.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 28-year old Para l\* woman presented at the Gynecological Emergency Unit of a tertiary health facility in Nigeria with a 3-month history of amenorrhoea and generalized body weakness of one week duration. Her past medical history was notable for a uterine evacuation that she had four years earlier on the suspicion of hydatidiform mole. Investigations showed a hematocrit of 09% and positive urinary pregnancy tests. She had an emergency pelvic exploration on a strong suspicion of ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Operative findings， however， showed grossly normal and intact reproductive tract. Her rapidly declining hematocrit in spite of blood transfusions and passage of tarry stool in the following week postoperative necessitated a referral to the General Surgery Unit with a provisional diagnosis of upper GI bleeding possibly from chronic duodenal ulcer. However， this diagnosis was excluded by an emergency esophago-duodenoscopy at the surgical unit. Her deteriorating clinical condition necessitated a surgical abdominal re-exploration that showed hemorrhagic jejunal tumors and an ileo-ileal intussusception. Histological examination of the excised specimen showed features in keeping with metastatic choriocarcinoma. Her clinical condition improved on chemotherapy and has remained satisfactory on follow-up.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Diagnosis of metastatic choriocarcinoma of the small bowel requires a high index of suspicion and a multidisciplinary approach to its management in order to reduce the risk of severe morbidity and mortality. Prompt surgical intervention by laparotomy may be life-saving in situations where the source of bleeding cannot be readily ascertained either as a result of diagnostic obscurity or limitations in diagnostic facilities.

【6】Key words： gastrointestinal bleeding · choriocarcinoma · small bowel· Metastasis Bleeding from the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) is a symptom of a disease rather than being a disease it-self and some of the associated conditions could be life threatening . Locating the source of bleeding is very important and every other patient with fea-tures of GIT bleeding should be seriously evaluated. Institution of appropriate and timely management may be hampered by inadequate diagnostic facilities. In this report， we present a case of metastatic choriocar-cinoma that was managed at a tertiary health facility in Nigeria to create awareness among clinicians and highlight the difficulties associated with the manage-ment of such cases in resource-limited settings.

【7】CASE REPORT

【8】A 28-year-old Para 1+ woman presented at the Gynecological Emergency Unit of Olabisi Onabanjo University Teaching Hospital， Sagamu， Nigeria with a 3-month history of amenorrhoea and generalised body weakness of one-week duration. There was no history of vaginal blood loss or fainting attacks. Few days prior to presentation， she experienced epigastric pain that later resolved spontaneously without treat-ment. Her appetite was good and there had been no vomiting or change in bowel habit. She complained of generalised headache， which had persisted for 6weeks prior to presentation and had not responded to ingested analgesics.

【9】Her past medical history was notable for a uterine evacuation that she had four years earlier on the suspicion of hydatidiform mole at a private hospital. However， histological investigation of the evacu-ated specimen was not performed and she did not receive any follow-up management. Two years after the evacuation， she had an uneventful pregnancy and spontaneous vaginal delivery of her only child. Review of the systems did not provide any additional information.

【10】General physical examination showed that she was acutely ill-looking， severe pale， anicteric and not fe-brile to touch. Her pulse rate was 110 beats per min-ute and blood pressure was 100/60 mmHg. Systemic examinations did not yield any abnormal findings. Bimanual pelvic examination showed a slightly bulky uterus but there was no adnexal tenderness. Investigations showed that her hematocrit was 09%and urinary pregnancy tests were positive on four different but consecutive occasions. Her white cell count， electrolytes and urea were all within normal limits. The hospital had no CT scan facility and abdomino-pelvic ultrasound examination could not be performed at the moment because the machine was under repair. In view of the clinical picture and positive pregnancy tests， the gynaecological team decided to perform an emergency pelvic exploration on a strong suspicion of ruptured ectopic pregnancy. She was stabilised with blood transfusion and subse-quently had an emergency pelvic exploration through a Pfannenstiel's incision. However， operative findings revealed grossly normal and intact uterus， ovaries and fallopian tubes. The surgery was concluded and the decision was to maintain an adequate hemoglobin concentration by repeated blood transfusions while she undergoes further investigations. Her immediate postoperative condition was clinically satisfactory and her general condition remained stable. Her headache also subsided few days after admission.

【11】One week postoperative， her hematocrit was noticed to have dropped from 32% that it was in the immedi-ate postoperative period to 19% in spite of transfusion with six units of blood during the period. She was also noticed to be passing watery tarry stool during the same period. At this point， she was then referred to the General Surgery Unit with a provisional diag-nosis of upper gastrointestinal bleeding possibly from a chronic duodenal ulcer. At the surgical unit， she had an emergency esophago-gastroduodenoscopy， which did not show any evidence of upper GI bleeding. In spite of the finding， she was empirically managed conservatively with cold saline gastric lavage and aspiration， nil per oral and intravenous cimetidine injections. The following morning， she passed about500 ml of watery tarry stool but there was no hema-tochezia. Her clinical condition deteriorated further and this necessitated a surgical re-exploration of the abdomen by the General Surgeons. Operative findings included a 5 cm x 5 cm hemorrhagic tumor at the mid-portion of the jejunum that had eroded through the serosal surface ； a 2 cm x 2 cm hemorrhagic nodule approximately 25 cm from the tumor； an ileo-ileal intussusception approximately100 cm from the ileo-cecal junction with a 2 cm x 2cm nodule at its leading point. The main tumor and the nodule were resected along with the affected por-tion of the bowel and a wedge-resection of the lead-ing point of the intussusception was also performed after reduction. Bowel continuity was restored by jejuno-jejunal and ileo-ileal anastomoses.

【12】She was transfused with a total of 15 units of blood during the perioperative and immediate postoperative period. Her postoperative hematocrit was 28% and the postoperative period was largely uneventful. She was commenced on oral intake on the 5th postoperati ve day， which was well tolerated. Histological examination of the excised specimen showed features consistent with metastatic choriocarcinoma of the small intestine . In view of the histological diagnosis， the patient was transferred back to the Gynecological Unit of the hospital for further management. She received che-motherapy for a period of 6 months and her condition has remained satisfactory on follow-up.

【13】DISCUSSION

【14】Acute gastrointestinal bleeding continues to be a frequent cause of hospital surgical admission， which is associated with considerable risk of morbidity and mortality . The reported mortality rates lie between 10 and 20 percent although this is de-pendent on many other factors . Identification of the source of bleeding may be a serious problem but it is extremely important in order to reduce the associated morbidity and mortality risks. The case presented showed that prompt surgical intervention by exploratory laparotomy may be life-saving in situations where the source of bleeding cannot be readily ascertained.

【15】The diagnostic difficulties presented by this woman highlight the importance of adequate history and physical examination in patients with severe anae-mia of unknown origin in resource-limited settings. It also shows that a high index of suspicion of the condition needs to be maintained in spite of its rar-ity. The initial clinical picture was in keeping with ruptured ectopic pregnancy considering the severe anaemia， amenorrhoea and positive pregnancy tests. The lack of facility for serum B-hCG precluded the diagnosis of choriocarcinoma at the initial stage of the management. A diagnostic laparoscopy before the first surgical exploration， which could have pre-vented an unnecessary surgical intervention， was probably not performed to avoid further delay. Such decision may be justified by the fact that majority of cases of ectopic pregnancy presenting to our hospi-tal are of the ruptured variety and clinical diagnosis and timely surgical intervention often limit the case fatality rate. The antecedent molar pregnancy that she had four years before presentation was probably not considered to be a clue to the diagnosis because there was no histological confirmation and the fact that only a small percentage (2-3%) of such preg-nancies progress to choriocarcinoma . The normal pregnancy and childbirth that she had two years later also downplayed the possibility of choriocarcinoma more so that there were no pelvic manifestations of the disease. Although choriocarcinoma is frequently diagnosed within one year after the antecedent preg-nancy， the literature shows that the interval may vary widely and it could be as long as 9 years .

【16】In addition to adequate history and thorough physical examination， management of cases of suspected gas-trointestinal bleeding requires extensive investigations notably endoscopy. A more extensive endoscopic investigation by inclusion of enteroscopy in this case could have ensured a pre-operative identifica-tion of the source of bleeding. This was however not performed because the facility was not available in our hospital. Series of reports in the literature have emphasised the importance of panendoscopy and angiographic studies in the management of obscure gastrointestinal bleeding .

【17】It is important for clinicians to realise that in ap-proximately one-third of cases， the presenting fea-tures of choriocarcinoma are not gynecological but originate from distant metastasis especially to the lungs， liver and brain . Our patient presented with a small bowel metastasis in the absence of features consistent with metastasis to the three most common sites of secondaries. The persistent headache that the patient experienced could not be attributed to cerebral metastasis as this commonly presents with focal neurological signs， convulsions and evidence of intracerebral or sub-arachnoid haemorrhage . Besides， it is unusual for cerebral metastasis to oc-cur in the absence of pulmonary or liver metastasis. The headache was probably as a result of the chronic anaemia that she experienced as it resolved spontane-ously without any specific treatment.

【18】It is imperative to distinguish gestational choriocar-cinoma from nongestational choriocarcinoma arising in an ovarian germ cell tumour or from trophoblastic differentiation in a common epithelial carcinoma as the prognosis and therapy are distinct in each type.

【19】Nongestational choriocarcinoma tends to be less responsive to chemotherapy and has a less favour-able prognosis than gestational choriocarcinoma. Extragonadal nongestational choriocarcinoma along the gastrointestinal system is extremely rare and in-volvement of only the duodenum  and rectum  has been reported in the literature.

【20】CONCLUSIONS

【21】This report highlights some of the challenges encoun-tered in the diagnosis and management of gastroin-testinal bleeding due to an uncommon disease entity in resource-limited settings. Severe morbidity and increased risk of mortality often accompany delay in diagnosis and institution of appropriate management. Diagnosis of metastastic choriocarcinoma of the small bowel requires a high index of suspicion and a mul-tidisciplinary approach to its management. Prompt surgical intervention by laparotomy may be life-sav-ing in situations where the source of bleeding cannot be readily ascertained either as a result of diagnostic obscurity or limitations in diagnostic facilities.

【0】Background：

【1】Thrombocytopenia is a potentially treatment-limiting adverse event of particular interest with the PARPinhib-itor niraparib. This adverse event may necessitate niraparib dose reduction or treatment discontinuation， re-sulting in suboptimal treatment outcomes. Here， we report on niraparib dose optimization in 2 patients with breast cancer and 4 patients with ovarian cancer through concurrent administration of the thrombopoietin re-ceptor stimulating agent avatrombopag to mitigate thrombocytopenia， enabling niraparib reescalation and im-proved clinical response.

【2】Case Reports：

【3】Three of 6 patients received niraparib 300 mg daily， the highest recommended dose， for a sustained period. Avatrombopag therapy enabled niraparib dose escalation that led to reductions in biomarkers associated with disease progression. Before initiation of avatrombopag， increases in CA-125 levels， a marker for ovarian can-cer， were observed in association with niraparib dose interruption， and in 2 patients with ovarian cancer CA-125 levels fell in response to niraparib dose escalation enabled by concurrent avatrombopag therapy. Further， in 2 patients with metastatic breast cancer， intracranial response was observed in association with avatrom-bopag-enabled niraparib therapy. In 1 patient with metastatic breast cancer， niraparib induced an intracrani-al response， while previous use of talazoparib had not， confirming preclinical findings of superior blood-brain-barrier penetrance with niraparib.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Avatrombopag is currently approved for use in chronic immune thrombocytopenia and thrombocytopenia as-sociated with chronic liver disease in patients undergoing a surgical procedure. A clinical trial of avatrombopag for chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia is ongoing. Preliminary results in these 6 patient cases demon-strate the need for a confirmatory trial of avatrombopag for optimizing the dose of niraparib.

【6】MeSH Keywords：

【7】Breast Neoplasms · Ovarian Neoplasms ·Poly(ADP-ribose) Polymerases · Receptors， Thrombopoietin·Thrombocytopenia By interfering with DNA repair mechanisms， such as the ho mologous recombination repair pathway ， poly-ADP ribose polymerase (PARP) inhibitors have been shown to be effective in the maintenance treatment of advanced ovarian cancer  and in advanced breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2 muta-tions . Clinical trials of niraparib indicate responses in pa-tients with both germline and somatic BRCA mutations， with a smaller degree of benefit in BRCA-negative homologous re-combination deficiency (HRD)-positive patients， and the least benefit in BRCA-negative HRD-negative patients . Most recently， on April 29， 2020， niraparib was approved for first-line maintenance treatment of ovarian cancer following complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy . In an analysis of the NOVA trial， niraparib improved progres-sion-free survival outcomes in a dose-related manner . Moreover， the unique pharmacology of niraparib， including improved blood-brain-barrier penetrance over other PARP in-hibitors， has been shown to induce intracranial response in animal models .

【8】Although niraparib has unique characteristics， its therapeutic efficacy may be limited by adverse events such as thrombocy-topenia . The FDA-approved labeling for niraparib advises interruption of niraparib therapy or dose reduction for man-agement of thrombocytopenia，which may compromise effica-cy . Unfortunately， there are no medications currently approved for management of this potential treatment-limiting adverse event . Although one agent， oprelvekin， was ap-proved for the management of chemotherapy-induced throm-bocytopenia， this agent has been discontinued . Based on the mechanism of action of thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor ag-onists， these agents have the potential to treat thrombocyto penia associated with therapeutic agents for cancer， such as niraparib .

【9】TPO receptor agonists increase platelet levels by interacting with the TPO receptor on megakaryocytes， the endogenous target of thrombopoietin. Given that TPO receptor agonists in-crease platelet production， use of these agents may counter-act or mitigate PARP-induced thrombocytopenia . Approved TPO receptor agonists are avatrombopag， eltrombopag， and lusutrombopag， all of which are administered orally， as well as romiplostim， which is administered as a subcutaneous in-jection . Unlike eltrombopag， avatrombopag does not require regular monitoring for liver test abnormalities during therapy， which can reduce the complexity of monitoring in high-ly comorbid patients with cancer receiving maintenance treat-ment with niraparib. In addition， use of avatrombopag offers flexibility in oral dosing. Unlike eltrombopag， avatrombopag can be taken with polyvalent cations such as calcium， magne-sium， and iron . As a result， based on its mechanism of action， safety， and flexible dosing， avatrombopag is a rational choice for the prevention and management of thrombocyto-penia associated with niraparib therapy.

【10】This case series reviewed the treatment of 2 patients with breast cancer and 4 patients with ovarian cancer. All patients received niraparib for the maintenance treatment of advanced breast cancer or advanced ovarian cancer in combination with avatrombopag to reduce the risk of thrombocytopenia and im-prove the dose-intensity of niraparib therapy. By optimizing the dose-intensity of therapy， avatrombopag has the potential to optimize treatment outcomes， consistent with the dose-re-sponse relationship observed in multiple clinical trials of ni-raparib . In this case series， outcomes were evaluated prospectively over the course of treatment for breast or ovar-ian cancer in 6 patients.

【11】Case Reports

【12】Case 1： Breast cancer with brain metastases

【13】A patient with breast cancer， born in 1977， was diagnosed with ER-positive HER2-negative stage lll breast cancer in August2016. From September 2016 to January 2017， she received 4cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by main-tenance letrozole from a different provider. By January 2019， she had progressive disease with brain metastases. She re-ceived radiosurgery (Gamma Knife@) and subsequently start-ed abemaciclib， which she did not tolerate well. Before pre-senting in July 2019 for her fourth opinion， she had previously been seen at multiple other centers.

【14】From July 2019 to October 2019， she received talazoparib and experienced progressive disease in the brain with no response to therapy. Radiosurgery (Gamma Knife@) was not feasible and she declined whole-brain radiotherapy. The patient was then switched to a different PARP inhibitor， niraparib. Niraparib was chosen based on its ability to cross the blood-brain barrier and favorable results in regression of intracranial tumors in animal models . The patient started treatment with niraparib 300mg daily in November 2019， with CT-verified response in early January and late February 2020. This response was accompa-nied by clinical improvement， including successful discontin-uation of steroids and absence of reported seizures between December 2019 and March 2020. As of her latest CT scan per-formed April 16， 2020， this patient has experienced complete intracranial response .

【15】Use ofavatrombopag in this patient

【16】Before starting therapy with avatrombopag， this patient ex-perienced a dramatic drop in platelet count to 31 000/pL on January 8， 2020， shortly after initiating niraparib 300 mg daily on December 29， 2019. After starting treatment with avatrom-bopag 20 mg daily， the patient experienced a dramatic increase in platelet counts， which peaked at a supranormal level of757 000/pL on January 23， 2020. As this patient was extreme-ly responsive to avatrombopag， avatrombopag was held and reinitiated at a lower total weekly dose of 60 mg (20 mg admin-istered on Monday， Wednesday， and Friday each week) start-ing on February 5， 2020. The patient was able to take niraparib at the maximal dose of 300 mg daily while receiving avatrom-bopag. Before initiating avatrombopag， niraparib 300 mg dai-ly had previously caused profound thrombocytopenia. After carboplatin in combination with paclitaxel and a checkpoint inhibitor. On the clinical trial， the patient achieved partial re-sponse， until she developed progressive disease in July 2018. She received treatment with fulvestrant， palbociclib， leupro-lide， and exemestane from July 2018 until the onset of pro-gressive disease with brain metastases in April 2019.She re fused cranial radiotherapy and experienced no response with single-agent doxorubicin. On May 30， 2019， she was started on niraparib and achieved partial response in the brain， liv-er， and lungs.

【17】Use ofavatrombopag in this patient

【18】From May 30， 2019 to March 16， 2020， the patient received weekly dose of niraparib ranging from 200 mg to 2100 mg，co-administered with avatrombopag weekly doses ranging from140 mg weekly to 280 mg weekly. Of note， following an inter-ruption in niraparib dosing the week of June 15， 2019， there were a total of 3 weeks in which avatrombopag was not ad-ministered . The gap in use of avatrombopag during July and August led to subsequent low platelet levels on of140 000/pL on September 26，2019 and 148 000/pL on October21，2019. These low platelet levels due to a gap in avatrom-bopag therapy led to 2 additional interruptions in nirapar-ib therapy the weeks of November 25， 2019， and December26，2019. Despite the interruption of avatrombopag therapy， use of avatrombopag in this patient aided in escalating the dose of niraparib from 1800 mg weekly to 2000 mg weekly from August 29， 2019 to October 27， 2019. Most recently，the dose of avatrombopag was increased from 140 mg weekly to280 mg weekly， resulting in a rebound in platelet counts from48 000/pL on February 25， 2020 to 94 000/pL on March 2，2020. The increase in avatrombopag dose also enabled esca-lation of the weekly dose of niraparib from 200 mg weekly to1400 mg weekly as of March 16， 2020. On August 26， 2019 and on January 8， 2020， CT assessments indicated intracranial par-tial response . In addition to 2 standard-dose plate-let transfusions， continuous administration of avatrombopag for all but 3 weeks during the dose titration helped enable ad-ministration of the optimal dose of niraparib in this patient

【19】Case 3： Ovarian cancer

【20】A patient with stage lV ovarian cancer， born in 1959， was di-agnosed in October 2018. She received carboplatin， paclitax-el， and bevacizumab from November 2018 to February 2019. After experiencing partial response to primary treatment， she received maintenance niraparib therapy. On her last CT scan， January 26， 2020， she was found to have stable disease. Her CA-125 levels indicate response to treatment.

【21】Before receiving avatrombopag， this patient was initiated on a maximal dose of niraparib of 2100 mg weekly starting on March 18， 2019， which rapidly led to a profound reduction in platelet counts， as low as 36 000/pL Following 2 interruptions of niraparib therapy the weeks of March 25， 2019 and April 29，2019， CA-125 levels increased from 33 units/mL to 57 units/mL. When platelet counts had recovered by May 8， 2019， the pa-tient was again initiated on niraparib at a reduced weekly dose of 1400 mg， which gradually increased to 1900 mg weekly by October 15， 2019. Although platelet counts were initially sta-ble during dose escalation， shortly after the dose of nirapa-rib was escalated to 2000 mg weekly on October 19， 2019， the patient's platelet count dropped below 100 000/pL short-ly afterward on October 29， 2019. As a result， the patient was prescribed avatrombopag at a dose of 20 mg daily (140 mg weekly) to stabilize platelet counts. Initiation of avatrombopag enabled further niraparib dose escalation to 2100 mg week-ly on December 15， 2019. Notably， the patient's last platelet count was 219 000/pL on March 17， 2020 on the same dose of niraparib that had previously caused a precipitous decline in platelet counts prior to receiving avatrombopag. Additionally， CA-125 levels in this patient have more than halved since ini-tiating treatment with avatrombopag， falling from 69 units/mL to 32 units/mL. This reduction in CA-125 levels occurred con-currently with dose escalation of niraparib to 2000 mg/week and then 2100 mg/week， which was enabled by concurrent administration of avatrombopag .

【22】Case 4： Ovarian cancer

【23】A female patient born in 1954 was diagnosed with stage ll ovar-ian cancer concurrent with uterine cancer and fallopian tube cancer in July 2017. She received debulking surgery followed by 6 cycles of carboplatin and docetaxel from August 2017 to December 2017. In August 2019， she developed recurrence in the liver and peritoneum. Following recurrence， from August2019 to December 2019， she received carboplatin， paclitaxel， and bevacizumab， followed by maintenance therapy with bevaci-zumab plus niraparib. A recent CT scan indicated stable disease.

【24】Use ofavatrombopag in this patient

【25】In this patient， administration of avatrombopag 20 mg daily concurrently with initiation of niraparib 300 mg daily may have reduced the severity of platelet count reduction， to 63 000/pL by February 20， 2020. The use of avatrombopag 40 mg dai-ly has enabled the patient to tolerate niraparib 300 mg daily， with a platelet count of 155 000/pL measured on March 19，2020， 1 week after starting niraparib. CA-125 levels were sta-ble in this patient while using niraparib in combination with avatrombopag.

【26】A female patient born in 1966 was diagnosed with stage ⅢII ovarian cancer in October 2018. She received 6 cycles of car-boplatin， paclitaxel， and bevacizumab from November 2018to April 2019 followed by niraparib maintenance therapy. She declined dual maintenance therapy with bevacizumab and ni-raparib. Her CA-125 levels showed a rise when niraparib main-tenance was interrupted， and a subsequent decline when ni-raparib therapy was reintroduced and the dose was escalated.

【27】Use ofavatrombopag in this patient

【28】Before starting avatrombopag， the patient experienced 3 ep-isodes of platelet count declines in association with nirapar-ib use from April 2019 to August 2019 . After starting avatrombopag at a weekly dose of 140 mg， the patient was able to tolerate an increase in her weekly niraparib dose from500 mg to 900 mg on December 2， 2019 and a further increase to 1000 mg weekly on March 18， 2020. On February 5， 2019， the dose of avatrombopag increased from 140 mg weekly to280 mg weekly. Despite continued up-titration in the dose of niraparib， platelet counts continued to rise. CA-125 levels fell from 43 U/mL on February 5， 2020 to 37 U/mL by March 4，2020 concurrent with continuous use of niraparib and avatrom-bopag in this patient.

【29】Case 6： Ovarian cancer

【30】A patient born in 1944 was diagnosed with stage Ill ovarian cancer in March 2019. From March 2019 to May 2019，she re-ceived 4 cycles of carboplatin， paclitaxel， and bevacizumab， fol-lowed by debulking surgery in June 2019. Following disease progression， she received 4 cycles of carboplatin and paclitax-el until September 2019， followed by rucaparib maintenance. CA-125 levels in this patient had normalized since surgical in-tervention and have remained stable throughout treatment. As of March 2020， she was disease-free.

【31】Use ofavatrombopag in this patient

【32】In this patient， niraparib therapy was initiated at a dose of700 mg weekly on December 4， 2019， which was gradually in-creased to 2100 mg weekly by January 7， 2020. With upward dose titration， platelet counts fell from a peak of 199 000/pL on December 11，2019 to 106 000/uL by December 26，2019. As a result of this drop in platelet counts， avatrombopag was also initiated on December 26， 2019 at a daily dose of 20 mg(140 mg weekly). As a result of avatrombopag coadministra-tion， the patient experienced an increase in platelet counts to 163 000/pL on January 7， 2020. To support further dose escalation and platelet count stabilization on January 7，2020， the daily dose of avatrombopag was escalated to 40 mg daily(280 mg weekly) and the niraparib dose was escalated to the maximal dose of 2100 mg weekly. Although 2 troughs in plate-let levels occurred despite avatrombopag therapy ， these troughs were managed through niraparib dose reduction ini-tially to 1400 mg weekly on January 29， 2020， and then to 700mg weekly by March 11， 2020. Although dose reductions were necessary to maintain platelet counts above 100 000/pL， this patient has been able to continue niraparib therapy， which may not have been possible in the absence of avatrombopag therapy.

【35】Three of 6 patients were able to sustain treatment with the maximum dose of niraparib (300 mg daily) for at least 3 con-tinuous weeks. Continuous administration of avatrombopag mitigated thrombocytopenia and enabled dose escalation of niraparib to induce CT-confirmed response in 2 patients with breast cancer (cases 1 and 2). Reductions in CA-125 levels were observed in association with niraparib therapy enabled by avatrombopag therapy in 2 of 4 patients with ovarian can-cer (cases 3 and 5). The remaining 2 patients had stable CA-125 levels (cases 4 and 6). One of these patients (case 6) has experienced complete response and was disease-free as of March 2020. One patient with breast cancer who experienced profound thrombocytopenia (31000/pL) on niraparib attained supranormal platelet counts (757 000/pL) within 3 weeks of initiating avatrombopag 20 mg daily and was transitioned to a reduced dose (20 mg 3 times weekly)， which enabled contin-ued therapy with niraparib and continued response .

【36】Discussion

【37】Use of niraparib is limited by potential adverse events， in-cluding thrombocytopenia ， which can lead to dose in-terruption or treatment discontinuation， which may reduce efficacy . With a lack of approved medications for man-agement of thrombocytopenia， there is a need for new ther-apeutic options . Notably， in 1 patient with metastatic breast cancer， niraparib induced intracranial response， while previous use of talazoparib had not. This observation is confir-matory of preclinical findings with niraparib indicating superior blood-brain-barrier penetrance over other PARP inhibitors .

【39】To reduce the risk of adverse events with niraparib， includ-ing thrombocytopenia， the starting dose of niraparib may be adjusted based on baseline bodyweight and platelet count. Specifically， patients with a baseline bodyweight <77 kg or with a baseline platelet count <150 00/pL may receive a re-duced starting dose of 200 mg of niraparib daily， rather than a starting dose of 300 mg daily. However， the initial dose ad-justment of niraparib does not eliminate the issue of throm bocytopenia， as 14.8% of patients receiving individualized starting dose niraparib in PRIMA experienced thrombocyto-penia of grade 3 severity or higher. Preliminary results in these 6 patient cases demonstrate the need for a confirmato-ry trial of avatrombopag for optimizing the dose of niraparib.
